Interval Mud Discussion:

After drilling shoe track and rate hole with carried Bentonite mud from previous section Salt/KCl/Polymer mud will be employed to drilling this hole section.

Saturated Salt Muds are primarily used to prevent excessive hole enlargement while drilling massive salt beds. They can also be used to reduce dispersion and hydration of shales and clays.

Potassium chloride is the primary source of the potassium ions in this system. In case of soft, sticky red Marl &amp;amp; Clay which encountered problems such as bit balling additions of drilling KCl (3-5 %) to inhibit clays in Aghajari is recommended.

Potassium is used in areas where inhibition is required to limit chemical alteration of shales. Potassium performance is based on cationic exchange of potassium for sodium or calcium ions on smectites and interlayered clays. Potassium-based muds perform best on shales containing large quantities of smectite or interlayered clays in the total clay fraction. Shallow shales, containing large amounts of montmorillonite.

Potassium interactions with clay surfaces can be traced to two effects: ionic size and hydrational energy. Potassium ions are of the proper size to fit snugly into the spaces between the two silica tetrahedral layers which contact each other in the formation of a three-layer clay packet. The ionic diameter of potassium is 2.66 Å, very close to the available distance of 2.8 Å in the lattice space of the clay structure. A cation slightly smaller than 2.8 Å is desirable to allow for crystalline compaction.

In addition of using KCl, despite Aghajari is an un-permeable formation and seems that isn’t necessary to control Fluid loss, Starch and PAC LV may be used to keep FL under control.

While drilling this section XC Polymer will be used as base of rheology to extend hole cleaning and providing suitable YP and LSRV. An YP between 14-20 lb/100ft2 for sufficient carrying capacity and a LSRYP at range of 7-15 to preventing any Barite sag in system is required.

As it is seen in geological forecast, soft &amp;amp; sticky marls referred as Gumbo, contained large amount of Smectite and/or Illite could be associated with problems such as bit balling, mud rings, plugged flow lines and hole washout&amp;amp; cause low process of drilling and unnecessary trips and some more difficulties to drill the section as fast as possible. With all those problems reduction of ROP was inevitable, blinding of shaker screens, excessive over pull on trips, washout and stuck pipes has been experienced as well. For problem Solve can add 3-5% KCl in system.

In case of necessary the inhibition of system can be increased by adding PHPA which adheres to the surface of the drilled cuttings, encapsulating them, and also coating the well bore reducing the hydration of clays in the formation.

Also while drilling this section encounter with Ca2+ based Gypsum is inventible. Gyp is calcium sulfate with water of crystallization (CaSO4.2H2O), Calcium sulfate contamination is similar to cement contamination because both liberate calcium ions, which in turn cause flocculation. Unlike cement, calcium sulfate does not cause a pH increase since it supplies a sulfate ion in lieu of an

hydroxyl ion. The sulfate ion contributes to flocculation of clay solids, although its effect is small compared to calcium ions. The severity of flocculation depends to a great degree on clay content. When CaSO4 causes the calcium concentration to increase and viscosity may fluctuate drastically. As calcium ion concentrations further increase, a base exchange occurs in which sodium montmorillonite becomes calcium montmorillonite. There are several methods for handling CaSO4 contamination. The drilling fluid can be maintained as a low-calcium fluid by chemically precipitating by adding soda ash.

4.4 12-1/4” Hole Section:

After cementing the 13 3/8” inch casing and confirmation of its proper cementing, The 12¼“ section will be drilled from casing shoe to an estimated section TD of 2400 m with Salt Saturated Polymer mud system necessitating a minimum requirement of 135 pcf to 140 pcf based on nearby well data.

The carried mud from previous section will be used for start of drilling this section after performing necessary treatments.

It is necessary to adjust mud weight and mud properties as hole condition dictate. Some tight hole, well flow and low ROP maybe experienced in this hole section. The drilling fluid engineer will advise the drilling supervisor of any extended circulation or sweep requirement. It uses clarified viscosifier to provide viscosity and carrying capacity and starch to reduce mud filtrate.

Interval Mud Discussion:

Salt and Salt Saturated Muds are used to prevent excessive hole enlargement while drilling massive salt beds. They can also be used to reduce dispersion and hydration of shales and clays. Solids content (percent by volume) should be maintained within a desired range by mechanical removal or dilution with saturated salt water to prevent unacceptable increases in gel strengths and viscosity.

The chloride content of saturated salt muds is 188,000 mg/l at saturation. As the temperature of the mud increases, more salt is able to go into solution. This means that a fluid which is saturated under surface conditions may not be saturated in down hole temperatures and can cause substantial washout in a salt zone due to increased salt solubility.

Control of the pH of saturated salt muds varies widely. Saturated salt muds require larger additions of caustic soda to maintain a pH in Salt saturate muds. Maintaining an±9.5 pH offers several advantages:

• Deflocculants are more effective

• Corrosion is reduced

• Lower concentrations of filtration control additives are required when Ca++ and Mg++ solubility is reduced

• Foaming tendency is lessened

• Mud is generally more stabl

Saturated salt muds will normally contain soluble calcium due to the formations penetrated and the type of makeup water used. Also, the sodium ions from the salt will undergo a base exchange and release calcium ions from the clay platelets, thereby contributing to the free calcium. Generally, the presence of calcium does not produce detrimental effects on the mud; except when the pH is increased beyond 12.0 and then the fluid loss will be difficult to control.

Foaming is generally restricted to surface foam and is not troublesome unless aggravated by mechanical agitation. The degree of foaming may sometimes be decreased by increasing the

alkalinity of the mud (Pm). A Defoaming agent may be necessary. Unless Mg++ sensitive additives are used, a Saturated Salt Mud is less prone to foam and air cut with a

9.5 - 10 pH. The temperature limitation of Saturated Salt Muds is around 250°F and is normally dictated by the filtration control additive used. Ca++ and Mg++ hardness do not adversely affect filtration control in Saturated Salt Muds when using starch; however.

Usually there are no problems associated with saturated salt mud conversions. Conversion can be accomplished in two circulations. The mixing hopper discharge should be located away from the main pump suctions to reduce foaming and air cutting. When a freshwater mud is to be converted to a saturated salt mud, it is desirable to use as much of the old mud as possible.

The amount of salt required to saturate the system should be calculated and then added through the hopper. A saturated salt mud will generally weight 75 pcf without weight material addition. Next, a fluid loss additive is added through the hopper while the mud is circulated. Starch is generally used for fluid loss control and as a supplementary viscosifier. Normally, 10 - 14 lb/bbl starch will be required to obtain a fluid loss of less than 4 cc/30 minutes. If a higher density is required, Barite which will beuse. When weighting up with Barite, a Lignosulphonate Deflocculant is recommended to avoid excessive viscosity and high gel strengths as contingency.

4.5 8 ½” Hole Section :

After cementing the 9 5/8” inch casing and confirmation of its proper cementing, The 8 1/2“ section will be drilled from casing shoe to an estimated section TD Salt/KCl/Polymer mud system necessitating a minimum requirement of 70 pcf to 76 pcf based on nearby well data.

In case of having problem with Marl and Shale layer addition of 5-7 wt. % of KCl , 2-5% Vol. of Glycol should be added to system to minimize associated problem.

It is necessary to adjust mud weight and mud properties as hole condition dictate. Some tight hole, well flow and low ROP maybe experienced in this hole section. The drilling fluid engineer will advise the drilling supervisor of any extended circulation or sweep requirement. It uses clarified viscosifier to provide viscosity and carrying capacity and starch to reduce mud filtrate.

* In the directional and horizontal section required amount of Lubricant such as Bit Lube , Water Base Lubricants and Glass beads will be added to active system to minimize torque and drag.

Interval Mud Discussion:

The water-based KCL Polymer system provides effective inhibition when drilling reactive shales through Below mechanism:

Potassium Chloride provides a source of Potassium ions, which are small enough to fit between the clay platelets without distorting the shale lattice. The Potassium ions are adsorbed on the exchangeable cation sites in the shale lattice and this holds the platelets together, which helps to minimize clay and shale hydration, swelling and dispersion. A low solids, non-dispersed Salt/KCl/CaCo₃ Polymer drilling fluid is selected for drilling this section. This system is used primarily to drill moderately reactive shales. It can be used effectively at temperatures up to 275˚ F – 300˚.

4.6 COMPLETION FLUID

The completion fluid for this section will be fresh water treated with a scavenger, inhibitor and biocide.

 Recovered permeability: ≥90%

 Corrosion rate: ＜0.076mm/a

 Diameter of solid particle: ≤2μm

Solids-Free Nacl Fluid Systems

This fluid is recommended to make from fresh water or is solutions made with water and the addition of one or more electrolytes. These fluids do not contain either suspended particles or viscosifiers, which mean neither filtration control nor viscosity control, are provided. Some NaCl is corrosive and when corrosion inhibitors are required, compatibility studies should be performed. Some brine is toxic and precautions should be taken to prevent contact with unprotected skin. Brine solutions can be prepared to give good inhibition of clays or shales in producing formations. In addition, common contaminants do not affect the brines.

Salt solutions were formerly considered too corrosive to be used as work-over or completion fluids or as acker fluids. The corrosion problem can be solved by adjusting the pH of the solution to above

10.5 - 11; however, pH measurements may be less important than measuring and controlling the palkalinity of the filtrate; this value should be kept above 1 cc. Lime be used for pH control.

Adjustment of pH, or alkalinity, does not necessarily ensure the solution to be corrosion resistant. It may be necessary to use a corrosion inhibitor to achieve lower corrosion rates. In some cases, an oxygen scavenger might be used in conjunction with a filming amine inhibitor.

Corrosion Control

Corrosion control in completion fluids is important to protect tubular goods and equipment. Corrosion can be limited by controlling the fluid pH at the neutral or alkaline level, and treating out dissolved oxygen. In severe environments such as high temperature or contamination with acid gases, the addition of filming amines can limit corrosion to acceptable levels.

The completion fluid for this section will be Local water treated with a scavenger, and inhibitor.

Pit management will be a key in the successful completion of this interval and sufficient time for planning and preparation should be allowed.

Page 74

All valves should be checked for leakage before hand and defects identified to be reported and rectified by drilling contractor.

The rig pumps are to displace all clean up pills as well as the NACL at 69 pcf. Prepare spacers and wash pills as per program in the tanks. Ensure that sufficient spacer is prepared to account for any dead tanks volume.

Prepare all inhibited NACL before starting the displacement process. After preparing the brine should be filtered through filtration unit and store in a clean pit before displacement.

Filtration Process:

Filtration provides clean fluids that will prevent damage to the formation, the reservoir and its permeability. It does this by removal of solids and particulates from the fluid that may otherwise block the open space within the rock formation containing the hydrocarbon fluid within the production zone.

Any solids and contaminates in the completion fluid will reduce its effectiveness. An efficiently filtered and completely solid free completion fluid will add value to both the productivity and the dependability of the well in the long term.

dual pod filtration cartridge unit is recommended for filtering brines and produced water in completion, stimulation, and workover operations. The pods are connected by a manifold, providing staged filtration capability. Staged filtration utilizes cartridge filters with different ratings to maximize filtration efficiency. Cartridge filtration is designed for use with fluids containing a low percent by volume of suspended solids. Cartridge filtration is not economic when fluids are contaminated with oil or other substances.

Displacement Process:

It is recommended to circulate and condition the mud prior to displacement and to spot the open hole section to conditioned mud or a solids-free fluid loss pill. Circulate and condition the mud as needed prior to pumping the clean out pills to optimum displacement properties).

Completion fluid

1. Fill up tank as require drill water

2. Added 2 lb/bbl Lime to adjust PH about 10-11

3. Added 71 lb/bbl NaCl to weight up at 69 pcf.

4. Corrosion inhibitor Packer fluid design at rate of 0.4 GPB.

5. Oxygen scavenger (to eliminate dissolved oxygen as source of corrosion) at rate of 0.2 GPB.

6. H2S Scavenger at rate of 0.2 GPB.

RIG CLEAN UP CHECK LIST

A. Areas to clean.

1. Surface pits.

2. Clean the suction, return, settling, and reserve pits.

3. Clean the sand traps.

4. Clean the ditches and troughs.

5. Clean the trip tank.

6. Clean the shaker area including all solids equipment and lines.

7. Clean the mixing hoppers.

8. Clean the cement unit.

9. Cycle all valves in mixing system.

B. Items to flush out.

1. All mud pumps and suction lines.

2. All centrifuges and lines.

3. Chemical and weighting mixing lines in contact with the completion fluid.

4. Lines from the pit room to the trip tank.=

5. Lines from the rig floor to the trip tank.

6. Choke, choke manifold and kill lines.

7. Standpipes.

8. Degassing and solids control equipment.

9. Lines to the cement unit and/or other pumping equipment.

10. Casings fill up line.

11.Lines to and from the filtration line.

12. Take on and return lines to and from the boat.

13. Any other lines that the completion fluid may contact.

Displacement Procedure

1. Run bit and dual or tandem scrapers.

2. Circulate and condition mud. Reduce funnel viscosity as much as possible while maintaining adequate rheological properties to clean hole and prevent settling of solids. Maintain critical annular velocity to assure that liner tops are thoroughly cleaned prior to displacement.

3. Rig up equipment for displacement of completion fluid. All tanks, circulating lines, and pumps to be used in the displacement should be cleared of residual mud.

4. Insure sufficient space is available to store displaced mud

مناقصه "طرح منصورآباد در قالب یک بسته یکپارچه از طرح عملیات محور

افزایش و نگهداشت تولید 27مخزن منتخب شرکت ملی مناطق نفتخیز جنوب"

شماره مناقصه: (م م/)97/0331

Page 83

6.1 18-5/8” Casing

6.1.1 String Design

 18-5/8” Casing Guide Shoe, 87.5 ppf, J-55, BTS

 One joint ( Approx. 11 m) 18-5/8” Casing, 87.5 ppf, J-55, BTS

 18-5/8” Stab-in Collar, 87.5 ppf, J-55, BTS

 ±139m (Approx.13 Jts) 18-5/8” Casing, 87.5 ppf, J-55, BTS (Est.

length for each joint of CSG=11m) to Surface.

 26” x 18-5/8” bow Centralizers on each 3 joints.

6.1.2 Preparation

 Visually and mechanically check the stab- in collar for proper

operation.

 Ensure all connections are thoroughly cleaned using steam or a grease

solvent.

 Ensure that all casing running equipment are available and in good

operation condition.

 Ensure the correct casing drifts are supplied to the rig.

 Ensure that all casing joints have been drifted.

 Company man to check stab in adaptor matches stab in shoe.

 Ensure spare seals for stab in adaptor are available.

 Ensure all cement bulk lines have been checked for blockage with bulk

tanks fluffed and pressurized to the required transfer pressure.

 Inspect and pressure test cement manifold.

مناقصه "طرح منصورآباد در قالب یک بسته یکپارچه از طرح عملیات محور

افزایش و نگهداشت تولید 27مخزن منتخب شرکت ملی مناطق نفتخیز جنوب"

شماره مناقصه: (م م/)97/0331

Page 84

6.1.3 Casing Specifications

Pipe OD (in) 18-5/8Weight (lb/ft) 87.5Pipe ID (in) 17.755Wall Thickness (in) 0.435Grade J-55Connection ButtressCollapse Resistance (psi) 630Pipe Body Yield (lbm) 1367000Pipe Body Internal Yield (psi) 2250Make Up Torque (ft-lb), optimum Based on Triangle

6.1.4 Sequence of Operations

 Conduct safety meeting with all crews involved.

 Rig up casing handling and running equipment.

 P/U 18-5/8”, 87.5 ppf, J-55, BTS, guide shoe, soft make

up on first joint, P/U and make up to the optimum torque. Do not

engage the tong close to bottom of shoe. Use thread lock compound

for shoe.

 P/U 18-5/8”, 87.5 ppf, J-55, BTS, stab-in collar and make up to the

optimum torque. Use thread lock compound for stab-in collar.

 Run 18-5/8” casing &amp;amp; centralizers according to tally.

 Run casing at speed calculated by WSS. A rate of 5

Joints/hr could be used as a guide.

 Work slightly through any tight spots if necessary. Circulate if deemed

necessary.

 Fill casing while running in each joint.

مناقصه "طرح منصورآباد در قالب یک بسته یکپارچه از طرح عملیات محور

افزایش و نگهداشت تولید 27مخزن منتخب شرکت ملی مناطق نفتخیز جنوب"

شماره مناقصه: (م م/)97/0331

Page 85

6.2 13-3/8” Casing

6.2.1 String Design

 13 3/8” Casing differential fill up Shoe, 72 ppf, N-80 , BTC.

 Two Joints (Approx. ±24m) of 13 3/8” Casing, 72 ppf, N-80 , BTC.

 13 3/8” Casing differential fill up Collar, 72 ppf, N-80 , BTC.

 Approx ±476m (±43 Jts) of 13 3/8” Casing, 72 ppf, N-80 , BTC.

(Est. length for each joint of CSG=11m)

 Approx ±700m (±63 Jts) of 13 3/8” Casing, 68 ppf, N-80 , BTC.

(Est. length for each joint of CSG=11m)

 Bow Centralizer on the first 5 joints.

 Bow Centralisers on each five for the rest joints.

 13 3/8” rigid centraliser on third and fourth joints from top.

6.2.2 Preparation

Visually and mechanically check the differential fill up shoe and collar for proper operation.

Ensure all connections are thoroughly cleaned using steam or a grease solvent.

Ensure that all casing running equipment are available and in good condition.

Ensure the correct casing drifts are supplied to the rig.

Check the plugs fins not to be squeezed or damaged.

Ensure that all casing joints have been drifted, including 13 3/8”swedge (If required to wash casing down).

Ensure all cement bulk lines have been checked for blockage with bulk tanks fluffed and pressurized to the required transfer pressure. Ensure that the air supply for cement is functioning properly.

Inspect and pressure test cement manifold.

مناقصه "طرح منصورآباد در قالب یک بسته یکپارچه از طرح عملیات محور

افزایش و نگهداشت تولید 27مخزن منتخب شرکت ملی مناطق نفتخیز جنوب"

شماره مناقصه: (م م/)97/0331

Page 86

6.2.3 Casing Specifications

Pipe OD (in) 13 3/8 13 3/8Weight (lb/ft) 72 68Pipe ID (in) 12.347 12.415Wall Thickness (in) 0.514 0.480Grade N-80 N-80Connection BTC BTCCollapse Resistance (psi) 2670 2260Pipe Body Yield (lpm) 1661000 1556000Pipe Body Internal Yield (psi) 5380 5020Make Up Torque (ft-lb), optimum Based on triangle Based on triangle

6.2.4 Sequence of Operations

 Rig up casing handling and running equipment.

 M/U 13 3/8”, 72 ppf, N-80 , BTC, differential fill up shoe. If it is

not already made up on joint, soft make up on first joint, P/U and make up to the optimum make up torque based on triangle using casing tong. Do not engage the ong close to bottom of shoe. Repeat the same for collar.

 Use thread locking compound for shoe track plus two joints on top of

differential fill up float collar. Take special care on thread locking these joints, since the consequence of improper locking would be disastrous.

 Run two joints of 13 3/8”, 72 ppf, N-80 , BTC casings.

 Make up 13 3/8”, 72 ppf, N-80 , BTC differential fill up collar.

 Run Approx. ±476m (±43 Jts) of 13 3/8”, 72 ppf, N-80 , BTC casing.

 Run Approx. ±700m (±63 Jts) of 13 3/8”, 68 ppf, N-80 , BTC casing.

Note: Circulate through casing after running of totally 5 jts for one Casing capacity.

Manage to have two meters of rat hole and 1.5 meters of casing stick up on rig floor.

 Pump one and half the casing volume @ 18-5/8” shoe and on TD.

 Run casing at controlled speed. For example, 10 Jts/hr could be used as a guide.

 Using stabbing board &amp;amp; single jt elevator to run casing would be time saving.

 Work slightly through any tight spots. Circulate if deemed necessary.

 Precautionary wash the last joint.

 When landed the casing, M/U cement head. Load the plugs accordingly.

6.3.1 String Design

 9 5/8” Casing differential fill up Shoe, 53.5 ppf, P-110, N.Vam.

 Two Joints (Approx.±24m) of 9 5/8” Casing, 53.5 ppf, P-110, N.Vam.

 9 5/8” Casing differential fill up Collar, 53.5 ppf, P-110, N.Vam.

 Approx. ±208m (±18 Joints) of 9 5/8” Casing, 53 ppf, P-110, N.Vam

(Est. length for each joint of CSG=12m).

 Approx. ±1264m (±105 Joints) of 9 5/8” Casing, 47 ppf, L-80, N.Vam

 Approx. ±36m (±3 Joints) of 9 5/8” Casing, 53.5 ppf, P-110, N.Vam

(Est. length for each joint of CSG=12m).

 Bow Centralizer on the first 5 joints.

 Bow Centralizer on each five for the rest joints.

 9 5/8” rigid centralizer on third and fourth joints from top.

6.3.2 Preparation

 Visually and mechanically check the shoe &amp;amp; collar for proper operation.

 Ensure all connections are thoroughly cleaned using steam or a grease

solvent.

 Ensure that all casing running equipment is available and in good

condition.

 Ensure the correct casing drifts are supplied to the rig.

 Check the plugs fins not to be squeezed or damaged.

 Ensure that all casing joints have been drifted, including 9 5/8”swedge (If

required to wash casing down)

 Ensure all cement bulk lines have been checked for blockage with bulk

tanks fluffed and pressurized to the required transfer pressure. Ensure that

the air supply system for cement is functioning properly.

 Inspect and pressure test cement manifold.

6.3.4 Sequence of Operations

 Rig up casing handling and running equipment.

 M/U 9 5/8”, 53.5ppf, P-110 , N.Vam, differential fill up shoe. M/U to

The optimum make up torque. Do not engage the tong close to bottom of shoe.

 Use thread locking compound for shoe track plus two joints on top of collar.

 Run two joints of 9 5/8”, 53.5ppf, P-110 , N.Vam casing.

 Make up 9 5/8”, 53.5ppf, P-110 , N.Vam differential fill up collar.

 Run Approx. ±208m (±18 Joints) of 9 5/8” Casing, 53.5ppf, P-110 , N.Vam.

 Run Approx. ±900m (±75Joints) of 9 5/8” Casing,53.5ppf,L-80, N.Vam.

 Run Approx. ±1264m (±105Joints) of 9 5/8” Casing,47ppf,L-80, N.Vam.

 Run Approx. ±36m (±3 Joints) of 9 5/8” Casing, 53.5ppf, P-110 , N.Vam.

Note: Circulate through casing after running of totally 5 jts for one Casing capacity.

Manage to have 0.5m of rat hole and 1.5 meters of casing stick up on rig floor.

 Pump a complete casing volume @ shoe and on section TD.

 Run casing at speed calculated by Company Man. 10 Jts/hr could be used as a guide.

 Work slightly through any tight spots if necessary. Circulate if deemed

necessary.

 Precautionary wash the last joint.

 When landed the casing, M/U cement head. Load the plugs accordingly.

Check the flag to operate properly.

6.4.2 Sequence of Operations

Notes:

 WSS is to supervise the loading of liner wiper plug in liner running tool, and

loading of drill pipe wiper dart in cementing head.

 The liner hanger engineer is to be on the rig floor at all times that the liner is

being run in open hole.

 Hold pre-job safety meeting. When running-in, apply thread lock to all

connections of the shoe track.

 Rig up liner running equipment. Run 7” liner string considering the

following arrangements:

 7”, 29 ppf, L-80, N.VAM, float shoe.

 Two joints (Approx. 24m) of 7”, 29 ppf, L-80, N.VAM.

افزایش و نگهداشت تولید 27مخزن منتخب شرکت ملی مناطق نفتخیز جنوب"

Page 90

 7”, 29 ppf, L-80, N.VAM, Latch down collar.

 Approx. ±294m (±27 Joints) 7”, 29 ppf, L-80, N.VAM.

(Est. length for each joint of liner=12m).

 Hydraulic set liner hanger + liner top packer (if available).

 Liner setting sleeve C/W liner setting tool connected

 5”, 19.5 lb/ft, drill pipe to surface

 Centralizers:

- 1 Bow centralizers for the first 5 joints.

- 1 Bow centralizer per 3 joint for the rest of the open hole.

- 1 Bow centralizer per 5 joint for the rest liner joints inside 9 5/8” casing

- Use rigid centralizer on the third and forth joint from the top.

Place each centralizer between stop collar and casing collar. Do not place

Centralizers over casing collars

1. After making up the shoe track, lower through rotary table and check that the

floats are holding. Fill up with mud and pick up to check float functionality.

Circulate for 10 min.

2. Run liner in at controlled speed to minimize pressure surges (approx. 12

joints/hr). Check returns constantly.

3. Fill up each liner joint whilst running in the hole. Fill up liner completely every

10 joints run.

4. When the required numbers of liner joints have been made up, make up the liner

hanger &amp;amp; liner top packer, running tool as per liner hanger engineer’s

instructions.

5. Use Liner setting tool retrievable pack off assembly for positive cement job.

6. Circulate 120% of the liner capacity. (Record Liner weight)

7. Run the liner with 5” drill pipe to the casing shoe. Circulate a minimum of one

string capacity before running into open hole, RIH in the open hole at 4-5

min/stand. Liner hanger engineer should be on rig floor while running liner into

open hole.(check the loss while RIH if need decrease the speed of the RIH).SLM

&amp;amp; drift the drill pipe while RIH the liner.

مناقصه "طرح منصورآباد در قالب یک بسته یکپارچه از طرح عملیات محور

افزایش و نگهداشت تولید 27مخزن منتخب شرکت ملی مناطق نفتخیز جنوب"

Page 91

8. Work through any tight spots with maximum 50 klbs slack off / over pull and

wash down if necessary. Establish full circulation slowly prior to washing down.

Immediately call the WSS and Tool pusher to the rig floor, if there is tight hole.

9. M/U combination plug dropping head to the last joint. Use pup joint, if

necessary. Check flag sub for proper functioning.

10. The hanger will be set 60m above the 9 5/8” casing shoe. Try to avoid setting

hanger on casing coupling. Set the Hanger as per hanger engineer procedures.

Ensure that the running tool is free of the liner (work string 0.5m up and down

– record loss of weight as the hanger sets) before starting to cement.

11. Circulate 120% of the string contents.

12. Cement 7" liner as per cementing program.

13. Displace the cement with the cementing pump to the liner wiper plug. Shear out

liner wiper plug (Record the volume pumped and shearing pressure). Displace

combined wiper plugs to latch down collar.

14. Bump the plug with 500 psi over final displacement pressure (or 1500 psi

bumping press.) (Record and report final displacement pressure prior to bump

the plug). If there is no bump, do not displace more than 50% of the shoe-track

volume. Displace with Cementing Pump and record cement losses.

15. Hold bumping pressure for 5 minutes. If the plugs bumped.

16. If plugs bumped, pressure up and test liner to 2000 psi for 15 minutes.

17. Bleed off pressure slowly and check for back-flow.

18. P/U setting tool for two meters and apply weight to set liner packer (If available).

Apply maximum 15,000 lbs to make sure that the packer is set. CBU clean hole.

Check the bottom’s up for cement return. In case of not available packer, check

for U tube f/ DP &amp;amp; check how many meter of cement is on top of liner.

19. N/D cementing head. POOH to surface.

20. Clean well to liner lap @ 1800m with 8 ½” bit#RR

21. P/U 3-1/2 drill pipe and 4-3/4" drill collar, with 6-1/8" bit, Clean and drill out

cement (if any) to top of LDC.

22. Circulate and POOH to 2700m, pressure test liner lap to 2000 psi for 30 min.

23. Dry test liner lap if liner top packer didn’t use.

- Drift Drill pipe while run the liner with suitable Drift.

- If liner top packer didn’t used after finishing the cement displacing, pull the drill

lay down setting tools.

- Perform injectivity test into 7” liner lap if necessary and inject cement around

7 Cement Program

7.1 18-5/8” Cement Program

Important: The following program is a sample; therefore it should be tested using the field drilling water, cement sample and additives.

For cementing operation, note the followings:

By Stinger:

 M/U Cement Stinger C/W spring bow 20” x 5” centralizer and RIH to 10m above the

shoe using the C-plate.

 Circulate 60 bbls of mud and wash down to flush the top of the stab in shoe from any

debris.

 Flush and fill surface lines with water and pressure test to 3,000psi for 5 minutes prior

to start of the cement job.

 Stab in to the shoe. Set down string weight

 Circulate mud clean casing annulus. Observe DP’s annulus for any leakage.

 Pump spacer, Mix and pump cement as per program.

 All samples of mix water and slurry should be stored until the success of the

cement job has been verified, then they may be discarded.

 Displace cement with mud. Displace for 15 bbls (1.78 bbls Short).

 Stop pumping, sting out, flush pipe, check for float, POOH. L/D stinger, wait on

cement to get hard.

and mark all joints to be left out. Check cement. Mix a pilot sample. Hold liner

running / configuration meeting with liner engineer.

Drilling Fluid Program

1. Objectives

 This program has been designed by Pars Drilling Fluids Co. (PDF) for the

provision of drilling fluids engineering and operational services to drill

Asmari Oil Producer Well in Mansour Abad Oil Field, operated by PEDC.

 This program is based on the provided information by PEDC Drilling

Department for the normal operation.

 In case of having contingency or emergency situations variation from the

program is required based on the hole conditions and dictation to obtain

optimum drilling fluid parameters until returning to the normal

condition.

 This program has been design based on 50% / 50% Dewatered and Drill

Water. In case of using 100% Dewatered chemicals, deviation from the

program should be considered and will be justified to be economical.

Drilling Fluid Program

2. Engineering Guidelines

Mud Weight Maintain mud density at recommended weight with dilution and efficient use of the solid control equipment. Increases in mud weight to be achieved by the addition of salts for all intervals, BARA-WATE (barite) (and HEMA-WATE in case of more weight requirement) for the first intervals and CARBO-WATE F (Calcium Carbonate) should be used for the last two intervals to avoid formation damage, unless an emergency situation arises.

Plastic Viscosity Plastic Viscosity should be maintained as low as possible by minimizing drill solids and maximizing use of solids control equipment, and maintaining dilution rate.

Yield Point The Yield Point should be maintained in the programmed ranges once the mud has sheared through the bit. The hole should be monitored for signs of poor hole cleaning, quantity and quality of the cuttings on the shaker, especially after trips. Additions of BIO-XCD (Xanthan Gum) and/or PAC UHV should be used to maintain or increase rheology.

Gels / 6 RPM Gels can be increased if necessary by additions of BIO-XCD (Xanthan Gum).

Filtration The API/HPHT filtrate should be maintained in the programmed ranges by using PAC LV-TG and AMYLOSE LV.

pH pH should be maintained between 9.5 and 10.5 with CAUSTIC SODA and LIME, depending on hole section.

Calcium Maintained, preferably at less than 400mg/l by addition of SODA ASH in all sections.

KCl If cuttings quality and/or hole conditions indicate, the concentration of KCl R-UPG will be increased.

Chlorides The chloride content will be kept in the programmed range.

M.B.T. To be maintained well below 35 Kg/m3 (10 lb/bbl) (equivalent Bentonite) by maintaining a satisfactory dilution rate and an accurate usage of the solids control equipment. It is very important to determine MBT of fresh mud and monitor MBT increasing during drilling.

Centrifuges The centrifuges should be run judicially to control mud weight and buildup of low gravity solids.

Shakers shaker screen’s inventory should be reported at the end of each week. Using proper screen size to drill each section is a crucial point. If use

3.1.2. Interval Key Issues (Potential Risks and Mitigations)

 Loss Zone: There is a possibility of complete loss in this interval with No Return mud,

so LCM pill should be prepared before drilling of this section as contingency.

 Hole Cleaning: Hole cleaning problems could be avoided by proper use of viscosifiers,

e.g. BENTO-GEL API.

3.1.3. Engineering Outline &amp;amp; System Maintenance

 The Plastic Viscosity value should be minimized by optimum usage of the solids control

equipment and by dilution with pre-mix, where applicable, to generate new volume and / or

reduce mud rheology.

 Yield point should be kept high (the program range) to reduce the annular flow rates

required and gel value are required to reach to maximum hole cleaning.

 It is essential to remove drilled solids rather than dilute with water to acceptable levels.

Therefore every effort must be made to maximize the efficiency of the solids control

equipment. Where possible all centrifuges should be used to process the active mud and

Desilter discharge.

3.2. 17 1/2″ Hole Size

Hole Size(in)Casing Size(in)Casing Setting DepthMD (m)GeologicalFormationLithology Drilling Fluids Design17 ½ ” 13 3/8 ” 1200Aghajari, Mishan, GachsaranMarl, Sand-Shale CLAY-BOND FLUID SYSTEM

3.2.1. Drilling Operation Overview

To solve problems associated with this interval and increase the ROP, CLAY-BOND FLUID SYSTEM has been designed to drill the formation and inhibit clay and marl problems in this section.

CLAY-BOND L has also been successfully used to drill clay interbeds in both saline and non-saline systems. It is very important to determine MBT of mud during drilling and keep it in the program range. Controlling of MW could be done by running SCE and dressing the shakers with finest mesh screens, start with 65 pcf MW and increase using salts till 75 pcf (This can be achieved by adding saturated salt water to system) and BARA-WATE API for &amp;gt;75 pcf.

Note: Due to the importance of drilling this section, before each connection and continuing drilling wash and ream should be done completely.

3.2.3. Drilling Fluid Formulation

After cementing 20" casing, it is required to prepare the new mud system “CLAY-BOND FLUID SYSTEM " for 17 1/2" Hole section and displace the hole before drilling the new section.

Mix every batch based on the following formulation:

 Mixing should be done with waste water, inform company man if waste water condition

is not good.

 If ROP is low, Pump Salt Water. In addition, pump 50 bbl Salt Water (69-70 pcf) every

stand by company man order (Optional).

 To clean the hole, pump 50 bbl Hi-Vis Pill as Required or every stand by using BIO-XCD

/PAC UHV (Hi-Vis Pill viscosity should be 65 sec/qt.)

** For every 3 stands add 2 Sack of Torque-Free GB M600 and 2 sacks of Torque-Free GB M100 from the suction tank

Note: To adjust pH in this interval (Gachsaran formation) use LIME instead of CAUSTIC SODA.

3.2.4. Drilling Fluids Formulation based on Maximum MW

3.2.5. Interval Key Issues (Potential Risks and Mitigations)

 Loss Zone: There is a possibility of complete loss in this interval with No Return mud, so

LCM pill should be prepared before drilling this section as contingency.

 Bit Balling: Due to the clay and marl characteristic of the formation, bit balling is one of

the main problems. It is required to use KCL R-UPG and CLAY-BOND L according to the

above mentioned to provide cutting encapsulation during drilling.

 Clay &amp;amp; Marl Inhibition: Tight hole might be experienced in this interval due to existence

of clay &amp;amp; marl in the formation. Good inhibition will be helpful to provide stable hole

condition.

 Salt Water Flow: There is a possibility of salt water flow. Therefore close monitoring is

required to maintain Ca++ and pH level.

Drilling Fluid Program

3.2.6. Engineering Outline &amp;amp; System Maintenance

 Mud weight is in the range of 65 and 101 pcf unless hole dictates, salts and BARA-WATE

API will be used to rise the mud weight. Controlling of MW could be done by running SCE

and dressing the shakers with finest mesh screens (150/ 200 mesh size) if possible.

 Dump and dilution is one of the best ways to keep the MW on the guideline especially

with clean mud systems. Running all solids equipment and dump and dilution would be

the best way to control the MW.

 Rheological properties of the mud should be monitored to ensure maximum hole

cleaning.

 Contamination with cement will increase the rheological properties of the mud

especially the yield point. Therefore, prior to cement, YP should be reduced to the

minimum level if practical.

3.3. 12 ¼″ Hole Size

Hole Size(in)Casing Size(in)Casing Setting DepthMD (m)GeologicalFormationLithology Drilling Fluids Design12 ¼ “ 9 5/8 ” 2420 Gachsaran FormationAnhydrite and clay stone, Marl, Limestone, with high pressure salt aquifer.HEAVY-DRILL FLUID SYSTEM

3.3.1. Drilling Fluids Formulation

To drill this section a HEAVY-DRILL FLUID SYSTEM with 105-125 pcf would be used. Salt would be used saturation level (1.2 SG) to prohibit the thin inter bedded layers of Salt in member 7 &amp;amp; 2 from being washed and also will act as a strong shale inhibitor in the system and maintain MW as per pore pressure curve dictates in the drilling program using BARA-WATE I and HEMA WATE I.

AMYLOSE LV, a modified starch would be used as a filtration control agent in this section. The main concern in this section is the effect of the formation water on the mud properties. If any problem rises during the drilling, AMYLOSE LV should be replaced with the PAC ULV at the concentration between 0.5-1.5 lb/bbl.

Note 1: Due to undesirable hole condition while tripping and casing running, performing wash and ream on each drilled stand is the best way to have good hole condition.

Note 3: Check Hardness, Fluid loss, MBT and other properties every 3 hours and be sure all of them are in range based on plan.

3.3.2. Interval Key Issues

 Salt Water Flow: Gachsaran formation has the potential of salt water flow. The hardness

of this water is between 35000-53000 mg/l, so any increase in the hardness of mud

would be an indication of possible salt water flow. Therefore, during drilling this section,

hardness of the system must be checked and monitored three times per day for any

increase in Ca++ ions.

 Losses: In the upper part of Gachsaran a weak zone has been experienced. Layers

interbedded in the salts in Gachsaran Members 2 &amp;amp; 3 can have normal pressure, and

therefore a reduced fracture gradient compared to the salt layers. Heavy losses might be

experienced in Gachsaran. Losses have also been seen in the first shale layer of Cap Rock,

its second layer from the top, so it is very important not to drill deeper than

approximately one meter into this Member.

 Stuck Pipe: Tight hole / stuck pipe in the 12 1/4" hole section is typically isolated to the

Shales/Clay stones and salt beds. The stuck in Shales and clay stones as far as the MW is

adjusted correctly and FL is tight and the salinity is saturation is not a matter of concern.

Drilling Fluid Program

3.3.3. Engineering Outline &amp;amp; System Maintenance

Mud Weight

In the initial mixing, salt would be the first weighting agent to Saturation level, then BARA WATE I and HEMA WATE I will be used as per above instruction to reach to 105-125 pcf as hole conditions dictate. Controlling the mud weight meanwhile drilling would be done by running all SCE and dump and dilution. Pore pressure is expected to be marginally above the normal pressure in the Jurassic / Upper Triassic.

Mud weight selection is critical in this interval. In some offset wells, excessive losses may occur in the Gachsaran member 3 when the mud weight is higher than the optimum. On the other hand, in some offset wells, water flow could be encountered when the mud weight is allowed to fall down below optimum MW.

It is important to drill this section with the mud weight being kept as per the guide line, also by running all solids control equipment and dressing the shakers with finest mesh screens; it is possible to minimize the ECD and the potential for induced losses.

PH

The viscosity of a clay suspension is lowest in the pH range of 7 to 9.5 so in this section, pH should be kept at the range of 9-9.5.

Shale Inhibition

Salt would be used for shale inhibition to combat the Gachsaran Marl/Shale’s. However, the very tight FL would be the other shale inhibition property of the system. Controlling the salinity saturation is vital to drill into Gachsaran formation against troublesome Shales/Marls.

Rheological Properties

 PV is always to be kept as low as possible by reducing the drilled solids concentrations of

mud using the proper installation of the solids control equipment so that the hydraulics is

optimized. High gel values are required to support the high quantity of weighting agents

while tripping, making connections and during survey times. PV should be kept in the

range mentioned in the drilling fluid program.

 A thin salt bed in Gachsaran member 2 is a red flag for Geologist that means reaching to

cap rock is imminent, salinity below the saturation will cause the salt samples to be

dissolved in the system resulting in no salt sample over the shakers.

3.4.1.2. Interval Key Issues

 Swab possibility

Special care must be taken when the BHA is inside the previous casing. In contrary to popular belief, pressure does travel easily in drilling fluids, so tripping speed must be controlled to avoid swabbing.

 Stuck Pipe

The combination of different size of CARBO-WATE incorporated into the mud will form a thin and slick filter cake in borehole and prevent the risk of stuck pipe.

 Drilling Issues

When drilling through reservoir, swabbing of hydrocarbons can be experienced. Influx due to overpressure vs. influx due to swabbing must be differentiated.

 Losses

It is recommended to drill with as low as possible mud weight through the reservoir to prevent any losses.

 H2S &amp;amp; CO2 Gases

There is possibility for existence of H2S and CO2 Gases in the reservoir zone (Asmari), it is recommended to keep the pH around 9.5 to 10 and also using H2S SCAV P to prevent mud properties from being changed.

Drilling Fluid Program

4. Completion Fluids Design and Program

4.1. Clean up and Completion Program

This program describes the procedure to clean up and displace the cased hole from water based mud brine as safely and effectively as possible prior to running the completion equipment.

Clean working practices and good housekeeping as always are important.

All rig pits, ditches, and lines (including gun lines) should be cleaned using solvents and detergents. If it is practical, lines should be opened to check for any mud solids that might have settled in them.

All the pits, sand traps, and under the shale shakers should be cleaned out and washed down using high pressure cleaning equipment. In the pit room, all gratings should be cleaned, all the lights and beams should be washed down.

All cleaning should be done well in advance wherever possible. To clean pits and lines, 15 m3 of water containing 1 to 2 drums of CLEAN SURF should be mixed up and circulated through all lines, gun lines, mixing lines etc. This can also be used to clean the tank system initially.

 Pump should be worked at the maximum safe rate.

 The below check list should be filled by the supervisor in the site.

Equipment CompleteBrine Storage TanksTransfer LinesPill and Slug PitsReserve/Mix PitRig PumpsTrip TankPump Charge LinesCement Unit LinesChoke Unit LinesKill Lines

 It should be noted that all dump valves should seal with grease to ensure they are in good order.

 All ditch gates should be sealed with silicon on each side of the gate. This will need to be

replaced if the gate is opened.

 Under no circumstances should barite, bentonite or polymers be used to seal anything.

 All pump packing should be examined before starting the cleaning.

Drilling Fluid Program

4.2. Completion Fluids Design and Formulation

The completion fluid for this section will be fresh water treated with a scavenger, inhibitor and biocide.

Solids-Free Nacl Fluid Systems

This fluid is recommended to make from fresh water or is solutions made with water and the addition of one or more electrolytes. These fluids do not contain either suspended particles or viscosifiers, which mean neither filtration control nor viscosity control, are provided.

Corrosion Control:

Some NaCl is corrosive and when corrosion inhibitors are required, compatibility studies should be performed. The corrosion problem can be solved by adjusting the pH of the solution to above 10.5 - 11; however, pH measurements may be less important than measuring and controlling the. It may be necessary to use a corrosion inhibitor to achieve lower corrosion rates. In some cases, an oxygen scavenger might be used in conjunction with a filming amine inhibitor.

Filtration Process:

Filtration provides clean fluids that will prevent damage to the formation, the reservoir and its permeability. It does this by removal of solids and particulates from the fluid that may otherwise block the open space within the rock formation containing the hydrocarbon fluid within the production zone.

Any solids and contaminates in the completion fluid will reduce its effectiveness. An efficiently filtered and completely solid free completion fluid will add value to both the productivity and the dependability of the well in the long term.

Dual pod filtration cartridge unit is recommended for filtering brines (5 microns and 25 microns filter cartdriges) and produced water in completion, stimulation, and workover operations. The pods are connected by a manifold, providing staged filtration capability. Staged filtration utilizes cartridge filters with different ratings to maximize filtration efficiency. Cartridge filtration is designed for use with fluids containing a low percent by volume of suspended solids. Cartridge filtration is not economic when fluids are contaminated with oil or other substances.

Displacement Process:

It is recommended to circulate and condition the mud prior to displacement and to spot the open hole section to conditioned mud or a solids-free fluid loss pill. Circulate and condition the mud as needed prior to pumping the clean out pills to optimum displacement properties).

Completion fluid

1. Fill up tank as require drill water

2. Added 2 lb/bbl Lime to adjust PH about 10-11

3. Added 71 lb/bbl NaCl to weight up at 69 pcf.

4. Corrosion inhibitor Packer fluid design at rate of 0.4 GPB.

5. Oxygen scavenger (to eliminate dissolved oxygen as source of corrosion) at

rate of 0.2 GPB.

6. H2S Scavenger at rate of 0.2 GPB.

4.3. RIG CLEAN UP CHECK LIST

A. Areas to clean.

1. Surface pits.

2. Clean the suction, return, settling, and reserve pits.

3. Clean the sand traps.

4. Clean the ditches and troughs.

5. Clean the trip tank.

6. Clean the shaker area including all solids equipment and lines.

7. Clean the mixing hoppers.

8. Clean the cement unit.

9. Cycle all valves in mixing system.

B. Items to flush out.

1. All mud pumps and suction lines.

2. All centrifuges and lines.

3. Chemical and weighting mixing lines in contact with the completion fluid.

4. Lines from the pit room to the trip tank.

5. Lines from the rig floor to the trip tank.

6. Choke, choke manifold and kill lines.

7. Standpipes.

13. Any other lines that the completion fluid may contact.

4.4. Displacement Procedure

To ensure effective mud displacement and water wetting of the casing, the displacement pill needs to be designed carefully. The use of a weighted push pills with a viscosity greater than that of the mud, will minimize channeling and ensure good cleaning of the low side of the well bore.

The best fluid for thinning the mud is the continuous phase of the mud. In addition, SPERSEEN CFL could be used to reduce the yield point and gel strengths. The yield point should be between 8 to10 Pa and the 10 minute gel to &amp;lt;10 Pa. The actual quantity of material required to do this must be determined by the pilot testing performed by the mud engineer to determine the most cost-effective treatment.

Throughout the drilling fluid conditioning process, the flow rate used should be the maximum practical rate.

 The drill string should be reciprocated and rotated during the operation. The combined effect of

scrapers being run in the hole, the high flow rate and the reciprocation/rotation will help to

remove/disperse large quantities of mud solids and general debris. The reciprocation stroke

should be +/- 10 m. and the rotation speed should be +/- 60 RPM

 During this operation, as much of the surface volume of mud as possible should be removed

from the pits to accommodate the inhibited water and the well clean up pills. Once the mud has

been back-loaded, surface preparation can be done.

1. General Information

1.1 Field Introduction

Azadegan South Oil Field is situated in West Karoun province on a large long-axis anticline with N-S trending with approximate dimensions about 20 km width and 60 km length near to Iran-Iraq border, to the east of Yaran Oil Field.

The trap area of the south Azadegan is limited to 43.2x17.2 km. The Azadegan Oil field was discovered in 1999, when Well AZN-1 was drilled vertically down to the Cretaceous Fahliyan Formation with total depth of 4,643m. The results of this well, revealed the reservoir characteristics of the field. Following to the result of the well no. AZN-1, another 5 exploration wells was drilled in different parts of this huge field down to Fahliyan Formation. In the later stage the well No.10 assumed as exploration well for evaluation of deeper formations. This well was drilled in 2008, down to the depth of 5340m (Neyriz Fm.), mainly to evaluate the Jurassic formations.

Based on the exploration wells results, carbonate reservoir of Sarvak Formation is broadly developed in Azadegan Field. This formation was penetrated in all of seven exploration wells (AZN-1, AZN-2, AZN- 3, AZN-4, AZN-5, AZN-6 and AZN-10). Clastic oil-bearing zones of Kazhdumi Formation developed in main anticline of Azadegan Field, extending from north to center of South Azadegan. The Clastic oilbearing zones of Gadvan Formation developed only in crest area and south parts of South Azadegan Filed, which was discovered by AZN-1 in crest and AZN-4 in south parts. The carbonates of Fahliyan Formation also developed in Azadegan field, but the oil reservoir of this formation developed in South part of South Azadegan.

The Azadegan Field is an elongated anticline, trending in N-S direction, belonging to "Arabian Trend".

The stratigraphy sequence of the field includes AghaJari, Gachsaran, Fahliyan, Pabdeh, Gurpi, Ilam, Laffan, Sarvak, Kazhdumi, Dariyan, Gadvan and Fahliyan Formations, from top to bottom. This sequence in well no AZN-10, the deepest up to now drilled well of the field, continues with Garau, Gotnia, Najmah, Sargalu, Alan, Mus and Neyriz formations.

The Dominant lithofacies of Sarvak Formation are Rudist-bearing packstone and partially grainstone, which contains abundant bioclasts. Some other facies like matrix-dominated wackestone and mudstone are also found.

The AZADEGAN Oilfield is Located in Khuzestan Province and is Approximately Located 80 Kilometers West of Ahwaz City, near to Iran-Iraq Border. It is in The Northwest of The YADAVARAN Field and in The West of JUFEYR Field. The Average Monthly Temperature is 45ºc in summer, and Highest Temperature is 52ºc. The Lowest Temperature is -4.4ºc in winter. Maximum Rainfall is 78 mm in February, Winter Season.

Block I is located on the north part of the CONTRACT AREA in north of well AZN-010. Gachsaran formation is characterized by abnormal high pressure in this block.

Block II is located between well AZN-010 and AZN-011. In this block, Gachsaran formation is characterized by pressure tending to normal

Block III is located on the south of line well AZN-011. In this block, Gachsaran formation is characterized by normal pressure and all drilled wells in this block suffered from complete loss at Pabdeh formation.

1.7 Drilling History

26" Hole Section

Spud the rig FATH 64 on 1387.04.15 at 12:00 o’clock.

Commenced drilling 26” hole section from 14m to 155.5m. Run 20” casing (J-55m 133#, BTC) to 154m, perform cemented 20” casing (S.W:115 pcf), got CMT in return. Install 20” 3K C.H.H (type ABB).

17 1/2" Hole section

Drilling of 17-1/2” hole section started on 1387/05/20 from 154m to 1259m with No Loss- No Gain. Perform condition trip. Run CDR/GR log.

R/U 13-3/8" casing running equipment, held PJSM and run 13-3/8" casing with 13-3/8" float shoe (Nasr Mobtakeran) + 2 Jt 13 3/8” CSG + 13-3/8” float Collar (Nasr Mobtakeran) + 106 Jts 13 3/8” CSG (C-95, 72#, BTC to 1259 m. perform Cement 13-3/8” casing (883 bbl head CMT, S.W: 90 pcf, 135 bbl tail CMT S.W:115 pcf). Install DSA 20” 3 K X 16 ¾” 5k &amp;amp; 16 ¾” 5K (MCEVOY) X 13 5/8” 5K (ABB).

12 1/4" Hole section

Drilling of 12-1/4” hole section started on 1387/06/10 from 1259 m to 1585 m, Obs. complete loss, cure the loss by pumping LCM, Cont. Drlg to 1600 m. Obs. No return. POOH to surface, RIH with C.Cut bit, spot 120 bbl 94 pcf CMT, POOH to surface, RIH with bit, Cont. Drlg formation to 1860 m with heavy loss (cure the loss using LCM pill), @ 1860 m, Obs. 500 psi pressure drop, POOH to surface, Obs. 12 ¼” bit + bit sub + 2 Jts 8 ½” D. Collar left in hole. Retrieve the fish, RIH with open end drill pipes, pump 150 bbl CMT 94 pcf in 2 stage, D/O CMT, Cont. Drlg to 2130 m, 50-80 BPHL. stuck string, work on stuck, free the pipe, POOH to surface, obs. String twist off from Jar mandrel. Retrieve the fish. riH W/ BIT &amp;amp; Cont. Drlg formation to 2245 m, Obs. Pressure drop, Obs. 92.26 m fish left in hole. Retrieve the fish. RIH with bit &amp;amp; Cont. Drlg formation to 3792 m (section TD). Perform condition Trip, run BHC/HRLA/TLD/HGNS/GPIT/HNGS log, POOH to surface, run MDT log. Perform 230 bbl balance CMT plug in 2 stage. RIH with D/O BHA, D/O CMT &amp;amp; to 3450 m (9 5/8” CSG point), POOH to surface.

5. Sequence of Operation

5.1 Main Objective

Decision has been made to de-complete he well &amp;amp; re-complete with new completion equipment. Check and smooth collapse interval from 3889-3911m.

5.2 Main plan

1. Held PJSM. Spud the Rig.

2. Check the wellhead for any damage or leakage. Record well head pressures; check all

annulus pressure.

3. Apply pressure in control line &amp;amp; check same for any leakage, try to open 3SV (check

indication of opening 3SV flapper) &amp;amp; monitor well pressure again.

4. Secure the well by closing all XMT valves except BTM master valve.

5. L/U pump truck to 7 1/16” 5K sweep bend &amp;amp; L/U F/ 7” to 9 5/8” completion annulus

to rig choke manifold, release annulus pressure through burning pit &amp;amp; monitor

pressure.

6. Remove 7 1/16” XMT cap, R/U 7 1/16” 5K lubricator &amp;amp; pressure test same against

Deeping valve, R/U slick line meanwhile monitor completion annulus pressure.

7. RIH with gauge cutter to top of 3SV, POOH to surface. RIH with pulling tools of

WLR 3SV (3SV Spec: Baker, Landing Nipple: 5.950”, AF), Retrieve 3SV, POOH to

surface, RIH with dummy valve, set dummy in 3SV profile, POOH to surface.

Note: If unable to RIH gauge cutter with slick line or unable to retrieve 3SV with slick line, follow contingency plan #1.

8. RIH with gauge ring to TOF (2800 m) , POOH to surface &amp;amp; L/D same. R/U CT &amp;amp;

RIH with CT to TOF while pumping chemical wash, Displace inside completion

string with proper mud weight (85 pcf)) POOH CT to surface &amp;amp; R/D same.

Note: if wellhead pressure is no zero, follow contingency Plan#2.

9. Install TWCV in TBG HGR, perform pressure test same, open tie down screw &amp;amp;

pressure test same. (TWCV should be provided by client.)

Note: If unable to set TWCV in TBG HGR due to damaged TBG HGR profile, follow contingency Plan#3.

South Azadegan Oilfield Project

AZNS12 ST-1 Workover Program Page 29 of 64

10. N/D X.M.T

11. N/U 13 5/8” 10 K BOP stack &amp;amp; pressure test same as per NIOC Policy.

12. Retrieve TWCV.

13. P/U &amp;amp; M/U L.J &amp;amp; TBG HGR running tools, screw on TBG HGR. ( 6 ½” fishing Jar

should be ready in location by OEOC)

Note: In case of unable to screw L.J on TBG HGR follow contingency Plan#4.

14. Unlatch completion string from Anchor Seal (Baker, KC-22) (Approximately 291 Jts

7” TBG (L-80, 29#, VAM) between 3SV &amp;amp; X.O.S and 5 Jts above 3SV and 9 Jts 4

½” TBG 13.5#, L-80, VAM between XOS &amp;amp; expansion Jt. (Approximate length of 7”

TBG: 3250 m, Yield Strength of 7” TBG 29#, L-80 is 676 Klb, maximum make up

TRQ of 7” TBG 29pp, L-80, VAM is 15250 [[ft.lb](http://ft.lb)]([http://ft.lb](http://ft.lb)). Yield strength of 4 ½” TBG 13.5#,

L-80, is 307 Klb. maximum make up TRQ of 4 1/2” TBG 13.5pp, L-80, VAM, is

6000 [[ft.lb](http://ft.lb)]([http://ft.lb](http://ft.lb)))

Note: In case of unable to unlatch completion string from Anchor Seal, due to string pack off with huge amount of debris follow contingency Plan#5.

Note: In case of while trying to unlatch completion string, the string was parted from weak point due to string wash out, follow contingency Plan#6.

15. POOH completion string to surface precautionary due to probable trapped pressure

below fish. While POOH monitor the wells and annulus to make sure the well is safe

and over balance.

16. P/U &amp;amp; M/U &amp;amp; RIH with proper fishing tools to TOF, try to catch &amp;amp; retrieve fish in

several attempts the POOH to surface.

17. P/U &amp;amp; M/U 8 3/8” M.M.J Mill &amp;amp; 5” DP as Jt by Jt &amp;amp; RIH with clean out BHA to 7”

L. Lap (3285 m). confirm 7” L. Lap, Pump Hi-Vis pill to sweep the well, POOH to

surface.

18. P/U &amp;amp; M/U 6” or 5 7/8” M.M Junk Mill &amp;amp; 63 Jt 3 ½” DP as Jt by Jt &amp;amp; RIH, mill

completion PKR &amp;amp; chase same to 5” L.Lap (3779 m) while pump Hi-Vis periodically,

CBU, POOH to surface.

19. RIH with 2”*4” Taper tap &amp;amp; catch tail of completion string, recover the PKR, POOH

to surface.

Note: if string stuck while recovering completion PKR follow contingency plan#7

South Azadegan Oilfield Project

AZNS12 ST-1 Workover Program Page 30 of 64

20. RIH with 6” or 6 1/8” Mill and clean out BHA to 5" Liner lap (3779m), pump Hi-Vis

pill &amp;amp; CBU till shakers clean, POOH to surface.

21. RIH with 4 1/8” Mill 15 Jt 3 1/8” DC &amp;amp; 15 Jts 2 7/8” DP as Jt by Jt and clean out

BHA to BTM (TD: 3945m), take care inside pre-perforation interval (3867m –

3908m), CBU till hole clean, POOH to surface.

22. M/U Tandem scraper BHA, RIH with tandem scrapers including 9-5/8" casing

scraper &amp;amp; 7" liner scraper to top of 5" liner (3779m). Scrap inside 9-5/8” casing and

7” liner to 5” L.Lap, Pump Hi-Vis pill &amp;amp; CBU to sweep the well, POOH to surface

and L/D same.

23. P/U &amp;amp; M/U logging equipment &amp;amp; Perform (SBT/CBL/VDL) log from Inside 7" Liner,

as TLC method, POOH to Surface.

24. Perform Corrosion log from inside 7” LNR as TLC method. POOH to surface &amp;amp; R/D

same.

25. R/U shooting nipple, M/U wireline equipment, take corrosion log from 9 5/8” CSG to

surface. R/D wireline equipment.

Note: for change THS Follow Contingency plan #08:

Note: Based on corrosion log, tie back operation will be needed, contractor will perform tie-back operation as extra work if needed.

26. P/U &amp;amp; M/U 6” or 6 1/8” Tri Cone bit &amp;amp; 7” scraper &amp;amp; RIH with scraper BHA &amp;amp; scrap

7” completion PKR setting depth, pump Hi-Vis pill &amp;amp; sweep the well, displace the

well with CaCl2 as completion fluid, POOH to surface &amp;amp; L/D all tubulars.

27. Run 7.5 K completion string as per program.

28. Set BPV inside TBH, N/D BOP's &amp;amp; install new 10K XMT.

29. Retrieve BPV, install TWCV and Pressure test the XMT.

30. Secure the well by set BPV in TBG Hanger, close all X-mas Tree valves except

BMV, and Release the Rig.

31. Retrieve TWCV, R/U Slick Line, Set protection sleeve, retrieve plug &amp;amp; prong from

NO GO landing nipple, POOH.

32. RIH with CT to bottom, displace the well with diesel or nitrogen &amp;amp; observe well,

POOH.

33. R/U SL, RIH &amp;amp; retrieve protection sleeve, POOH, R/D SL.

South Azadegan Oilfield Project

AZNS12 ST-1 Workover Program Page 31 of 64

34. Flow the well as pre-acid clean up till acceptable BSW &amp;amp; reading stable flow rate on

2 different choke size for 72 hrs.

35. R/U &amp;amp; RIH S.L, Set protection sleeve, POOH &amp;amp; R/D S.L

36. RIH with C/T &amp;amp; perform acid wash as per program, POOH to surface. RIH w/SL and

retrieve protection sleeve"

37. Flow the well as post-acid clean-up till acceptable BSW &amp;amp; reading stable flow rate on

2 different choke size for min 96 hrs.

Note: The time is only for flowing duration (R/U, R/D &amp;amp; preparation time is excluded).

Note: Acidizing &amp;amp; post-acid clean-up maybe perform as rig less job upon contractor request &amp;amp; client approval but in case of any failure in well integrity the contractor should provide drilling rig &amp;amp; required services in own responsibility &amp;amp; fix the problem.

38. RIH with S/L, set protection Sleeve, POOH &amp;amp; R/D SL.

39. RIH with C/T to bottom &amp;amp; displace the well with diesel, POOH.

40. RIH with S/L, install plug &amp;amp; prong into NO GO landing nipple, POOH.

41. RIH with S/L, retrieve protection sleeve.

42. Secure the well by set BPV in TBG Hanger, close all X-mas Tree valves except

BMV.

Contingency Plans of Well AZNS12 ST-1 Work-over:

Based on operation situation in each step, the following contingency plans might be followed:

Contingency plan #1: R/U CT &amp;amp; RIH &amp;amp; Wash 3SV by Chemical wash &amp;amp; Try to Retrieve 3SV by CT if no Success Remedial Plan will be Prepared in advance by Operator &amp;amp; Will be Follow After Client approval.

Contingency plan #2: R/U Wireline &amp;amp; PCE (pressure control equipment), RIH with punching tools, (colliding tools should be on rig site as back up) punch 4 ½” TBG from top fish, POOH WL to surface &amp;amp; R/D same. Perform direct Circ. To balance mud weight in &amp;amp; out. Observe the well.

Contingency plan #3: Install 3SV blanking plug or 7” WL bridge plug.

Contingency plan #4: RIH with proper spear &amp;amp; engage with TBG HGR.

South Azadegan Oilfield Project

AZNS12 ST-1 Workover Program Page 32 of 64

Contingency plan #5: R/U &amp;amp; RIH with FPIT tools to check string free point, POOH to surface &amp;amp; L/D. R/U &amp;amp; RIH with colliding tools &amp;amp; collide completion string from proper depth, POOH to surface &amp;amp; L/D same. POOH completion string to surface precautionary due to probable trapped pressure below fish. While POOH monitor the wells and annulus to make sure the well is safe and over balance.

Contingency plan #6: pull completion string (maximum 80% of TBG yield strength) until string part from weak point then POOH &amp;amp; L/D string. it is assumed to part from 4 ½” expansion joint as weak point. (Approximately 291 Jts 7” TBG (L-80, 29#, VAM) between 3SV &amp;amp; X.O.S and 5 Jts above 3SV. (Approximate length of 7” TBG: 3250 m, Yield Strength of 7” TBG 29#, L-80: 676 Klb, Yield strength of 4 ½” TBG 13.5#, L-80 is 307 Klb). POOH completion string as main plan, RIH with proper Fishing tools, try to catch the fish &amp;amp; work on unlatch completion string from anchor seal, POOH rest of completion string to surface. If No Success, Mill the remainder of fish &amp;amp; packer. Follow the rest of main plan.

Contingency plan #7: RIH w/6" or 6 1/8" Mill &amp;amp; Mill the tail of completion string &amp;amp; Tail in Several Runs, POOH to Surface &amp;amp; L/D mill.

Contingency plan #8: RIH and set RTTS in 9 5/8” CSG as a barrier. N/D BOP, Change DSA pack off to new one. (or change section C) N/U BOP and pressure test.

Note: DSA pack off Shall be Provided by Client.

COMPLETION FLUID SECTION

The completion fluid for this section will be fresh water treated with a scavenger, inhibitor and biocide.

Solids-Free CaCl₂ Fluid Systems

This fluid is recommended to make from fresh water or is solutions made with water and the addition of one or more electrolytes. These fluids do not contain either suspended particles or viscosifiers, which mean neither filtration control nor viscosity control, are provided. Some Brine is corrosive and when corrosion inhibitors are required, compatibility studies should be performed. Some brine is toxic and precautions should be taken to prevent contact with unprotected skin. Brine solutions can be prepared to give good inhibition of clays or shales in producing formations. In addition, common contaminants do not affect the brines.

Salt solutions were formerly considered too corrosive to be used as work-over or completion fluids or as packer fluids. The corrosion problem can be solved by adjusting the pH of the solution to above 9 (min) to 10; however, pH measurements may be less important than measuring and controlling the p-alkalinity of the filtrate; this value should be kept above 1 cc. Lime be used for pH control.

Adjustment of pH, or alkalinity, does not necessarily ensure the solution to be corrosion resistant. It may be necessary to use a corrosion inhibitor to achieve lower corrosion rates. In some cases, an oxygen scavenger might be used in conjunction with a filming amine inhibitor.

Corrosion Control

Corrosion control in completion fluids is important to protect tubular goods and equipment. Corrosion can be limited by controlling the fluid pH at the neutral or alkaline level, and treating out dissolved oxygen. In severe environments such as high temperature or contamination with acid gases, the addition of filming amines can limit corrosion to acceptable levels.

The completion fluid for this section will be Local water treated with a scavenger, and inhibitor.

Pit management will be a key in the successful completion of this interval and sufficient time for planning and preparation should be allowed.

All valves should be checked for leakage beforehand and defects identified to be reported and rectified by drilling contractor.

The mud pits which are to be used to mix the completion brine, should emptied and cleaned adequately and associated lines flushed with water

The rig pumps are to displace all clean up pills as well as the CaCl₂ at intended weight. Prepare spacers and wash pills as per program in the tanks. Ensure that sufficient spacer is prepared to account for any dead tanks volume.

Prepare all inhibited CaCl₂ before starting the displacement process. After preparing the brine should be filtered through filtration unit and store in a clean pit before displacement.

Filtration Process:

Filtration provides clean fluids that will prevent damage to the formation, the reservoir and its permeability. It does this by removal of solids and particulates from the fluid that may otherwise block the open space within the rock formation containing the hydrocarbon fluid within the production zone.

Any solids and contaminates in the completion fluid will reduce its effectiveness. An efficiently filtered and completely solid free completion fluid will add value to both the productivity and the dependability of the well in the long term.

VIRA dual pod filtration cartridge unit is recommended for filtering brines and produced water in completion, stimulation, and workover operations. The pods are connected by a manifold, providing staged filtration capability. Staged filtration utilizes cartridge filters with different ratings to maximize filtration efficiency. Cartridge filtration is designed for use with fluids containing a low percent by volume of suspended solids. Cartridge filtration is not economic when fluids are contaminated with oil or other substances.

Total Solids can be measured at the wellsite using a turbidity meter. Solids that are not added to the system to enhance the performance of a brine are considered contamination. Contaminations include formation clays, precipitates, and polymer residues, among other things. These contaminations can be filtered at the well site using diatomaceous earth, a plate and frame press, and Five-micron to ten absolute cartridges.

Note: a clear completion fluid should not be sent to the wellsite with an NTU (Nephelometric Turbidity Unit) greater than 30-60 or a suspended-solid Concentration greater than 30-60 ppm and for fluid returning from the well NTU should be less than 150.

RIG CLEAN UP CHECK LIST (Should be done by Rig Operator)

A. Areas to clean.

1. Surface pits.

2. Clean the suction, return, settling, and reserve pits.

3. Clean the sand traps.

4. Clean the ditches and troughs.

5. Clean the trip tank.

6. Clean the shaker area including all solids equipment and lines.

7. Clean the mixing hoppers.

8. Clean the cement unit.

9. Clean any other pits or equipment that the completion fluid may contact.

10. Cycle all valves in mixing system.

B. Items to flush out.

1. All mud pumps and suction lines.

2. All centrifuges and lines.

3. Chemical and weighting mixing lines in contact with the completion fluid.

4. Lines from the pit room to the trip tank.

5. Lines from the rig floor to the trip tank.

6. Choke, choke manifold and kill lines.

7. Standpipes.

8. Degassing and solids control equipment.

9. Lines to the cement unit and/or other pumping equipment.

10. Casings fill up line.

11. Lines to and from the filtration line.

12. Take on and return lines to and from the boat.

13. Any other lines that the completion fluid may contact.

Displacement Procedure

Pre-Displacement Steps

1. Run bit and dual or tandem scrapers.

2. Circulate and condition mud. Reduce funnel viscosity as much as possible while maintaining adequate rheological properties to clean hole and prevent settling of solids. Maintain critical annular velocity to assure that liner tops are thoroughly cleaned prior to displacement.

3. Rig up equipment for displacement of completion fluid. All tanks, circulating lines, and pumps to be used in the displacement should be cleared of residual mud.

4. Insure sufficient space is available to store displaced mud.

11. Health, Safety and Environments

12.1 WELL CONTROL

All the drilling operation shall obey the requirement of Well Control Manual of MSA and contractor’s well control manual; under no circumstances should the deviation from well control policy be permitted without prior approval through MSA. If the contractor’s well control manual or anywhere has conflict with Well Control Manual of MSA, take Well Control Manual of MSA as the standard.

12.1.1 WORK Requirement of Well Control Equipment

 With shut-in casing pressure lower than 1,000psi, while snubbing with annular preventer, drill tools

shall have 18-deg shoulder tool joints, and the snubbing velocity shall not be greater than 0.2m/s.

 After shut off the annular preventer or ram preventer, with the shut-in casing pressure not greater

than 2,000psi, drill tools are allowed to pull up and down with the velocity less than 0.2m/s,

however, rotating or tool joint passing through are forbidden.

 While drilling through pay zone and thereafter, BOP function (close-open) test for the BOPs shall be

performed regularly.

 Kill manifolds shall not be used for drilling fluid fill-in.

 The maximum allowed shut-in casing pressure shall be remarkably indicated on choke manifolds.

 All gate valves of well control manifolds shall be tagged with serial numbers, and be indicated with

on/Off.

 In case shear rams were used, after shearing the drill pipe with shear rams, retrieve the upper sheared

drill pipe, lower a drill pipe joint with TIW valve installed into the hole and close pipe rams on it to

prevent the possibility of shear ram’s failure.

12.1.2 Management of Well Control Equipment

 Well control equipment used by the drilling crew shall be managed and operated by designated

personnel with clear post responsibilities.

 Well site shall have specified component storeroom and rubber element storeroom with air

conditioners respectively. The temperature of storerooms shall meet storage requirements of

components and rubber elements.

 At least 1 set is available as back-up for every type ram assembly in the well site. Ram preventer

side door seals and ram rubber, every type gasket and bolt etc. should be enough for backup.

South Azadegan Oilfield Project
