12.2 Recording Reference

All BOP tests, drills, function tests, any malfunctions, repair or maintenance to the mud System and well control equipment shall be recorded in the IADC daily reports and shall be signed by both the Drilling Contractor's Tool Pusher and Drilling Supervisor on the well site. They shall also be recorded in the Daily Drilling Report.

12.3 Flow Check Procedure

To avoid a kick situation, it is recommended that a flow check be conducted at specific times during the drilling operation.

While drilling (any warning sign).

Prior to tripping the drill string.

While tripping (any warning sign).

While out of hole (continuously).

Trip out:

After pulling 5% of the drill pipe

At the midpoint depth of the wellbore

Prior to pulling the first stand of drill collars

After all the drill string is out of hole.

Trip in:

Upon reaching surface casing shoe

At midpoint of the wellbore

12.4 Primary Control Reference

It is the responsibility of the Drilling Contractor to keep the hole full at all times by using all the available equipment. The Drilling Supervisor shall monitor that the correct preventive practices are being implemented and/or conducted at all times.

Extreme care shall be taken to monitor mud volume, drilling breaks and gas cut mud.

The MACP (Maximum allowable casing pressure) shall be confirmed by the Drilling Supervisor, either after setting each new casing string or, whenever the density of the drilling mud changes.

The MACP shall be clearly written on a kick control sheet that will be posted near the choke control panel.

The predetermined distance at which the Tool Joint is to be pulled above the rotary should be posted on rig floor near the BOP control panel.

The Driller is responsible for carefully measuring and recording the slow pump pressure.

Awareness of these values is an important element in killing operations, in order to avoid formation breakdown.

South Azadegan Oilfield Project

AZNS12 ST-1 Workover Program Page 52 of 64

Take a measure and record the slow pump pressure at three different flow rates with all pumps at the following times:

Once per tour.

Whenever changes occur in the mud density/rheology.

Whenever changes occur in the dimension and characteristics of the string, BHA, jet size, jet plugged or jet lost, etc.

12.5 Secondary Control Reference

Any time a drilling break is noticed, drilling shall stop and a static monitoring of the well shall be carried out. Space-out for all Pipe Rams and Annular Preventer must be known to the Driller at all times to keep tool joints clear of annular preventer and rams.

12.6 Well control during drilling and completion operation

The drilling design shall be strictly implemented by the drilling contractor and when it is discovered there is incompliance of downhole situation with design and the design will be amended, the procedure for amendment of design shall be followed. If emergency is encountered, and safe operation can be affected, after the discussion between drilling rig manager and the drilling supervisor, practical technical measures can be taken first and then report to the top management. The Company shall approve and notice in time as per the drilling program amendment procedure.

The curve of well equivalent mud weight as per predicted formation pressure, curve of mud weight in drilling program and curve of actual mud weight must be drawn during drilling operation. For exploratory well and key well, the curve of dc index while drilling formation pressure equivalent mud weight for sandstone, mudstone and shale shall be drawn by the comprehensive mud logging crew.

When entering oil and gas formation or drilling master reservoir, high diameter nozzle shall be selected for the drilling bit to treat well killing and mud loss.

SCR (Slow Circulation Rate) shall be conducted at the start of drilling activity, pump strokes, pumping rate and circulating pressure should be recorded. While drilling in pay zone, SCR is required to be conducted with all pumps separately as follows, pump strokes, pumping rate and circulating pressure shall be recorded in Daily Drilling Report and Kill Sheet.

Once for every 12 hours in general;

After bit change or BHA change; 3) Mud weight change exceeds 3.75pcf.

Oil and gas invasion and overflow shall be checked with wiper trip and shall be conducted under the following situation:

Each time before POOH after drilling oil and gas formations.

Severe invasion of oil and gas occurs during drilling, but overflow does not occur before POOH.

POOH after killing well.

POOH after lowering mud weight in wellbore.

POOH after curing mud loss during drilling oil and gas formation.

POOH after drilling oil and gas formation and a prolonged period of time is needed for other operations (E logging, running casing, running tubing and DST etc.).

Regarding the shut-in methods selection

Soft shut-in method is recommended for gas well;

Hard shut-in method is recommended for oil well;

Hard shut-in method is recommended for the well of which the well has strong formation strength in EMW as per FIT test;

Soft shut-in method is recommended for the well of which the well has weak formation strength in EMW as per FIT test.

South Azadegan Oilfield Project

AZNS12 ST-1 Workover Program Page 53 of 64

Main technical measures for prevention of kicking and blowout during tripping.

Before POOH, circulation duration of mud in wellbore shall not be less than one and a half cycles. The observation time after wiper trip shall be no less than one and a half cycles. The density differential of inlet and outlet shall not exceed 1.248 pcf.

Flow check shall be conducted regularly via trip tank as follows

Prior to POOH (keep string rotation at 10 rpm for preventing stuck pipe)

POOH to last casing shoe

Before POOH BHA through BOP stack

Note: Tripping should be shut-off immediately and flow check shall be performed later on when any suspected well kick is observed.

During POOH, fill up hole every 3-5 stands of DP and every stand of DC. If the nozzle is plugged, during POOH, mud shall be filled full for each joint or continuous filling shall be conducted and trip sheet shall be recorded carefully.

When the bit is in the oil and gas formation and 300m above top of oil and gas formation, POOH speed shall be controlled to maintain the excellent well building property and rheological property of mud to avoid severe swabbing in the wellbore.

During RIH, the running speed shall be controlled to avoid the loss of circulation due to down hole pressure surge.

During tripping, check and repair of the equipment shall be arranged at the time when running to the casing shoe. if equipment have to be checked and repaired during POOH, due blowout prevention measures shall be taken during and after the check and repair, drill string shall be run to bottom and circulate for one and a half cycles. After everything is normal, drilling shall be resumed. Equipment check and repair shall not be conducted for empty well condition.

Treatment measures for invasion of gas during normal drilling:

When invasion of gas is discovered, it shall be discharged with circulation in time. The gas invaded mud shall not be pumped in the hole before eliminating gas.

Increasing mud weight shall be conducted when stop drilling and after invaded gas eliminated from mud. Mud weight incremental of each circulation cycle shall be controlled within 3.121 pcf

"In-post" policy

"In-post" will be initiated after the surface casing is cemented.

The "in-post" personnel must be trained and verified qualified by the technical staff of drilling rig.

During drilling, specific personnel shall be arranged to be "in-post", the mud logging personnel shall monitor the level of the circulating tank etc. as per the requirements. During tripping, other auxiliary operation or drilling suspension, specific personnel for "in-post" shall be arranged by the drilling and mud logging personnel in the meantime.

"In-post" requirements:

For drilling operation, variation of the outlet flow, drilling time, lithology, bubble, smell, showings, pit volume, density and mud viscosity, gas measured values and content of chloride etc. shall be carefully monitored. The level of the circulating tank shall be observed and recorded each 15 minutes and if special situation occurs, the measurement and record shall be intensified. If anomaly occurs, it shall be reported to the driller in time.

For tripping operation, trip sheet shall be filled accordingly. If anomaly occurs, it shall be reported to the driller.

South Azadegan Oilfield Project

AZNS12 ST-1 Workover Program Page 54 of 64

For other operations, it shall be observed whether there is overflow of mud at the wellhead or mud level from wellhead. If anomaly occurs, it shall be reported to the driller.

Treatment of loss of circulation

Before cementing non-target zone or pay zone, if loss of circulation occurs during drilling, POOH shall be carried to run open ended drill pipe for cement plug job if condition allows. During RIH, mud shall be filled from annulus to balance formation pressure to avoid blowout.

Treatment of loss of circulation during drilling after production casing cemented

Mud level not at wellhead after loss of circulation. Stop drilling, pick up TDS or Kelly, stop pumps and observe with moving the drill string and prepare well control related work. Each 10 minutes, mud with density no lower than the drilling weight shall be reversely filled up from the annulus. Each time, the filling up shall be 1~2m3, or continuous reserve injecting mud with small speed to maintain that the column pressure of mud in wellbore is higher than the formation pressure. POOH to casing shoe or safety interval for observation. Additional treatment shall be made as per the situation of loss of circulation.

Mud level at wellhead after loss of circulation. Stop drilling, pick up TDS or Kelly, stop pumps and move the drill string to observe with well control well prepared. When the well is static, pull the bit upward to the casing shoe or safe interval for observation. If no anomaly is observed, circulate with slow pump rate. The measures such as plugging back job, POOH or condition mud etc. shall be carried out as per the situation of loss of circulation. If loss of circulation occurs to pay zone, mud weight shall be acquired by static pressure. After pulling out to casing shoe and observing for one tripping cycle, when no more loss of circulation occurs after running to bottom, drilling operation can be resumed.

Well control for E logging, cementing and DST

Before E logging, down hole condition shall be stable and static. If it takes long time for electrical logging, one more condition trip shall be conducted between logging. Shooting nipple is required for logging. Logging service shall be furnished with tools for cutting the cables.

Continuously fill the well during performing wireline logging, and keep closely monitoring for the well via trip tank.

Before running casing, ensure the well is in static condition without any flowing. Pipe ram shall be changed to casing ram with proper size. Casing circulating head or crossover sub between casing and in used DP shall be kept at rig floor at all times during casing running.

The hydrostatic pressure shall be kept balance with formation pressure during whole cementing job to avoid blowout due to loss of circulation, loss of balance for pressure and cement weight loss during WOC.

12.7 HEALTH

This well is committed to develop for oil in a responsible manner that promotes employees' and local inhabitants' health.

A trained Paramedic and proper MEDIVAC equipment and ambulance shall be stationed on the drilling rig during the drilling campaign.

An emergency medical evacuation plan shall be coordinated, and shall keep in touch with emergency response centres manned by qualified doctor 24-hours per day in Ahwaz city.

South Azadegan Oilfield Project

AZNS12 ST-1 Workover Program Page 55 of 64

Medical emergency report and investigation shall be performed as soon as possible in accordance with Medical Emergency Procedures.

12.8 SAFETY

Due to high concentration of H2S in Sarvak, Kazhdumi and Gadvan reservoirs, Make detail H2S operation procedures, in particular, and carry it out strictly.

Lifesaving equipment like SCBA, Escape Mask, H2S detectors (Multi portable and personal detector) and implement the H2S Services system during drilling activity should be provided.

All lifting equipment and cranes must be certified by approved 3rd party (approved by Institute of Standards &amp;amp; Industrial Research of Iran)

All electrical equipment should be designed for such locations, and listed by nationally recognized testing laboratory. All wiring components and electrical equipment should be maintained in accordance with the manufacturers’ recommendation.

PSSR (Pre-Startup Safety Review) before spud-in and penetrating into oil and gas formations are mandatory by contractor under the supervision of Company and approved by Company.

12.9 ENVIRONMENT

Requirement on location

The access road and well location construction shall be accorded with construction program of well location. It minimizes any impacts on the local residents, prevent all soil contamination, prevent all ground water contamination, and prevent all surface water contamination. Cutting and waste water pit shall be lining and drainage system shall be good and to avoid farm and season canal contamination.

Management regulation for transportation truck, drilling operation machine and tools shall be carried out strictly to avoid damage farm and trees, etc.

Well site shall be flat and clean. All the equipment, materials, drilling tools shall be put in order.

Control the rig noise to decrease the influence to surroundings while drilling at the inhabitation area.

Contractor shall perform on‐site segregation of wastes prior to transfer to the transfer area and/or delivery to the transportation Contractor in accordance with the following waste hazard classification.

Non-Hazardous Wastes (Re-usable, Recyclable and Recoverable Wastes)

Ferrous and non-ferrous metals, plastics, and wood wastes, PETs and potentially paper and glass.

Materials shall be separately segregated and provision may be made for size reduction and containerization equipment.

The Contractor/Generators are encouraged to seek for recycle/re-use alternatives based on the Local available facilities, for final disposal of these materials.

It should be noted that landfill disposal of metal waste materials and wood wastes shall be prohibited. For wood wastes re-use of and/or salvage of commercial timber, or deliver/release to.

Local community are recommended.

Hazardous Wastes

Facilities of environment protection supplied to well site

Mud purifying circulation system.

Cooling water spraying and circulating system for drilling pump.

Special recovery tank for deposed oil.

Reserve house for valuable mud chemicals.

Automatic mud weighting supply system.

BOP stack is equipped according to drilling design.

Requirement of environment protection on location

Sewage pit Area of the sewage pit: 1500 m2.

Prior to spud, mud pit and sewage pit must comply with the standard. Install cooling water spraying and circulating system for drilling pump and sewage circulating system for cleaning rig floor and equipment.

Install BOP stack and pressure test shall be operated according to the drilling design to avoid blowout.

Install oil supply lines and check whether there is any leakage.

Management of environment protection on location

In drilling operation keep mud and sewage from overflowing. If it happens, clean up timely.

Mud chemicals shall be stored according to the standard and shall not be scattered around well site. If mud chemicals scatter while loading or unloading, clean it up at once. The sack of mud chemicals shall be recovered. Do not dispose it on site.

Enhance water management at well location and do not wash equipment with fresh water. Stop water flowing for long time. Overhead tanks shall be utilized.

Oil management shall be carefully at the well site. No oil dirt on site, no dripping and leaking at oil tank and manifold system area.

After the well is completed, reinforce the sewage pit solidify the disposed mud and have environment procedure fulfilled.

Install fuel supply lines and keep them in good condition.

All the drilling fluid materials shall be recovered and shall not be left at the well site after completion.

The environmental protection personnel from contractor and operator side shall check and accept the well site environment according to the regulation after completion. Only well site environment is qualified, the well can be delivered.

12. H2S Monitoring &amp;amp; Prevention Measure

13.1 Monitoring H2S

Somewhere on the well site is apt to accumulate H2S, such as mud pit, shale shaker, and drilling platform, should be installed one set of. Make sure H2S monitor and alarm system can be used. Alarm threshold setting for H2S warning indicator: the first warning level is 10mg/m3, unable warning sound, just show present value of H2S content to operators. The second warning level is 20mg/m3, when the H2S content in air exceed 20mg/m3, H2S warning indicator can give an alarm automatically, and warning sound should be heard by everyone work in well site. The audible alarm should be installed on Kelly board.

Equip enough gas masks on drilling platform, shaker screen (total amount should large than 24), and equip 12 sets of 30min positive pressure Air Aspirators 2 sets of portable H2S monitor and appropriative H2S warning indicator. Arrange a person specially assigned for taking charge all the protective apparatus. This man must do periodical check to keep these equipment in a good condition.

H2S monitor should be done weekly check and compulsory examination.

After drilling into the pay zone, strengthen the detection of H2S content in mud.

13.2 Measures for H2S prevention

Windsocks shall be set on the drill floor and in the monsoon direction or/and prevailing wind direction of Azadegan oil field, off well site. In emergency, employees must follow the evacuation procedure.

Explosion-proof blowers shall be installed around the rig, shale shaker, and drilling fluid tanks to blow away toxic and flammable gas at the well site.

The rig crew in the H2S area shall be furnished with H2S monitors and adequate protective apparatus. Everybody shall be able to use, maintain, and check the apparatus.

The technicians of rig crew are responsible for H2S proof training and the tool pusher is in charge of the supervision and examination.

The pH value of drilling fluid in the H2S area shall be kept over 9.5. Pay attention to measurement of H2S concentration in drilling fluid. The H2S concentration shall be kept at less than 50mg/cm3 by using sulphur removal agents and degassers.

Personnel safety and protection shall be carried out according to SY/T5087 during operations in polluted areas where H2S content exceeds the critical concentration.

When the rig crew makes decision to bleed and fire because well control cannot be performed due to well site conditions, operations shall be performed according to procedures in SY/T5087.

Once blowout occurs, the incident shall be reported to the higher level department as soon as possible and firefighting trucks, ambulances, medical care personnel and technicians shall be on duty at the well site.

South Azadegan Oilfield Project

AZNS12 ST-1 Workover Program Page 59 of 64

After the blowout is controlled, H2S concentration should be measured in the places where H2S is possible to gather.

The personnel are not allowed to access until the H2S concentration is below the critical concentration.

South Azadegan Oilfield Project

AZNS12 ST-1 Workover Program Page 60 of 64

1. General Information

1.1 Field Introduction

Azadegan South Oil Field is situated in West Karoun province on a large long-axis anticline with N-S trending with approximate dimensions about 20 km width and 60 km length near to Iran-Iraq border, to the east of Yaran Oil Field.

The trap area of the south Azadegan is limited to 43.2x17.2 km. The Azadegan Oil field was discovered in 1999, when Well AZN-1 was drilled vertically down to the Cretaceous Fahliyan Formation with total depth of 4,643m. The results of this well, revealed the reservoir characteristics of the field. Following to the result of the well no. AZN-1, another 5 exploration wells was drilled in different parts of this huge field down to Fahliyan Formation. In the later stage the well No.10 assumed as exploration well for evaluation of deeper formations. This well was drilled in 2008, down to the depth of 5340m (Neyriz Fm.), mainly to evaluate the Jurassic formations.

Based on the exploration wells results, carbonate reservoir of Sarvak Formation is broadly developed in Azadegan Field. This formation was penetrated in all of seven exploration wells (AZN-1, AZN-2, AZN-3, AZN-4, AZN-5, AZN-6 and AZN-10). Clastic oil-bearing zones of Kazhdumi Formation developed in main anticline of Azadegan Field, extending from north to center of South Azadegan. The Clastic oil-bearing zones of Gadvan Formation developed only in crest area and south parts of South Azadegan Filed, which was discovered by AZN-1 in crest and AZN-4 in south parts. The carbonates of Fahliyan Formation also developed in Azadegan field, but the oil reservoir of this formation developed in South part of South Azadegan.

The Azadegan Field is an elongated anticline, trending in N-S direction, belonging to "Arabian Trend".

The stratigraphy sequence of the field includes AghaJari, Gachsaran, Fahliyan, Pabdeh, Gurpi, Ilam, Laffan, Sarvak, Kazhdumi, Dariyan, Gadvan and Fahliyan Formations, from top to bottom. This sequence in well no AZN-10, the deepest up to now drilled well of the field, continues with Garau, Gotnia, Najmah, Sargalu, Alan, Mus and Neyriz formations.

The Dominant lithofacies of Sarvak Formation are Rudist-bearing packstone and partially grainstone, which contains abundant bioclasts. Some other facies like matrix-dominated wackestone and mudstone are also found.

The AZADEGAN Oilfield is Located in Khuzestan Province and is Approximately Located 80 Kilometers West of Ahwaz City, near to Iran-Iraq Border. It is in The Northwest of The YADAVARAN Field and in The West of JUFEYR Field. The Average Monthly Temperature is 45ºc in summer, and Highest Temperature is 52ºc. The Lowest Temperature is -4.4ºc in winter. Maximum Rainfall is 78 mm in February, Winter Season.

This Document covers the work over of well AZNS-122. Main headlines of program are de-complete the well and run new completion string.

1.7 Drilling History

The AZNS – 127 well was drilled &amp;amp; completed by TDDC on date 1395.10.08 at 12:00 as describe below:

 26" hole size drilled to 150m w/ Mw 66 – 68pcf &amp;amp; 20" casing ran to 146m &amp;amp; cemented as program

by 170bbl cement.

 17 – 1/2" hole size drilled to 1441m, while increased Mw from 68 to 90pcf, 13 – 3/8" casing ran

&amp;amp; cemented to 1441m by 780bb cement.

 12 – 1/4" hole size drilled to 3910m w/ performance drlg &amp;amp; 3 – 15BPH loss. At depth 2354m

suddenly pressure dropped f/ 2850 to 1950psi &amp;amp; string twist off from float sub &amp;amp; 9.18m fish left

in hole. Fish recovered by overshot 10 – 1/8”. At depth 3117mdue to pressure dropped f/ 2560

to 2320psi POOH string but string got stuck at 3040m &amp;amp; free by applied 50klbs overpull, POOH

to surface &amp;amp; observed wash out on float sub above 8” PDM. Took

MSFL/DLL/SONIC/CALIPER/GR/CDR &amp;amp; ZDL/CNC/DSL/WTS/TTRM logs, 9 – 5/8" casing

ran &amp;amp; cemented to 3909m with 1133bbl cement.

 8 – 1/2" hole size drilled to 4226m with no major problem, took VDL/SBT/CCL/GR logs, string

held up at 3905m, tried to pass this point several times with no success, logged up from this pont

to 100m above 13 – 3/8” casing shoe. Due to tight hole Mw increased f/ 104 to 105pcf. Took first

full suite log as DLL/SONIC/MSFL/CDR from TD to 3810m &amp;amp; second full suite log as

CNT/LDT/NGS/GR from 3910m to TD. 7" liner ran to 4226m. Due to first dry test results,

decided was made to tie back 7” liner to 3777m. The well suspended with cement plug &amp;amp;

completion string &amp;amp; rig released @1396.06.27.

 Re – entry the well at 1396.11.03 by retrieving completion string &amp;amp; ran new completion &amp;amp; rig

released at 24:00 on 1396.12.23

 Rig less operation was performed on date 17.05.1398. tried to RIH with coiled tubing to unload

the well. There was an obstruction in the well at depth 3918m. Unable to pass the depth. Several

runs were performed by coiled tubing and mill to remove the obstruction.

 Rig less operation for unloading and well flowing was performed on date 30.01.1400.

 Pressure monitoring was performed on tubing head spool vent port, it was 4,000psi. Metal seal

of tubing hanger is damaged.

 Try to run coiled tubing to TD and wash the wellbore with xylene. Run CCL/GR/MFC logging

BHA in the well. It was observed 7” liner ID has been decreased to about 3inches in interval

3889 – 3911m.

 Flow the well, an abnormal annulus pressure was observed.

 The other Rig less monitoring well annulus pressure on date 18.09.1400. It was annulus pressure

is 5,300psi. Sampling was performed from annulus fluid. It was contained with gas and

hydrocarbon.

1. Open the well, set plug tester in T.H.S &amp;amp; perform BOP test as NIOC policy, retrieve plug

tester.

2. P/U &amp;amp; M/U 6 – 1/8” centre cut bit and RIH to 3100m Whipstock, while fill up string with

104pcf fresh mud due to mud in hole is galled up &amp;amp; break Circ. every 3 stands.

3. Perform CBU in 2 stages to balance mud weight.

4. L/U &amp;amp; pressure test cement line, perform 20bbl cement balance plug job, POOH 10 stands,

flush string, Cont. POOH to surface.

5. P/U &amp;amp; M/U 8 – 1/2” rock bit &amp;amp; related BHA, RIH to top of cement estimated @ 3011m,tag

cement, D/O &amp;amp; dress cement to 3065m, perform CBU, POOH to surface.

6. P/U &amp;amp; M/U 8 – 1/2” rock bit &amp;amp; 9 – 5/8” scraper BHA &amp;amp; RIH to bottom while scrap inside

9 – 5/8” casing (Whipstock packer depth), perform CBU, POOH to surface &amp;amp; L/D scraper.

7. P/U &amp;amp; M/U 8 – 1/2” 9 – 5/8” hydraulic set Whipstock including UBHO sub, align Whipface

to UBHO (Gyro sub), RIH to setting depth @ ±3060m (KOP will be @3055m).

8. R/U wireline, run Gyro, orient Whipface &amp;amp; adjust toolface (Azi: 340 Deg), POOH Gyro,

L/D wireline.

9. Set Whipstock packer as per procedure &amp;amp; check, pull string upward &amp;amp; shear mill pins,

displace the well with proper mud (82 – 84pcf) &amp;amp; Cont. Circ. to balance mud weight.

10. Start opening window in 9 – 5/8” casing, pump Hi-Vis pill, sweep the well, in order to

change mill, POOH to surface.

11. P/U &amp;amp; M/U new mill RIH to bottom, Cont. opening window &amp;amp; drill to 3m inside formation.

Check window condition.

12. POOH to surface &amp;amp; L/D mill.

13. Perform BOP test as NIOC policy.

14. P/U &amp;amp; M/U 8 – 1/2” Tri – Cone bit &amp;amp; directional BHA (including MWD &amp;amp; Gyro sub),

perform shallow hole test, RIH to bottom.

15. R/U wireline, run Gyro, adjust toolface, POOH Gyro &amp;amp; L/D wireline.

16. Profile the bit, Cont. directional drilling hole section from 3090m to 3300m, perform CBU.

17. In order to change the BHA, POOH to surface.

18. P/U &amp;amp; M/U 8 – 1/2” PDC bit &amp;amp; directional BHA (including MWD), RIH to bottom,

perform CBU to uniform mud weight.

19. Cont. directional drilling hole section to 3550m while pump Hi-Vis pill periodically.

Completion Section

1. R/U completion running equipment, run 3 – 1/2" * 4 – 1/2", 10K completion string as per

program, R/D completion running.

2. Install TWCV in tubing hanger, N/D BOP stack, N/U X.M.T, perform required test as per

program.

3. Secure the well by set BPV in tubing hanger, close all X – mas tree valves except BMV,

and Release the Rig.

4. Retrieve BPV, R/U slickline, set protection sleeve, retrieve prong &amp;amp; plug from NO GO

landing nipple, POOH.

5. RIH with CT to bottom, displace the well with diesel or nitrogen &amp;amp; observ well, POOH.

6. R/U SL, RIH &amp;amp; retrieve protection sleeve, POOH, R/D SL.

7. Flow the well as pre – acid clean up till acceptable BSW &amp;amp; reading stable flow rate on 2

different choke size for 72 hrs.

8. R/U &amp;amp; RIH S.L, set protection sleeve, POOH &amp;amp; R/D S.L

9. RIH with C/T &amp;amp; perform acid wash as per program, POOH to surface. RIH w/SL and

retrieve protection sleeve

10. Flow the well as post – acid clean up till acceptable BSW &amp;amp; reading stable flow rate on 2

6. Directional Drilling Operation

6.1 Hydraulic Set Whipstock System Operation Procedure

SCOPE

The following procedures are intended to provide concise but definitive steps to follow in operations involving the milling of lateral hole sections from a parent well using the Hydraulic Set Whipstock System.

The Hydraulic Set Whipstock System is a hydraulically set whipstock that requires a hydraulic force to activate the packer assembly, setting itself in the casing.

Milling a window in casing using a whipstock usually consists of one run for setting the Whipstock in place and milling and completing the window through the casing wall and into the formation, while dressing the window to eliminate drag.

EQUIPMENT REQUIRED

Hole Preparation Run Equipment

• A Full Gauge Drift Mill

• Casing Scrapper

• Cross Over Sub

• String Stabilizer

• Pony Drill Collar or 1 Joint of Drill collar

• String Stabilizer

• Drill Collars

• Drilling Jar

• Drill Collars

• HWDP’s

• Balance Of Drill Pipes To Surface

The stiffness of this assembly will serve to identify any problem doglegs or restrictions in the hole that may hamper running of the whipstock assembly.

Whipstock Run Equipment

• Hydraulic Set Whipstock

• Tri-Mill (Optional Bi-Mill or a combination of Rugby/Back/Window Mill)

• Running Tools

• Nuzzle plug Assembly

• Flex Joint (1 joint of HWDP)

AZNS-127 Side Track-2 Program Page 43 of 179

• Universal Bottom Hole Orientation Sub (UBHO sub) or MWD

• Pup joints (for space-out if necessary)

• Tool kit

PRE-OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES

Pre-Run Checklist

As part of the Pre-operational Procedures, all whipstock jobs should include a completed

Pre-Run Preparation Checklist.

Pre‐Run Preparation Checklist

† The Packer slip is in place, is in good condition, and is the correct size for the casing size and weight and the

Allen screws are tight.

† The shear pins are properly installed and in good condition and the Number of Shear pins are enough.

† The shear screw is the proper size, and it will make up into the Whipface.

† The shear screw will fit through the Rugby/Lead Mill hole.

† Running Tools, Nuzzle plug Assembly and Hydraulic Lines and Fittings are in good condition and properly installed.

† All mills are on location and the OD’s are correct for the casing’s size/weight. (Check mill OD’s with a gauge ring that is OD + 1/32").

† All downhole equipment has been properly measured and OD’s, ID’s, and lengths have been properly recorded.

† The slots on the gyro match and are compatible with the lug assembly on the orientation sub.

† The survey tools will pass through all drill string tool joints and drill collar ID’s.

† All rotary connections are compatible.

† All rotary shouldered connections are made up to the recommended torque.

† Enough Pump Pressure is available on Site for setting the Packer.

Making the Hole Preparation Run

1. Make a run to ensure that the casing is clean and there is smooth and clean place for setting the packer. The run should include the following (from the bottom):

• A Full Gauge Drift Mill

• Casing Scrapper (Do not run casing scrapers across open perforations.)

• Cross Over Sub (Bit Sub with Float)

• String Stabilizer

• Pony Drill Collar or 1 Joint of Drill collar

• String Stabilizer

• Drill Collars

• Drilling Jar

• Drill Collars

• HWDP’s

• Balance of Drill Pipes To Surface

South Azadegan Oilfield Project

Contract No:

AZNS-127 Side Track-2 Program Page 45 of 179

2. Run this assembly in the well to the Packer setting depth.

3. Tally the pipe while running in or out of the well to get an accurate measurement to the Packer setting depth.

4. Record the measurements to ensure that:

• the whipstock can be run and set at the desired depth

• the depth measurement to the Packer setting depth is accurate

• the casing wall is clean where the whipstock is to be set

NOTE: Scrape Packer setting depth twice.

Note: It is very important to get an accurate measurement for the packer setting depth so the Whipstock will be oriented as to setting depth as possible. Using this measurement facilitates proper placement of the Whipstock.

Preparing the Milling Equipment

1. Lay the whipstock on the catwalk, face up, with the top of the whipstock pointing toward the rig.

WARNING

Never use a nylon sling to lift or move a Whipstock because nylon may be cut. Always us a wire sling or wire rope to lift or move a Whipstock.

2. Complete the whipstock assembly, checking all OD’s, ID’s, and descriptions.

3. Pick up a joint of S-135 Drill Pipe (FLEXJOINT) and make up the Flow Through Valve to the top of the drill pipe and make up the Mill Assembly covered with Running Tool to the bottom of Drill Pipe.

Note: If the window is exiting through two or more strings of casing or into a known hard formation, exclude the Watermelon Mills (in the case of using combination mills), using only the Rugby Mill below the single joint of DP. Depending on the casing size and grade, more than one Rugby Mill may be required to make multiple exits.

Once the casing string(s) has been exited into the formation, pull out of the hole. Make up the Back Mill (and Window Mill) in the assembly as described above and run in the hole, reaming through the window with the Watermelon Mills.

4. Make up one joint of S-135 Drill Pipe (with cone type DP strainer installed) to the top of Flow Through Valve and make Up MWD to the top of Drill Pipe. (or Make up UBHO Sub to the top of Flow Through Valve).

5. If a bit float have to be used, place the bit float sub above the Flow Through Valve and beneath the UBHO sub.

6. Make up all connections to the recommended torque.

7. Ensure that everything is properly made up before continuing (see Figure).

screw hole on the Rugby Mill and scribe a line from this blade, up the Back Mill (and Window Mill), Bit Sub, and the single joint of HWDP to the top of the UBHO Sub.

9. Have the survey company representative back out the set screws that hold the internal key in the UBHO Sub, and rotate the key until it is aligned with the scribed line. After it is in position, tighten the setscrews to lock the key in alignment with the scribed line.

10. Run the Mill assembly through the BOP stack and into the casing liner/hanger (being careful not to damage the wear bushings or strike any closed BOP rams) to ensure that the whipstock’s OD is compatible with the drift diameter of the casing. Remove wear bushing if necessary.

11. Pull the assembly out of hole.

12. Secure a safety clamp around the whipstock body about halfway down the face of the

Whipface while the whipstock is lying on the pipe deck/catwalk.

13. Pick up the Whipstock with tugger from the catwalk. A whip handling device is provided which is bolted onto the back of whipstock. This is to be used as a false rotary to support the assembly in the Rotary Table when making up the mill to whip via the shear screw. Assist with a crane as necessary.

14. Set Whipstock in the rotary table (rams shut).

15. Lower the whipstock into the mouse hole (or other suitable work hole on the drill floor), allowing both the safety clamp and the winch/tugger line to support the whipstock’s weight.

Note: Larger Whipstocks (9⅝ to 20 inches) are usually too big for the mouse hole and must be set in the rotary to attach to the Mill assembly. Properly sized rotary slips must be used. The 13⅜” whipstock will not fit through the standard rotary (10⅝" ID) and the rotary bushing, in this event must be pulled. Use of an API bowl and slips to hold the whipstock in

the rotary is required.

CAUTION

• Close the BOP Shear/Blind ram when working on Whipstock.

• Do not drop anything in the wellbore when working over the wellbore.

• Use extreme caution when handling the whipstock, setting drill collar slips, safety clamps, etc. to prevent dropping the whipstock in the hole.

• Run the draw works in low. Pick up and set down the whipstock easily in the slips to prevent damage or premature setting.

• Ensure the lead tongs have most of the slack out of the snub line to prevent jerking against the back-up tongs.

16. Put a light amount of thread compound on the shear screw, adjust Rugby Mill hole and

Whipface and connect the whipstock assembly to the mill assembly with shear screw.

Shear screws with a higher value should be considered when:

• running the whipstock in a highly deviated hole

• heavy mud is in the well

• other wellbore restrictions such as a liner hanger may be encountered

Shear screws with a lower shear value should be considered when:

• whipstock is being set shallow (less than 1500 m)

• running and setting Whipstock with coiled tubing

17. Attach the Hydraulic Line to the connection on the bottom of the Milling Assembly and back of whipstock.

18. Fill Whipstock and Mill Assembly / Running Tool with Hydraulic Oil, allow air to bleed out, fit piston ensuring the top of piston is below the top running tool box connection.

19. Run the Whipstock &amp;amp; Mill Assembly below the rotary table to the top of UBHO sub, Break the connection and top-up with Hydraulic Oil.

20. Pick up the Milling / whipstock assembly.

21. Install the rotary table cover.

22. Remove the safety clamp and whip handling device which is bolted onto the back of whipstock.

23. Remove the rotary table cover.

24. Lower the whipstock slowly into the well, setting the rotary slips on the DP.

25. Check the orientation of the key in the UBHO sub, make any adjustments necessary, and tighten the setscrews again.

Note: For safety purposes, install a drill pipe wiper to prevent dropping the Allen wrench in the hole.

CAUTION

Run the draw works in low. Pick up and set down the whipstock gently in the slips to prevent damage or premature setting. Make sure the lead tongs have most of the slack out of the snub line to prevent jerking against the back-up tongs.

RUNNING PROCEDURE

Running and Orienting the Whipstock

1. Lower the whipstock assembly slowly into the wellbore and do not pump anything in the

well to prevent premature setting of the whipstock.

Do not alter the orientation of the UBHO sub to the Whipface's face when making the first connection. Do not let the UBHO sub turn or move, or the direction of the milled window could be affected.

2. Refer to dogleg checklist for doglegs greater than 4 degrees. Watch the weight indicator

carefully and record up-weights regularly.

3. Monitor trip-tank for proper fill up.

4. Run the whipstock slowly, like a packer assembly, at a rate of 2 to 3 minutes per stand.

5. Do not turn string.

6. Do not Pump in the Well (unless an open Flow Throgh Valve is Run above the Running

Tools).

7. Fill the drill string every 5 strands.

Proceed slowly and with caution while running the whipstock assembly through the BOPs, wellhead, liner top, and any other restrictive sections to prevent damage or premature setting. The difference between the whipstock OD and the casing ID is minimal, making it similar to a piston, so lower the assembly very slowly in these small bypass areas. DO NOT PUMP IN THE WELL.

8. Run slowly into the hole until approximately 30 feet off the bottom.

9. Slowly move the whipstock assembly up and down from 5 to 20 feet to remove all trapped torque from the drill string.

10. Record up and down free weights.

11. Run survey tools on wireline to the UBHO sub if using a survey.

12. Take survey readings

13. To orient the whipstock, rotate the drill pipe to the right in ¼ turn increments (no more that ½ turn at a time) until the whipstock assembly is oriented in the correct position.

14. Take another survey, making additional corrections as needed and lowering 4 to 5 feet after each increment.

South Azadegan Oilfield Project

Contract No:

AZNS-127 Side Track-2 Program Page 53 of 179

CAUTIONA crooked hole may require several readings and corrections to remove all of thetrapped torque from the drill string. Work slowly and carefully in order to achieve proper orientation.CAUTIONThis Model of Whipstock, because it is hinged, must be set within 30° on either side of the low side to prevent the whipstock’s whipface from falling across the wellbore.

15. Continue taking readings until 3 sequential reading are within a 5° range before assuming the direction is correct.

16. After reaching and verifying the proper direction, call a meeting with the customer, driller, and survey/MWD company representative to review the orientation of the whipstock’s Whipface once more.

17. Continue the procedure if everyone is in agreement.

18. POOH the survey tools and make a mark on the rotary table and the Drill Pipe, make up the Kelly (or Top Drive), DO NOT ALTER THE ORIENTATION WHILE MAKING UP THE KELLY.

19. Lower the whipstock assembly slowly to the setting depth.

20. Start pump and increase pressure until the packer shear pins are sheared and the packer sets in place (at 1200-1400 psi), hold pressure for 10 minutes to confirm the setting).

Note: In case of Using MWD and Flow Through Valve, increase pump rate until the Flow Through Valve shear pins are sheared and the valve closes, then continue pumping until the packer shear pins are sheared and the packer sets in place.

21. Slack off 10-15klbs and over pull 10-15k lbs to prove packer is set.

22. Pick-up 35,000-55,000 lbs (Depend on whipstock size) over pull, continue over pull on the screw as required to initiate the shear. A sharp drop in the pipe occurs when the shear screw shears.

23. Raise the drill string approximately 1 to 2 feet.

24. Set the drill string back down to make sure the shear screw has sheared. Repeat if necessary.

25. Mark the depth on the pipe each time. It should read the same each time.

26. Set the pipe back down with approximately 20,000 lb of pressure to ensure that the Whipface is over against the casing wall.

27. Raise the drill string so that the Rugby Mill is 5 to 10 feet above the top of the whipstock.

28. Lay down the necessary drill pipe to pick up the kelly.

South Azadegan Oilfield Project

Contract No:

AZNS-127 Side Track-2 Program Page 54 of 179

29. Start pump with maximum allowable GPM (According to the standpipe pressure). Engage with Whipface with Reduced RPM (20-30). Monitor pressure drop due to breaking Nozzle plugs.

Note: Do not Mill and work on Nozzle plugs more than One min with low GPM which leads to Mill burning.

30. Displace the Mud in the well (if needed) and check mud properties for proper rheology for steel removal.

31. The milling operation can now begin.

Running Milling Assembly and Opening the Window

This section assumes that the Rugby Mill has been sheared from the whipstock and raised 5 to 10 feet above the whipstock.

NOTE: Install Ditch Magnets

1. Make up the kelly to the drill string.

2. Record string weight up and down.

3. Engage the pumps, slowly increasing to the planned circulation rate, and record pump pressure and rate.

4. Engage the rotary and slowly increase the speed between 20 and 40 RPM.

5. After the rotary has stabilized, slowly increase between 50 and 75 RPM (depending on the mill size).

6. Record the following information:

• Free rotary torque

• Pump pressure

• Pump rate

• Free weight – up and down (string weight with zero weight on mill)

7. While rotating, slowly lower the drill string until the Rugby Mill contacts the whipstock and the casing wall, causing an immediate and substantial increase in rotary torque.

8. Mark the kelly. This is the starting point for the Rugby Mill run.

9. After making the initial mark on the kelly, raise the Mill 3 to 5 feet.

10. While rotating, slowly lower the drill string again to see if the increase in rotary torque is indicated at the same place. Work slowly and carefully; repeat if necessary.

11. After marking the kelly with the correct starting point for the Mill, begin milling, using light weights on the Mill (1,000 to 3,000 lb depending on the size of the mill and grade of the casing). As the window milling process begins, an increase in torque and decrease in weight will be indicated.

12. As the torque increases, increase the rotary speed to the recommended RPM (based on the mill size).

13. Continue milling with a constant rotary torque and weight (1,000 to 3,000 lb) on the mill.

Additional weight may be required if the rate of penetration (ROP) begins to slow.

South Azadegan Oilfield Project

Contract No:

AZNS-127 Side Track-2 Program Page 57 of 179

Use recommended parameters as follows.

Casing Size (in) Weight on Mill (klb) Milling RPM9 ⅝” 2 – 15 60 – 1207” 2 – 12 60 – 1205” 1 – 7 60 – 120

14. Monitor returns for cuttings during milling operations and pump high viscosity sweeps

as needed to remove cuttings from the well. This practice is especially important if the window is being milled in a lateral section.

15. The Window Mill run is completed after milling down the Whipface’s face into the formation AND when the Dress Mill is centered at the bottom of the window.

16. Ream back and forth through the window until no signs of additional torque or drag are indicated.

17. Stop the rotary and slide the Mill assembly through the window several times. If any weight or drag is indicated, start the rotary and ream back and forth through the window until weight or drag is eliminated.

18. Stop the rotary and check for weight or drag again. Repeat this process as necessary.

19. Once the window is complete, stop the rotary, clean the hole of cuttings with high viscosity sweeps, and pull out of the hole without rotating.

20. Closely inspect and gauge all mills for wear using a gauge ring of OD + 1/32"

21. Determine the estimated size of the window.

22. Review the window requirements with the customer to determine if the Elongation Run is required.

Note: The Elongation run is recommended if:

• You have run a bi-Mill Assembly for opening the Window and:

• The customer requests it.

• PDC bit will be used through the window for additional drilling

• Drill collars and stabilizers will be used through the window for additional drilling

• Liner will be installed through the window

• Double bent sub and PDM assembly will be used through the window for additional drilling

• Unusual wear is indicated on the Rugby Mill, resulting in an under-gauge hole

Elongation run

1. Assemble the Elongation run components

• Balance of drill string

• One or more drill collars or heavy weight

• Bit Sub (minimum length, bored for float assembly)

• Crossover sub (double pin, if Bit sub is used)

• Tri-Mill

Note: Be sure to eliminate the one joint of drill pipe above the Bit Sub and replace it with one or more drill collars/heavy weight to provide “stiffness” to the milling assembly.

South Azadegan Oilfield Project

AZNS-127 Side Track-2 Program Page 60 of 179

2. Lower the Elongation run assembly into the hole, stopping 5 to 10 feet above the whipstock.

3. Make up the kelly to the drill string.

4. Engage the pumps and slowly increase to the desired circulation rate.

5. Engage the rotary and slowly increase to between 50 and 75 RPM (depending on the mill size).

6. Record the following information:

• Free rotary torque

• Free weight – up and down (string weight with zero weight on mill)

• Pump pressure

• Pump rate

7. While rotating, slowly lower the drill pipe string and ream back into the window.

8. As the torque increases, increase the rotary speed to the recommended RPM (based on the mill size).

9. Continue milling with a constant rotary torque and weight on the mill.

10. Monitor returns for cuttings during milling operations. Pump high viscosity sweeps as needed to remove cuttings from the well.

11. Continue milling down the Whipface, elongating the milled window at the top with the

Dress Mill.

12. The Elongation run is complete (unless directed otherwise by the customer) when the

Dress Mill is centered at the bottom of the window.

AZNS-127 Side Track-2 Program Page 61 of 179

13. While rotating, ream back and forth through the window until no additional weight or drag is indicated.

South Azadegan Oilfield Project

Note: If using stabilizers for additional drilling through the window, it is recommended to drill enough hole into the formation to accommodate the stabilizers. The additional rathole should allow the stabilizers to be in the formation BEFORE drilling commences. Rotating the stabilizers or drill bits while on the Whipface can damage the Whipface and the

window.

14. Stop the rotary and slide the Mill assembly through the window several times. If any weight or drag is indicated, start the rotary and ream back and forth through the window until weight or drag is eliminated.

15. Circulate the hole clean with one or more high viscosity sweeps to remove all cuttings from the well.

16. When circulation is complete, stop the rotary and pull out of the hole without rotating.

17. Inspect and gauge all mills using a gauge ring of OD + 1/32", to determine wear to the mill and to estimate window/hole size. Review signs of wear with the customer. Repeat Run #3 if the hole appears to be undersized.

18. Lay down the Elongation Run assembly.

Abnormal Conditions

Whipstock stuck

• Try to release the whipstock with 20000klb overpull in 7" hole and 30000klb over pull in 9-5/8" hole.

• Close an annular preventor hydrill and apply 500-1000 psi pressure in annulus to remove casing collapse.

• Apply weight on bit.

• If no success, shear screw and pull out the whipstock out of hole with fishing tool later.

South Azadegan Oilfield Project

Contract No:

AZNS-127 Side Track-2 Program Page 63 of 179

No success in passing the whipstock through liner lab

• Come back to neutral point and turn string 1/4 round in clockwise direction and try to pass through liner lab again.

The packer does not set with designed setting pressure

• Release the pressure and apply the pressure again.

• Pull out of hole to surface and check the tools.

Pressure drop during the milling operation

• Twisting off the string or mill:

• In this case the torque will be constant and progress will be stop.

• Pressure drop due to string washing out:

• In this case the standpipe pressure will decrease gradually.

• Pressure drop due to breaking the nozzle plugs:

• In this case the pressure decreases suddenly and no change in other parameters will happen.

• Pressure drop due to washing out the nozzles:

• In this case the standpipe pressure will decrease gradually.

Note: In all the above items pulling the string out of hole to surface and checking the tools will be necessary.

No progress during milling

• Change the drilling parameters, for example increase or decrease RPM, increase WOB, decrease GPM.

South Azadegan Oilfield Project

Contract No:

AZNS-127 Side Track-2 Program Page 64 of 179

• If you observe no progress in 2 hours, pulling the string out of hole to surface will be necessary.

Observing complete loss during milling

• Don’t continue milling till curing the complete loss.

• If the client insists in continuing the operation, due to working with low GPM, stop the milling operation for 30 minutes after each hour of milling to cool the mill and prevent from thermal cracking.

POH string due to failure of whipstock:

• Do not shock the string while put and pick up slips

• Do not shock the string while wrenching

• Ensure that the rotary table is locked for prevent of rotating string

• Pick up each stand in 5 to 7 minutes

• Disconnect the connections with wrench and air wrench.

• Be careful for 5” and 7” whipstocks , because it will has more swing in larger casing size

Caution: do not use rotary table for disconnect the connections

8.2.1.1 Interval Mud Discussion

The water-based KCl Polymer system provides effective inhibition when drilling reactive shale’s through below mechanism:

Potassium Chloride provides a source of Potassium ions, which are small enough to fit between the clay platelets without distorting the shale lattice. The Potassium ions are adsorbed on the exchangeable caution sites in the shale lattice and this holds the platelets together, which helps to minimize clay and shale hydration, swelling and dispersion.

A low solids, non-dispersed Salt/KCl/CaCO₃ Polymer drilling fluid is selected for drilling this section. This system is used primarily to drill moderately reactive shale’s. It can be used effectively at temperatures up to 275˚ F – 300˚

8.4 Technical Appendix

Loss Control Procedure

Loss of fluid returns will lower the hydrostatic head of the drilling fluid in the wellbore, thereby inducing a kick. The influx fluid will then flow to the surface or into the zone of lower pressure. Lost circulation can occur in naturally occurring fractured, vuggy, cavernous, sub-normally pressured or pressure depleted formations. Induced losses can occur from mechanical fracturing due to pressure surges while breaking circulation. In all cases of lost circulation, attempts should be made to keep the hole full. The hole can be filled with either light drilling fluid or water. A record of the amount of fluid pumped should be made.

The concentration of LCM will vary according to losses. In the event of seepage losses, treat system with a finer grade of LCM at 20 – 30 Kg/m³. In the event of moderate to high rate of well bore loss, prepare pills at different graded concentrations and spot over thief zone. The concentration may vary between 18 to 70 lb/bbl. In order to avoid LCM plugging MWD tools a circulation sub should be installed in the drill string. The MWD engineer is to advise on the size and concentration of LCM that can be pumped through MWD Tools. Ensure that the drilling displace the LCM pill out of the string prior to shutting down the mud pumps.

Important Note: Please note below concentration and recommended materials may be change with same materials on rig site.

In case of having circulation losses:

Losses less than 10 bbls/hr:

- Active system to be loaded with 10 lb/bbl of Fiber Fine.

Losses 10- 40 bbls/hr:

- Active mud to be loaded with 15- 20 lb/bbl of Fiber Medium.

- Sweep the hole frequently with 50 bbls high viscous pill contains;

- 15 lb/bbl Mica Medium - Corse.

- 10 lb/bbl Walnut Shells Medium -Fine.

- 10 lb/bbl Oyster Shell Fine.

Losses 40 – 100 bbl/hr:

- Stop Drilling.

- Pull out string above the loss zone

- Spot 100 bbls pill contains;

- 30 lb/bbl Fiber coarse.

- 30 lb/bbl Walnut Fine.

Losses more than 100 bbls:

- Up to company procedure, may be squeeze 50 bbls of Cement squeeze.

8.4.1.1 Mixing LCM Pill

The amount of LCM that can be added to a mud depends very much on the mud properties. High gels and YP will help keep the material in suspension. Since LCM is generally of low gradient, excess material tends to float on top if too much is added. The following procedure may prove useful for mixing LCM pills and avoiding the problem of flotation.

1. ENSURE the pill has enough viscosity to keep the low gradient material in

suspension before addition of LCM. ADD appropriate viscosifier if required.

2. ADD the material in stages e g. 5, 10, 15, 20 etc. ppb.

3. STOP after desired concentration has been reached, or when it is observed that the

material cannot be held in suspension

4. If a higher LCM content is desired, LEAVE the pill to soak for a period of time

and then TRY ADDING more material.

8.4.1.2 LCM Pill Spotting Procedure

1. After spotting LCM pill, pull the bit above the calculated top of the pill. Wait

30minutes and monitor the annulus.

2. After 30 minutes, attempt to fill the annulus, if not already full. If the hole can be

filled, close the BOP and squeeze 10 bbls of LCM pill into the formation without

exceeding 200 psi.

3. If the hole remains stable, continue to drill ahead.

4. Should the LCM pill fail to reduce the losses or the hole cannot be filled, then mix

and spot another 50 bbls of LCM pill.

5. Attempt to fill the annulus. If successful, close the BOP and squeeze 20 bbls of

LCM pill into the formation without exceeding 200 psi. If a squeeze pressure

develops, hold the pressure for 1 hour before staging the drill string back to bottom.

Notes:

- All time hole must be full, transfer mud to trip tank and asked driller to

fill hole from trip tank.

- All LCM pills must be thoroughly mixed and homogenised before being

pumped.

- When pumping an LCM pill through a bit with nozzle smaller than 18/64,

DO NOT USED LCM Medium and Coarse sizes.

- Remove filter screens from the drill pipe and if necessary from the mud

pump suction lines.

- This is particularly true if the mud density is high, 14 lb/gal or greater.

Fine loss circulation material which does not adsorb a lot of water should

be used in weighted mud.

Guide Line for Fiel Engineers for Shale Inhibition

Shale Hydration takes two forms in water-sensitive shales: surface and osmotic adsorption. Surface hydration occurs when a small volume of water is strongly adsorbed onto the planar surfaces of the clays which causes little softening or swelling, but can lead to excessive stresses if the swelling is confined.

Osmotic swelling occurs when a large volume of weakly held water is attracted to the clay surfaces by electrostatic forces. Osmotic swelling causes softening and significant swelling as the adjacent clay layers hydrate water and expand. Osmostic swelling does not generate excessive stresses, even when confined, and can be substantially reduced if Extremely difficult drilling conditions have led to more systematic approaches to analysing wellbore instabilities.

One such approach that can be used as a guideline for the mud engineer involves three basic steps:

1. Monitor and analyse the fundamental failure mechanism.

2. Determine and understand the factors governing this failure mechanism.

South Azadegan Oilfield Project

Contract No:

AZNS-127 Side Track-2 Program Page 81 of 179

3. Model the problem considering impact of proposed changes.

8.4.1.3 Monitor &amp;amp; Analyze the Failure Mechanism

Monitoring of data and events on the rig is the first step of the process and involves:

• Collection, organization and processing of drilling data. Drilling data such as Rate of Penetration (ROP), Revolutions per Minute (RPM), Weight-on-Bit (WOB), Bottom-Hole Assembly (BHA), torque, over pull Trip In Hole (TIH) and Pull Out Of Hole (POOH), swab and surge, flow rate, mud weight, mud Rehology , etc. should be collected, organized and analyzed on a continual basis and compared to the symptoms of wellbore stability being observed. This will help evaluate performance and establish trends or any deviations and measure the effectiveness of treatments and changes.

• Formation characterization. The standard procedure in drilling operations is to apply the knowledge

gained from previous wells to subsequent wells drilled in similar geologic regions. Wellbore-instability

investigation requires evaluation of shales during the drilling process. Since rig site shale testing is limited

due to equipment and time limitations, most evaluations are performed in a properly equipped laboratory.

Laboratory tests are conducted to evaluate shale swelling, dispersibility, cation exchange capacity, hydration capacity, colloidal content, capillary suction time, shale hardness tests and mud compatibility properties.

A number of methods have been used to perform rig site tests. These include tests as simple as the methylene blue test (CEC) measurement of shale; shale hardness measurements; hot-rolled dispersion testing with various mud formulations and additives; and sophisticated analytical measurements of various clay properties. It is particularly important to try and determine the failure mechanism: swelling and softening or brittle spalling. Information from these tests, current shaker observations and mud logger

South Azadegan Oilfield Project

Contract No:

AZNS-127 Side Track-2 Program Page 82 of 179

data are used to evaluate drilling fluid performance, adjust mechanical drilling parameters and making casing design decisions. The primary options to counter shale problems at the rig site are:

 Change the drilling fluid density.

 Change to an oil- or synthetic-base system.

 Change to a more inhibited water-base mud.

 Reduce fluid loss to very low levels and increase filtrate viscosity.

 Utilize pore-plugging additives, emulsified insoluble materials or plastering

agents.

 Adjust mechanical drilling parameters.

 Evaluation and analysis of instability symptoms.

Instability warning signs such as the presence of excessive cavings on the shakers for a given ROP, fill on connections, tripping difficulties, torque, stuck pipe, etc. indicate that something is wrong down hole. The magnitude or volume of failed rock should be estimated and recorded with the other drilling parameters. The number and location of specific incidents should be recorded, such as pipe

sticking, fill or packing-off, reaming and re-drilling. All of this information can then be organized and correlated with time and depth to detect the location and quantify the severity of critical sections in the well.

8.4.1.4 Determine &amp;amp; Understand Failure Mechanism

All of the monitored and plotted parameters are then evaluated to identify the most probable mechanism causing the instability. The most useful symptoms used to indicate the mechanism responsible for wellbore instability are:

 Cavings analysis.

 Tripping difficulties.

 Drilling conditions.

 Mud system analysis.

AZNS-127 Side Track-2 Program Page 83 of 179

 In-situ conditions.

These symptoms should be evaluated based on an interdisciplinary knowledge of the causes of wellbore instability to determine the most likely failure mechanism.

8.4.1.5 Model &amp;amp; Considering Proposed Changes

Once the monitoring and determination steps have produced parameters, organize and analyze this data to obtain qualitative solutions and evaluate proposed changes. One good way to do this is through the use of a decision tree or flowchart approach to evaluate the possible failure mechanism and to identify the most promising remedies. After arriving at a proposed solution, a corrective measure should be applied and

the results used as feedback into the method and decision tree method.

A decision tree or flowchart, such as shown in Figure 9 for evaluating the cause of excessive cavings, provides a logical path for identification of the mechanism and a qualitative solution. Maintaining hole stability while drilling shale sections can be particularly troublesome. Simple solutions do not always exist, but good drilling practices combined with good mud practices are most often successful. Analysis of the mechanical stress/strain relationships has helped to develop the proper density requirements for hole stability.

8.5 Directional Drilling

Drilling Fluid Properties &amp;amp; Selection

It is common knowledge among drilling engineers and drillers that borehole problems can be considerably more severe in a directional hole than in a vertical well. The problems are magnified as the hole angle and horizontal displacement increases. Although most of these reactions are mechanical in nature, much can be done to alleviate them by proper selection and maintenance of the drilling fluid. For example, if a waterbase fluid is being used, lubricants can be added to lower the coefficient of friction between the drill string and borehole or casing. Inhibiting salts can be added to reduce the interaction of the drilling fluid with the exposed formations, thereby improving borehole stability.

There are a number of drilling factors influenced by the drilling fluid, but the following are of primary concern in drilling a horizontal well.

 Borehole instability

 Hole cleaning

 Torque and drag

 Formation damage

 Barite sag

 Hydraulics

Borehole Instability

Borehole instability is one of the more costly, but relatively common problem associated with drilling oil and gas wells. Not only can it impede drilling, it can result in loss of the hole. The term normally conjures thoughts of borehole collapse with accompanying stuck pipe. This is one of the more critical reactions of borehole instability, but it can manifest itself in more subtle ways such as hole-fill, bridges, hole enlargement, or hole size reduction.

These reactions lead to other associated problems including increased torque and drag, logging difficulties, poor cement jobs, and increased drilling days, all of which add significantly to the drilling cost. It should be pointed out that the discussions to follow

do not cover hole enlargement problems from weakly consolidated sands, or rubble zones that erode from the hydraulic action of the drilling fluid.

AZNS-127 Side Track-2 Program Page 86 of 179

Stabilization

The swelling activity is controlled by adjusting the electrolyte content of the fluid to minimize expansion of the clays. Lime and gypsum-treated fluids have long been used for this purpose, but basically do not satisfy the inhibition needs of the more troublesome shales. The potassium ion is an effective swelling inhibitor and is used extensively for this purpose through the addition of potassium salts. The concentration of potassium utilized ranges from several hundred mg/L to over 60,000 mg/L. The most cost-effective potassium concentration, however, appears to be in the 3000 to 7000 mg/L range. In marine environments, seawater or seawater with additional sodium chloride, are good alternates to potassium. The tendency for the shale to disperse or subdivide into discrete particles appears to be best controlled by the addition of an adsorptive, high molecular weight water-soluble polymer.

One of the more effective polymers for this purpose is the partially hydrolyzed poly acrylamide with molecular weight in excess of 15 million. These anionic polymers adsorb on to the surface of the cuttings and borehole wall to act as a binder or elastic coating to retard dispersion. Another approach to stabilizing the hard brittle shales that contain natural or induced micro fractures is the use of water-dispersible asphalt or asphaltines. The addition of these type materials appear to plug the micro-fractures, or perhaps even surface pore throats to retard further fluid invasion. This action has proven very effective in certain shales and can be applied in most water base fluids.

Hole Cleaning

Cleaning cuttings from a vertical hole has been covered extensively by numerous investigators. Hole cleaning in a vertical hole is essentially a matter of overcoming the slip velocity of the cuttings with sufficient annular velocity and carrying capacity of the drilling fluid. Although any velocity greater than the settling velocity of the largest cutting will theoretically lift all the cuttings to surface eventually, too low an annular velocity will lead to an undesirable high concentration of cuttings in the annulus. Experience has shown that cuttings concentrations more than 5% by volume cause tight hole or stuck pipe when circulation is stopped.

Cuttings Bed Formation

Radial slip velocity increases with increasing angle of inclination, forcing more cuttings to the low side of the annulus, which eventually results in the formation of a cuttings bed. reported that bed formation was dramatic in the 40° to 50° angle with the bed sliding downward against the flow, resulting in a very high cuttings concentration.

The fact that a cutting bed forms is a serious problem, but the instability of the bed in this critical angle of the well makes the problem even more severe. High torque and drag resulting from the high cutting concentration at the lower part of the angle can obviously result in stuck pipe or loss of circulation.

Hole Cleaning Sweeps

In static drill string concluded that high-density sweeps were more effective than highdensity high-viscosity sweeps based on field measurements. The higher viscosity of the latter caused flow diversion to the high side of the wellbore. Not surprisingly, highviscosity sweeps also performed poorly. Also concluded that the best hole cleaning sweeps were high-density low viscosity sweeps, with a density 3 – 4 ppg higher than that of the drilling fluid. the following procedure is recommended:

 Calculate sweep height in the vertical part of the annulus, and added hydrostatic

head in the annulus.

 Rotate at 80+ rpm while pumping the sweep, 180+ rpm is preferred. It is not

recommended to pump a weighted sweep while sliding.

 Keep pumping until the sweep is out of the hole. If pumping stops while the

sweep is in the deviated hole, it falls out of the “jet stream” and re-deposits

captured fines.

 Avoid increasing the viscosity of the weighted sweep.

 Plan to run 3 – 4 sweeps to achieve desired results when hole cleaning problems

are indicated. One sweep will probably not be sufficient to remedy an existing

situation.

 Avoid checking for flow or closing the annulus with the weighted sweep in the

drill pipe.

 If desired for preventative maintenance: 1) schedule sweeps every 6 – 8 hours or

500 – 1000 feet (whichever comes first, unless the hole dictates greater

frequency); barite/silt build- ups are dependent on time and footage: and 2) pump

a sweep while circulating bottom up before tripping, and another once back on

bottom.

concluded that high-density sweeps were more effective than high-viscosity sweeps.

They strongly advocated the use of sweep reports, which should be standard practice in any drilling fluids operation.

South Azadegan Oilfield Project

Contract No:

AZNS-127 Side Track-2 Program Page 89 of 179

Short Tripping

Another technique that has proven helpful in controlling problems created by the cuttings bed in the high-angle portion of the well is to make periodic short trips. Tripping the bit through the bed not only assures that the bottom hole assembly and bit can be pulled through it, but the action should agitate the bed to the point that a portion will slide down the hole and subsequently be picked up when circulation is commenced. The time intervals for these short trips will be determined by the torque and drag conditions that exist in any particular well. Lacking specific well history, a general rule of thumb is to short trip at least once for every 500 feet of new hole.

Drill String Rotation

The industry is in total agreement that drill string rotation improves hole cleaning, especially in hole sizes less than 17 ½”. The general opinion in the industry is that the optimum drill string rotation rate is approximately 120 rpm. It is believed that the drill string rotation improves hole cleaning by mechanically disturbing the cuttings bed on the low side of the hole. There could also be effects due to skewing the velocity profile in the wellbore and the creation of Taylor Vortices. Encouraged the use of rotary steerable systems.

Turbulance

Bottom hole assembly design becomes important because the flow restrictions of some of the components, such as the measurement-while-drilling tools or positive displacement motors, may not allow sufficient flow to reach turbulence in the annulus. Turbulence can, of course, be induced at some constant flow rate by decreasing the annular area. This may be more difficult to accomplish in a horizontal well because of limitations on the design of drill strings and tool assemblies. An increase in the effective viscosity of the drilling fluid will decrease the Reynolds Number, and thus increase the flow rate required to obtain turbulent flow. Thus, a lower effective viscosity fluid may be desirable in the horizontal well, but attention must also be given to cleaning the larger diameter portion of the upper hole or possible washed-out sections where it is impractical to maintain turbulent flow.

It is interesting to point out a basic fact between static fluid pressure and dynamic fluid pressure. Static fluid pressure is a function of true vertical depth, while dynamic fluid pressure, or ECD, is a function of measured depth. Thus, the ECD will continue to increase, albeit slowly, even after the hole becomes essentially horizontal. The fracture pressure could be reached if the hole was extended to sufficient depth and the fluid density is close to the fracture gradient.

South Azadegan Oilfield Project

Contract No:

AZNS-127 Side Track-2 Program Page 90 of 179

Hole Cleaning Guideline

The single most important factor related to hole cleaning in deviated wells is flow rate. During directional drilling operations drilled cuttings will settle on the low side of the hole and form a stationary bed if insufficient annular fluid velocity is used. The critical flow rate required to prevent cuttings bed formation must be determined .

Typically few hole cleaning problems exist in vertical or horizontal sections. Most problems

associated with hole cleaning are seen on deviated wells and occur in the 40 – 60 degree section where gravity effects can cause cuttings beds to slump down the hole.Typical flow rates to aim for in ERD wells:

Hole Size Typical Flow Rates17 ½” 800 gpm minimum. Some rigs achieve 850 – 1000 gpm.12 ¼”Aim for 800 gpm (although 800 – 1000 gpm is typically achieved). If 800 gpm is not achievable, ensure tripping procedures are in place for poorly cleaned hole.8 ½” Aim for 400 gpm.

When correctly designed, both laminar and turbulent flow regimes will effectively clean a deviated well. In general increasing the viscosity of a fluid in laminar flow will improve hole cleaning as will a reduction of the viscosity of a fluid in turbulent flow. It is important that one or other regime is selected and that the transition zone between the two is avoided.

Generally viscous fluids in laminar flow are preferred because:

 It is possible to achieve higher cleaning capacity.

 Viscous fluids give better transport in the near-vertical sections.

 Viscous fluids have better suspension characteristics when circulation is stopped.

 It is difficult to achieve “turbulent flow” except in small hole sizes.

South Azadegan Oilfield Project

AZNS-127 Side Track-2 Program Page 91 of 179

Experience has shown that good drilling fluid rheological properties are extremely important to hole cleaning when drilling a high angle well. Studies show that the effects of drilling fluid

rheological properties and annular flow regime are mutually dependent. In the laminar flow regime, increasing fluid viscosity will improve hole cleaning and this is particularly effective if the Yield Stress is high. In the turbulent regime, however, reducing fluid viscosity will help removing cuttings. Therefore the drilling fluid rheological properties should be designed to avoid the transitional flow regime. For hole sizes above 8 ½”, the annular flow is laminar under most circumstances. Therefore it is necessary to specify a minimum Yield Stress. The optimum level required is best established based on field data and experience.

A higher ROP requires a higher flow rate to clean the hole. It is good practice to drill the hole with a steady ROP and select the required flow rate for hole cleaning accordingly. Before making a connection, the hole should be circulated at the normal flow rate to clear the cuttings from around the BHA. Depending upon the hole angle and length of BHA, a circulation time of 5 to 10 minutes is often required.

Before tripping out, the hole should be circulated at the normal flow rate until the shakers are clean, and the drill pipe be rotated at maximum speed/reciprocated in the meantime. This may require up to 3 bottoms-ups, depending on the hole angle and hole size. Below are listed the recommended number of bottoms-up prior to tripping.

Hole Angle, deg 8 ½” 12 ¼” 17 ½”0 – 10 1.3 1.3 1.510 – 30 1.4 1.4 1.730 – 60 1.6 1.8 2.560+ 1.7 2.0 3.0

Overall friction can become so great in an extended-reach well or horizontal section that the drill string can only be rotated with great difficulty. Needless to say, this condition is conducive to stuck pipe. Obviously, this coefficient of friction will be significantly affected by the lubricating properties of the drilling fluid.
