any of the causes of torque and drag are mechanical, while others are related to hole geometry. Several, however, can be directly attributed to the drilling fluid. Since wall contact with the drill string will be extremely high in a horizontal hole, it is imperative that the lubricating characteristics of the fluid be considered.

Formation Damage

The obvious reason for drilling a horizontal well is to expose more of the producing zone to the wellbore for increased production. Thus, the importance of preventing formation damage during drilling and completion of the horizontal well is just as important as it is in its vertical counterpart.

In fact, it may be more important since the increased cost of drilling the horizontal well must show additional production for its justification. A 50% damage or permeability loss in a potential 500 bbl/day horizontal well represents a considerably greater loss in production than a 50% damage in a 100 bbl/day vertical hole through the same reservoir.

Sandstone production is by far the most susceptible reservoir rock to damage or permeability loss during drilling and completion operations. Though formation damage may be caused by poor drilling and completion practices, one of the primary causes is due to exposure to the drilling and completion fluid.

This loss, attributable to the fluid, can be caused by one or more of the following occurrences:

 Particle transport from the drilling fluid into the production zone, subsequently

plugging pore throats.

 Fluid filtrate reacting with expandable clays in the rock to decrease pore throat

diameters.

 Particle movement within the permeable rock due to dispersion of clays and other

minerals from quartz surfaces.

 Wettability changes of the formation from exposure to the drilling fluid filtrate.

 Interaction of fluid filtrate with formation fluids to form water - insoluble

precipitants.

The effect of these actions on the permeability of sandstones has been the subject of a considerable investigation. In almost all cases, some damage is caused by the drilling and completion fluid. The primary objective is to limit this damage as much as possible.

South Azadegan Oilfield Project

Contract No:

AZNS-127 Side Track-2 Program Page 93 of 179

Consequently, selection of the drilling and completion fluid becomes an extremely important function in drilling the horizontal well.

Recommended Fluid Parameters

 Velocity – One of the major obstacles to overcome in horizontal and ERD

drilling is hole cleaning. In vertical holes, cuttings have room to settle without

causing problems. In horizontal wells, cuttings only have to settle 4+ inches to

form a cuttings bed. Research and practical experience has shown that cuttings

bed formation is analogous to sand dunes on an ocean beach. The bed moves in

a wave fashion up the hole. If sufficient annular velocity is not present, the bed

thickens until it reaches equilibrium, which usually occurs when turbulent flow

conditions exist. With water, turbulent flow is easily obtained since viscosity is

in the denominator of the turbulent flow equation, and water has a viscosity of 1.

Fluids other than water require more pump output to approach turbulent flow

conditions. Practical experience in other industries has proven that materials can

be transported in water slurries if the fluid velocity is between 3 and 7 ft/sec.

 Rheological Properties – Ideally one would want a true thixotropic fluid to drill

horizontally. In effect, two different conditions exist simultaneously. One occurs

in the vertical portion of the hole where larger diameter casing may be set, or

wash-outs in the open hole occur. In that case, a fluid having a high Yield Stress,

or if the fluid is visco-elastic, the initial gel strength needs to be elevated. The

opposite is needed in the horizontal section from a hole-cleaning point of view.

Here one wants water for the reasons pointed out earlier. Compromises are the

result. If casing is set into the zone of interest, or if formations up-hole are not a

problem, then water may be possibly combined with occasional sweeps.

 Surface Apparatus – Special attention must be placed on the solids removal

equipment at the surface. Solids removal efficiency must be continually

monitored so that unwanted particulate material is not retained in the fluid system

that may negatively affect fluid weight or filter cake quality, resulting in lost

circulation or increased torque and drag. The cost of problems that may occur

due to not doing this correctly may far outweigh the cost of equipment needed.

8.6 Hydrogen Sulphide Gas in Drilling Fluid

Description of Hydrogen Sulphide Gas

Hydrogen sulphide is a colourless gas, with an offensive odour and a sweetish taste. It is soluble in water, alcohol, oils, and many other solvents. It has a specific gravity of 1.1895

South Azadegan Oilfield Project

Contract No:

AZNS-127 Side Track-2 Program Page 94 of 179

with reference to air. It is considered a weak acid, it is toxic to humans and corrosive to metals. Hydrogen sulphide can be dangerous to personnel on the surface as it is extremely toxic to human and even animal life, and is extremely corrosive to most metals as it can cause cracking of drill pipe and tubular goods, and destruction of testing tools and wire lines. When hydrogen sulphide enters the borehole during drilling, completion, or testing for hydrocarbons, it creates several very detrimental problems. These problems are encountered regardless of the source of the hydrogen sulphide. Hydrogen sulphide has created unsolved problems in the oil field.

Origin of Hydroge Sulphide

During oil and gas operations, hydrogen sulphide can be found as a component of formation gases, dissolved in water, hydrocarbons, or even liquid sulphur. Thermal degradation of organic materials and sulphate reducing bacteria (SRB) can create hydrogen sulphide along with other gases.

Problem Cused by Hydroge Sulphide Gas

8.6.1.1 Health &amp;amp; Safety of the Personnel

One of the main problems hydrogen sulphide causes is in respect to the health and safety and safety of the personnel. A maximum of eight hours exposure to concentrations greater than 100 ppm H2S will cause hemorrhage and death. Concentrations above 600 ppm can be fatal in three to five minutes. Highly stressed, high strength steel can fail in a matter of minutes in the presence of 50 ppm H2S. At high pressure, as little as 0.1 ppm H2S can greatly reduce the time to failure of highly stressed, high strength steel. Relying solely on its odour is not a good idea because at concentrations above 100 ppm it deadens a person’s sense of smell within a few minutes. The pure gas is heavier than air and can collect in low areas such as pit rooms and accommodation. below Table shows the potential hazards hydrogen sulphide can cause to the personnel from short-term exposures. There are many historical cases to document the ill effects of hydrogen sulphide exposure.

The documented cases reported in Table 2 indicate that hydrogen sulphide is very toxic and it takes only a matter of minutes to affect unprotected workers.

8.6.1.2 Effects of Hydrogen Sulphide on Metal

Hydrogen sulphide mainly cause corrosion problems to drill strings, transport pipes, storage tanks etc. Hydrogen sulphide causes sulphide stress cracking, hydrogen embrittlement and pitting corrosion in oil and gas operations. The corrosion of iron in the presence of hydrogen sulphide and water is dependent upon the dissociation of the hydrogen-sulphide molecule. Iron is oxidized to the ferrous form at the anode and hydrogen sulphide under- goes a two-step dissociation at the cathode. Tung et al22propose the following equilibrium reactions below.

At the anode:

Fe Fe2+ + 2eAnd at the cathode hydrogen is produced and either enters the steel or forms hydrogen gas and bubbles off:

If H2S is present:

2H+ + 2e- H° + H°

If H2S is not present:

Hydrogen enters the steel first by adsorption onto the water to steel interface and then by being absorbed into the steel as hydrogen. The amount of hydrogen entry depends on the corrosion rate of the steel surface and the concentration of anions such as HS- that reduce the tendency to produce hydrogen gas (as shown in second equation above) and promotes the hydrogen (Ho) to enter the steel. pH also has an influence on amount of corrosion damage. Basically, the term “sulphides” used in oil and gas operations includes all three water-soluble species, H2S, HS- and S2-, which coexist in a sulphide-water system. Shown in the ionization chart for hydrogen sulphide in figure 1, it can be observed that molecular H2S predominates in the acidic range, where the pH is below 7. In the range of 7 to 12, monovalent HS- predominates and above pH 12, divalent S2- predominates.

The illustration in figure 1 indicates that the most important practice is that when H2S enters in alkaline mud, it reacts to form an alkaline sulphide, most often sodium sulphide.17 While elevated pH is a good way to keep H2S from causing problems under certain conditions, it does not remove it from the fluid and any drop in pH can create a significant hazard. This then brought about the advent of sulphide scavengers in the history of oil and gas operations. The only safe method for the total removal of hydrogen sulphide or soluble sulphides is with a sulphide scavenger.

8.6.1.1 Effects of Hydrogen Sulphide on Drilling Fluids

The first positive identification of soluble sulphide in the drilling fluids must be taken as a possible indication of H2S entering the fluid from some source. In the simplest case an increase in mud weight may be sufficient to control minor influxes. If levels persist chemical treatment will be required. This can take two forms; neutralization and scavenging. The two terms must not be confused. Neutralization of H2S in drilling fluid by caustic soda or lime is a common field approach. This alkalinity maintenance method has proved successful when small amounts of H2S enter the drilling fluid, for example, from drilling up pore spaces containing the gas.

This is not a suitable approach to the control on influxes of Hydrogen Sulphide. The alkalinity neutralization of H2S is instantly reversible by reduction in pH. Should the pH of the fluid decrease due to further influxes of H2S, Co2 or brine flows the sulphids may come out of solution as hydrogen sulphide gas. To ensure that such influxes are handled safely, it is essential to employ a sulphide scavenger. This term refers to any additive which is capable of reacting with one or more of the sulphide species and as a result, converting them to a more inert form. To be truly effective an irreversible and complete reaction must occur. As a mutual equilibrium exist between the three sulphide species in

solution (H2S, HS‐ and S2‐) irreversible and complete removal of one serves to removal all three.

To remove the problem it is necessary to precipitate the sulphide as an insoluble inorganic sulphide. Zinc or iron compounds are usually chosen because of the relative inertness of the sulphids formed. Zinc source (Zinc oxide or carbonate) has in the past been the preferred treatment. However, continuous treatment with Zinc carbonate will produce significant undesirable carbonate concentration (Carbonate contamination) which can adversely effect on drilling fluid rehology and fluid loss. As a precaution against Hydrogen Sulphide influxes into the drilling fluid system should be pre‐ treated with Zinc Source. Zinc oxide can be used as an alternative, provided that the possible environmental payloads associated with its use are appreciated. pH and alkalinity tests (Pf/Mf) are a good first indicator of Hydrogen Sulphide influx. However, the use of scavenger is used up. It can be seen from this that while a scavenger increase safety levels, it also makes detection of small Hydrogen Sulphide influxes difficult by conventional methods. Measurement of the concentration of scavenger in the mud system is possible but the analysis method is not safe for use on the rig.

The most effective environmentally acceptable scavengers for Hydrogen Sulphide in water base muds are Zinc sources like Zinc Carbonate or Oxide, primarily because of their solubility which leads to very fast reaction rates compared to other scavengers.

Zinc Sources clearly reacts very much faster than the other scavengers. This is due to the fact that the iron in solution ensures a fast reaction with the sulphides and the chemistry in this case produces elemental sulphur as the reaction product. Elemental sulphur is completely insoluble in water. The iron is reduced from Fe+3 to Fe+2 in the process and some of this will be regenerated to produce Fe+3 when the mud comes in to contact with the air. Any regeneration of Fe+3 will aid in reducing product consumption without affecting is scavenging properties.

8.6.1.1 Testing, Reporting, Treatment of Hydrogen Sulphide

The active mud system must be regularly analyzed and monitored for the presence of active soluble Sulphide with the Garrett Gas train. This test must be carried out at the same time as each complete mud check, i.e.: three times per day while drilling.

Alkalinity checks should be carried out intermittently in between these full checks and any significant reduction in the pH and Mf/Pf should be followed up by testing for the presence of active soluble sulphides with the Garrett Gas Train.

For routine checks lead acetate paper can be used to give a qualitative check. Should this test be positive then it must be followed by a qualitative analysis with a Dragger tube.

The following actions must be taken after the initial positive test result:

1. Inform the Drilling Supervisor

2. Start adding H2S Scavenger to the active mud system. Active soluble sulphides

can be analysed and monitored because of their characteristic of readily

regenerating hydrogen Sulphide gas in reaction with mild acid. By adding citric

acid to whole mud sample in a Garrett gas train detection of Hydrogen Sulphide

on lead acetate paper indicates the presence of active Sulphides in the mud. When

this qualitative test proves positive a dragger tube should be used to give

qualitative results.

However it must be remembered that pre‐treating the mud with MILGARD Fe means that no Sulphides will be delectable until all the scavenger has reacted, i.e.: it is impossible to detect small influxes of Hydrogen Sulphide in a system pre‐ treating with MILGARD Fe .

8.6.1.1 Contingency Stock to be Kept on Hand on the Rig

The following Contingency stock of treatment chemicals must be kept on hand on the rig over and above the normal mud maintenance material requirements.

Lime 200 Sxs 25 kg

C. Selection of PR (Performance Requirement)

According to API Specification 6A 19th edition, performance requirements are specific and unique to the product in the as-shipped condition. All products shall be designed to perform according to the requirements of API 6A clauses 4 and clauses 10 while in the pressure and temperature ranges and corrosion environment. Other requirements include load capability, cycles, and operating force or torque. There are two performance requirement levels: PR1 and PR2. Valves operating as safety valves shall be of the PR2 performance level and meet the requirements of Annex I in API 6A For SA wells, the guideline for PR selection is that all parts not contacting well fluids in normal production period are PR1, all parts contacting well fluids are PR2 as follow, Casing head housing and casing head spool assembly - PR1. Tubing head spool, tubing hanger and X-mas tree - PR2.

11.3 Expected Challenges

8 – 1/2” Hole Section from 3055m to 3940m

11.3.1.1 Challenges

 Hole instability issues

 Wellbore losses.

 Shale

 Tight hole and well instability

11.3.1.2 Recommendation

 It is mandatory to monitor closely the rheological properties in order to ensure

adequate hole cleaning, run Hydraulic calculation to ensure that mud carrying

capacity is enough to meet this critical goal.

 Mud can be treated with additional shale inhibitor if deemed necessary to control

shale reactivity and washouts.

 Optimize the procedure to fight the losses (see the guide at the end of this mud

program) and be ready with adequate LCM material to mix LCM pill as quick as

possible.

 The previouse mud in hole must be dump, due to have enoght surface volume,

keep 300 bbl heavy mud in mud pits as kill mud. The concentration of KCl in the

system is insufficient; shale cuttings will be soft and mushy. If the concentration

of KCl is sufficient, they will retain their integrity. As drilling commences the

potassium ion becomes depleted and must be replenished. The rate of depletion

provides an indication of how reactive the shales are. While drilling gumbo, the

appearance of soft mushy cuttings at surface is a good indication that the

potassium concentration should be increased. Other indicators include a drilled

solids increase, a CEC increase and the occurrence of tight hole or mud rings.

 Since this system is very solids-sensitive, it is best to mix the system from scratch

instead of converting an existing drilling fluid (containing drill solids) to a

potassium chloride system.

 This system is very sensitive to solids and hardness contamination so the first

step in mixing this system is to treat the hardness.

 Due to necessary of directional drilling, it is recommended to pump (at the first

20 bbl Low Vis pill follow by 20 bbl Hi Vis Pill should be pumped every stand)

for clean the hole. For better understanding of hole cleaning procedure based on

hole angels please refer to technical appendix.

South Azadegan Oilfield Project

Contract No:

AZNS-127 Side Track-2 Program Page 124of 179

 Due to face with torque and drag, it is recommended to mix water base mud

lubricant 1 – 3% vol reduce torque and drag while drilling horizontal or vertical.

 In the directional drilling section, it is recommended to use Glass beads 2 – 3 ppb

as due to have torque and drag.

 The mud weight in this interval is critical for successful drilling, hole condition

will dictate the density. Mud weight will be increased by adding CaCO3 F.

11.3.1.3 Interval Description

The 8 1/2“section will be drilled from KOP to an estimated section TD KCl/Caco3 Polymer mud system necessitating a minimum requirement of 80pcf to 85pcf based on nearby well data.

In case of having problem with Marl and Shale layer 3 - 5wt. % of KCl, should be added to system to minimize associated problem.

It is necessary to adjust mud weight and mud properties as hole condition dictate. Some tight hole, well flow and low ROP maybe experienced in this hole section. The drilling fluid engineer will advise the drilling supervisor of any extended circulation or sweep requirement. It uses clarified viscosifier to provide viscosity and carrying capacity and starch to reduce mud filtrate.

In the directional and horizontal section required amount of Lubricant such as Bit Lube and Glass beds will be added to active system to minimize torque and drag.

High Performance Filter Unit

Filtration plays an important role in the natural treatment of waste water as it percolates through the soil. It is also a major part of most water treatment. Groundwater that has been softened, or treated through iron and manganese oxidation, requires filtration to remove floc created by coagulation or oxidation processes. Since surface water is subject to run-off and does not undergo natural filtration.

it must be filtered to remove particles and impurities. Filtration can be compared to a sieve or micro- strainer that traps suspended material between the grains of filter media. However, since most suspended particles can easily pass through the spaces between grains of the filter media, straining is the least important process in filtration. Filtration primarily depends on a combination of complex physical and chemical mechanisms, the most important being adsorption. Adsorption is the process of particles sticking onto the surface of the individual filter grains or onto the previously deposited materials. Forces that attract and hold particles to the grains are the same as those that work in coagulation and flocculation. In fact, coagulation and flocculation may occur in the filter bed, especially if coagulation and flocculation before filtration was not properly controlled. Incomplete coagulation can cause serious problems in filter operation.

12.8 Well Control

1. Installation Requirements of BOP Stack and Control System:

 The distance between BOP control lines and relief lines shall be not less than

1m. Steel Gap Bridge should be placed in such a way to protect lines from

damage by vehicle crossing. Sundries shall not be packed on the control line

shield, on which welding operations are forbidden.

 The air supply shall be separated from that of driller’s console and directly

connected to the main air supply system, and shall be equipped with liquid/gas

separators. Excessive bending and pinching on air hoses are forbidden.

 Electric power to BOP control system shall be directly from the main switch of

the power board, and controlled by independent switches.

 Accumulators shall be in good condition, charged at its rated value, and ready

for work at any time.

2. Installation Requirements of Choke Lines and Kill Lines, and Relief Lines:

a) Beside the drilling spool, one manual and one HCR gate valves on the side of

chock manifold and two manual gate valves on the side of kill manifold shall

be equipped, and the manual gate valve close to the spool shall be always open.

b) The high-pressure co-flex hose shall be installed as straight as possible and

fixed by anchor after installation.

c) Relief lines (burning line and bleed line):

 No field welding is permitted on relief lines and the connecting style of relief

lines must be flanged.

 The arrangement of relief lines shall take wind directions, dwellings, roads, oil

tank areas, power lines and other facilities into consideration.

 While the two lines go in the same trend, the distance between the lines shall

be at least 0.3m, and the two lines shall be fixed independently.

 The outlets of bleed line connecting with choke manifold shall be in a safe area

which is at least 300m. The bleed line on the kill manifold side connecting with

drilling spool shall be prepared and connected when necessary (about 70m from

the wellhead).

 At every 10m~15m, turning points, and outlets, the lines shall be supported and

fixed by cement foundations with anchor bolts or ground anchors. Hanging

South Azadegan Oilfield Project

Contract No:

AZNS-127 Side Track-2 Program Page 156of 179

portions shall be supported firmly. If crossing the stumbling blocks such as

brooks or ponds is needed, metal bridging supports are necessary.

 Pre-buried anchor bolts for cement foundations shall not be less than 20mm or

3/4" in diameter, and greater than 0.5m in length.

3. Pressure test value and requirements:

a) A pressure test shall be conducted successfully where there is no pressure

decline in 5 minutes for a low-pressure test and a minimum of 10 minutes for a

high-pressure test.

b) Prior to each high-pressure test, a low-pressure test with 200-300 psi shall be

carried out to verify sealing capability at the circumstance of low pressure and

avoid washing out sealing elements.

c) High pressure test should be to the rated working pressure of ram preventers or

the rated working pressure of the wellhead, whichever is the lowest, or to the

rating required in DRILLING ROGRAM. Variable bore rams should be

initially pressure tested on the largest and smallest OD pipe sizes that may be

used during the OPERATION. Annular preventers, with a joint of drill pipe

installed, should be tested to 70% of their working pressure. The high test for

Kelly cocks, kill lines and choke lines should be to their rated working

pressures, each part in the choke manifold is tested respectively to its rated

working pressures, the relief lines be pressure tested to no less than 1,450psi

(10Mpa).

d) When casing cup tester is used, the above test pressure should not exceed 80%

of the internal yield pressure (burst pressure) of the exposed casing.

e) The control system of BOP shall be pressure tested to 3,000psi (21Mpa) for its

reliability before putting into use.

f) Except that the BOP control system is tested with hydraulic oil, other well

control equipment shall be pressure tested by clear water.

g) Testing tools

 All required sizes of the plug type testers, and cup type testers should be

available for pressure testing purpose.

 When the cup type tester(s) is used for pressure test, the connection of the cup

testers has to be checked, to ensure it will stand the load during the high

pressures test. For surface casing, the cup tester is to be set in middle of the first

casing joint in the top, so the first casing connection (between wellhead and

South Azadegan Oilfield Project

Contract No:

AZNS-127 Side Track-2 Program Page 157of 179

casing head housing) below the well head is to be tested too while testing BOP

and wellhead.

4. Pressure test frequency:

All ram type preventers, annular BOP, valves, choke and kill lines, choke manifold, Kelly valves and safety valves should be pressure tested at the following frequencies:

 Prior to installation where possible.

 After installation of wellhead and BOP assembly and prior to drilling.

 After the disconnection or repair of any pressure containment seal in the BOP

stack, choke line, or choke manifold, but limited to the affected component.

 Prior to drilling into a confirmed or suspected high-pressure zone.

 At any time requested by the COMPANY REPRESENTATIVE.

 In any case, every one month or during the first trip after the one-month interval

with a maximum interval of 45 days. This frequency is not required for shear

rams. As a minimum, the shear rams are to be tested prior to resume drilling

operation after 9-5/8” casing string has been set and adequate WOC.

5. Work Requirement of Well Control Equipment:

 With shut-in casing pressure lower than 1000psi, while snubbing with annular

preventer, drill tools shall have 18-deg shoulder tool joints, and the snubbing

velocity shall not be greater than 0.2m/s.

 After shut off the annular preventer or ram preventer, with the shut-in casing

pressure not greater than 2000psi, drill tools are allowed to pull up and down

with the velocity less than 0.2m/s, however, rotating or tool joint passing

through are forbidden.

 While drilling through pay zone and thereafter, BOP function (close-open) test

for the BOPs shall be performed regularly.

 Kill manifolds shall not be used for drilling fluid fill-in.

 The maximum allowed shut-in casing pressure shall be remarkably indicated

on choke manifolds.

 All gate valves of well control manifolds shall be tagged with serial numbers,

and be indicated with on/Off.

South Azadegan Oilfield Project

Contract No:

AZNS-127 Side Track-2 Program Page 158of 179

 In case shear rams were used, after shearing the drill pipe with shear rams,

retrieve the upper sheared drill pipe, lower a drill pipe joint with TIW valve

installed into the hole and close pipe rams on it to prevent the possibility of

shear ram’s failure.

6. Management of Well Control Equipment:

 Well control equipment used by the drilling crew shall be managed and

operated by designated personnel with clear post responsibilities.

 Well site shall have specified component storeroom and rubber element

storeroom with air conditioners respectively. The temperature of storerooms

shall meet storage requirements of components and rubber elements.

 At least 1 set is available as back-up for every type ram assembly in the well

site. Ram preventer side door seals and ram rubber, every type gasket and bolt

etc. should be enough for backup.

7. Killing Method and Shut-in Method:

 Driller's method is recommended for well killing.

 The hard Shut-in method is recommended for shutting in the well in Fahliyan

reservoir.

8. Well Control during drilling:

a) Shut in Procedure in While on Bottom

 Position Kelly (if in use) and tool joint so that tool joints are clear of sealing

elements.

 Shut off pumps, check for flow.

 If flow is noted, close the annular preventer and open remote-controlled choke

line valve (HCR).

 If the well has been closed using the annular preventer, check space out (pipe

rams vs. toll joint relative position) and close pipe rams and ram locks

 Bleed off pressure between pipe rams and annular preventer (if possible).

 Record shut-in drill pipe and casing pressures.

 Record volume gain and mark pits.

 Weigh mud in suction pits.

 Check blowout preventer and manifold for leaks.

 Check flowline and choke exhaust for flow.

 Check accumulator pressure.

South Azadegan Oilfield Project

Contract No:

AZNS-127 Side Track-2 Program Page 159of 179

b) Shut in Procedure in While Tripping

 If a flow is detected, install full opening safety valve and close same.

 Position tool joints clear of the sealing elements and close annular preventer

and open remote-controlled choke line valve (HCR).

 Make up grey valve (dart type inside BOP on full open safety valve). Then

Make up Kelly or top drive (insert a pup joint or single between safety valve

and top drive) and open safety valve.

 Record casing pressure.

 Check blowout preventer, stack, and manifold for leaks.

 Check valves for correct position.

 Check accumulator pressure.

 Begin stripping to bottom.

c) Shut in Procedure for Empty Wells

 Try to RIH with drill pipe as more as possible if hole condition permits, and the

drill pipe must be installed a Kelly cock or safety valve.

 Close the annular preventer and open remote-controlled choke line valve

(HCR).

 If the well has been closed using the annular preventer, check space out (pipe

rams vs. tool joint relative position) and close pipe rams and ram locks

 Bleed off pressure between pipe rams and annular preventer (jf possible).

 Record casing pressure

9. Well Control During Running Casing:

The well control while running casing is important and critical, best practices shall be followed, including but not limited to:

 Change out pipe rams to casing rams prior to running casing into hydrocarbon

bearing formation, if possible.

 The crossover between casing and drill pipe has to be available, and good

practice is to make it up with a joint of DP and keep on V-door.

10. Shut in Procedure During Logging:

Cable shall be pull out of the hole immediately when overflow is found during logging. If pit gain exceeds the specified amount, the cable shall be cut immediately and treat the overflow in accordance with the shut-in procedure for empty wells. Continuing to pull the cable through the closed annular preventer is not recommended.

11. Well Control During Testing:

South Azadegan Oilfield Project

Contract No:

AZNS-127 Side Track-2 Program Page 160of 179

 No difference to while DRILLING OPERATION, since either there is testing

string in the well (same as Shut-in procedure while on bottom), or tripping the

string. (Same as shut-in procedure while tripping).

 Likely there is some crude in the testing string, and precaution has to be taken

while circulating the crude out of hole during killing operations to ensure it is

properly handled without causing environmental impact.

 To minimize the formation damage, the killing fluids used shall be weighted

brine if possible, however in well control case when it occurs, killing well safely

will take priority rather than protecting formation from damage on selection of

killing fluids.

12. Well Control During Stimulation:

 Similar to during testing.

 For any residual or alive acid to be circulated out during killing operations,

measures have to be taken to treat the returned acid properly to avoid personnel

from getting hurt, and without causing any environmental damage.

13. Well Control Drills:

Drills shall be conducted only when hole conditions and other rig activities permit. Drills should be scheduled so that crews can practice drills while on bottom, while tripping in and while out of the hole. Each operating shift shall perform at least one BOP drill under different situations per month.

14. Basic Requirement of Well Control:

 For 13-5/8”, 10K BOP, BOP should be schemed as follows: upper rams 5”,

middle rams are shear rams, lower rams is variable rams (2-7/8” to 5”). For

easily connecting, armored fire-resistant 10000psi and ID 4-1/16" flexible

hoses are recommended as kill/choke lines which connected with BOP directly.

 The BOP stack and choke manifold, kill line and choke line, HCR and manual

gate valves, inside BOP (including kelly cock) have to be H2S trimmed and

stand the working temperature from -10 degrees C (in case of doing N2 for

DST) to the maximum up to 100 deg C (estimated highest temperature

condition).

 The BOP equipment shall be visually inspected, function tested, and

hydrostatically pressure tested during commissioning and Acceptance of

Drilling Unit prior to Commencement Date, then upon installation on a

wellhead, prior to drilling any hole section with a potential hydrocarbon bearing

reservoir, after breaking any BOP connection (such as after installation of an

South Azadegan Oilfield Project

Contract No:

AZNS-127 Side Track-2 Program Page 161of 179

additional wellhead section after running casing), and at least every 14-21 days

while the BOP is installed on the Well.

 CONTRACTOR shall submit the current well control procedures manual of

CONTRACTOR to COMPANY for review and approval by COMPANY.

Valid IWCF Well Control Certificates (or IADC equivalent) must be held by

all tool pushers, Drillers (optional) at Drilling Supervisor level and Drillers and

Assistant Drillers at Driller level, as further specified in CONTRACTOR

Personnel HSE Requirements.

 The accumulator must be of sufficient capacity so that it is possible to close one

(1) ram and the bag, open a ram and the bag, re-close a ram and the bag and

retain 1200psi accumulator pressure.

 The “OPEN” and “CLOSED” operating positions of BOP activators of the

rams, annular, and remote actuated valves must be clearly identified on the BOP

master control panel and remote panels, in English in addition to the native

language of the majority of the senior drilling crew.

 Shear-ram BOP activator must have a flap-cover to ensure only pre-meditated

and deliberated activation and to prevent accidental WORK.

 All lines and connections in the choke and kill manifold, standpipe manifold,

choke and kill lines and high-pressure mud lines should be welded hard-piping

with weld-on FMC Weco “hammer-lug” 1502 unions (or Western equivalent,

such as Anson) or weld-on API flanges. The well control system should not

include any threaded screw-on hammer-lug unions, flanges, or other threaded

screw-on connections.

 All adapter or spacer spools between the wellhead and BOP must be

manufactured in accordance with API 6A, and must be complete with all

required studs, nuts, and ring gasket seals for both lower and upper connections;

minimum spare parts should include two (2) OEM spare studs complete with

nuts and two spare OEM ring gasket seals for both bottom and top connections.

 There should be a wide-bore gas vent line from the “poor-boy” degasser; the

line and line outlet must be securely anchored, the line outlet must be a safe

distance from the well cellar, rig floor, choke manifold, and mud logging unit.

 Well Control Equipment Welding: All welds in the well control system must

be NDT inspected and records maintained of all welding and weld inspections,

including choke and kill manifold, standpipe manifold, mud pump discharge

manifold, choke and kill lines.

 Well Control Rig Floor Information: The following must be posted on the rig

floor (in the Driller’s shack / “dog-house”): Well Shut-In Procedure, Well

Information Sheet (showing casing and hole sizes, depths, and such like), Kill

Sheet (including most recent slow circulation rate pressures, formation integrity

leak-off test information and MAASP, present mud weight, present drill string

and well volumes, and such like).

 The derrick substructure clear height (rotary table to ground level) needs to be

enough for fitting in above BOP configuration (including a tubing head and a

bell nipple). This need to be double checked in rig tender process. According to

the calculation of height of BOP stack, the substructure clear height is at least

9 m.

 In the case if drilling 6-1/8" hole becomes necessary, or using 3-1/2" drill pipe

for the cleanup run (including drill 7" shoe track), then taper drilling string (5"

DP + 3-1/2" DP) is to be run, so a pair variable ram be installed in the single

ram preventer. The defect installing variable ram in single ram preventer is that

the ram may be damaged and the string fall in hole bottom due to the ram

hanging up too much weight when the drill pipe be cut. If the pipe ram be

installed in the single ram preventer and the variable ram be installed in the

double ram preventer, it would be very dangerous due to the variable ram failure

in frequently using.

12.9 H2S Monitoring and Prevention Measure

As per PPL/PEDEC SOW South Azadegan oilfield contains H2S bearing formations, precautions shall be taken in place especially in 12-1/4” &amp;amp; 8-1/2” hole section (for typical Fahliyan vertical well) while drilling, completion and well testing operation.

H2S can be released any time while drilling, completion and well testing operation, therefore:

 The Rig shall be prepared for H2S (Training, procedures and protective gear).

 Make sure everyone on the Rig should be made aware of the hazard presented

by H2S during their induction when they first arrive on the rig.

 The mud shall be treated to protect the drill pipe and the casing.

 All training program shall be recorded and reported.

 H2S emergency drill must be conducted frequently.

 Adequate sensors and alarms must be installed for the scope of monitoring

the H2S releases.

1. General Information

1.1 Field Introduction

Azadegan South Oil Field is situated in West Karoun province on a large long-axis anticline with N-S trending with approximate dimensions about 20 km width and 60 km length near to Iran-Iraq border, to the east of Yaran Oil Field.

The trap area of the south Azadegan is limited to 43.2x17.2 km. The Azadegan Oil field was discovered in 1999, when Well AZN-1 was drilled vertically down to the Cretaceous Fahliyan Formation with total depth of 4,643m. The results of this well, revealed the reservoir characteristics of the field. Following to the result of the well no. AZN-1, another 5 exploration wells was drilled in different parts of this huge field down to Fahliyan Formation. In the later stage the well No.10 assumed as exploration well for evaluation of deeper formations. This well was drilled in 2008, down to the depth of 5340m (Neyriz Fm.), mainly to evaluate the Jurassic formations.

Based on the exploration wells results, carbonate reservoir of Sarvak Formation is broadly developed in Azadegan Field. This formation was penetrated in all of seven exploration wells (AZN-1, AZN-2, AZN-3, AZN-4, AZN-5, AZN-6 and AZN-10). Clastic oil-bearing zones of Kazhdumi Formation developed in main anticline of Azadegan Field, extending from north to center of South Azadegan. The Clastic oil-bearing zones of Gadvan Formation developed only in crest area and south parts of South Azadegan Filed, which was discovered by AZN-1 in crest and AZN-4 in south parts. The carbonates of Fahliyan Formation also developed in Azadegan field, but the oil reservoir of this formation developed in South part of South Azadegan.

The Azadegan Field is an elongated anticline, trending in N-S direction, belonging to "Arabian Trend".

The stratigraphy sequence of the field includes AghaJari, Gachsaran, Fahliyan, Pabdeh, Gurpi, Ilam, Laffan, Sarvak, Kazhdumi, Dariyan, Gadvan and Fahliyan Formations, from top to bottom. This sequence in well no AZN-10, the deepest up to now drilled well of the field, continues with Garau, Gotnia, Najmah, Sargalu, Alan, Mus and Neyriz formations.

The Dominant lithofacies of Sarvak Formation are Rudist-bearing packstone and partially grainstone, which contains abundant bioclasts. Some other facies like matrix-dominated wackestone and mudstone are also found.

The AZADEGAN Oilfield is Located in Khuzestan Province and is Approximately Located 80 Kilometers West of Ahwaz City, near to Iran-Iraq Border. It is in The Northwest of The YADAVARAN Field and in The West of JUFEYR Field. The Average Monthly Temperature is 45ºc in summer, and Highest Temperature is 52ºc. The Lowest Temperature is -4.4ºc in winter. Maximum Rainfall is 78 mm in February, Winter Season.

This Document covers the work over of well AZNS-122. Main headlines of program are de-complete the well and run new completion string.

1.3 Area Distribution

According to the drilling history, the CONTRACT AREA is distributed into three blocks as per the geological features with regard to DRILLING OPERATION. This distribution may differ according to knowledge accumulated in the future WORK.

Contract area is as per below:

X (m) Y (m)185640 3434275188020 3477361205224 3476408202842 3433327

Table 1-2 Area Distribution

Block I is located on the north part of the CONTRACT AREA in north of well AZN-010. Gachsaran formation is characterized by abnormal high pressure in this block.

Block II is located between well AZN-010 and AZN-011. In this block, Gachsaran formation is characterized by pressure tending to normal

Block III is located on the south of line well AZN-011. In this block, Gachsaran formation is characterized by normal pressure and all drilled wells in this block suffered from complete loss at Pabdeh formation.

1.7 Drilling History

26" Hole Section

Rig moving initiated on 95.09.27 and spudded rig 304 on 95.10.08 at 1200hrs.

Commenced drilling 26” hole section from 14m to 150m while experienced low ROP and bit balled up several times. Pulled out to surface, Ran in hole with same rock bit and 26" reamer to 150m and reamed from surface to 150m. Ran 20” casing as following with no major problem:

 20" stab in shoe 94ppf, k-55, BTC (KTK Co.)

 2 joints 20" casing 94ppf, k-55, BTC to 25m

 Circulated mud and check float shoe-ok

 Continued run with 10 joints 20" casing 94ppf, K-55, BTC to 146m (Totally run: 12 joints 20" casing 94ppf, K-55, BTC) to 146m. Cemented 20” casing in place as below:

 Sting in, lined up cement line and tested it with 2000psi-ok.

 Pumped 20bbl fresh water as spacer, mixed and pumped 689sxs cement class "G" Kerman (slurry weight: 118pcf, slurry volume: 170bbl), displaced with 7bbl 68pcf mud (1.7bbl short displace).

Note: Got 40bbl cement slurry and 10bbl contaminate as return on surface.

17 1/2" Hole section

Drilling of 17-1/2” hole section started on 12th Dey 1395 by new 17-1/2” rock bit and 17-1/2” string stabilizer placed at 20m, from 150m to 1064m while pumped salt saturated water several times to prevent balled up bit and displaced hole with 74pcf Kcl polymer mud at 502m.

Continued drilling 17-1/2” hole section by 17-1/2” from 1064m to 13-3/8” casing point at 1441m with 3-6bph loss while pumped hi-vis pill several times and pumped salt saturated water several times to prevent balled up bit. Condition hole prior logging, pulled out to surface and ran in hole with Sonic/Caliper/CDR/GR wire line logging tool string to 1438m (3m off bottom), took weight, tried to pass this point-not succeed, logged up from 1438 to 1280m, due to failure of Sonic tools, stopped log up and pulled out of hole to surface, changed sonic tools and ran in hole with same logging tool string

Bleed off Press to 3000 psi, Build up to3800 psi in 1 Min. Increase Press f/ 3800 to 3900 psi in 5 Min.

P/U 60 Jts 5" DP Jt by Jt, made &amp;amp; R/B 20 Stds to derrick. Monitored annulus pressure build up to 4800psi after 6 hrs. Opened the annulus thru choke manifold to oil storage; after 6min. decreased pressure to 980psi. Decreased pressure gradually to 500psi in 20min. Closed the annulus; Shut in pressure 500psi. Built up to 1000psi in 15min. Opened the annulus, suddenly dropped to zero. After 6min closed the annulus. Opened the 2SV, top master valve &amp;amp; production valve. Tightened XMT cap. Connected hand pump to exit block, tried to open TR3SV. Monitored tubing pressure 3400psi. Opened the well f/ TBG to oil storage tank; dropped pressure to zero in 2min. Closed the well. Built up to 3700psi in 2min. L/U annulus to choke manifold. Obs. annulus pressure built up to 4300psi in 3 hrs. Opened the well &amp;amp; pressure decreased to 600psi. Closed the annulus. Pressure rapidly built up to 3300psi. Opened the well again. Pressure suddenly dropped to zero. Flew the well for 10min. Closed the well, built up to 3300psi. Monitored the well for1 hrs. Pressure built up to 4300psi.

Due to jammed stem of inside SOV of THS in close position, installed pressure gauge on annulus to choke manifold line &amp;amp; pressure test same to 7000psi, Ok. R/U slickline equipment. Installed slickline BOP &amp;amp; lubricator on XMT cap. Tried to pressure test, Obs. leakage between lubricator &amp;amp; BOP. Changed lubricator O-ring &amp;amp; tried to pressure test; No-Success. L/D previous BOP. Installed another slickline BOP &amp;amp; Lubricator on XMT cap. Pressure test slickline BOP &amp;amp; lubricator w/ 7000psi to 15min; Ok. RIH w/ 3.4" gauge cutter to TBG HGR, tried to pass this depth; No-Success. Pulled out to surface &amp;amp; R/D slickline BOP &amp;amp; lubricator.

Installed 4 – 1/16" 10k lubricator on XMT. Pressure test to 7000psi for 15min; Ok. RIH w/ BPV retrieving tools to TBG HGR &amp;amp; retrieved 4" BPV f/ TBG HGR. L/D 4 – 1/16" 10k lubricator. Due to unable to open TR3SV, decided M/U 5" DPs. R/D slickline equipment.

R/U slickline equipment. Pressure test; Ok. Fixed CL port exit block. Ran 3.4" gauge cutter to 206ft, RIH w/ 3.437" protection sleeve to 190ft, opened TR3SV while holding pressure to 1200psi. Applied 7500psi pressure in CL &amp;amp; opened TR3SV. Cont. running tools to 200ft, took weight, tried to set protection sleeve by jarring several times; No-Success. Flew the well with 1/4" choke size &amp;amp; Cont. work on set protection sleeve; No-Success. Pulled out tools to 191ft. Obs. stuck tools. Worked on stuck to max. 60lb over-pull; No-Success. Finally flew the well by annulus &amp;amp; tubing. Tools got free. Cont. pulled out tools to 50ft &amp;amp; stuck tools again. R/D lubricator. Obs. cut the slickline wire from 50ft &amp;amp; left

in hole about 3m tools &amp;amp; 13m wire. RIH w/ 2.5" LIB to 157ft, POOH to surface; Obs. wire mark on same.

While wait on OEOC slickline service, RIH w/ 2.8" spear to TOF. Worked on fish &amp;amp; retrieved 2.45m of wire after 3 attempts. RIH w/ 2.8" LIB to 157ft, POOH to surface. Obs. rope socket marked on same. RIH w/ 2.8" blind box, POOH to surface. Rope socket marked on same. Welded 3.2" skirt on 2.2" JDC, RIH w/ JDC to TOF. Engaged w/ same. Tried to pull out, Obs. indication of shear JDC Shear pin. POOH to surface. Obs. sheared JDC Shear pin. Redressed w/ steel shear pin. RIH w/ JDC to TOF again. Engaged &amp;amp; worked on fish, Pulled to surface. Obs. retrieved 10ft stem of fish. RIH w/ 2.8" LIB to TOF, POOH to surface. Obs. slickline mechanical jar on the same. RIH w/ JDC to engage w/ jar. Worked on fish, jarring up. Pulling out fish 20ft. Cont. worked on stuck. RIH w/ blind box &amp;amp; knock on TOF, without progress. POOH to surface. RIH w/ JDC to engage w/ Jar. Worked on fish, jarring up. POOH to surface. R/D slickline equipment.

In order to work on fish w/ coiled tubing, wait on receive coiled tubing unit. While waiting on OEOC slickline service, R/U CT &amp;amp; M/U 2 – 1/8" dimple connector on 1 – 1/2" CT pipe &amp;amp; performed pull test to max 20klb. Obs. failure in dimple connector, disconnected same. M/U 1 – 11/16" roll on connector on 1 – 1/2" CT pipe &amp;amp; performed pull test to max 20klb, Ok. Installed CT riser on XMT &amp;amp; CT BOP. Close CT blind rams &amp;amp; tried to perform pressure test; No-Success. Tightened between two risers flange &amp;amp; tried to perform pressure test; No-Success. P/U riser &amp;amp; BOP; Tried to perform pressure test; NoSuccess. Changed 1 Jt CT riser &amp;amp; performed pressure test CT BOP &amp;amp; risers, Ok. RIH CT BHA to 48m &amp;amp; engaged w/ the fish; Obs. stuck the fish. Worked on stuck to max 18klb over-pull; No-Success. While shearing JDC Shear pin @ 2 times &amp;amp; POOH to surface &amp;amp; redressed w/ brass shear pin.

In the 3rd attempt, caught the fish &amp;amp; worked on same upward to 18klb over-pull while bleeding off annulus pressure f/ 4800 to 2000psi. Obs. fish got free, jumped same &amp;amp; sheared the JDC Shear Pin. POOH to surface. Cut 12m 1 – 1/2" CT pipe &amp;amp; changed roll on connector. Performed pull test to 20klb; Ok. RIH w/ 1 – 1/2" CT &amp;amp; 3.2" JDC to 48m. Worked on fish &amp;amp; POOH to surface. In the last attempt caught, engaged the fish &amp;amp; bleed off annulus pressure f/ 4800 to 2000psi. Pulled out f/ 48 to 10m w/ 2 – 3klb drag. Obs. took over-pull. Worked on stuck upward to max 18klb; No-Success. Then Obs. CT got free &amp;amp; POOH to surface. Closed swab valve &amp;amp; unable close TMV. Obs. sheared JDC Shear pin &amp;amp; TOF located in TMV. Installed 1 No 4 – 1/16" 10k gate valve on XMT. Redressed JDC shear pin to steel &amp;amp; M/U on CT BHA. Tightened all bolts. Performed pressure test to 6000psi for 10min; Ok.

Due to refused work on fish &amp;amp; stopped operation from OEOC CT service, wait on CT Service to make a decision. Changed JDC shear pin to brass. RIH w/ 1 – 1/2" CT &amp;amp; 3.2" JDC to 11m &amp;amp; engaged w/ the fish. Worked on stuck upward to max 18klb over-pull; No-Success. Slack off 6klb weight on JDC &amp;amp; sheared JDC Shear Pin. POOH to surface. R/D CT injector head. R/U slickline equipment &amp;amp; worked on fish w/ JDC jarring up several times; No-Success.

Performed injectivity test &amp;amp; monitored the well &amp;amp; checked communication between string &amp;amp; annulus; Ok. Pumped &amp;amp; direct Circ. 30bbl fresh water by applying back pressure in order to check communication between string &amp;amp; annulus; Ok. Commenced killing the well by W&amp;amp;W method,

Ran back in hole w/ protection sleeve to 61m (3SV depth) &amp;amp; tried to set protection sleeve for several times, No Success. POOH separation sleeve to surface. 1. RIH w/ 8 – 1/2" bit &amp;amp; 9 – 5/8" scraper, scrap 9 – 5/8" casing prior to Corrosion log, POOH

to surface.

2. Change ram, install shooting nipple, R/U wireline logging equipment.

3. RIH w/ Corrosion log to check 9 – 5/8" casing, POOH to surface &amp;amp; R/D logging equipment,

change ram.

4. R/U &amp;amp; run 5" &amp;amp; 3 – 1/2" open end DPs to 3390mMD, set 40bbl cement as balance plug, POOH.

5. RIH 8 – 1/2" bit &amp;amp; dress cement to 3350mMD. Perform positive pressure test CMT POOH.

6. RIH w/ 8 – 1/2" bit &amp;amp; 9 – 5/8" scraper, scrap whipstock setting depth &amp;amp; displace mud in

hole wby 85pcf mud, observe the well, POOH.

7. M/U &amp;amp; RIH w/ 9 – 5/8" permanent hydraulic set whipstock (suitable for 9 – 5/8" casing

53.5ppf), set same &amp;amp; open window @ 3337m.

8. Drill 3m in formation to 3340m, POOH to surface.

9. P/U &amp;amp; M/U new 8 – 1/2" rock bit &amp;amp; directional BHA, RIH to bottom.

10. Continue drilling 8 – 1/2" f/ 3340 to 3496m.

11. Perform hole condition, POOH to surface.

12. P/U &amp;amp; M/U new 8 – 1/2" rock bit &amp;amp; directional BHA, RIH to bottom.

13. Continue drilling 8 – 1/2" hole to 3652m (DOP).

14. Perform hole condition, POOH to surface to change BHA.

15. P/U &amp;amp; M/U new 8 – 1/2" PDC bit &amp;amp; BHA, RIH to bottom.

16. Continue directional drilling 8 – 1/2" hole f/ 3652 to section TD @3939m.

17. CBU, perform condition trip to last casing shoe prior to logging, RIH to bottom, CBU,

spot pill.

18. POOH to surface &amp;amp; L/D PDC bit.

19. R/U casing running gear, run 7" liner to bottom, R/D casing running gear.

20. Perform 7" liner cementing operation.

21. POOH w/ liner hanger setting tool to 2800m, flush string &amp;amp; CBU.

22. POOH to surface &amp;amp; L/D liner hanger setting tool.

23. P/U &amp;amp; M/U 8 – 1/2" MT bit BHA, RIH to liner lap @ ±3150m while D/O cement, Circulate

&amp;amp; clean the well, POOH.

24. L/D excess 5" DPs/HWDP.

27. RIH w/ 5 – 7/8" MT bit &amp;amp; tandem scraper (7" &amp;amp; 9 – 5/8") to LDC depth, scrap inside 7"

liner &amp;amp; 9 – 5/8" casing before dry test, CBU, POOH to surface.

28. Perform BOP test as NIOC policy.

29. RIH with 9 – 5/8" dry test BHA, RIH to liner lap @ ±3150m, perform 7" liner lap drey test

6. Directional Drilling Operation

6.1 Hydraulic Set Whipstock System Operation Procedure

SCOPE

The following procedures are intended to provide concise but definitive steps to follow in operations involving the milling of lateral hole sections from a parent well using the Hydraulic Set Whipstock System.

The Hydraulic Set Whipstock System is a hydraulically set whipstock that requires a hydraulic force to activate the packer assembly, setting itself in the casing.

Milling a window in casing using a whipstock usually consists of one run for setting the Whipstock in place and milling and completing the window through the casing wall and into the formation, while dressing the window to eliminate drag.

EQUIPMENT REQUIRED

Hole Preparation Run Equipment

• A Full Gauge Drift Mill

• Casing Scrapper

• Cross Over Sub

• String Stabilizer

• Pony Drill Collar or 1 Joint of Drill collar

• String Stabilizer

• Drill Collars

• Drilling Jar

• Drill Collars

• HWDP’s

• Balance Of Drill Pipes To Surface

The stiffness of this assembly will serve to identify any problem doglegs or restrictions in the hole that may hamper running of the whipstock assembly.

Whipstock Run Equipment

• Hydraulic Set Whipstock

• Tri-Mill (Optional Bi-Mill or a combination of Rugby/Back/Window Mill)

• Running Tools

• Nuzzle plug Assembly

• Universal Bottom Hole Orientation Sub (UBHO sub) or MWD

• Pup joints (for space-out if necessary)

• Tool kit

PRE-OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES

Pre-Run Checklist

As part of the Pre-operational Procedures, all whipstock jobs should include a completed

Pre-Run Preparation Checklist.

Pre‐Run Preparation Checklist

† The Packer slip is in place, is in good condition, and is the correct size for the casing size and weight and the

Allen screws are tight.

† The shear pins are properly installed and in good condition and the Number of Shear pins are enough.

† The shear screw is the proper size, and it will make up into the Whipface.

† The shear screw will fit through the Rugby/Lead Mill hole.

† Running Tools, Nuzzle plug Assembly and Hydraulic Lines and Fittings are in good condition and properly installed.

† All mills are on location and the OD’s are correct for the casing’s size/weight. (Check mill OD’s with a gauge ring that is OD + 1/32").

† All downhole equipment has been properly measured and OD’s, ID’s, and lengths have been properly recorded.

† The slots on the gyro match and are compatible with the lug assembly on the orientation sub.

† The survey tools will pass through all drill string tool joints and drill collar ID’s.

† All rotary connections are compatible.

† All rotary shouldered connections are made up to the recommended torque.

† Enough Pump Pressure is available on Site for setting the Packer.

Making the Hole Preparation Run

1. Make a run to ensure that the casing is clean and there is smooth and clean place for setting the packer. The run should include the following (from the bottom):

• A Full Gauge Drift Mill

• Casing Scrapper (Do not run casing scrapers across open perforations.)

• Cross Over Sub (Bit Sub with Float)

• String Stabilizer

• Pony Drill Collar or 1 Joint of Drill collar

• String Stabilizer

• Drill Collars

• Drilling Jar

• Drill Collars

• HWDP’s

• Balance of Drill Pipes To Surface

2. Run this assembly in the well to the Packer setting depth.

3. Tally the pipe while running in or out of the well to get an accurate measurement to the Packer setting depth.

4. Record the measurements to ensure that:

• the whipstock can be run and set at the desired depth

• the depth measurement to the Packer setting depth is accurate

• the casing wall is clean where the whipstock is to be set

NOTE: Scrape Packer setting depth twice.

Note: It is very important to get an accurate measurement for the packer setting depth so the Whipstock will be oriented as to setting depth as possible. Using this measurement facilitates proper placement of the Whipstock.

Preparing the Milling Equipment

1. Lay the whipstock on the catwalk, face up, with the top of the whipstock pointing toward the rig.

WARNING

Never use a nylon sling to lift or move a Whipstock because nylon may be cut. Always us a wire sling or wire rope to lift or move a Whipstock.

2. Complete the whipstock assembly, checking all OD’s, ID’s, and descriptions.

3. Pick up a joint of S-135 Drill Pipe (FLEXJOINT) and make up the Flow Through Valve to the top of the drill pipe and make up the Mill Assembly covered with Running Tool to the bottom of Drill Pipe.

Note: If the window is exiting through two or more strings of casing or into a known hard formation, exclude the Watermelon Mills (in the case of using combination mills), using only the Rugby Mill below the single joint of DP. Depending on the casing size and grade, more than one Rugby Mill may be required to make multiple exits.

Once the casing string(s) has been exited into the formation, pull out of the hole. Make up the Back Mill (and Window Mill) in the assembly as described above and run in the hole, reaming through the window with the Watermelon Mills.

4. Make up one joint of S-135 Drill Pipe (with cone type DP strainer installed) to the top of Flow Through Valve and make Up MWD to the top of Drill Pipe. (or Make up UBHO Sub to the top of Flow Through Valve).

5. If a bit float have to be used, place the bit float sub above the Flow Through Valve and beneath the UBHO sub.

6. Make up all connections to the recommended torque.

7. Ensure that everything is properly made up before continuing (see Figure).

CAUTION

• Close the BOP Shear/Blind ram when working on Whipstock.

• Do not drop anything in the wellbore when working over the wellbore.

• Use extreme caution when handling the whipstock, setting drill collar slips, safety clamps, etc. to prevent dropping the whipstock in the hole.

• Run the draw works in low. Pick up and set down the whipstock easily in the slips to prevent damage or premature setting.

• Ensure the lead tongs have most of the slack out of the snub line to prevent jerking against the back-up tongs.

16. Put a light amount of thread compound on the shear screw, adjust Rugby Mill hole and

Whipface and connect the whipstock assembly to the mill assembly with shear screw.

Shear screws with a higher value should be considered when:

• running the whipstock in a highly deviated hole

• heavy mud is in the well

• other wellbore restrictions such as a liner hanger may be encountered

Shear screws with a lower shear value should be considered when:

• whipstock is being set shallow (less than 1500 m)

• running and setting Whipstock with coiled tubing

RUNNING PROCEDURE

Running and Orienting the Whipstock

1. Lower the whipstock assembly slowly into the wellbore and do not pump anything in the

well to prevent premature setting of the whipstock.

Do not alter the orientation of the UBHO sub to the Whipface's face when making the first connection. Do not let the UBHO sub turn or move, or the direction of the milled window could be affected.

2. Refer to dogleg checklist for doglegs greater than 4 degrees. Watch the weight indicator

carefully and record up-weights regularly.

3. Monitor trip-tank for proper fill up.

4. Run the whipstock slowly, like a packer assembly, at a rate of 2 to 3 minutes per stand.

5. Do not turn string.

6. Do not Pump in the Well (unless an open Flow Throgh Valve is Run above the Running

Tools).

7. Fill the drill string every 5 strands.

Proceed slowly and with caution while running the whipstock assembly through the BOPs, wellhead, liner top, and any other restrictive sections to prevent damage or premature setting. The difference between the whipstock OD and the casing ID is minimal, making it similar to a piston, so lower the assembly very slowly in these small bypass areas. DO NOT PUMP IN THE WELL.

8. Run slowly into the hole until approximately 30 feet off the bottom.

9. Slowly move the whipstock assembly up and down from 5 to 20 feet to remove all trapped torque from the drill string.

10. Record up and down free weights.

11. Run survey tools on wireline to the UBHO sub if using a survey.

12. Take survey readings

13. To orient the whipstock, rotate the drill pipe to the right in ¼ turn increments (no more that ½ turn at a time) until the whipstock assembly is oriented in the correct position.

14. Take another survey, making additional corrections as needed and lowering 4 to 5 feet after each increment.

South Azadegan Oilfield Project

Contract No:

CCA/C/1401/27 AZNS-127 Re-Entry#01 Program Page 86 of 229

CAUTIONA crooked hole may require several readings and corrections to remove all of thetrapped torque from the drill string. Work slowly and carefully in order to achieve proper orientation.CAUTIONThis Model of Whipstock, because it is hinged, must be set within 30° on either side of the low side to prevent the whipstock’s whipface from falling across the wellbore.

15. Continue taking readings until 3 sequential reading are within a 5° range before assuming the direction is correct.

16. After reaching and verifying the proper direction, call a meeting with the customer, driller, and survey/MWD company representative to review the orientation of the whipstock’s Whipface once more.

17. Continue the procedure if everyone is in agreement.

18. POOH the survey tools and make a mark on the rotary table and the Drill Pipe, make up the Kelly (or Top Drive), DO NOT ALTER THE ORIENTATION WHILE MAKING UP THE KELLY.

19. Lower the whipstock assembly slowly to the setting depth.

20. Start pump and increase pressure until the packer shear pins are sheared and the packer sets in place (at 1200-1400 psi), hold pressure for 10 minutes to confirm the setting).

Note: In case of Using MWD and Flow Through Valve, increase pump rate until the Flow Through Valve shear pins are sheared and the valve closes, then continue pumping until the packer shear pins are sheared and the packer sets in place.

21. Slack off 10-15klbs and over pull 10-15k lbs to prove packer is set.

22. Pick-up 35,000-55,000 lbs (Depend on whipstock size) over pull, continue over pull on the screw as required to initiate the shear. A sharp drop in the pipe occurs when the shear screw shears.

23. Raise the drill string approximately 1 to 2 feet.

24. Set the drill string back down to make sure the shear screw has sheared. Repeat if necessary.

25. Mark the depth on the pipe each time. It should read the same each time.

26. Set the pipe back down with approximately 20,000 lb of pressure to ensure that the Whipface is over against the casing wall.

27. Raise the drill string so that the Rugby Mill is 5 to 10 feet above the top of the whipstock.

28. Lay down the necessary drill pipe to pick up the kelly.

Note: Do not Mill and work on Nozzle plugs more than One min with low GPM which leads to Mill burning.

30. Displace the Mud in the well (if needed) and check mud properties for proper rheology for steel removal.

31. The milling operation can now begin.

Running Milling Assembly and Opening the Window

This section assumes that the Rugby Mill has been sheared from the whipstock and raised 5 to 10 feet above the whipstock.

NOTE: Install Ditch Magnets

1. Make up the kelly to the drill string.

2. Record string weight up and down.

3. Engage the pumps, slowly increasing to the planned circulation rate, and record pump pressure and rate.

4. Engage the rotary and slowly increase the speed between 20 and 40 RPM.

5. After the rotary has stabilized, slowly increase between 50 and 75 RPM (depending on the mill size).

6. Record the following information:

• Free rotary torque

• Pump pressure

• Pump rate

• Free weight – up and down (string weight with zero weight on mill)

7. While rotating, slowly lower the drill string until the Rugby Mill contacts the whipstock and the casing wall, causing an immediate and substantial increase in rotary torque.

8. Mark the kelly. This is the starting point for the Rugby Mill run.

9. After making the initial mark on the kelly, raise the Mill 3 to 5 feet.

10. While rotating, slowly lower the drill string again to see if the increase in rotary torque is indicated at the same place. Work slowly and carefully; repeat if necessary.

11. After marking the kelly with the correct starting point for the Mill, begin milling, using light weights on the Mill (1,000 to 3,000 lb depending on the size of the mill and grade of the casing). As the window milling process begins, an increase in torque and decrease in weight will be indicated.

12. As the torque increases, increase the rotary speed to the recommended RPM (based on the mill size).

13. Continue milling with a constant rotary torque and weight (1,000 to 3,000 lb) on the mill.

Additional weight may be required if the rate of penetration (ROP) begins to slow.

Use recommended parameters as follows.

Casing Size (in) Weight on Mill (klb) Milling RPM9 ⅝” 2-15 60-1207” 2-12 60-1204-1/2” 1-7 60-120

14. Monitor returns for cuttings during milling operations and pump high viscosity sweeps

as needed to remove cuttings from the well. This practice is especially important if the window is being milled in a lateral section.

15. The Window Mill run is completed after milling down the Whipface’s face into the formation AND when the Dress Mill is centered at the bottom of the window.

16. Ream back and forth through the window until no signs of additional torque or drag are indicated.

17. Stop the rotary and slide the Mill assembly through the window several times. If any weight or drag is indicated, start the rotary and ream back and forth through the window until weight or drag is eliminated.

18. Stop the rotary and check for weight or drag again. Repeat this process as necessary.

19. Once the window is complete, stop the rotary, clean the hole of cuttings with high viscosity sweeps, and pull out of the hole without rotating.

20. Closely inspect and gauge all mills for wear using a gauge ring of OD + 1/32"

21. Determine the estimated size of the window.

22. Review the window requirements with the customer to determine if the Elongation Run is required.

Note: The Elongation run is recommended if:

• You have run a bi-Mill Assembly for opening the Window and:

• The customer requests it.

• PDC bit will be used through the window for additional drilling

• Drill collars and stabilizers will be used through the window for additional drilling

• Liner will be installed through the window

• Double bent sub and PDM assembly will be used through the window for additional drilling

• Unusual wear is indicated on the Rugby Mill, resulting in an under-gauge hole

Abnormal Conditions

Whipstock stuck

• Try to release the whipstock with 20000klb overpull in 7" hole and 30000klb over pull in 9-5/8" hole.

• Close an annular preventor hydrill and apply 500-1000 psi pressure in annulus to remove casing collapse.

• Apply weight on bit.

• If no success, shear screw and pull out the whipstock out of hole with fishing tool later.

South Azadegan Oilfield Project

Contract No:

CCA/C/1401/27 AZNS-127 Re-Entry#01 Program Page 96 of 229

No success in passing the whipstock through liner lab

• Come back to neutral point and turn string 1/4 round in clockwise direction and try to pass through liner lab again.

The packer does not set with designed setting pressure

• Release the pressure and apply the pressure again.

• Pull out of hole to surface and check the tools.

Pressure drop during the milling operation

• Twisting off the string or mill:

• In this case the torque will be constant and progress will be stop.

• Pressure drop due to string washing out:

• In this case the standpipe pressure will decrease gradually.

• Pressure drop due to breaking the nozzle plugs:

• In this case the pressure decreases suddenly and no change in other parameters will happen.

• Pressure drop due to washing out the nozzles:

• In this case the standpipe pressure will decrease gradually.

Note: In all the above items pulling the string out of hole to surface and checking the tools will be necessary.

No progress during milling

• Change the drilling parameters, for example increase or decrease RPM, increase WOB, decrease GPM.

8.2.1.1 Interval Mud Discussion

South Azadegan Oilfield Project

Contract No:

CCA/C/1401/27 AZNS-127 Re-Entry#01 Program Page 105 of 229

Sal KCL Polymer Mud are used to prevent excessive hole enlargement while drilling massive salt beds. They can also be used to reduce dispersion and hydration of shales and clays. Solids content (percent by volume) should be maintained within a desired range by mechanical removal or dilution with saturated salt water to prevent unacceptable increases in gel strengths and viscosity.

The chloride content of saturated salt muds is 170,000- 188,000 mg/l at saturation. As the temperature of the mud increases, more salt is able to go into solution. This means that a fluid which is saturated under surface conditions may not be saturated in down hole temperatures and can cause substantial washout in a salt zone due to increased salt solubility.

Control of the pH of saturated salt muds varies widely. Saturated salt muds require larger additions of caustic soda to maintain a pH in Salt saturate muds. Maintaining an±9.5 pH offers several advantages:

 Deflocculants are more effective

 Corrosion is reduced

 Lower concentrations of filtration control additives are required when Ca++ and Mg++

solubility is reduced

 Foaming tendency is lessened

 Mud is generally more stable

Caco3 Polymer Mud will normally contain soluble calcium due to the formations penetrated and the type of makeup water used. Also, the sodium ions from the salt will undergo a Base Exchange and release calcium ions from the clay platelets, thereby contributing to the free calcium. Generally, the presence of calcium does not produce detrimental effects on the mud; except when the pH is increased beyond 12.0 and then the fluid loss will be difficult to control.

Foaming is generally restricted to surface foam and is not troublesome unless aggravated by mechanical agitation. The degree of foaming may sometimes be decreased by increasing the alkalinity of the mud (Pm). A Defoaming agent may be necessary. Unless Mg++ sensitive additives are used, a Saturated Salt Mud is less prone to foam and air cut with a 9.5 - 10 pH. The temperature limitation of Saturated Salt Muds is around 250°F and is normally dictated by the filtration control additive used. Ca++ and Mg++ hardness do not adversely affect filtration control in Saturated Salt Muds when using starch; however.

Usually there are no problems associated with saturated salt mud conversions. Conversion can be accomplished in two circulations. When a freshwater mud is to be converted to a saturated salt mud, it is desirable to use as much of the old mud as possible.

South Azadegan Oilfield Project

Contract No:

CCA/C/1401/27 AZNS-127 Re-Entry#01 Program Page 106 of 229

The amount of salt required to saturate the system should be calculated and then added through the hopper. A saturated salt mud will generally weight 75 pcf without weight material addition. Next, a fluid loss additive is added through the hopper while the mud is circulated. Starch is generally used for fluid loss control and as a supplementary viscosifier. Normally, 12 lb/bbl starch will be required to obtain a fluid loss of less than 3 cc/30 minutes. If a higher density is required, Barite which will beuse. When weighting up with Barite, a Lignosulphonate Deflocculant is recommended to avoid excessive viscosity and high gel strengths as contingency.

Potassium is used in areas where inhibition is required to limit chemical alteration of shales. Potassium performance is based on cationic exchange of potassium for sodium or calcium ions on smectites and interlayered clays. The potassium ion compared to calcium ion or other inhibitive ions, fits more closely into the clay lattice structure, thereby greatly reducing hydration of clays. Potassium-based muds perform best on shales containing large quantities of smectites or interlayered clays in the total clay fraction. Potassium interactions with clay surfaces can be traced to two effects: ionic size and hydrational energy. Potassium ions are of the proper size to fit snugly into the spaces between the two silica tetrahedral layers which contact each other in the formation of a three-layer clay

packet. The ionic diameter of potassium is 2.66 Å, very close to the available distance of 2.8 Å in the lattice space of the clay structure. A cation slightly smaller than 2.8 Å is desirable to allow for crystalline compaction.

8.4 Technical Appendix

Loss Control Procedure

Loss of fluid returns will lower the hydrostatic head of the drilling fluid in the wellbore, thereby inducing a kick. The influx fluid will then flow to the surface or into the zone of lower pressure. Lost circulation can occur in naturally occurring fractured, vuggy, cavernous, sub-normally pressured or pressure depleted formations. Induced losses can occur from mechanical fracturing due to pressure surges while breaking circulation. In all cases of lost circulation, attempts should be made to keep the hole full. The hole can be filled with either light drilling fluid or water. A record of the amount of fluid pumped should be made.

The concentration of LCM will vary according to losses. In the event of seepage losses, treat system with a finer grade of LCM at 20 – 30 Kg/m³. In the event of moderate to high rate of well bore loss, prepare pills at different graded concentrations and spot over thief zone. The concentration may vary between 18 to 70 lb/bbl. In order to avoid LCM plugging MWD tools a circulation sub should be installed in the drill string. The MWD engineer is to advise on the size and concentration of LCM that can be pumped through MWD Tools. Ensure that the drilling displace the LCM pill out of the string prior to shutting down the mud pumps.

Important Note: Please note below concentration and recommended materials may be change with same materials on rig site.

In case of having circulation losses:

Losses less than 10 bbls/hr:

- Active system to be loaded with 10 lb/bbl of Fiber Fine.

Losses 10- 40 bbls/hr:

- Active mud to be loaded with 15- 20 lb/bbl of Fiber Medium.

- Sweep the hole frequently with 50 bbls high viscous pill contains;

- 15 lb/bbl Mica Medium - Corse.

- 10 lb/bbl Walnut Shells Medium -Fine.

- 10 lb/bbl Oyster Shell Fine.

Losses 40 – 100 bbl/hr:

- Stop Drilling.

- Pull out string above the loss zone

South Azadegan Oilfield Project

Contract No:

CCA/C/1401/27 AZNS-127 Re-Entry#01 Program Page 116 of 229

- Spot 100 bbls pill contains;

- 30 lb/bbl Fiber coarse.

- 30 lb/bbl Walnut Fine.

- 20 lb/bbl Mica Med.

- Repeat the previous pill minimum of two times.

Losses more than 100 bbls:

- Up to company procedure, may be squeeze 50 bbls of Cement squeeze.

8.4.1.1 Mixing LCM Pill

The amount of LCM that can be added to a mud depends very much on the mud properties. High gels and YP will help keep the material in suspension. Since LCM is generally of low gradient, excess material tends to float on top if too much is added. The following procedure may prove useful for mixing LCM pills and avoiding the problem of flotation.

1. ENSURE the pill has enough viscosity to keep the low gradient material in suspension

before addition of LCM. ADD appropriate viscosifier if required.

2. ADD the material in stages e g. 5, 10, 15, 20 etc. ppb.

3. STOP after desired concentration has been reached, or when it is observed that the material

cannot be held in suspension

4. If a higher LCM content is desired, LEAVE the pill to soak for a period of time and then

TRY ADDING more material.

8.4.1.2 LCM Pill Spotting Procedure

1. After spotting LCM pill, pull the bit above the calculated top of the pill. Wait 30minutes

and monitor the annulus.

2. After 30 minutes, attempt to fill the annulus, if not already full. If the hole can be filled,

close the BOP and squeeze 10 bbls of LCM pill into the formation without exceeding 200

psi.

3. If the hole remains stable, continue to drill ahead.

4. Should the LCM pill fail to reduce the losses or the hole cannot be filled, then mix and spot

another 50 bbls of LCM pill.

5. Attempt to fill the annulus. If successful, close the BOP and squeeze 20 bbls of LCM pill

into the formation without exceeding 200 psi. If a squeeze pressure develops, hold the

pressure for 1 hour before staging the drill string back to bottom.

Notes:

Guide Line for Fiel Engineers for Shale Inhibition

Shale Hydration takes two forms in water-sensitive shales: surface and osmotic adsorption. Surface hydration occurs when a small volume of water is strongly adsorbed onto the planar surfaces of the clays which causes little softening or swelling, but can lead to excessive stresses if the swelling is confined.

Osmotic swelling occurs when a large volume of weakly held water is attracted to the clay surfaces by electrostatic forces. Osmotic swelling causes softening and significant swelling as the adjacent clay layers hydrate water and expand. Osmostic swelling does not generate excessive stresses, even when confined, and can be substantially reduced if Extremely difficult drilling conditions have led to more systematic approaches to analysing wellbore instabilities.

One such approach that can be used as a guideline for the mud engineer involves three basic steps:

1. Monitor and analyse the fundamental failure mechanism.

2. Determine and understand the factors governing this failure mechanism.

3. Model the problem considering impact of proposed changes.

8.4.1.3 Monitor &amp;amp; Analyze the Failure Mechanism

Monitoring of data and events on the rig is the first step of the process and involves:

• Collection, organization and processing of drilling data. Drilling data such as Rate of Penetration (ROP), Revolutions per Minute (RPM), Weight-on-Bit (WOB), Bottom-Hole Assembly (BHA), torque, over pull Trip In Hole (TIH) and Pull Out Of Hole (POOH), swab and surge, flow rate, mud weight, mud Rehology , etc. should be collected, organized and analyzed on a continual basis and compared to the symptoms of wellbore stability being observed. This will help evaluate performance and establish trends or any deviations and measure the effectiveness of treatments and changes.
