• Formation characterization. The standard procedure in drilling operations is to apply the knowledge

gained from previous wells to subsequent wells drilled in similar geologic regions. Wellboreinstability

investigation requires evaluation of shales during the drilling process. Since rig site shale testing is limited

due to equipment and time limitations, most evaluations are performed in a properly equipped laboratory.

Laboratory tests are conducted to evaluate shale swelling, dispersibility, cation exchange capacity, hydration capacity, colloidal content, capillary suction time, shale hardness tests and mud compatibility properties.

A number of methods have been used to perform rig site tests. These include tests as simple as the methylene blue test (CEC) measurement of shale; shale hardness measurements; hot-rolled dispersion testing with various mud formulations and additives; and sophisticated analytical measurements of various clay properties. It is particularly important to try and determine the failure mechanism: swelling and softening or brittle spalling. Information from these tests, current shaker observations and mud logger

data are used to evaluate drilling fluid performance, adjust mechanical drilling parameters and making casing design decisions. The primary options to counter shale problems at the rig site are:

 Change the drilling fluid density.

 Change to an oil- or synthetic-base system.

 Change to a more inhibited water-base mud.

 Reduce fluid loss to very low levels and increase filtrate viscosity.

 Utilize pore-plugging additives, emulsified insoluble materials or plastering agents.

 Adjust mechanical drilling parameters.

 Evaluation and analysis of instability symptoms.

Instability warning signs such as the presence of excessive cavings on the shakers for a given ROP, fill on connections, tripping difficulties, torque, stuck pipe, etc. indicate that something is wrong down hole. The magnitude or volume of failed rock should be estimated and recorded with

the other drilling parameters. The number and location of specific incidents should be recorded, such as pipe

sticking, fill or packing-off, reaming and re-drilling. All of this information can then be organized and correlated with time and depth to detect the location and quantify the severity of critical sections in the well.

8.4.1.4 Determine &amp;amp; Understand Failure Mechanism

All of the monitored and plotted parameters are then evaluated to identify the most probable mechanism causing the instability. The most useful symptoms used to indicate the mechanism responsible for wellbore instability are:

 Cavings analysis.

 Tripping difficulties.

 Drilling conditions.

 Mud system analysis.

 In-situ conditions.

These symptoms should be evaluated based on an interdisciplinary knowledge of the causes of wellbore instability to determine the most likely failure mechanism.

8.4.1.5 Model &amp;amp; Considering Proposed Changes

Once the monitoring and determination steps have produced parameters, organize and analyze this data to obtain qualitative solutions and evaluate proposed changes. One good way to do this is through the use of a decision tree or flowchart approach to evaluate the possible failure mechanism and to identify the most promising remedies. After arriving at a proposed solution, a corrective measure should be applied and

the results used as feedback into the method and decision tree method.

A decision tree or flowchart, such as shown in Figure 9 for evaluating the cause of excessive cavings, provides a logical path for identification of the mechanism and a qualitative solution. Maintaining hole stability while drilling shale sections can be particularly troublesome. Simple solutions do not always exist, but good drilling practices combined with good mud practices are most often successful. Analysis of the mechanical stress/strain relationships has helped to develop the proper density requirements for hole stability.

8.5 Directional Drilling

Drilling Fluid Properties &amp;amp; Selection

It is common knowledge among drilling engineers and drillers that borehole problems can be considerably more severe in a directional hole than in a vertical well. The problems are magnified as the hole angle and horizontal displacement increases. Although most of these reactions are mechanical in nature, much can be done to alleviate them by proper selection and maintenance of the drilling fluid. For example, if a water-base fluid is being used, lubricants can be added to lower the coefficient of friction between the drill string and borehole or casing. Inhibiting salts can be added to reduce the interaction of the drilling fluid with the exposed formations, thereby improving borehole stability.

There are a number of drilling factors influenced by the drilling fluid, but the following are of primary concern in drilling a horizontal well.

 Borehole instability

 Hole cleaning

 Torque and drag

 Formation damage

 Barite sag

 Hydraulics

Borehole Instability

Borehole instability is one of the more costly, but relatively common problem associated with drilling oil and gas wells. Not only can it impede drilling, it can result in loss of the hole. The term normally conjures thoughts of borehole collapse with accompanying stuck pipe. This is one of the more critical reactions of borehole instability, but it can manifest itself in more subtle ways such as hole-fill, bridges, hole enlargement, or hole size reduction.

These reactions lead to other associated problems including increased torque and drag, logging difficulties, poor cement jobs, and increased drilling days, all of which add significantly to the drilling cost. It should be pointed out that the discussions to follow do not cover hole enlargement problems from weakly consolidated sands, or rubble zones that erode from the hydraulic action of the drilling fluid.

South Azadegan Oilfield Project

Contract No:

CCA/C/1401/27 AZNS-127 Re-Entry#01 Program Page 121 of 229

Stabilization

The swelling activity is controlled by adjusting the electrolyte content of the fluid to minimize expansion of the clays. Lime and gypsum-treated fluids have long been used for this purpose, but basically do not satisfy the inhibition needs of the more troublesome shales. The potassium ion is an effective swelling inhibitor and is used extensively for this purpose through the addition of potassium salts. The concentration of potassium utilized ranges from several hundred mg/L to over 60,000 mg/L. The most cost-effective potassium concentration, however, appears to be in the 3000 to 7000 mg/L range. In marine environments, seawater or seawater with additional sodium chloride, are good alternates to potassium. The tendency for the shale to disperse or subdivide into discrete particles appears to be best controlled by the addition of an adsorptive, high molecular weight water-soluble polymer.

One of the more effective polymers for this purpose is the partially hydrolyzed poly acrylamide with molecular weight in excess of 15 million. These anionic polymers adsorb on to the surface of the cuttings and borehole wall to act as a binder or elastic coating to retard dispersion. Another approach to stabilizing the hard brittle shales that contain natural or induced micro fractures is the use of water-dispersible asphalt or asphaltines. The addition of these type materials appear to plug the micro-fractures, or perhaps even surface pore throats to retard further fluid invasion. This action has proven very effective in certain shales and can be applied in most water base fluids.

Hole Cleaning

Cleaning cuttings from a vertical hole has been covered extensively by numerous investigators. Hole cleaning in a vertical hole is essentially a matter of overcoming the slip velocity of the cuttings with sufficient annular velocity and carrying capacity of the drilling fluid. Although any velocity greater than the settling velocity of the largest cutting will theoretically lift all the cuttings to surface eventually, too low an annular velocity will lead to an undesirable high concentration of cuttings in the annulus. Experience has shown that cuttings concentrations more than 5% by volume cause tight hole or stuck pipe when circulation is stopped.

Cuttings Bed Formation

Radial slip velocity increases with increasing angle of inclination, forcing more cuttings to the low side of the annulus, which eventually results in the formation of a cuttings bed. reported that bed formation was dramatic in the 40° to 50° angle with the bed sliding downward against the flow, resulting in a very high cuttings concentration.

The fact that a cutting bed forms is a serious problem, but the instability of the bed in this critical angle of the well makes the problem even more severe. High torque and drag resulting from the high cutting concentration at the lower part of the angle can obviously result in stuck pipe or loss of circulation.

Hole Cleaning Sweeps

In static drill string concluded that high-density sweeps were more effective than high-density high-viscosity sweeps based on field measurements. The higher viscosity of the latter caused flow diversion to the high side of the wellbore. Not surprisingly, high-viscosity sweeps also performed poorly. Also concluded that the best hole cleaning sweeps were high-density low viscosity sweeps, with a density 3 – 4 ppg higher than that of the drilling fluid. the following procedure is recommended:

 Calculate sweep height in the vertical part of the annulus, and added hydrostatic head in

the annulus.

 Rotate at 80+ rpm while pumping the sweep, 180+ rpm is preferred. It is not recommended

to pump a weighted sweep while sliding.

 Keep pumping until the sweep is out of the hole. If pumping stops while the sweep is in

the deviated hole, it falls out of the “jet stream” and re-deposits captured fines.

 Avoid increasing the viscosity of the weighted sweep.

 Plan to run 3 – 4 sweeps to achieve desired results when hole cleaning problems are

indicated. One sweep will probably not be sufficient to remedy an existing situation.

 Avoid checking for flow or closing the annulus with the weighted sweep in the drill pipe.

 If desired for preventative maintenance: 1) schedule sweeps every 6 – 8 hours or 500 –

1000 feet (whichever comes first, unless the hole dictates greater frequency); barite/silt

build- ups are dependent on time and footage: and 2) pump a sweep while circulating

bottom up before tripping, and another once back on bottom.

concluded that high-density sweeps were more effective than high-viscosity sweeps.

They strongly advocated the use of sweep reports, which should be standard practice in any drilling fluids operation.

Short Tripping

Another technique that has proven helpful in controlling problems created by the cuttings bed in the high-angle portion of the well is to make periodic short trips. Tripping the bit through the bed not only assures that the bottom hole assembly and bit can be pulled through it, but the action should agitate the bed to the point that a portion will slide down the hole and subsequently be picked up when circulation is commenced. The time intervals for these short trips will be determined by the torque and drag conditions that exist in any particular well. Lacking specific well history, a general rule of thumb is to short trip at least once for every 500 feet of new hole.

CCA/C/1401/27 AZNS-127 Re-Entry#01 Program Page 123 of 229

Drill String Rotation

The industry is in total agreement that drill string rotation improves hole cleaning, especially in hole sizes less than 17 ½”. The general opinion in the industry is that the optimum drill string rotation rate is approximately 120 rpm. It is believed that the drill string rotation improves hole cleaning by mechanically disturbing the cuttings bed on the low side of the hole. There could also be effects due to skewing the velocity profile in the wellbore and the creation of Taylor Vortices. Encouraged the use of rotary steerable systems.

Turbulance

Bottom hole assembly design becomes important because the flow restrictions of some of the components, such as the measurement-while-drilling tools or positive displacement motors, may not allow sufficient flow to reach turbulence in the annulus. Turbulence can, of course, be induced at some constant flow rate by decreasing the annular area. This may be more difficult to accomplish in a horizontal well because of limitations on the design of drill strings and tool assemblies. An increase in the effective viscosity of the drilling fluid will decrease the Reynolds Number, and thus increase the flow rate required to obtain turbulent flow. Thus, a lower effective viscosity fluid may be desirable in the horizontal well, but attention must also be given to cleaning the larger diameter portion of the upper hole or possible washed-out sections where it is impractical to maintain turbulent flow.

It is interesting to point out a basic fact between static fluid pressure and dynamic fluid pressure. Static fluid pressure is a function of true vertical depth, while dynamic fluid pressure, or ECD, is a function of measured depth. Thus, the ECD will continue to increase, albeit slowly, even after the hole becomes essentially horizontal. The fracture pressure could be reached if the hole was extended to sufficient depth and the fluid density is close to the fracture gradient.

Hole Cleaning Guideline

The single most important factor related to hole cleaning in deviated wells is flow rate. During directional drilling operations drilled cuttings will settle on the low side of the hole and form a stationary bed if insufficient annular fluid velocity is used. The critical flow rate required to prevent cuttings bed formation must be determined .

Typically few hole cleaning problems exist in vertical or horizontal sections. Most problems

associated with hole cleaning are seen on deviated wells and occur in the 40 – 60 degree section where gravity effects can cause cuttings beds to slump down the hole.Typical flow rates to aim for in ERD wells:

CCA/C/1401/27 AZNS-127 Re-Entry#01 Program Page 124 of 229

Hole Size Typical Flow Rates17 ½” 800 gpm minimum. Some rigs achieve 850 – 1000 gpm.12 ¼”Aim for 800 gpm (although 800 – 1000 gpm is typically achieved). If 800 gpm is not achievable, ensure tripping procedures are in place for poorly cleaned hole.8 ½” Aim for 400 gpm.

When correctly designed, both laminar and turbulent flow regimes will effectively clean a deviated well. In general increasing the viscosity of a fluid in laminar flow will improve hole cleaning as will a reduction of the viscosity of a fluid in turbulent flow. It is important that one or other regime is selected and that the transition zone between the two is avoided.

Generally viscous fluids in laminar flow are preferred because:

 It is possible to achieve higher cleaning capacity.

 Viscous fluids give better transport in the near-vertical sections.

 Viscous fluids have better suspension characteristics when circulation is stopped.

 It is difficult to achieve “turbulent flow” except in small hole sizes.

Experience has shown that good drilling fluid rheological properties are extremely important to hole cleaning when drilling a high angle well. Studies show that the effects of drilling fluid

rheological properties and annular flow regime are mutually dependent. In the laminar flow regime, increasing fluid viscosity will improve hole cleaning and this is particularly effective if the Yield Stress is high. In the turbulent regime, however, reducing fluid viscosity will help removing cuttings. Therefore the drilling fluid rheological properties should be designed to avoid the transitional flow regime. For hole sizes above 8 ½”, the annular flow is laminar under most circumstances. Therefore it is necessary to specify a minimum Yield Stress. The optimum level required is best established based on field data and experience.

A higher ROP requires a higher flow rate to clean the hole. It is good practice to drill the hole with a steady ROP and select the required flow rate for hole cleaning accordingly. Before making a connection, the hole should be circulated at the normal flow rate to clear the cuttings from around the BHA. Depending upon the hole angle and length of BHA, a circulation time of 5 to 10 minutes is often required.

Since wall contact with the drill string will be extremely high in a horizontal hole, it is imperative that the lubricating characteristics of the fluid be considered.

Formation Damage

The obvious reason for drilling a horizontal well is to expose more of the producing zone to the wellbore for increased production. Thus, the importance of preventing formation damage during drilling and completion of the horizontal well is just as important as it is in its vertical counterpart.

In fact, it may be more important since the increased cost of drilling the horizontal well must show additional production for its justification. A 50% damage or permeability loss in a potential 500 bbl/day horizontal well represents a considerably greater loss in production than a 50% damage in a 100 bbl/day vertical hole through the same reservoir.

Sandstone production is by far the most susceptible reservoir rock to damage or permeability loss during drilling and completion operations. Though formation damage may be caused by poor drilling and completion practices, one of the primary causes is due to exposure to the drilling and completion fluid.

This loss, attributable to the fluid, can be caused by one or more of the following occurrences:

South Azadegan Oilfield Project

Contract No:

CCA/C/1401/27 AZNS-127 Re-Entry#01 Program Page 126 of 229

 Particle transport from the drilling fluid into the production zone, subsequently plugging

pore throats.

 Fluid filtrate reacting with expandable clays in the rock to decrease pore throat diameters.

 Particle movement within the permeable rock due to dispersion of clays and other minerals

from quartz surfaces.

 Wettability changes of the formation from exposure to the drilling fluid filtrate.

 Interaction of fluid filtrate with formation fluids to form water - insoluble precipitants.

The effect of these actions on the permeability of sandstones has been the subject of a considerable investigation. In almost all cases, some damage is caused by the drilling and completion fluid. The primary objective is to limit this damage as much as possible. Consequently, selection of the drilling and completion fluid becomes an extremely important function in drilling the horizontal well.

Recommended Fluid Parameters

 Velocity – One of the major obstacles to overcome in horizontal and ERD drilling is hole

cleaning. In vertical holes, cuttings have room to settle without causing problems. In

horizontal wells, cuttings only have to settle 4+ inches to form a cuttings bed. Research

and practical experience has shown that cuttings bed formation is analogous to sand dunes

on an ocean beach. The bed moves in a wave fashion up the hole. If sufficient annular

velocity is not present, the bed thickens until it reaches equilibrium, which usually occurs

when turbulent flow conditions exist. With water, turbulent flow is easily obtained since

viscosity is in the denominator of the turbulent flow equation, and water has a viscosity

of 1. Fluids other than water require more pump output to approach turbulent flow

conditions. Practical experience in other industries has proven that materials can be

transported in water slurries if the fluid velocity is between 3 and 7 ft/sec.

 Rheological Properties – Ideally one would want a true thixotropic fluid to drill

horizontally. In effect, two different conditions exist simultaneously. One occurs in the

vertical portion of the hole where larger diameter casing may be set, or wash-outs in the

open hole occur. In that case, a fluid having a high Yield Stress, or if the fluid is viscoelastic, the initial gel strength needs to be elevated. The opposite is needed in the

horizontal section from a hole-cleaning point of view. Here one wants water for the

reasons pointed out earlier. Compromises are the result. If casing is set into the zone of

interest, or if formations up-hole are not a problem, then water may be possibly combined

with occasional sweeps.

 Surface Apparatus – Special attention must be placed on the solids removal equipment at

the surface. Solids removal efficiency must be continually monitored so that unwanted

particulate material is not retained in the fluid system that may negatively affect fluid

weight or filter cake quality, resulting in lost circulation or increased torque and drag. The

cost of problems that may occur due to not doing this correctly may far outweigh the cost

of equipment needed.

8.6 Hydrogen Sulphide Gas in Drilling Fluid

Description of Hydrogen Sulphide Gas

Hydrogen sulphide is a colourless gas, with an offensive odour and a sweetish taste. It is soluble in water, alcohol, oils, and many other solvents. It has a specific gravity of 1.1895 with reference to air. It is considered a weak acid, it is toxic to humans and corrosive to metals. Hydrogen sulphide can be dangerous to personnel on the surface as it is extremely toxic to human and even animal life, and is extremely corrosive to most metals as it can cause cracking of drill pipe and tubular goods, and destruction of testing tools and wire lines. When hydrogen sulphide enters the borehole during drilling, completion, or testing for hydrocarbons, it creates several very detrimental problems. These problems are encountered regardless of the source of the hydrogen sulphide. Hydrogen sulphide has created unsolved problems in the oil field.

Origin of Hydroge Sulphide

During oil and gas operations, hydrogen sulphide can be found as a component of formation gases, dissolved in water, hydrocarbons, or even liquid sulphur. Thermal degradation of organic materials and sulphate reducing bacteria (SRB) can create hydrogen sulphide along with other gases.

Problem Cused by Hydroge Sulphide Gas

8.6.1.1 Health &amp;amp; Safety of the Personnel

One of the main problems hydrogen sulphide causes is in respect to the health and safety and safety of the personnel. A maximum of eight hours exposure to concentrations greater than 100 ppm H2S will cause hemorrhage and death. Concentrations above 600 ppm can be fatal in three to five minutes. Highly stressed, high strength steel can fail in a matter of minutes in the presence of 50 ppm H2S. At high pressure, as little as 0.1 ppm H2S can greatly reduce the time to failure of highly stressed, high strength steel. Relying solely on its odour is not a good idea because at concentrations above 100 ppm it deadens a person’s sense of smell within a few minutes. The pure gas is heavier than air and can collect in low areas such as pit rooms and accommodation. below Table shows the potential hazards hydrogen sulphide can cause to the personnel from shortterm exposures. There are many historical cases to document the ill effects of hydrogen sulphide exposure.

Basically, the term “sulphides” used in oil and gas operations includes all three water-soluble species, H2S, HS- and S2-, which coexist in a sulphide-water system. This then brought about the advent of sulphide scavengers in the history of oil and gas operations. The only safe method for the total removal of hydrogen sulphide or soluble sulphides is with a sulphide scavenger.

8.6.1.1 Effects of Hydrogen Sulphide on Drilling Fluids

The first positive identification of soluble sulphide in the drilling fluids must be taken as a possible indication of H2S entering the fluid from some source. In the simplest case an increase in mud weight may be sufficient to control minor influxes. If levels persist chemical treatment will be required. This can take two forms; neutralization and scavenging. The two terms must not be confused. Neutralization of H2S in drilling fluid by caustic soda or lime is a common field approach. This alkalinity maintenance method has proved successful when small amounts of H2S enter the drilling fluid, for example, from drilling up pore spaces containing the gas.

This is not a suitable approach to the control on influxes of Hydrogen Sulphide. The alkalinity neutralization of H2S is instantly reversible by reduction in pH. Should the pH of the fluid decrease due to further influxes of H2S, Co2 or brine flows the sulphids may come out of solution as hydrogen sulphide gas. To ensure that such influxes are handled safely, it is essential to employ a sulphide scavenger. This term refers to any additive which is capable of reacting with one or more of the sulphide species and as a result, converting them to a more inert form. To be truly effective an irreversible and complete reaction must occur. As a mutual equilibrium exist between the three sulphide species in solution (H2S, HS‐ and S2‐) irreversible and complete removal of one serves to removal all three.

Zinc or iron compounds are usually chosen because of the relative inertness of the sulphids formed. Zinc source (Zinc oxide or carbonate) has in the past been the preferred treatment. However, continuous treatment with Zinc carbonate will produce significant undesirable carbonate concentration (Carbonate contamination) which can adversely effect on drilling fluid rehology and fluid loss. 8.6.1.1 Testing, Reporting, Treatment of Hydrogen Sulphide

The active mud system must be regularly analyzed and monitored for the presence of active soluble Sulphide with the Garrett Gas train. This test must be carried out at the same time as each complete mud check, i.e.: three times per day while drilling.

Alkalinity checks should be carried out intermittently in between these full checks and any significant reduction in the pH and Mf/Pf should be followed up by testing for the presence of active soluble sulphides with the Garrett Gas Train.

For routine checks lead acetate paper can be used to give a qualitative check. Should this test be positive then it must be followed by a qualitative analysis with a Dragger tube.

The following actions must be taken after the initial positive test result:

1. Inform the Drilling Supervisor

2. Start adding H2S Scavenger to the active mud system. Active soluble sulphides can be

analysed and monitored because of their characteristic of readily regenerating hydrogen

Sulphide gas in reaction with mild acid. By adding citric acid to whole mud sample in a

Garrett gas train detection of Hydrogen Sulphide on lead acetate paper indicates the

presence of active Sulphides in the mud. When this qualitative test proves positive a

dragger tube should be used to give qualitative results.

However it must be remembered that pre‐treating the mud with MILGARD Fe means that no Sulphides will be delectable until all the scavenger has reacted, i.e.: it is impossible to detect small influxes of Hydrogen Sulphide in a system pre‐ treating with MILGARD Fe .

8.6.1.1 Contingency Stock to be Kept on Hand on the Rig

The following Contingency stock of treatment chemicals must be kept on hand on the rig over and above the normal mud maintenance material requirements.

Zinc Carbonate or Oxide 120 Sxs 25 kg

Lime 200 Sxs 25 kg

As above mentioned Hydrogen Sulphide is a poisonous and dangerous acidic gas encountered in many formations. It can quickly deaden senses and can be fatal, even at low concentration. Hydrogen Sulphide is characterized by its typical “rotten egg” smell. For safety reasons, it should be neutralized immediately with caustic soda or lime to increase pH to &amp;gt;11.5 to form sulphide (S2‐), then precipitated with a source of Zinc.

Neutralization with caustic soda:

2 NaOH + H2S 2Na+ + S2‐ + 2H2O (at pH&amp;gt;11.5)

South Azadegan Oilfield Project

Contract No:

CCA/C/1401/27 AZNS-127 Re-Entry#01 Program Page 132 of 229

Neutralization with maintaining excess lime:

2 Ca(OH)2 + H2S Ca2+ + S2‐ + 2H2O (at pH&amp;gt;11.5)

Converting Hydrogen Sulphide into just sulphide by increasing pH is not a permanent reaction. If the pH were drop into the acid region, sulphide will be converting back into the poisonous H2S form. For this reasons H2S should always be precipitated by adding a source of Zinc such as Zinc Oxide.

Removal by precipitation with treatments of (ZnO):

H2S + ZnO ZnS + H2O

if H2S gas detected in mud following action should be taken to:

3. Immediately rise up the pH to at least 11.5 to 12 with caustic soda.

4. Buffer the pH with lime.

5. Begin treatment with Zinc oxide to remove sulphide (S2‐) from the system. (1 lb/bbl

treatment of Zinc oxide removes approximately 1100 mg/lit of sulphide. No more than 2

lb/bbl of Zinc oxide should be used to pre‐treat the system for H2S)

If it appears that H2S bleeding in (flowing) form the formation, the mud density should be increased to shut off the flow of gas into the well‐bore.

Hazard &amp;amp; Risk Assessment

The use of chemicals in the workplace presents hazards and risks to personnel involved in their handling and application. In order to minimize these hazards risk assessments are performed and HSE control measures and management systems are established to achieve the following:-

 Identify hazards

 Safely manage those hazards.

 Identify risks

 Where possible, eliminate those risks through control / engineering measures e.g.

ventilation and collection of dust.

 Where not possible, manage those risks through processes including the use of PPE.

 Provide training and awareness systems designed to achieve the above and promote

continuous improvement.

Hazardous Materials

 The effect on a person of a hazardous material depends on:

 The nature of the hazardous material.

 The site of the action.

 The amount of the hazardous material involved (“dose”).

 The reaction of the individual (“susceptibility”).

Hazardous Material Effects

8.7.1.1 Local Effects

 Skin and eye irritation &amp;amp; burns.

 Skin defatting leading to dermatitis.

8.7.1.2 Systemic Effects

 Central nervous system (headaches, nausea, dizziness).

 Cardiovascular system (CO poisoning).

 Sensitisation (allergy) and asthma.

 Teratogenic and carcinogenic.

Chemical hazardous effects may be :

8.8.1.1 DRILLING FLUID FORMULATION

Kill Mud Mixing Procedure:

1. Fill tanks with calculated amount of Drill Water 0.576bbl./bbl.

2. Treat Drill Water with Caustic soda and Soda Ash by 0.3pbb

3. Mix NaCl at 66ppb.

4. Add Xanthan-Gum by 0.2pbb.

5. Add CaCO3-F (325ppb) to reach MW of ±106pcf

 In case of foaming use Alcohol-Based Defoamer.

Note: Use Hi Vis pill to clean hole if necessary.

Calculation is based on per bbl. of mud.

Completion Fluid Mixing Procedure:

1. Make sure that all pits and lines involved with completion fluid are thoroughly cleaned,

flushed and free of any fluid and solid.

 Make sure that at least one large pit is kept empty for transferring ready brine into after

given time for settling. After transferring one pit to empty pit, the first one is to be

flushed and cleaned for accommodating the brine of next ready pit, and so on to the

last pit.

 Depends on the rig facilities and structure, mud engineer on board may find it better

to prepare the fluids pit-by-pit.

2. Transfer the content of CaBr2 drums into designated pits.

South Azadegan Oilfield Project

Contract No:

CCA/C/1401/27 AZNS-127 Re-Entry#01 Program Page 138 of 229

 Record the number of drums poured in each tank for accurate volume in it as the base

of calculation for adding other additives into; do not rely on pit gauge, sounding or

mud logging sensor, but have a look on them for comparison and/or correlation if

found useful.

3. Mix Corrosion Inhibitor into pits at concentration of 3.5pbb (1% by volume).

4. Mix H2S Scavenger Liquid into pits at concentration of 0.5% by Volume.

5. Do not add Oxygen Scavenger CA at this stage as it should be added directly from the top

of the pit, just prior to pump the fluid into the well.

6. Shut down all agitators and mixing pumps, and leave the mixed fluid in the pits for at least

12 hours to let any solid particle inside (mostly insoluble Lime) settles down.

7. Start transferring the clear fluid of the first pit to the empty pit by means of an air-powered

Wilden pump.

 Make sure that the suction hose of the Wilden pump is not put deep close to the bottom

of the pit, otherwise, settled solids are sucked in.

8. After finishing the first pit, stop Wilden pump, wash, flush and clean the pit, use it as the

empty pit for accommodating the fluid of second pit using the and same above method.

Note: all CaBr2 brine inside the well must be retrieved by the time of displacing the well by kill mud. In case of need, filtration must be applied to retrieved amount of CaBr2.

Based on well readings and the operation, mud weight may be varied.

8.8.1.2 DOWNHOLE LOSSES

As perforation had been done in well AZN#85 &amp;amp; there is exposure to reservoir, risk of any probable formation losses must be taken into consideration.

Losses will be minimized/avoided by the planned use of properly sized bridging/weight material (and Polymer) in conjunction with appropriate drilling practices. If seepage losses are noted on the well no specific action will be taken but close monitoring of the loss rate is to be made. For moderate loss rates addition of CaCO3 50 micron and 150 micron is recommended to ensure that there is adequate correctly sized material to act as bridging agents.

Seepage losses Less than 10 bbl. /hr.

No specific action will be taken, but close monitoring of the probable loss rate is made.

Losses from 10-30 bbl. /hr.

 Load CaCO3-M (150-300 micron) in system up to 5ppb

*If loss not cured and even tends to increase, then:

 Pump 40-60bbl of pill made by 7-10ppb CaCO3 150-300μ &amp;amp; 7-10ppb CaCO3 600μ

Losses from 30-50 bbl. /hr.

Losses more than 100 bbl/hr.

High concentrated LCM pill of various sizes of Calcium Carbonate and Oyster Shell-F&amp;amp;M&amp;amp;C should be pumped and spotted and gently squeezed over the loss zone.

Spotting Procedure

1. After spotting LCM pill, pull the bit above the calculated top of the pill. Wait 30 minutes

and monitor the annulus.

2. After 30 minutes, attempt to fill the annulus, if not already full. If the hole can be filled,

close BOP and squeeze 10bbl LCM pill into formation without exceeding 200psi.

3. If the hole remains stable, continue to drill ahead.

4. Should the LCM pill fail to reduce the losses or the hole cannot be filled, then mix and

spot another 50bbl of LCM pill.

5. Attempt to fill the annulus. If successful, close the BOP and squeeze 20bbl of LCM pill

into the formation without exceeding 200psi.

South Azadegan Oilfield Project

Contract No:

CCA/C/1401/27 AZNS-127 Re-Entry#01 Program Page 140 of 229

6. If a squeeze pressure develops, hold the pressure for 1 hour before running the drill string

back to bottom.

Notes:

 LCM pills must be thoroughly homogenised and viscous enough before being pumped.

 Pumping high-concentrated LCM pill is subject to use of open-end DP or Mule-Shoe.

 Remove filter screens from the drill pipe (if there is any) and if necessary, remove

strainers from the mud pump suction lines.

10. Casing Program

10.1 Material Selection

Casing, Liner and Tubing Material selection for South Azadegan oilfield will be describe in the following.

Corrosive Environment Analysis and Strength Check

Based on the data of offset wells in this oilfield, there is a certain degree of corrosive problems in the 4 layers to be produced. Corrosive medium is principally composed of 2 parts: one is the corrosive gases like H2S and CO2 existing in the produced fluid; and the other is the high salinity formation water. The contents of main corrosive fluids in offset wells are shown in below Table:

1) Corrosion in this oilfield is a result of combined action of H2S, CO2 and

high salinity formation water. The corrosive mechanism is complicated, and

the corrosive rate on the casing is difficult to determine. Based on the NACE

standard and the data from the Table, the producers result in severe corrosive

environment. However, by the research on development conditions and

technical indices, it can be found that although the corrosive fluid contents

are high in the oilfield, the corrosive environment is not extremely serious

as the following reasons:

2) In general, the temperature that cause the SSC/SCC is concentrated in the

range from 20℃ to 30℃. The average depth of the horizontal section is

2,730m with the reservoir temperature of 96℃, and tensional stress on the

South Azadegan Oilfield Project

Contract No:

CCA/C/1401/27 AZNS-127 Re-Entry#01 Program Page 148 of 229

casing does not exist in the horizontal section. Therefore, the influence of

SSC/SCC may not be considered for the casing/liner.

3) Based on the RMDP, the production GOR in the first development phase

should not be higher than the initial GOR, therefore, the flowing pressure is

higher than the bubble point pressure all the time, that is, degassing problems

do not exist in the horizontal section and some vertical section, the H2S and

CO2 have no chance of separation out of oil phase, and it is lack of

prerequisite for casing corrosion.

4) Based on above all, the corrosive environment of the casing string is not

severe. The optimal selection for the casing string can be stated briefly as

follows.

Material Selection of Casing String

In this oilfield, the corrosion of production string obviously occurs in 2 regions. One is the region where the pressure is above the bubble point; in which degassing problems do not exist, and the corrosion environment is relatively weak. Another one is the region where the pressure is below the bubble point; because of the decline of pressure, the concentration of corrosive gas will increase and the corrosion is relatively serious. Considering the corrosive environment is not serious in the low water cut production stage and the production practice in this oilfield has proved the L80 is fit for it, So, the L80 should be taken as the material of 9-5/8″ casing, 7″, 5 1/2″ and 4-1/2″ liner. In order to prevent the hazard of gas leakage after production degassing occurs, 9-5/8″ casing, 7″ and 4-1/2″ liner should be Gas tight thread. 2) The 110S is selected as the material of 9-5/8″, 7″ and4-1/2″ casing rather than L-80 due to the high strength requirement in Fahliyan wells, what’s more the 110S is fit for sour gas environment

C. Selection of PR (Performance Requirement)

According to API Specification 6A 19th edition, performance requirements are specific and unique to the product in the as-shipped condition. All products shall be designed to perform according to the requirements of API 6A clauses 4 and clauses 10 while in the pressure and temperature ranges and corrosion environment. Other requirements include load capability, cycles, and operating force or torque. There are two performance requirement levels: PR1 and PR2. Valves operating as safety valves shall be of the PR2 performance level and meet the requirements of Annex I in API 6A For SA wells, the guideline for PR selection is that all parts not contacting well fluids in normal production period are PR1, all parts contacting well fluids are PR2 as follow, Casing head housing and casing head spool assembly - PR1. Tubing head spool, tubing hanger and X-mas tree - PR2.

12. Waste Management Program

12.1 Drilling Waste Management Design

The contractor is responsible for designing the optimum practices for treating the produced waste during the operation. The initial technical waste management proposal should be included the practices for minimizing, treating and recovering of the wastes.

According to the below categories:

. Water based mud containing minerals and natural synthetic polymers, and

. Cuttings contaminated with WBM.

The contractor is encouraged to offer possible practices to minimize the drilling fluids waste and its regeneration.

Water based mud containing minerals, naturals and synthetic polymers

. Primary operation

The proposed primary solids control package should be able to control drilling fluid properties, reducing of mud materials usage against conventional solid control equipment's, and significantly reduce the number of excess fluids generated throughout drilling each phase of the well.

. Secondary Operation

All excess mud and spillage (water based) should be collected in rig site pits and free surface fluid should be treated using a built for propose flocculation station (has to join with centrifuge) consisting of integral dosing and pumps along with a centrifuge for efficient, quick and controlled separation of the solids before the cleaned fluids is returned to active system or buffer tanks.

This system should be able to remove colloidal sized particles that cannot be removed with primary solids control system.

This system may use to clean up the remaining water-based mud or decrease weight of oil base mud at the end of the drilling fluids programmed.

11.1.2 Cuttings contaminated with WBM

Spud mud and water-based mud cuttings should be fixed and be ready for transport to disposal zone. For fixing the cutting, 100-150 kg cement shall be used for each cubic meters of cutting as well as 3-4-liter Sodium Silicate for each cubic meter of cutting. (Consumption of cement and sodium silicate varies in different formations). Gypsum is not allowed for cutting fixation.

South Azadegan Oilfield Project

This method is physically Bonds Contaminants to Prevent Leaching to Environment. Final product will pass can test and in case of approval by company man it’ll send to landfill.

12.2 Waste discharge and handling

High Performance Filter Unit

Filtration plays an important role in the natural treatment of waste water as it percolates through the soil. It is also a major part of most water treatment. Groundwater that has been softened, or treated through iron and manganese oxidation, requires filtration to remove floc created by coagulation or oxidation processes. Since surface water is subject to run-off and does not undergo natural filtration.

it must be filtered to remove particles and impurities. Filtration can be compared to a sieve or micro- strainer that traps suspended material between the grains of filter media. However, since most suspended particles can easily pass through the spaces between grains of the filter media, straining is the least important process in filtration. Filtration primarily depends on a combination of complex physical and chemical mechanisms, the most important being adsorption. Adsorption is the process of particles sticking onto the surface of the individual filter grains or onto the previously deposited materials. Forces that attract and hold particles to the grains are the same as those that work in coagulation and flocculation. In fact, coagulation and flocculation may occur in the filter bed, especially if coagulation and flocculation before filtration was not properly controlled. Incomplete coagulation can cause serious problems in filter operation.

13.8 Well Control

1. Installation Requirements of BOP Stack and Control System:

 The distance between BOP control lines and relief lines shall be not less than

1m. Steel Gap Bridge should be placed in such a way to protect lines from

damage by vehicle crossing. Sundries shall not be packed on the control line

shield, on which welding operations are forbidden.

 The air supply shall be separated from that of driller’s console and directly

connected to the main air supply system, and shall be equipped with liquid/gas

separators. Excessive bending and pinching on air hoses are forbidden.

 Electric power to BOP control system shall be directly from the main switch of

the power board, and controlled by independent switches.

 Accumulators shall be in good condition, charged at its rated value, and ready

for work at any time.

2. Installation Requirements of Choke Lines and Kill Lines, and Relief Lines:

a) Beside the drilling spool, one manual and one HCR gate valves on the side of

chock manifold and two manual gate valves on the side of kill manifold shall

be equipped, and the manual gate valve close to the spool shall be always open.

b) The high-pressure co-flex hose shall be installed as straight as possible and

fixed by anchor after installation.

c) Relief lines (burning line and bleed line):

 No field welding is permitted on relief lines and the connecting style of relief

lines must be flanged.

 The arrangement of relief lines shall take wind directions, dwellings, roads, oil

tank areas, power lines and other facilities into consideration.

 While the two lines go in the same trend, the distance between the lines shall

be at least 0.3m, and the two lines shall be fixed independently.

 The outlets of bleed line connecting with choke manifold shall be in a safe area

which is at least 300m. The bleed line on the kill manifold side connecting with

drilling spool shall be prepared and connected when necessary (about 70m from

the wellhead).

 At every 10m~15m, turning points, and outlets, the lines shall be supported and

fixed by cement foundations with anchor bolts or ground anchors. Hanging

South Azadegan Oilfield Project

Contract No:

CCA/C/1401/27 AZNS-127 Re-Entry#01 Program Page 205 of 229

portions shall be supported firmly. If crossing the stumbling blocks such as

brooks or ponds is needed, metal bridging supports are necessary.

 Pre-buried anchor bolts for cement foundations shall not be less than 20mm or

3/4" in diameter, and greater than 0.5m in length.

3. Pressure test value and requirements:

a) A pressure test shall be conducted successfully where there is no pressure

decline in 5 minutes for a low-pressure test and a minimum of 10 minutes for a

high-pressure test.

b) Prior to each high-pressure test, a low-pressure test with 200-300 psi shall be

carried out to verify sealing capability at the circumstance of low pressure and

avoid washing out sealing elements.

c) High pressure test should be to the rated working pressure of ram preventers or

the rated working pressure of the wellhead, whichever is the lowest, or to the

rating required in DRILLING ROGRAM. Variable bore rams should be

initially pressure tested on the largest and smallest OD pipe sizes that may be

used during the OPERATION. Annular preventers, with a joint of drill pipe

installed, should be tested to 70% of their working pressure. The high test for

Kelly cocks, kill lines and choke lines should be to their rated working

pressures, each part in the choke manifold is tested respectively to its rated

working pressures, the relief lines be pressure tested to no less than 1,450psi

(10Mpa).

d) When casing cup tester is used, the above test pressure should not exceed 80%

of the internal yield pressure (burst pressure) of the exposed casing.

e) The control system of BOP shall be pressure tested to 3,000psi (21Mpa) for its

reliability before putting into use.

f) Except that the BOP control system is tested with hydraulic oil, other well

control equipment shall be pressure tested by clear water.

g) Testing tools

 All required sizes of the plug type testers, and cup type testers should be

available for pressure testing purpose.

 When the cup type tester(s) is used for pressure test, the connection of the cup

testers has to be checked, to ensure it will stand the load during the high

pressures test. For surface casing, the cup tester is to be set in middle of the first

casing joint in the top, so the first casing connection (between wellhead and

South Azadegan Oilfield Project

Contract No:

CCA/C/1401/27 AZNS-127 Re-Entry#01 Program Page 206 of 229

casing head housing) below the well head is to be tested too while testing BOP

and wellhead.

4. Pressure test frequency:

All ram type preventers, annular BOP, valves, choke and kill lines, choke manifold, Kelly valves and safety valves should be pressure tested at the following frequencies:

 Prior to installation where possible.

 After installation of wellhead and BOP assembly and prior to drilling.

 After the disconnection or repair of any pressure containment seal in the BOP

stack, choke line, or choke manifold, but limited to the affected component.

 Prior to drilling into a confirmed or suspected high-pressure zone.

 At any time requested by the COMPANY REPRESENTATIVE.

 In any case, every one month or during the first trip after the one-month interval

with a maximum interval of 45 days. This frequency is not required for shear

rams. As a minimum, the shear rams are to be tested prior to resume drilling

operation after 9-5/8” casing string has been set and adequate WOC.

5. Work Requirement of Well Control Equipment:

 With shut-in casing pressure lower than 1000psi, while snubbing with annular

preventer, drill tools shall have 18-deg shoulder tool joints, and the snubbing

velocity shall not be greater than 0.2m/s.

 After shut off the annular preventer or ram preventer, with the shut-in casing

pressure not greater than 2000psi, drill tools are allowed to pull up and down

with the velocity less than 0.2m/s, however, rotating or tool joint passing

through are forbidden.

 While drilling through pay zone and thereafter, BOP function (close-open) test

for the BOPs shall be performed regularly.

 Kill manifolds shall not be used for drilling fluid fill-in.

 The maximum allowed shut-in casing pressure shall be remarkably indicated

on choke manifolds.

 All gate valves of well control manifolds shall be tagged with serial numbers,

and be indicated with on/Off.

South Azadegan Oilfield Project

Contract No:

CCA/C/1401/27 AZNS-127 Re-Entry#01 Program Page 207 of 229

 In case shear rams were used, after shearing the drill pipe with shear rams,

retrieve the upper sheared drill pipe, lower a drill pipe joint with TIW valve

installed into the hole and close pipe rams on it to prevent the possibility of

shear ram’s failure.

6. Management of Well Control Equipment:

 Well control equipment used by the drilling crew shall be managed and

operated by designated personnel with clear post responsibilities.

 Well site shall have specified component storeroom and rubber element

storeroom with air conditioners respectively. The temperature of storerooms

shall meet storage requirements of components and rubber elements.

 At least 1 set is available as back-up for every type ram assembly in the well

site. Ram preventer side door seals and ram rubber, every type gasket and bolt

etc. should be enough for backup.

7. Killing Method and Shut-in Method:

 Driller's method is recommended for well killing.

 The hard Shut-in method is recommended for shutting in the well in Fahliyan

reservoir.

8. Well Control during drilling:

a) Shut in Procedure in While on Bottom

 Position Kelly (if in use) and tool joint so that tool joints are clear of sealing

elements.

 Shut off pumps, check for flow.

 If flow is noted, close the annular preventer and open remote-controlled choke

line valve (HCR).

 If the well has been closed using the annular preventer, check space out (pipe

rams vs. toll joint relative position) and close pipe rams and ram locks

 Bleed off pressure between pipe rams and annular preventer (if possible).

 Record shut-in drill pipe and casing pressures.

 Record volume gain and mark pits.

 Weigh mud in suction pits.

 Check blowout preventer and manifold for leaks.

 Check flowline and choke exhaust for flow.

 Check accumulator pressure.

South Azadegan Oilfield Project

Contract No:

CCA/C/1401/27 AZNS-127 Re-Entry#01 Program Page 208 of 229

b) Shut in Procedure in While Tripping

 If a flow is detected, install full opening safety valve and close same.

 Position tool joints clear of the sealing elements and close annular preventer

and open remote-controlled choke line valve (HCR).

 Make up grey valve (dart type inside BOP on full open safety valve). Then

Make up Kelly or top drive (insert a pup joint or single between safety valve

and top drive) and open safety valve.

 Record casing pressure.

 Check blowout preventer, stack, and manifold for leaks.

 Check valves for correct position.

 Check accumulator pressure.

 Begin stripping to bottom.

c) Shut in Procedure for Empty Wells

 Try to RIH with drill pipe as more as possible if hole condition permits, and the

drill pipe must be installed a Kelly cock or safety valve.

 Close the annular preventer and open remote-controlled choke line valve

(HCR).

 If the well has been closed using the annular preventer, check space out (pipe

rams vs. tool joint relative position) and close pipe rams and ram locks

 Bleed off pressure between pipe rams and annular preventer (jf possible).

 Record casing pressure

9. Well Control During Running Casing:

The well control while running casing is important and critical, best practices shall be followed, including but not limited to:

 Change out pipe rams to casing rams prior to running casing into hydrocarbon

bearing formation, if possible.

 The crossover between casing and drill pipe has to be available, and good

practice is to make it up with a joint of DP and keep on V-door.

10. Shut in Procedure During Logging:

Cable shall be pull out of the hole immediately when overflow is found during logging. If pit gain exceeds the specified amount, the cable shall be cut immediately and treat the overflow in accordance with the shut-in procedure for empty wells. Continuing to pull the cable through the closed annular preventer is not recommended.

11. Well Control During Testing:

South Azadegan Oilfield Project

Contract No:

CCA/C/1401/27 AZNS-127 Re-Entry#01 Program Page 209 of 229

 No difference to while DRILLING OPERATION, since either there is testing

string in the well (same as Shut-in procedure while on bottom), or tripping the

string. (Same as shut-in procedure while tripping).

 Likely there is some crude in the testing string, and precaution has to be taken

while circulating the crude out of hole during killing operations to ensure it is

properly handled without causing environmental impact.

 To minimize the formation damage, the killing fluids used shall be weighted

brine if possible, however in well control case when it occurs, killing well safely

will take priority rather than protecting formation from damage on selection of

killing fluids.

12. Well Control During Stimulation:

 Similar to during testing.

 For any residual or alive acid to be circulated out during killing operations,

measures have to be taken to treat the returned acid properly to avoid personnel

from getting hurt, and without causing any environmental damage.

13. Well Control Drills:

Drills shall be conducted only when hole conditions and other rig activities permit. Drills should be scheduled so that crews can practice drills while on bottom, while tripping in and while out of the hole. Each operating shift shall perform at least one BOP drill under different situations per month.

14. Basic Requirement of Well Control:

 For 13-5/8”, 10K BOP, BOP should be schemed as follows: upper rams 5”,

middle rams are shear rams, lower rams is variable rams (2-7/8” to 5”). For

easily connecting, armored fire-resistant 10000psi and ID 4-1/16" flexible

hoses are recommended as kill/choke lines which connected with BOP directly.

 The BOP stack and choke manifold, kill line and choke line, HCR and manual

gate valves, inside BOP (including kelly cock) have to be H2S trimmed and

stand the working temperature from -10 degrees C (in case of doing N2 for

DST) to the maximum up to 100 deg C (estimated highest temperature

condition).

 The BOP equipment shall be visually inspected, function tested, and

hydrostatically pressure tested during commissioning and Acceptance of

Drilling Unit prior to Commencement Date, then upon installation on a

wellhead, prior to drilling any hole section with a potential hydrocarbon bearing

reservoir, after breaking any BOP connection (such as after installation of an

South Azadegan Oilfield Project

Contract No:

CCA/C/1401/27 AZNS-127 Re-Entry#01 Program Page 210 of 229

additional wellhead section after running casing), and at least every 14-21 days

while the BOP is installed on the Well.

 CONTRACTOR shall submit the current well control procedures manual of

CONTRACTOR to COMPANY for review and approval by COMPANY.

Valid IWCF Well Control Certificates (or IADC equivalent) must be held by

all tool pushers, Drillers (optional) at Drilling Supervisor level and Drillers and

Assistant Drillers at Driller level, as further specified in CONTRACTOR

Personnel HSE Requirements.

 The accumulator must be of sufficient capacity so that it is possible to close one

(1) ram and the bag, open a ram and the bag, re-close a ram and the bag and

retain 1200psi accumulator pressure.

 The “OPEN” and “CLOSED” operating positions of BOP activators of the

rams, annular, and remote actuated valves must be clearly identified on the BOP

master control panel and remote panels, in English in addition to the native

language of the majority of the senior drilling crew.

 Shear-ram BOP activator must have a flap-cover to ensure only pre-meditated

and deliberated activation and to prevent accidental WORK.

 All lines and connections in the choke and kill manifold, standpipe manifold,

choke and kill lines and high-pressure mud lines should be welded hard-piping

with weld-on FMC Weco “hammer-lug” 1502 unions (or Western equivalent,

such as Anson) or weld-on API flanges. The well control system should not

include any threaded screw-on hammer-lug unions, flanges, or other threaded

screw-on connections.

 All adapter or spacer spools between the wellhead and BOP must be

manufactured in accordance with API 6A, and must be complete with all

required studs, nuts, and ring gasket seals for both lower and upper connections;

minimum spare parts should include two (2) OEM spare studs complete with

nuts and two spare OEM ring gasket seals for both bottom and top connections.

 There should be a wide-bore gas vent line from the “poor-boy” degasser; the

line and line outlet must be securely anchored, the line outlet must be a safe

distance from the well cellar, rig floor, choke manifold, and mud logging unit.

 Well Control Equipment Welding: All welds in the well control system must

be NDT inspected and records maintained of all welding and weld inspections,

including choke and kill manifold, standpipe manifold, mud pump discharge

manifold, choke and kill lines.

 Well Control Rig Floor Information: The following must be posted on the rig

floor (in the Driller’s shack / “dog-house”): Well Shut-In Procedure, Well

Information Sheet (showing casing and hole sizes, depths, and such like), Kill

Sheet (including most recent slow circulation rate pressures, formation integrity

CCA/C/1401/27 AZNS-127 Re-Entry#01 Program Page 211 of 229

leak-off test information and MAASP, present mud weight, present drill string

and well volumes, and such like).

 The derrick substructure clear height (rotary table to ground level) needs to be

enough for fitting in above BOP configuration (including a tubing head and a

bell nipple). This need to be double checked in rig tender process. According to

the calculation of height of BOP stack, the substructure clear height is at least

9 m.

 In the case if drilling 6-1/8" hole becomes necessary, or using 3-1/2" drill pipe

for the cleanup run (including drill 7" shoe track), then taper drilling string (5"

DP + 3-1/2" DP) is to be run, so a pair variable ram be installed in the single

ram preventer. The defect installing variable ram in single ram preventer is that

the ram may be damaged and the string fall in hole bottom due to the ram

hanging up too much weight when the drill pipe be cut. If the pipe ram be

installed in the single ram preventer and the variable ram be installed in the

double ram preventer, it would be very dangerous due to the variable ram failure

in frequently using.

13.9 H2S Monitoring and Prevention Measure

As per PPL/PEDEC SOW South Azadegan oilfield contains H2S bearing formations, precautions shall be taken in place especially in 12-1/4” &amp;amp; 8-1/2” hole section (for typical Fahliyan vertical well) while drilling, completion and well testing operation.

H2S can be released any time while drilling, completion and well testing operation, therefore:

 The Rig shall be prepared for H2S (Training, procedures and protective gear).

 Make sure everyone on the Rig should be made aware of the hazard presented

by H2S during their induction when they first arrive on the rig.

 The mud shall be treated to protect the drill pipe and the casing.

 All training program shall be recorded and reported.

 H2S emergency drill must be conducted frequently.

 Adequate sensors and alarms must be installed for the scope of monitoring

the H2S releases.

1. General Information

1.1 Field Introduction

Azadegan South Oil Field is located in West Karoun province on a large long-axis anticline with N-S trending with approximate dimensions about 20km width &amp;amp; 60km length near to Iran-Iraq border, to the east of Yaran Oil Field.

The trap area of the south Azadegan is limited to 43.2x17.2km The Azadegan Oil field was discovered in 1999, when Well AZN-1 was drilled vertically down to the Cretaceous Fahliyan Formation with total depth of 4,643m. The results of this well, revealed the reservoir characteristics of the field. Following to the result of the well No. AZN-1, another 5 exploration wells was drilled in different parts of this huge field down to Fahliyan Formation. In the later stage the well No.10 assumed as exploration well for evaluation of deeper formations. This well was drilled in 2008, down to the depth of 5340m (Neyriz Fm.), mainly to evaluate the Jurassic formations.

Based on the exploration wells results, carbonate reservoir of Sarvak Formation is broadly developed in Azadegan Field. This formation was penetrated in all of seven exploration wells (AZN-1, AZN-2, AZN- 3, AZN-4, AZN-5, AZN-6 &amp;amp; AZN-10). Clastic oil-bearing zones of Kazhdumi Formation developed in main anticline of Azadegan Field, extending from north to center of South Azadegan. The Clastic oilbearing zones of Gadvan Formation developed only in crest area &amp;amp; south parts of South Azadegan Filed, which was discovered by AZN-1 in crest &amp;amp; AZN-4 in south parts. The carbonates of Fahliyan Formation also developed in Azadegan field, but the oil reservoir of this formation developed in South part of South Azadegan.

The Azadegan Field is an elongated anticline, trending in N-S direction, belonging to "Arabian Trend".

The stratigraphy sequence of the field includes AghaJari, Gachsaran, Fahliyan, Pabdeh, Gurpi, Ilam, Laffan, Sarvak, Kazhdumi, Dariyan, Gadvan &amp;amp; Fahliyan Formations, from top to bottom. This sequence in well no AZN-10, the deepest up to now drilled well of the field, continues with Garau, Gotnia, Najmah, Sargalu, Alan, Mus &amp;amp; Neyriz formations.

The Dominant lithofacies of Sarvak Formation are Rudist-bearing packstone &amp;amp; partially grainstone, which contains abundant bioclasts. Some other facies like matrix-dominated wackestone &amp;amp; mudstone are also found.

The AZADEGAN Oilfield is Located in Khuzestan Province &amp;amp; is Approximately Located 80 Kilometers West of Ahwaz City, near to Iran-Iraq Border. It is in The Northwest of The YADAVARAN Field &amp;amp; in The West of JUFEYR Field. The Average Monthly Temperature is 45ºc in summer, &amp;amp; Highest Temperature is 52ºc. The Lowest Temperature is -4.4ºc in winter. Maximum Rainfall is 78mm in February, Winter Season.

This Document covers the work over of well AZNS-85. Main headlines of program are perform 7" tieback liner lap dry test &amp;amp; complete the well for Fahliyan production. The well was drilled to the final depth of 4090m (Fahliyan Formation) on 2014 by NISOC to produce oil from Fahliyan formation.

Block I is located on the north part of the CONTRACT AREA in north of well AZN-010. Gachsaran formation is characterized by abnormal high pressure in this block.

Block II is located between well AZN-010 &amp;amp; AZN-011. In this block, Gachsaran formation is characterized by pressure tending to normal.

Block III is located on the south of line well AZN-011. In this block, Gachsaran formation is characterized by normal pressure &amp;amp; all drilled wells in this block suffered from complete loss at Pabdeh formation.

1.7 Drilling History

The AZNS-85 (Pad 79) was drilled by rig 86 Fath, which rig moving was spudded on 15-07-1394 @ 00:00.

 26" hole section drilling to 152m, run 20" casing to 150m (J-55, 133#, BTC) &amp;amp; cement job as

program with 60bbl cement return, Mw 68pcf.

 17-1/2" hole was drilled to 1279m, while increase mud weight f/67 to 85pcf, run 13-3/8" casing (N-

80, BTS, 72#, f/0 to 1099.15m &amp;amp; NKT, BTS, 72#, f/1099.5m to 1279m) &amp;amp; cement job as program

with 180bbl cement return.

 12-1/4" hole section was drilled to 3237m with 6-150BPH loss while pumping LCM Pill &amp;amp; bypass

system, take full set log, continue drilling to 3367m with 20-150BPH loss while pumping LCM Pill

&amp;amp; bypass system, complete loss pump LCM Pill several time, decrease Mw f/80 to 77pcf, hole

condition &amp;amp; While condition stuck string &amp;amp; complete loss, work on stuck &amp;amp; free pipes, pump

LCM Pill &amp;amp; increase Mw to 70pcf, drilling to 3361m, flow the well, twist-off string, fish left hole

f/3029.37m to 3496.85m (12-1/4" PDC bit, bit sub, 9 Jts D.C, 8" Jar, 3 Jts 8-1/2" D.C, XOS, 36 Jts

5" DPs), fish recovered, increase Mw to 78pcf, drilling to 3950m, take log as program, run 9-5/8"

casing (L-80, 53.5#, VAM f/0 to 1844m &amp;amp; 110SS, 47#, TPCQ f/1844m to 3950m) &amp;amp; cement job as

program, no cement return.

 The hole section 8-1/2" was drilled to 3957m, take CBL/VDL/CCL/GR log from 9-5/8" casing,

drilling to 4034m, increase Mw to 101pcf due to flow well, drilling to 4090m (TD), suddenly well

flow (20BPH total gain 30BPH oil &amp;amp; gas in mud; 92pcf) increasing Mw to 103pcf, run 7" liner

(VM110SS, 35#, N.VAM) to 4090m, pressure test &amp;amp; inject 150bbl cement in 9-5/8" casing @

3103m, dry test 7" liner lap was OK, take CBL/VDL/CCL/GR log from 7" liner, set cement plug

f/3882m to 3650m &amp;amp; test 9-5/8" casing was not OK, take CAST log f/3648m to 1200m in 9-5/8"

casing, observe tear 9-5/8" casing f/3157m to 3140m, first tie back 7" liner to 3829m (L-80, 29#,

HSM1), dry test 7" liner lap was not OK, second tie back 7" liner lap to 2903m (L-80, 29#,

VAM), set cement plugs f/3879m to 3663m &amp;amp; f/2903m to 2763m, suspension well without

completion string &amp;amp; release rig @ 1395-02-27.

R/U &amp;amp; RIH with SL, retrieve protection sleeve, POOH &amp;amp; R/D SL.

5. Sequence of Operation

5.1 Main Objective

Base on well condition, the decision has been made to perform 7" tied-back liner lap dry test &amp;amp;

Main plan

1. Held PJSM. Spud the Rig. Stand back required 5" DPs, 5" HWDPs and 6-1/2" DC.

2. Check the wellhead for any damage or leakage. Record well head pressures; check the all annulus

pressure. Check the return fluid &amp;amp; Bleed off any annulus pressure to Zero upon client’s approval

and recheck the well status.

Note: If wellhead pressure is not ZERO after bleed off, contractor shall inform client. Remedial plan to be prepared in advance by operators &amp;amp; will be followed after client's confirmation.

3. RIH with tubing hanger retrieving tool &amp;amp; engage with TBH. Pull out with TBH to surface.

4. N/U BOP and pressure test. Perform wellhead pressure integrity test with cup tester.

5. RIH with 8-1/2" D/O BHA to top of cement plug.

6. Drill out cement plug to 7" liner lap f/2768m to 2903m (take care of lap@ 2903m), POOH.

7. RIH with 5-7/8" clean-out BHA to top of cement @ 3663m &amp;amp; tag, CBU till shakers clean, POOH.

8. RIH with tandem scraper 9-5/8" * 7", scrape inside 9-5/8" casing &amp;amp; 7" liner (dry test packer

setting depths), CBU &amp;amp; POOH.

9. Perform BOP test.

10. RIH with wireline SBT/VDL/CCL/GR Logging tools to bottom, log up to surface (in two separate

runs for 9-5/8" CSG &amp;amp; 7" Liner), POOH.

11. RIH with wireline corrosion logging tools to bottom, log up to surface (in two separate runs for 9-

5/8" CSG &amp;amp; 7" Liner), POOH.

12. RIH with 9-5/8" RTTS packer &amp;amp; perform 7" liner lap dry test, POOH.

Note: If dry test is not OK, follow contingency plan #1.

13. Perform BOP test.

14. RIH with 5-7/8" D/O BHA (3-1/2" DPs JT by JT), drill-out cement plug inside 7" liner f/3663m

to 3879m, continue RIH to 4070m LDC, CBU till shakers clean, POOH to surface.

15. RIH with 7" scraper, scrape inside 7" liner, CBU till shakers clean, displace inside 7" liner with

non-solid fluid, POOH to surface.

16. Run perforation gun assembly &amp;amp; perforate 7" liner in Fah-2a (4031m to 4045m) &amp;amp; Fah-3a

(4057m to 4061m) tentatively, POOH to surface.

17. RIH with GR-CCL log to confirm perforation intervals.

18. Perform BOP test.

Contract No:

CCA/C/1401/27

AZNS-85 Workover Program

Project P/T Zone Dep. Disc. Type Sequence Rev. Page 26 of 65

SAC P IIIF85 DR DE PRG 0001 00

19. RIH with 7" scraper to scrape completion packer area &amp;amp; displace the well with non-solid as

completion fluid, POOH to surface &amp;amp; L/D DP's &amp;amp; DC's.

20. Run 10K completion string as per program.

21. Set TWCV inside TBH, N/D BOP &amp;amp; install 10K XMT, pressure test same.

22. Secure the well by set BPV in TBG Hanger, close all X-mas Tree valves except BMV, and

Release the Rig.

23. Retrieve TWCV, RIH with SL, set protection sleeve, retrieve Plug &amp;amp; Prong from NO-GO landing

nipple, POOH.

24. RIH with CT to bottom, displace the well with diesel, POOH.

25. R/U &amp;amp; RIH with SL, retrieve protection sleeve, POOH &amp;amp; R/D SL.

26. Flow the well as pre-acid clean-up till acceptable BSW &amp;amp; reading stable flow rate on 2 different

choke size for 72 hrs.

27. R/U &amp;amp; RIH with SL, set protection sleeve, POOH &amp;amp; R/D SL.

28. RIH with CT &amp;amp; perform acid wash as per program, POOH to surface.

29. R/U &amp;amp; RIH with SL, retrieve protection sleeve, POOH &amp;amp; R/D SL.

30. Flow the well as post-acid clean-up till acceptable BSW &amp;amp; reading stable flow rate on 2 different

choke size for minimum 96 hrs.

Note: The time is only for flowing duration (R/U, R/D time &amp;amp; preparation is excluded.

Note: Acidizing &amp;amp; post-acid clean-up maybe perform as rigless job upon contractor &amp;amp; client approval but in case of any failure in well integrity, contractor should provide drilling rig &amp;amp; required services in own responsibility &amp;amp; fix the problem.

31. Flow the well as post-acid clean-up till acceptable BSW &amp;amp; reading stable flow rate on 2 different

choke size for minimum 96 hrs.

32. RIH with SL, set protection sleeve.

33. RIH with CT to bottom &amp;amp; displace the well with diesel, POOH.

34. RIH with SL, install Plug &amp;amp; Prong into NO-Go landing nipple, POOH.

35. RIH with SL, retrieve protection sleeve.

36. Secure the well by set BPV in TBG Hanger, close all X-mas Tree valves except BMV.

5.2 Contingency Plan

Based on operation situation in each step, the following contingency plans might be followed.

5.2.1 Contingency Plan #1

Install liner SN-packer on top of 7" liner lap and set completion packer above 7'' lower Liner lap@ 3012m.

7.1.2.1 Mud type

Kill mud 106pcf will be used to kill the well and well will be displaced by Completion fluid of CaBr2 106pcf. Attention must be paid that there is Calcium Bromide Brine inside the well and all of them must be retrieved in separated mud tank by the time of displacing the well by kill mud. (As what the hole dictates, mud properties may be varied by the time).

7.1.2.3 Drilling Fluid Formulation

Kill Mud Mixing Procedure:

1. Fill tanks with calculated amount of Drill Water 0.576bbl./bbl.

2. Treat Drill Water with Caustic soda and Soda Ash by 0.3pbb

3. Mix NaCl at 66ppb.

4. Add Xanthan-Gum by 0.2pbb.

5. Add CaCO3-F (325ppb) to reach MW of ±106pcf

 In case of foaming use Alcohol-Based Defoamer.

Note: Use Hi Vis pill to clean hole if necessary.

Calculation is based on per bbl. of mud.

Completion Fluid Mixing Procedure:

1. Make sure that all pits and lines involved with completion fluid are thoroughly cleaned,

flushed and free of any fluid and solid.

 Make sure that at least one large pit is kept empty for transferring ready brine into after

given time for settling. After transferring one pit to empty pit, the first one is to be flushed

and cleaned for accommodating the brine of next ready pit, and so on to the last pit.

 Depends on the rig facilities and structure, mud engineer on board may find it better to

prepare the fluids pit-by-pit.

2. Transfer the content of CaBr2 drums into designated pits.

 Record the number of drums poured in each tank for accurate volume in it as the base of

calculation for adding other additives into; do not rely on pit gauge, sounding or mud

logging sensor, but have a look on them for comparison and/or correlation if found useful.

3. Mix Corrosion Inhibitor into pits at concentration of 3.5pbb (1% by volume).

4. Mix H2S Scavenger Liquid into pits at concentration of 0.5% by Volume.

5. Do not add Oxygen Scavenger CA at this stage as it should be added directly from the top of

the pit, just prior to pump the fluid into the well.

6. Shut down all agitators and mixing pumps, and leave the mixed fluid in the pits for at least 12

hours to let any solid particle inside (mostly insoluble Lime) settles down.

7. Start transferring the clear fluid of the first pit to the empty pit by means of an air-powered

Wilden pump.

 Make sure that the suction hose of the Wilden pump is not put deep close to the bottom of

the pit, otherwise, settled solids are sucked in.

8. After finishing the first pit, stop Wilden pump, wash, flush and clean the pit, use it as the

empty pit for accommodating the fluid of second pit using the and same above method.

Note: all CaBr2 brine inside the well must be retrieved by the time of displacing the well by kill mud. In case of need, filtration must be applied to retrieved amount of CaBr2.

Based on well readings and the operation, mud weight may be varied.

7.1.2.4 Downhole Losses

As perforation had been done in well AZN#85 &amp;amp; there is exposure to reservoir, risk of any probable formation losses must be taken into consideration.

Losses will be minimized/avoided by the planned use of properly sized bridging/weight material (and Polymer) in conjunction with appropriate drilling practices. If seepage losses are noted on the well no specific action will be taken but close monitoring of the loss rate is to be made. For moderate loss rates addition of CaCO3 50 micron and 150 micron is recommended to ensure that there is adequate correctly sized material to act as bridging agents.

Seepage losses Less than 10 bbl. /hr.

No specific action will be taken, but close monitoring of the probable loss rate is made.

Losses from 10-30 bbl. /hr.

 Load CaCO3-M (150-300 micron) in system up to 5ppb

*If loss not cured and even tends to increase, then:

 Pump 40-60bbl of pill made by 7-10ppb CaCO3 150-300μ &amp;amp; 7-10ppb CaCO3 600μ

Losses from 30-50 bbl. /hr.

 Load CaCO3-M (150-300 micron) in system up to 5ppb

 Since some of the CaCO3-M will be discarded over the shakers, CaCO3-M to compensate the

Losses more than 100 bbl/hr.

High concentrated LCM pill of various sizes of Calcium Carbonate and Oyster Shell-F&amp;amp;M&amp;amp;C should be pumped and spotted and gently squeezed over the loss zone.

Spotting Procedure

1. After spotting LCM pill, pull the bit above the calculated top of the pill. Wait 30 minutes and

monitor the annulus.

2. After 30 minutes, attempt to fill the annulus, if not already full. If the hole can be filled, close

BOP and squeeze 10bbl LCM pill into formation without exceeding 200psi.

3. If the hole remains stable, continue to drill ahead.

4. Should the LCM pill fail to reduce the losses or the hole cannot be filled, then mix and spot

another 50bbl of LCM pill.

5. Attempt to fill the annulus. If successful, close the BOP and squeeze 20bbl of LCM pill into

the formation without exceeding 200psi.

6. If a squeeze pressure develops, hold the pressure for 1 hour before running the drill string

7.1.2.6 Drilling Issues

There is no drilling objective in AZN-85 workover well; mud should be compatible with reservoir and work over operation.

Solid Control equipment

 Use shale shaker to remove debris and LCM particle in case of use.

 Personal Safety

7.1.2.7 Mud Type

Inhibited CaBr2 brine (Calcium Bromide Brine) will be applied as completion fluid. And simple salt saturated kill mud to kill the well and clean out inside 9 5/8”, 7” Liner.

Displacement Design

The combined effect of scrapers being run in the hole, the high flow rate will help to remove/disperse general debris.

At least 150m of pill/spacer coverage or 3 min contact time at the highest pump rates should be considered.

Saturated CaCl2 brine can be applied as spacer/Hi-Vis pill while displacing.

Pit levels should be monitor throughout the displacement operation to catch and prevent an influx entering the well contributing to an incident.

All CaBr2 brine inside the well must be retrieved by the time of displacing the well by kill mud. In case of need, filtration must be applied to retrieved amount of CaBr2.

8. Perforation Program

Displace 7" Liner volume with CaBr2 perforation fluid, perform 7" Liner perforation, run CCL/GR log to confirm perforated interval. RIH with 5 7/8" Bit to top of perforation while scrap 7" production PKR setting depth, displace well volume with CaBr2 completion fluid. Run 4-1/2" * 3-1/2", 10K Completion string. N/D BOP, N/U XMT. Perform well Pre-Acid clean up, Acid-Wash, Post-Acid clean-up and well performance test operations.

The perforation intervals will be in Fahliyan Formation Fah-2a &amp;amp; Fah-3a with a thickness of 14m &amp;amp; 4m TVD respectively. The Contractor must prepare the detail of perforation program under supervision of client.

8.1 Perforation Gun

Wireline conveyed perforation can be the first priority, and TCP (tubing conveyed perforating) to be considered as back-up plan in case of tough conditions in the wellbore.
