12. Health, Safety &amp;amp; Environments

12.1 WELL CONTROL

All the drilling operation shall obey the requirement of Well Control Manual of MSA &amp;amp; contractor’s well control manual; under no circumstances should the deviation from well control policy be permitted without prior approval through MSA. If the contractor’s well control manual or anywhere has conflict with Well Control Manual of MSA, take Well Control Manual of MSA as the standard.

12.1.1 WORK Requirement of Well Control Equipment

 With shut-in casing pressure lower than 1,000psi, while snubbing with annular preventer, drill tools

shall have 18-deg shoulder tool joints, &amp;amp; the snubbing velocity shall not be greater than 0.2m/s.

 After shut off the annular preventer or ram preventer, with the shut-in casing pressure not greater

than 2,000psi, drill tools are allowed to pull up &amp;amp; down with the velocity less than 0.2m/s, however,

rotating or tool joint passing through are forbidden.

 While drilling through pay zone &amp;amp; thereafter, BOP function (close-open) test for the BOPs shall be

performed regularly.

 Kill manifolds shall not be used for drilling fluid fill-in.

 The maximum allowed shut-in casing pressure shall be remarkably indicated on choke manifolds.

 All gate valves of well control manifolds shall be tagged with serial numbers, &amp;amp; be indicated with

on/Off.

 In case shear rams were used, after shearing the drill pipe with shear rams, retrieve the upper sheared

drill pipe, lower a drill pipe joint with TIW valve installed into the hole &amp;amp; close pipe rams on it to

prevent the possibility of shear ram’s failure.

12.1.2 Management of Well Control Equipment

 Well control equipment used by the drilling crew shall be managed &amp;amp; operated by designated

personnel with clear post responsibilities.

 Well site shall have specified component storeroom &amp;amp; rubber element storeroom with air

conditioners respectively. The temperature of storerooms shall meet storage requirements of

components &amp;amp; rubber elements.

 At least 1 set is available as back-up for every type ram assembly in the well site. Ram preventer

side door seals &amp;amp; ram rubber, every type gasket &amp;amp; bolt etc. should be enough for backup.

12.2 Recording Reference

All BOP tests, drills, function tests, any malfunctions, repair or maintenance to the mud System &amp;amp; well control equipment shall be recorded in the IADC daily reports &amp;amp; shall be signed by both the Drilling Contractor's Tool Pusher &amp;amp; Drilling Supervisor on the well site. They shall also be recorded in the Daily Drilling Report.

12.3 Flow Check Procedure

To avoid a kick situation, it is recommended that a flow check be conducted at specific times during the drilling operation.

While drilling (any warning sign).

Prior to tripping the drill string.

While tripping (any warning sign).

While out of hole (continuously).

Trip out:

After pulling 5% of the drill pipe

At the midpoint depth of the wellbore

Prior to pulling the first stand of drill collars

After all the drill string is out of hole.

Trip in:

Upon reaching surface casing shoe

At midpoint of the wellbore

12.4 Primary Control Reference

It is the responsibility of the Drilling Contractor to keep the hole full at all times by using all the available equipment. The Drilling Supervisor shall monitor that the correct preventive practices are being implemented and/or conducted at all times.

Extreme care shall be taken to monitor mud volume, drilling breaks &amp;amp; gas cut mud.

The MACP (Maximum allowable casing pressure) shall be confirmed by the Drilling Supervisor, either after setting each new casing string or, whenever the density of the drilling mud changes.

The MACP shall be clearly written on a kick control sheet that will be posted near the choke control panel.

The predetermined distance at which the Tool Joint is to be pulled above the rotary should be posted on rig floor near the BOP control panel.

The Driller is responsible for carefully measuring &amp;amp; recording the slow pump pressure.

Awareness of these values is an important element in killing operations, in order to avoid formation breakdown.

Take a measure &amp;amp; record the slow pump pressure at three different flow rates with all pumps at the following times:

Once per tour.

Whenever changes occur in the mud density/rheology.

Whenever changes occur in the dimension &amp;amp; characteristics of the string, BHA, jet size, jet plugged or jet lost, etc.

12.5 Secondary Control Reference

Any time a drilling break is noticed, drilling shall stop &amp;amp; a static monitoring of the well shall be carried out. Space-out for all Pipe Rams &amp;amp; Annular Preventer must be known to the Driller at all times to keep tool joints clear of annular preventer &amp;amp; rams.

12.6 Well control during drilling &amp;amp; completion operation

The drilling design shall be strictly implemented by the drilling contractor &amp;amp; when it is discovered there is incompliance of downhole situation with design &amp;amp; the design will be amended, the procedure for amendment of design shall be followed. If emergency is encountered, &amp;amp; safe operation can be affected, after the discussion between drilling rig manager &amp;amp; the drilling supervisor, practical technical measures can be taken first &amp;amp; then report to the top management. The Company shall approve &amp;amp; notice in time as per the drilling program amendment procedure.

The curve of well equivalent mud weight as per predicted formation pressure, curve of mud weight in drilling program &amp;amp; curve of actual mud weight must be drawn during drilling operation. For exploratory well &amp;amp; key well, the curve of dc index while drilling formation pressure equivalent mud weight for sandstone, mudstone &amp;amp; shale shall be drawn by the comprehensive mud logging crew.

When entering oil &amp;amp; gas formation or drilling master reservoir, high diameter nozzle shall be selected for the drilling bit to treat well killing &amp;amp; mud loss.

SCR (Slow Circulation Rate) shall be conducted at the start of drilling activity, pump strokes, pumping rate &amp;amp; circulating pressure should be recorded. While drilling in pay zone, SCR is required to be conducted with all pumps separately as follows, pump strokes, pumping rate &amp;amp; circulating pressure shall be recorded in Daily Drilling Report &amp;amp; Kill Sheet.

Once for every 12 hours in general;

After bit change or BHA change; 3) Mud weight change exceeds 3.75pcf.

Oil &amp;amp; gas invasion &amp;amp; overflow shall be checked with wiper trip &amp;amp; shall be conducted under the following situation:

Each time before POOH after drilling oil &amp;amp; gas formations.

Severe invasion of oil &amp;amp; gas occurs during drilling, but overflow does not occur before POOH.

POOH after killing well.

POOH after lowering mud weight in wellbore.

POOH after curing mud loss during drilling oil &amp;amp; gas formation.

POOH after drilling oil &amp;amp; gas formation &amp;amp; a prolonged period of time is needed for other operations (E logging, running casing, running tubing &amp;amp; DST etc.).

Regarding the shut-in methods selection

Soft shut-in method is recommended for gas well;

Hard shut-in method is recommended for oil well;

Hard shut-in method is recommended for the well of which the well has strong formation strength in EMW as per FIT test;

Soft shut-in method is recommended for the well of which the well has weak formation strength in EMW as per FIT test.

Before POOH, circulation duration of mud in wellbore shall not be less than one and a half cycles. The observation time after wiper trip shall be no less than one and a half cycles. The density differential of inlet and outlet shall not exceed 1.248 pcf.

Flow check shall be conducted regularly via trip tank as follows

Prior to POOH (keep string rotation at 10 rpm for preventing stuck pipe)

POOH to last casing shoe

Before POOH BHA through BOP stack

Note: Tripping should be shut-off immediately and flow check shall be performed later on when any suspected well kick is observed.

During POOH, fill up hole every 3-5 stands of DP and every stand of DC. If the nozzle is plugged, during POOH, mud shall be filled full for each joint or continuous filling shall be conducted and trip sheet shall be recorded carefully.

When the bit is in the oil and gas formation and 300m above top of oil and gas formation, POOH speed shall be controlled to maintain the excellent well building property and rheological property of mud to avoid severe swabbing in the wellbore.

During RIH, the running speed shall be controlled to avoid the loss of circulation due to down hole pressure surge.

During tripping, check and repair of the equipment shall be arranged at the time when running to the casing shoe. If equipment have to be checked and repaired during POOH, due blowout prevention measures shall be taken during and after the check and repair, drill string shall be run to bottom and circulate for one and a half cycles. After everything is normal, drilling shall be resumed. Equipment check and repair shall not be conducted for empty well condition.

Treatment measures for invasion of gas during normal drilling:

When invasion of gas is discovered, it shall be discharged with circulation in time. The gas invaded mud shall not be pumped in the hole before eliminating gas.

Increasing mud weight shall be conducted when stop drilling and after invaded gas eliminated from mud. Mud weight incremental of each circulation cycle shall be controlled within 3.121 pcf

"In-post" policy

"In-post" will be initiated after the surface casing is cemented.

The "in-post" personnel must be trained and verified qualified by the technical staff of drilling rig.

During drilling, specific personnel shall be arranged to be "in-post", the mud logging personnel shall monitor the level of the circulating tank etc. as per the requirements. During tripping, other auxiliary operation or drilling suspension, specific personnel for "in-post" shall be arranged by the drilling and mud logging personnel in the meantime.

"In-post" requirements:

For drilling operation, variation of the outlet flow, drilling time, lithology, bubble, smell, showings, pit volume, density and mud viscosity, gas measured values and content of chloride etc. shall be carefully monitored. The level of the circulating tank shall be observed and recorded each 15 minutes and if special situation occurs, the measurement and record shall be intensified. If anomaly occurs, it shall be reported to the driller in time.

For tripping operation, trip sheet shall be filled accordingly. If anomaly occurs, it shall be reported to the driller.

For other operations, it shall be observed whether there is overflow of mud at the wellhead or mud level from wellhead. If anomaly occurs, it shall be reported to the driller.

Treatment of loss of circulation

Before cementing non-target zone or pay zone, if loss of circulation occurs during drilling, POOH shall be carried to run open ended drill pipe for cement plug job if condition allows. During RIH, mud shall be filled from annulus to balance formation pressure to avoid blowout.

Treatment of loss of circulation during drilling after production casing cemented

Mud level not at wellhead after loss of circulation. Stop drilling, pick up TDS or Kelly, stop pumps and observe with moving the drill string and prepare well control related work. Each 10 minutes, mud with density no lower than the drilling weight shall be reversely filled up from the annulus. Each time, the filling up shall be 1~2m3, or continuous reserve injecting mud with small speed to maintain that the column pressure of mud in wellbore is higher than the formation pressure. safety interval for observation. Additional treatment shall be made as per the situation of loss of circulation.

Mud level at wellhead after loss of circulation. Stop drilling, pick up TDS or Kelly, stop pumps and move the drill string to observe with well control well prepared. When the well is static, pull the bit upward to the casing shoe or safe interval for observation. If no anomaly is observed, circulate with slow pump rate. The measures such as plugging back job, POOH or condition mud etc. shall be carried out as per the situation of loss of circulation. If loss of circulation occurs to pay zone, mud weight shall be acquired by static pressure. After pulling out to casing shoe and observing for one tripping cycle, when no more loss of circulation occurs after running to bottom, drilling operation can be resumed.

Well control for E logging, cementing and DST

Before E logging, down hole condition shall be stable and static. If it takes long time for electrical logging, one more condition trip shall be conducted between logging. Shooting nipple is required for logging. Logging service shall be furnished with tools for cutting the cables.

Continuously fill the well during performing wireline logging, and keep closely monitoring for the well via trip tank.

Before running casing, ensure the well is in static condition without any flowing. Pipe ram shall be changed to casing ram with proper size. Casing circulating head or crossover sub between casing and in used DP shall be kept at rig floor at all times during casing running.

The hydrostatic pressure shall be kept balance with formation pressure during whole cementing job to avoid blowout due to loss of circulation, loss of balance for pressure and cement weight loss during WOC.

Management of environment protection on location

In drilling operation keep mud and sewage from overflowing. If it happens, clean up timely.

Mud chemicals shall be stored according to the standard and shall not be scattered around well site. If mud chemicals scatter while loading or unloading, clean it up at once. The sack of mud chemicals shall be recovered. Do not dispose it on site.

Enhance water management at well location and do not wash equipment with fresh water. Stop water flowing for long time. Overhead tanks shall be utilized.

Oil management shall be carefully at the well site. No oil dirt on site, no dripping and leaking at oil tank and manifold system area.

After the well is completed, reinforce the sewage pit solidify the disposed mud and have environment procedure fulfilled.

Install fuel supply lines and keep them in good condition.

All the drilling fluid materials shall be recovered and shall not be left at the well site after completion.

The environmental protection personnel from contractor and operator side shall check and accept the well site environment according to the regulation after completion. Only well site environment is qualified, the well can be delivered.

13. H2S Monitoring &amp;amp; Prevention Measure

13.1 Monitoring H2S

Somewhere on the well site is apt to accumulate H2S, such as mud pit, shale shaker, and drilling platform, should be installed one set of. Make sure H2S monitor and alarm system can be used. Alarm threshold setting for H2S warning indicator: the first warning level is 10mg/m3, unable warning sound, just show present value of H2S content to operators. The second warning level is 20mg/m3, when the H2S content in air exceed 20mg/m3, H2S warning indicator can give an alarm automatically, and warning sound should be heard by everyone work in well site. The audible alarm should be installed on Kelly board.

Equip enough gas masks on drilling platform, shaker screen (total amount should large than 24), and equip 12 sets of 30min positive pressure Air Aspirators 2 sets of portable H2S monitor and appropriative H2S warning indicator. Arrange a person specially assigned for taking charge all the protective apparatus. This man must do periodical check to keep these equipment in a good condition.

H2S monitor should be done weekly check and compulsory examination.

After drilling into the pay zone, strengthen the detection of H2S content in mud.

13.2 Measures for H2S prevention

Windsocks shall be set on the drill floor and in the monsoon direction or/and prevailing wind direction of Azadegan oil field, off well site. In emergency, employees must follow the evacuation procedure.

Explosion-proof blowers shall be installed around the rig, shale shaker, and drilling fluid tanks to blow away toxic and flammable gas at the well site.

The rig crew in the H2S area shall be furnished with H2S monitors and adequate protective apparatus. Everybody shall be able to use, maintain, and check the apparatus.

The technicians of rig crew are responsible for H2S proof training and the tool pusher is in charge of the supervision and examination.

The pH value of drilling fluid in the H2S area shall be kept over 9.5. Pay attention to measurement of H2S concentration in drilling fluid. The H2S concentration shall be kept at less than 50mg/cm3 by using sulphur removal agents and degassers.

Personnel safety and protection shall be carried out according to SY/T5087 during operations in polluted areas where H2S content exceeds the critical concentration.

1. General Information

1.1 Field Introduction

Azadegan South Oil Field is situated in West Karoun province on a large long-axis anticline with N-S trending with approximate dimensions about 20 km width and 60 km length near to Iran-Iraq border, to the east of Yaran Oil Field.

The trap area of the south Azadegan is limited to 43.2x17.2 km. The Azadegan Oil field was discovered in 1999, when Well AZN-1 was drilled vertically down to the Cretaceous Fahliyan Formation with total depth of 4,643m. The results of this well, revealed the reservoir characteristics of the field. Following to the result of the well no. AZN-1, another 5 exploration wells was drilled in different parts of this huge field down to Fahliyan Formation. In the later stage the well No.10 assumed as exploration well for evaluation of deeper formations. This well was drilled in 2008, down to the depth of 5340m (Neyriz Fm.), mainly to evaluate the Jurassic formations.

Based on the exploration wells results, carbonate reservoir of Sarvak Formation is broadly developed in Azadegan Field. This formation was penetrated in all of seven exploration wells (AZN-1, AZN-2, AZN- 3, AZN-4, AZN-5, AZN-6 and AZN-10). Clastic oil-bearing zones of Kazhdumi Formation developed in main anticline of Azadegan Field, extending from north to center of South Azadegan. The Clastic oilbearing zones of Gadvan Formation developed only in crest area and south parts of South Azadegan Filed, which was discovered by AZN-1 in crest and AZN-4 in south parts. The carbonates of Fahliyan Formation also developed in Azadegan field, but the oil reservoir of this formation developed in South part of South Azadegan.

The Azadegan Field is an elongated anticline, trending in N-S direction, belonging to "Arabian Trend".

The stratigraphy sequence of the field includes AghaJari, Gachsaran, Fahliyan, Pabdeh, Gurpi, Ilam, Laffan, Sarvak, Kazhdumi, Dariyan, Gadvan and Fahliyan Formations, from top to bottom. This sequence in well no AZN-10, the deepest up to now drilled well of the field, continues with Garau, Gotnia, Najmah, Sargalu, Alan, Mus and Neyriz formations.

The Dominant lithofacies of Sarvak Formation are Rudist-bearing packstone and partially grainstone, which contains abundant bioclasts. Some other facies like matrix-dominated wackestone and mudstone are also found.

The AZADEGAN Oilfield is Located in Khuzestan Province and is Approximately Located 80 Kilometers West of Ahwaz City, near to Iran-Iraq Border. It is in The Northwest of The YADAVARAN Field and in The West of JUFEYR Field. The Average Monthly Temperature is 45ºc in summer, and Highest Temperature is 52ºc. The Lowest Temperature is -4.4ºc in winter. Maximum Rainfall is 78 mm in February, Winter Season.

1.7 Drilling History

The AZNS 122-ST1/F02 (Pad 55) was drilled by rig 92 Fath, which rig moving was spudded on 3- October-2016 @ 18:00.

 26" hole was spudded @ 21:00 on 3-October-2016 &amp;amp; drilled to casing point @ 156m, 09:30 on 5-

October-2016, Mw 67pcf.

 20" casing was run to 155m &amp;amp; cemented by inner stab-in string with slurry to surface.

 17-1/2" hole was started @ 02:30 on 10-October-2016 &amp;amp; drilled to 2170m @ 21:00 on 11-Dec-

2016, Mw 67 – 83pcf.

 In 17-1/2" hole section, drill string was twist off @ 1573m, tried to recovered fish with no

succeed, set cement plug &amp;amp; side track the well, KOP @ 1416m.

 In 17-1/2" hole section, drill string was twist off @ 1599, 1920 &amp;amp; 1960.5, fishing operation was

performed &amp;amp; fish was recovered in each operation.

 13-3/8" casing was run &amp;amp; cemented @ 2169m with slurry to surface.

 The 12-1/4" hole section was started @ 08:00 on 20-Dec-2016 &amp;amp; drilled to 3910 @ 07:00 on 20-

Jan-2017, Mw 79 – 83pcf.

 9-5/8" casing was run &amp;amp; cemented @ 3909.5m with slurry to surface.

 The 8-1/2" hole section was started @ 17:00 on 08-Feb-2017 &amp;amp; drilled to 4208m @ 24:00 on 16-

Feb-2017, Mw 100 – 107pcf.

 7" liner was run &amp;amp; cemented f/3782.2 to 4208m, the dry test result shows that the liner lap is OK.

 2192.5 hrs. Waiting for receive completion fluid.

 Displace mud in hole with completion fluid.

 4-1/2"*3-1/2"-10K Completion string (Weqixin Co.) was run, packer set @ 3930m, try to test

completion string several times with no succeed, disconnect completion string from anchor seal

&amp;amp; POOH to surface. P/U &amp;amp; M/U 4" anchor seal below first joint &amp;amp; RIH 4-1/2"*3-1/2"-10K

completion string (Anton Oil Co.), set packer @ 3832m, perform pressure test was OK, install Xmass tree &amp;amp; test, OK.

 The rig 92 Fath was released @ 24:00 on 08-July-2017. (1396/05/06)

5. Sequence of Operation

5.1 Main Objective

Decision has been made to de-complete he well &amp;amp; re-complete with new completion equipment.

5.2 Main plan

1. Check the wellhead &amp;amp; annulus pressure, bleed off any annulus pressure to zero.

2. Remove 7-1/16" XMT cap, R/U CT, RIH to top of perforation to confirm the well is clear, POOH to

surface, R/D CT.

Note #1: Chemical wash may be needed while RIH with CT.

3. R/U well testing package.

4. R/U SL, RIH with shifting tools &amp;amp; open SSD, POOH SL &amp;amp; displace the well with heavy mud, R/D

SL.

5. Install BPV in TBH, N/D XMT &amp;amp; N/U BOP &amp;amp; pressure test same.

6. Retrieve BPV, R/U casing running equipment, RIH with TBH retrieving tool &amp;amp; engage with TBH,

apply over pull to un-latch the seal assembly.

Note #2: If unable to unlatch the seal assembly, the contingency plan is RIH w/internal cutter &amp;amp; cut tubing f/top of packer, then mill tubing &amp;amp; packer.

7. Start circulation immediately after stinging out seal assy &amp;amp; observe the well.

8. Pull out &amp;amp; lay down completion string.

9. RIH with 9-5/8" tandem scraper BHA, scrap RTTS packer setting depth, CBU &amp;amp; POOH to surface,

L/D BHA.

10. RIH with wireline Corrosion Logging tools to bottom, log up to surface in two separate run ( 7'' Liner

&amp;amp; 9-5/8'' Casing )..

11. R/U, RIH with 9-5/8" RTTS packer &amp;amp; perform 7" liner lap dry test. L/D BHA.

Note #3: If dry test is not OK, the contingency plan is RIH &amp;amp; install liner top packer on top of 7" liner lap.

12. RIH with 5-7/8" mill &amp;amp; clean out BHA (7'' scraper included) to Top of second Packer @ 3832m,

displace the well with completion fluid (non-solid), POOH &amp;amp; L/D DP's.

13. Run 10K completion string as program.

Note #4: Annulus pressure test during completion operation is related to corrosion log result.

14. Set BPV inside TBH, N/D BOP &amp;amp; install 10K XMT.

15. Pressure test the XMT, retrieve BPV.

16. RIH with SL, set protection sleeve, retrieve plug &amp;amp; prong from NO GO landing nipple, POOH.

17. RIH with CT to bottom, displace the well with diesel &amp;amp; observe the well, POOH.

South Azadegan Oilfield Project

Contract No:

CCA/C/1401/27

AZNS-122 Workover Program

Project P/T Zone Dep. Disc. Type Sequence Rev. Page 25 of 61

SAC P IIF10 DR DE PRG 0001 00

18. R/U SL, RIH &amp;amp; retrieve protection sleeve, POOH, R/D SL.

19. Flow the well as pre-acid clean-up till acceptable BSW &amp;amp; reading stable flow rate on 2 different

choke size for 72 hrs.

20. RIH with CT &amp;amp; perform acid wash as per program, POOH to surface.

21. Flow the well as post-acid clean-up till acceptable BSW &amp;amp; reading stable flow rate on 2 different

choke size for minimum 96 hrs.

Note #4: The time is only for flowing duration (R/U, R/D &amp;amp; preparation time is excluded)

Note #5: Acidizing &amp;amp; post acid clean-up maybe perform as rigless job upon contractor request &amp;amp; client approval but in case of any failure in well integrity the contractor should provide drilling rig &amp;amp; required services in own responsibility &amp;amp; fix the problem.

22. RIH with SL, set protection sleeve.

23. RIH with CT to bottom &amp;amp; displace the well with diesel, POOH.

24. RIH with SL, install plug &amp;amp; prong into NO GO landing nipple, POOH.

25. RIH with SL, retrieve protection Sleeve.

26. Install BPV inside tubing hanger, secure the well &amp;amp; close all valves of XMT tree expect BMV.

7.1.2.3 Drilling Fluid Formulation

Kill Mud Mixing Procedure:

1. Fill tanks with calculated amount of Drill Water 0.576 bbl/bbl

2. Treat Drill Water with Caustic soda and Soda Ash by 0.3pbb.

3. Mix NaCl at 66 ppb.

4. Add Xanthan-Gum by 0.2pbb.

5. Add CaCO3-F (325ppb) to reach MW of ±106 pcf

 In case of foaming use Alcohol-Based Defoamer.

Note: Use Hi Vis pill to clean hole if necessary.

Calculation is based on per bbl of mud.

Completion Fluid Mixing Procedure:

1. Make sure that all pits and lines involved with completion fluid are thoroughly cleaned, flushed

and free of any fluid and solid.

 Make sure that at least one large pit is kept empty for transferring ready brine into after given

time for settling. After transferring one pit to empty pit, the first one is to be flushed and

cleaned for accommodating the brine of next ready pit, and so on to the last pit.

 Depends on the rig facilities and structure, mud engineer on board may find it better to

prepare the fluids pit-by-pit.

2. Transfer the content of CaBr2 drums into designated pits.

 Record the number of drums poured in each tank for accurate volume in it as the base of

calculation for adding other additives into; do not rely on pit gauge, sounding or mud logging

sensor, but have a look on them for comparison and/or correlation if found useful.

3. Mix Corrosion Inhibitor into pits at concentration of 3.5pbb(1% by volume).

4. Mix H2S Scavenger Liquid into pits at concentration of 0.5% by Volume.

5. Do not add Oxygen Scavenger CA at this stage as it should be added directly from the top of the

pit, just prior to pump the fluid into the well.

6. Shut down all agitators and mixing pumps, and leave the mixed fluid in the pits for at least 12

hours to let any solid particle inside (mostly insoluble Lime) settles down.

7. Start transferring the clear fluid of the first pit to the empty pit by means of an air-powered

Wilden pump.

 Make sure that the suction hose of the Wilden pump is not put deep close to the bottom of the

pit, otherwise, settled solids are sucked in.

8. After finishing the first pit, stop Wilden pump, wash, flush and clean the pit, use it as the empty

pit for accommodating the fluid of second pit using the and same above method.

Note: all CaBr2 brine inside the well must be retrieved by the time of displacing the well by kill mud. In case of need, filtration must be applied to retrieved amount of CaBr2.

Based on well readings and the operation, mud weight may be varied.

7.1.2.4 Downhole Losses

As perforation had been done in well AZN#122 and there is exposure to reservoir, risk of any probable formation losses must be taken into consideration.

Losses will be minimized/avoided by the planned use of properly sized bridging/weight material (and Polymer) in conjunction with appropriate drilling practices. If seepage losses are noted on the well no specific action will be taken but close monitoring of the loss rate is to be made. For moderate loss rates addition of CaCO3 50 micron and 150 micron is recommended to ensure that there is adequate correctly sized material to act as bridging agents.

Seepage losses Less than 10 bbl/hr.

No specific action will be taken, but close monitoring of the probable loss rate is made.

Losses from 10-30 bbl/hr.

 Load CaCO3-M (150-300 micron) in system up to 5 ppb

*If loss not cured and even tends to increase, then:

 Pump 40-60 bbl of pill made by 7-10 ppb CaCO3 150-300μ &amp;amp; 7-10 ppb CaCO3 600μ

Losses from 30-50 bbl/hr.

 Load CaCO3-M (150-300 micron) in system up to 5 ppb

 Since some of the CaCO3-M will be discarded over the shakers, CaCO3-M to compensate the

separated amount on the shakers.

*If loss not cured and even tends to increase, then:

 Pump 40-60 bbl of pill made by

 10-20 ppb CaCO3 200-300μ

 10-20 ppb CaCO3 600 μ

 10pbb Oyster Shell-F

 10pbb Oyster Shell-M.

Losses from 50-100 bbl/hr.

 Load CaCO3-M (150-300 micron) in system up to 5 ppb

 Load CaCO3-C (600-100 micron) in system up to 5 ppb

 Since some of the CaCO3-M&amp;amp;C will be discarded over the shakers, add CaCO3-M&amp;amp;C to

compensate the separated amount on the shakers.

*If loss not cured and even tends to increase, then:

 Pump 40-60 bbl of the following pill:

 10-20 ppb CaCO3 200-300 micron

 10-20 ppb CaCO3 600 micron

 7-10 ppb of each CaCO3 1000 micron &amp;amp; CaCO3 2000 micron

 5-10 pbb Oyster Shell -F

 5-10 pbb Oyster Shell -M

Losses more than 100 bbl/hr.

High concentrated LCM pill of various sizes of Calcium Carbonate and Oyster Shell-F&amp;amp;M&amp;amp;C should be pumped and spotted and gently squeezed over the loss zone.

Spotting Procedure

1. After spotting LCM pill, pull the bit above the calculated top of the pill. Wait 30 minutes and

monitor the annulus.

2. After 30 minutes, attempt to fill the annulus, if not already full. If the hole can be filled, close

BOP and squeeze 10 bbl LCM pill into formation without exceeding 200 psi.

3. If the hole remains stable, continue to drill ahead.

4. Should the LCM pill fail to reduce the losses or the hole cannot be filled, then mix and spot

another 50 bbl of LCM pill.

5. Attempt to fill the annulus. If successful, close the BOP and squeeze 20 bbl of LCM pill into the

formation without exceeding 200 psi.

6. If a squeeze pressure develops, hold the pressure for 1 hour before running the drill string back to

bottom.

Notes:

 LCM pills must be thoroughly homogenised and viscous enough before being pumped.

 Pumping high-concentrated LCM pill is subject to use of open-end DP or Mule-Shoe.

 Remove filter screens from the drill pipe (if there is any) and if necessary, remove strainers

from the mud pump suction lines.

7.1.2.5 Engineering Comments

Keep watching and control on well to record loss.

All CaBr2 brine inside the well must be retrieved by the time of displacing the well by kill mud. In case of need, filtration must be applied to retrieved amount of CaBr2.

7.1.2.6 Drilling Issues

There is no drilling objective in AZN-122 workover well; mud should be compatible with reservoir and work over operation.

Solid Control equipment

 Use shale shaker to remove debris and LCM particle in case of use.

 Personal Safety

7.1.2.7 Mud Type

Inhibited CaBr2 brine (Calcium Bromide Brine) will be applied as completion fluid. And simple salt saturated kill mud to kill the well and clean out inside 9 5/8”, 7” Liner.

Displacement Design

The combined effect of scrapers being run in the hole, the high flow rate will help to remove/disperse general debris.

At least 150 m of pill/spacer coverage or 3 min contact time at the highest pump rates should be considered.

Saturated CaCl2 brine can be applied as spacer/Hi-Vis pill while displacing.

Pit levels should be monitor throughout the displacement operation to catch and prevent an influx entering the well contributing to an incident.

All CaBr2 brine inside the well must be retrieved by the time of displacing the well by kill mud. In case of need, filtration must be applied to retrieved amount of CaBr2.

No. Description Volume [bbl.] Comment1 Viscous pill/spacer 50 Clean pill2 Displace to inhibited CaBr2 Brine at 106pcf (Completion Fluid)3 Continue pumping Completion Fluid until cleanliness specification has been met.

All CaBr2 retrieved from well must be stored in separated tanks. All CaBr2 left on surface, even dead volume of tanks, must be transferred back to drums at end of well. Not even a drop of Cabr2 is not allowed to be wasted or dump in whole operation duration.

It is recommended to use desander tank as active pit of CaBr2 to minimize dead volume and return path.

12. Health, Safety and Environments

12.1 WELL CONTROL

All the drilling operation shall obey the requirement of Well Control Manual of MSA and contractor’s well control manual; under no circumstances should the deviation from well control policy be permitted without prior approval through MSA. If the contractor’s well control manual or anywhere has conflict with Well Control Manual of MSA, take Well Control Manual of MSA as the standard.

12.1.1 WORK Requirement of Well Control Equipment

 With shut-in casing pressure lower than 1,000psi, while snubbing with annular preventer, drill tools

shall have 18-deg shoulder tool joints, and the snubbing velocity shall not be greater than 0.2m/s.

 After shut off the annular preventer or ram preventer, with the shut-in casing pressure not greater

than 2,000psi, drill tools are allowed to pull up and down with the velocity less than 0.2m/s,

however, rotating or tool joint passing through are forbidden.

 While drilling through pay zone and thereafter, BOP function (close-open) test for the BOPs shall be

performed regularly.

 Kill manifolds shall not be used for drilling fluid fill-in.

 The maximum allowed shut-in casing pressure shall be remarkably indicated on choke manifolds.

 All gate valves of well control manifolds shall be tagged with serial numbers, and be indicated with

on/Off.

 In case shear rams were used, after shearing the drill pipe with shear rams, retrieve the upper sheared

drill pipe, lower a drill pipe joint with TIW valve installed into the hole and close pipe rams on it to

prevent the possibility of shear ram’s failure.

12.1.2 Management of Well Control Equipment

 Well control equipment used by the drilling crew shall be managed and operated by designated

personnel with clear post responsibilities.

 Well site shall have specified component storeroom and rubber element storeroom with air

conditioners respectively. The temperature of storerooms shall meet storage requirements of

components and rubber elements.

 At least 1 set is available as back-up for every type ram assembly in the well site. Ram preventer

side door seals and ram rubber, every type gasket and bolt etc. should be enough for backup.

12.2 Recording Reference

All BOP tests, drills, function tests, any malfunctions, repair or maintenance to the mud System and well control equipment shall be recorded in the IADC daily reports and shall be signed by both the Drilling Contractor's Tool Pusher and Drilling Supervisor on the well site. They shall also be recorded in the Daily Drilling Report.

12.3 Flow Check Procedure

To avoid a kick situation, it is recommended that a flow check be conducted at specific times during the drilling operation.

While drilling (any warning sign).

Prior to tripping the drill string.

While tripping (any warning sign).

While out of hole (continuously).

Trip out:

After pulling 5% of the drill pipe

At the midpoint depth of the wellbore

Prior to pulling the first stand of drill collars

After all the drill string is out of hole.

Trip in:

Upon reaching surface casing shoe

At midpoint of the wellbore

12.4 Primary Control Reference

It is the responsibility of the Drilling Contractor to keep the hole full at all times by using all the available equipment. The Drilling Supervisor shall monitor that the correct preventive practices are being implemented and/or conducted at all times.

Extreme care shall be taken to monitor mud volume, drilling breaks and gas cut mud.

The MACP (Maximum allowable casing pressure) shall be confirmed by the Drilling Supervisor, either after setting each new casing string or, whenever the density of the drilling mud changes.

The MACP shall be clearly written on a kick control sheet that will be posted near the choke control panel.

The predetermined distance at which the Tool Joint is to be pulled above the rotary should be posted on rig floor near the BOP control panel.

The Driller is responsible for carefully measuring and recording the slow pump pressure.

Awareness of these values is an important element in killing operations, in order to avoid formation breakdown.

Take a measure and record the slow pump pressure at three different flow rates with all pumps at the following times:

Once per tour.

12.5 Secondary Control Reference

Any time a drilling break is noticed, drilling shall stop and a static monitoring of the well shall be carried out. Space-out for all Pipe Rams and Annular Preventer must be known to the Driller at all times to keep tool joints clear of annular preventer and rams.

12.6 Well control during drilling and completion operation

The drilling design shall be strictly implemented by the drilling contractor and when it is discovered there is incompliance of downhole situation with design and the design will be amended, the procedure for amendment of design shall be followed. If emergency is encountered, and safe operation can be affected, after the discussion between drilling rig manager and the drilling supervisor, practical technical measures can be taken first and then report to the top management. The Company shall approve and notice in time as per the drilling program amendment procedure.

The curve of well equivalent mud weight as per predicted formation pressure, curve of mud weight in drilling program and curve of actual mud weight must be drawn during drilling operation. For exploratory well and key well, the curve of dc index while drilling formation pressure equivalent mud weight for sandstone, mudstone and shale shall be drawn by the comprehensive mud logging crew.

When entering oil and gas formation or drilling master reservoir, high diameter nozzle shall be selected for the drilling bit to treat well killing and mud loss.

SCR (Slow Circulation Rate) shall be conducted at the start of drilling activity, pump strokes, pumping rate and circulating pressure should be recorded. While drilling in pay zone, SCR is required to be conducted with all pumps separately as follows, pump strokes, pumping rate and circulating pressure shall be recorded in Daily Drilling Report and Kill Sheet.

Once for every 12 hours in general;

After bit change or BHA change; 3) Mud weight change exceeds 3.75pcf.

Oil and gas invasion and overflow shall be checked with wiper trip and shall be conducted under the following situation:

Each time before POOH after drilling oil and gas formations.

Severe invasion of oil and gas occurs during drilling, but overflow does not occur before POOH.

POOH after killing well.

POOH after lowering mud weight in wellbore.

POOH after curing mud loss during drilling oil and gas formation.

POOH after drilling oil and gas formation and a prolonged period of time is needed for other operations (E logging, running casing, running tubing and DST etc.).

Regarding the shut-in methods selection

Soft shut-in method is recommended for gas well;

Hard shut-in method is recommended for oil well;

Hard shut-in method is recommended for the well of which the well has strong formation strength in EMW as per FIT test;

Soft shut-in method is recommended for the well of which the well has weak formation strength in EMW as per FIT test.

Main technical measures for prevention of kicking and blowout during tripping.

Before POOH, circulation duration of mud in wellbore shall not be less than one and a half cycles. The observation time after wiper trip shall be no less than one and a half cycles. The density differential of inlet and outlet shall not exceed 1.248 pcf.

Flow check shall be conducted regularly via trip tank as follows

Prior to POOH (keep string rotation at 10 rpm for preventing stuck pipe)

POOH to last casing shoe

Before POOH BHA through BOP stack

Note: Tripping should be shut-off immediately and flow check shall be performed later on when any suspected well kick is observed.

During POOH, fill up hole every 3-5 stands of DP and every stand of DC. If the nozzle is plugged, during POOH, mud shall be filled full for each joint or continuous filling shall be conducted and trip sheet shall be recorded carefully.

When the bit is in the oil and gas formation and 300m above top of oil and gas formation, POOH speed shall be controlled to maintain the excellent well building property and rheological property of mud to avoid severe swabbing in the wellbore.

During RIH, the running speed shall be controlled to avoid the loss of circulation due to down hole pressure surge.

During tripping, check and repair of the equipment shall be arranged at the time when running to the casing shoe. if equipment have to be checked and repaired during POOH, due blowout prevention measures shall be taken during and after the check and repair, drill string shall be run to bottom and circulate for one and a half cycles. After everything is normal, drilling shall be resumed. Equipment check and repair shall not be conducted for empty well condition.

Treatment measures for invasion of gas during normal drilling:

When invasion of gas is discovered, it shall be discharged with circulation in time. The gas invaded mud shall not be pumped in the hole before eliminating gas.

Increasing mud weight shall be conducted when stop drilling and after invaded gas eliminated from mud. Mud weight incremental of each circulation cycle shall be controlled within 3.121 pcf

"In-post" policy

"In-post" will be initiated after the surface casing is cemented.

The "in-post" personnel must be trained and verified qualified by the technical staff of drilling rig.

During drilling, specific personnel shall be arranged to be "in-post", the mud logging personnel shall monitor the level of the circulating tank etc. as per the requirements. During tripping, other auxiliary operation or drilling suspension, specific personnel for "in-post" shall be arranged by the drilling and mud logging personnel in the meantime.

"In-post" requirements:

For drilling operation, variation of the outlet flow, drilling time, lithology, bubble, smell, showings, pit volume, density and mud viscosity, gas measured values and content of chloride etc. shall be carefully monitored. The level of the circulating tank shall be observed and recorded each 15 minutes and if

special situation occurs, the measurement and record shall be intensified. If anomaly occurs, it shall be reported to the driller in time.

For tripping operation, trip sheet shall be filled accordingly. If anomaly occurs, it shall be reported to the driller.

For other operations, it shall be observed whether there is overflow of mud at the wellhead or mud level from wellhead. If anomaly occurs, it shall be reported to the driller.

Treatment of loss of circulation

Before cementing non-target zone or pay zone, if loss of circulation occurs during drilling, POOH shall be carried to run open ended drill pipe for cement plug job if condition allows. During RIH, mud shall be filled from annulus to balance formation pressure to avoid blowout.

Treatment of loss of circulation during drilling after production casing cemented

Mud level not at wellhead after loss of circulation. Stop drilling, pick up TDS or Kelly, stop pumps and observe with moving the drill string and prepare well control related work. Each 10 minutes, mud with density no lower than the drilling weight shall be reversely filled up from the annulus. Each time, the filling up shall be 1~2m3, or continuous reserve injecting mud with small speed to maintain that the column pressure of mud in wellbore is higher than the formation pressure. POOH to casing shoe or safety interval for observation. Additional treatment shall be made as per the situation of loss of circulation.

Mud level at wellhead after loss of circulation. Stop drilling, pick up TDS or Kelly, stop pumps and move the drill string to observe with well control well prepared. When the well is static, pull the bit upward to the casing shoe or safe interval for observation. If no anomaly is observed, circulate with slow pump rate. The measures such as plugging back job, POOH or condition mud etc. shall be carried out as per the situation of loss of circulation. If loss of circulation occurs to pay zone, mud weight shall be acquired by static pressure. After pulling out to casing shoe and observing for one tripping cycle, when no more loss of circulation occurs after running to bottom, drilling operation can be resumed.

Well control for E logging, cementing and DST

Before E logging, down hole condition shall be stable and static. If it takes long time for electrical logging, one more condition trip shall be conducted between logging. Shooting nipple is required for logging. Logging service shall be furnished with tools for cutting the cables.

Continuously fill the well during performing wireline logging, and keep closely monitoring for the well via trip tank.

Before running casing, ensure the well is in static condition without any flowing. Pipe ram shall be changed to casing ram with proper size. Casing circulating head or crossover sub between casing and in used DP shall be kept at rig floor at all times during casing running.

The hydrostatic pressure shall be kept balance with formation pressure during whole cementing job to avoid blowout due to loss of circulation, loss of balance for pressure and cement weight loss during WOC.

Lifesaving equipment like SCBA, Escape Mask, H2S detectors (Multi portable and personal detector) and implement the H2S Services system during drilling activity should be provided.

All lifting equipment and cranes must be certified by approved 3rd party (approved by Institute of Standards &amp;amp; Industrial Research of Iran)

All electrical equipment should be designed for such locations, and listed by nationally recognized testing laboratory. All wiring components and electrical equipment should be maintained in accordance with the manufacturers’ recommendation.

PSSR (Pre-Startup Safety Review) before spud-in and penetrating into oil and gas formations are mandatory by contractor under the supervision of Company and approved by Company.

12.9 ENVIRONMENT

Requirement on location

The access road and well location construction shall be accorded with construction program of well location. It minimizes any impacts on the local residents, prevent all soil contamination, prevent all ground water contamination, and prevent all surface water contamination. Cutting and waste water pit shall be lining and drainage system shall be good and to avoid farm and season canal contamination.

Management regulation for transportation truck, drilling operation machine and tools shall be carried out strictly to avoid damage farm and trees, etc.

Well site shall be flat and clean. All the equipment, materials, drilling tools shall be put in order.

Control the rig noise to decrease the influence to surroundings while drilling at the inhabitation area.

Contractor shall perform on‐site segregation of wastes prior to transfer to the transfer area and/or delivery to the transportation Contractor in accordance with the following waste hazard classification.

Non-Hazardous Wastes (Re-usable, Recyclable and Recoverable Wastes)

Ferrous and non-ferrous metals, plastics, and wood wastes, PETs and potentially paper and glass.

Materials shall be separately segregated and provision may be made for size reduction and containerization equipment.

13. H2S Monitoring &amp;amp; Prevention Measure

13.1 Monitoring H2S

Somewhere on the well site is apt to accumulate H2S, such as mud pit, shale shaker, and drilling platform, should be installed one set of. Make sure H2S monitor and alarm system can be used. Alarm threshold setting for H2S warning indicator: the first warning level is 10mg/m3, unable warning sound, just show present value of H2S content to operators. The second warning level is 20mg/m3, when the H2S content in air exceed 20mg/m3, H2S warning indicator can give an alarm automatically, and warning sound should be heard by everyone work in well site. The audible alarm should be installed on Kelly board.

Equip enough gas masks on drilling platform, shaker screen (total amount should large than 24), and equip 12 sets of 30min positive pressure Air Aspirators 2 sets of portable H2S monitor and appropriative H2S warning indicator. Arrange a person specially assigned for taking charge all the protective apparatus. This man must do periodical check to keep these equipment in a good condition.

H2S monitor should be done weekly check and compulsory examination.

After drilling into the pay zone, strengthen the detection of H2S content in mud.

13.2 Measures for H2S prevention

Windsocks shall be set on the drill floor and in the monsoon direction or/and prevailing wind direction of Azadegan oil field, off well site. In emergency, employees must follow the evacuation procedure.

Explosion-proof blowers shall be installed around the rig, shale shaker, and drilling fluid tanks to blow away toxic and flammable gas at the well site.

The rig crew in the H2S area shall be furnished with H2S monitors and adequate protective apparatus. Everybody shall be able to use, maintain, and check the apparatus.

The technicians of rig crew are responsible for H2S proof training and the tool pusher is in charge of the supervision and examination.

The pH value of drilling fluid in the H2S area shall be kept over 9.5. Pay attention to measurement of H2S concentration in drilling fluid. The H2S concentration shall be kept at less than 50mg/cm3 by using sulphur removal agents and degassers.

Personnel safety and protection shall be carried out according to SY/T5087 during operations in polluted areas where H2S content exceeds the critical concentration.

When the rig crew makes decision to bleed and fire because well control cannot be performed due to well site conditions, operations shall be performed according to procedures in SY/T5087.

Introduction

This document covers the drilling of special production well in AZAR Oilfield,

Iran. The well is intended to produce oil from Sarvak Formation (Upper &amp;amp; Lower

Zones). Well will be drilled vertically down to total depth @ 4687 m MD (-4590 m

TVDss). The exact TD will be determined based on the geologist confirmation and

logging results.

The AZR structure is an asymmetric anticline located in the foreland of the

Zagros fold and thrust belt. The width of the structure is ~30 km. The NE flank is

dipping with approximately 5-6 degrees, while the SW flank is dipping ~10

degrees and locally up to 17 degrees.

Location Map

AZR anticline is located in 1 km east of Mehran city and northwest of Changuleh

oil field. Based on geophysical map it has 22 km length and 13 km width on

Bangestan group. It has a single culmination which the azimuth of axial trend is

N60. Based on geophysical map it is a symmetric anticline.

The nearby well AZR-2 did not encounter any oil water contacts in Ilam and

Sarvak Formations. The dynamic test data indicate that two oil systems were

encountered, one in the Upper Sarvak and one in the Lower Sarvak. From the

After Drlg out CMT. &amp;amp; POB flow check 1.5 BPH gain. Running IDC S.N. Packer to prevent flow was not

successful, finally 7" liner tied back to 3245 m and cemented successfully.

pcf with 38000 ppm H2S &amp;amp; BS%W=5‐9%, Shut the well WHP=2900 psi, bullhead 570 bbls 15% HCl acid w/5200‐4800 psi

&amp;amp; 1‐4.5 bpm, flow the well but after a few hours well was choked up, result: H2S=45000, CO2=60000, Cl=176000, fluid

weight=54‐56 pcf &amp;amp; BS&amp;amp;W=0, Run PBMS/GR/CCL to 3747.5 m, tag obstruction, shut the well, WHP=1920 psi, bullhead

well w/88 pcf mud, unset Pkr &amp;amp; rev. circ, hard W&amp;amp;R f/4123‐4529 m w/5‐6 bph loss, dec MW to 86 pcf, Run Caliper/GR

32” Hole Section / 26” Casing

1.1.1 General

After commencing spud-in, drilling 32” hole will be started. The drilling would be

anticipated to go on fast.

Casing point 26” casing @ 150 m

Formation Aghajari

Risks and hole

problem Hole opener and bit balling

Deviation control TOTCO™ survey

Logging N/A

Hi- Vis pill/ Bentonite mud

MW 65- 67 pcf

FV 80- 100 sec/qrt

Drilling parameters

WOB Maximum safe load, not to make any

deviation

FR 900- 1100 gpm

Rotation 60- 110 rpm

1.1.2 Formation Sampling

Each 2- 5 meters one sample would be taken.

NOTE: In addition to this general rule, geologist may decide to take more samples.

1.1.3 Sequence of Operation

 Make up 32” BHA as per BHA design (including hole opener). Tag formation at ±14 m.

 Drill ahead formation down to ±150 m (26” casing point in Aghajari formation). Pay

enough attention to drill a straight hole.

Subcontractor:

Azar Oil Field Development

Doc. Title:

ARPF EDRGEN ENPE DBBI 0006 Page 41 of 136

o Use LCM pill if heavy loss is encountered. If loss couldn’t be cured by LCM

pill, use cement plug(s) to cure it.

o Use following parameters to drill this hole section:

WOB : Max safe load not to make any deviation

Rotation : 60- 110 rpm

Flow rate : 400-450 gpm to 35 m, 900-1100 gpm after 35 m

Note:

o 32” hole section TD is based on about ±150 m inside Aghajari formation.

o TD should be adjusted to have 1 m of rat hole below casing shoe.

o The exact TD will be determined based on 26” casing tally.

o Run Totco™ each 50 m to evaluate the verticality of the hole.

o During trips, at surface, driller is responsible to check BHA.

o Significant deviations from programmed values should be permitted by

authorized responsible level and explained.

o A material balance to determine the theoretical concentrations of additives

in the mud should be calculated and reported to WSS.

o Ensure that all drilling tools and equipment are at well site and are in

serviceable condition.

o Ensure that adequate fishing tools for this section of hole are available.

o Enough mud materials, LCM and cement should be available at rig site to use

in case of needing.

 At TD, circulate and clean the hole. Spot high viscosity pill at bottom, drop Totco

and POOH to surface. Check the bit and hole opener condition.

 Perform hole condition prior to run casing. If any indication of drag is observed, run

back to bottom. Wash and ream to make sure that the hole condition is good.

 Hold safety meeting.

 Rig up 26” casing running equipment.

Subcontractor:

 Run ±150 m (approx. 13 jt) 26" casing (136.2 ppf, X-42, HG5S, CSF= 1.5 ~ 65 pcf)

with stab-in type duplex shoe to bottom as per casing program. Casing shoe should

be adjusted to have 1 m of rat hole and enough stick up (1.5 m on rig floor). Fill

casing by non LCM fresh mud joint by joint.

Note:

o When running casing, take care not to set down excessive weight if tight

hole or ledges are encountered.

 Run stinger on DP’s using the “C-plate” &amp;amp; 5” x 26" centralizer. Sting in. M/U &amp;amp; test

cementing lines. Circulate as one casing annulus volume. While circulating, check

the DP’s annulus for any return. Use all the weight of DP string if observing any

minor leakage through DP’s annulus.

 Cement casing as per program. Any minor adjustment regarding the corrected depth

will be done in due time. Displace with mud (1-2 bbl short). Monitor for pressures.

Record and report the final pressure. Sting out. Check the float. POOH one stand,

circulate to flush/ clean drill pipes.

 After cement returns to cellar floor, open the 2" nipple on conductor &amp;amp; flush it.

 POOH to surface. L/D stinger.

 Keep the 26" casing on the elevator until cement surface samples get hard. Check

for casing to be centered inside 42” conductor pipe. In case of any problem, report

immediately.

Note:

o Based on the results obtained from cementing, decision will be made to

perform top-up jobs.

o If there is no cement return to surface, a top-up job should be performed to

fill the annulus. Use same slurry weight as the primary cement slurry.

Ensure the availability of adequate X-over for connecting line pipes to

cementing line. The cement should be accelerated with max. (2%) Calcium

Chloride BWOC and no other additives. Wait for the top job cement to get

hard.

 Check casing by slacking off the weight.

 Cut 42” conductor pipe from cellar base. Cut 26" casing, L/D landing joint. Dress and

bevel same.

 N/U diverter flange and perform cement top up job meanwhile.

the mud should be calculated and reported to WSS.

o Ensure that all drilling tools and equipment are at well site and are in

serviceable condition.

o Ensure that adequate fishing tools for this section are available.

o Ensure that enough amounts of LCM are available

 At section TD, CBU and sweep the hole cleaned. Perform condition trip to 7" shoe

observe the well for one hour.

 RIH to bottom and circulate to clean hole. Check bottoms up for any drag and influx.

Prior to run log, adjust mud weight if needed.

 Spot 50 bbl of High Vis pill to stabilize the hole prior to run log. POOH to surface.

 R/U logging equipment. Run Litho Density/ Compensated Neutron/ GR Spectrometry/

Induction/ Micro Resistivity. R/D logging equipment.

 RIH w/ 6 1/8" bit. Condition the hole. Circulate hole clean. POOH to surface &amp;amp; L/D

the bit.

 R/U logging equipment. Run Full Waveform Sonic/ CDR logs. Run Elemental Capture

Spectroscopy log. R/D logging equipment.

 RIH w/ 6 1/8" bit. Condition the hole. Circulate hole clean. POOH to surface &amp;amp; L/D

the bit.

 R/U logging equipment. Run Micro Electrical Image log. Run Combinable Magnetic

Resonance log. R/D logging equipment.

 Perform condition trip prior to run Pressure Test Log. RIH to BTM, CBU and check

bottoms up for any influx; POOH to surface.

 R/U wireline logging equipment and run pressure testing log. R/D wireline.

 RIH w/ 6 1/8" used rock bit. Condition the hole prior to run 5" liner. Check bottoms

up for any kick; adjust mud weight if required before running 5” Liner. POOH to

surface.

 R/U 5" liner running tools. Hold pre-job safety meeting.

 Run 5" liner as per program to bottom. P/U and run liner hanger and accessories.

Follow liner string with 3 1/2” DP’s (pass drift through DP’s &amp;amp; perform SLM while RIH

with liner).

 Set liner hanger. Release setting tool. M/U cement manifold. Load pump-down plug.

WSS is to witness the loading. Test the lines to 3000 psi/ 10 min and 500 psi/ 5 min.

Ensure that the cement manifold is capable of holding pressure while displacing and

testing cement (visually).

 Circulate mud at 1.2 time of string volume.

 Cement liner as per program.

 P/U 4 1/8" milled tooth bit or mill and new BHA. P/U 2 7/8" DP’s jt by jt. RIH and

Well Suspension

1.1.33 Sequence of Operations

 RIH with 2 7/8”, 3 ½” and 5" open end DP’s to 50 m above 5" liner.

 L/U CMT lines and test same. Set 100 m balanced CMT plug. POOH 10 STD's and flush

the string. WOC. Run back. Tag and confirm cement. Try to wash. POOH to surface

and L/D 2 7/8" DP's jt by jt.

 P/U &amp;amp; M/U 6 1/8" Bit &amp;amp; BHA. RIH to top of cement. Dress cement to confirm hard

cement. CBU and sweep well with Hi-Vis pill. POOH to surface. L/D the bit.

 RIH w/ 3 1/2" x 5" open end DP's to 50m above 7" liner, L/U CMT lines and test same,

Set 100m balanced CMT plug, POOH 10 STD's and flush STRG. WOC, Run back, Tag and

confirm cement, Try to Wash. Continue POOH to Surface.

 P/U &amp;amp; M/U 8 3/8" Bit &amp;amp; RIH to top of cement, Dress cement to confirm hard cement,

CBU and sweep well with Hi-Vis pill, POOH to surface, L/D the bit.

 RIH w/ 3 1/2" x 5" open end DP to 2050m, H/U CMT lines and test same, Set 100m

balanced CMT plug, POOH 10 STD's and flush STRG. WOC, Run back, Tag and confirm

cement, Try to wash. Continue POOH to surface.

 P/U &amp;amp; M/U 8 3/8" Bit &amp;amp; RIH to top of cement, Dress cement to confirm hard cement,

CBU, Displace the well w/ completion fluid f/ BTM to surface.

 POOH to surface, L/D DP's and bit.

 Remove kill, choke &amp;amp; related lines, N/D flow line, bell nipple, annular preventer, 13

5/8" 10k single &amp;amp; double rams &amp;amp; DSA.

 Install 11" Blind Flange and Test Same.

32'' Hole Section

This section will be drilled 150 m through Aghajari Formation and it contains the Red

marl and Claystone with thin bed of Sandstone also occasionally treads of Gypsum

will be drilled.

This hole section will be drilled by using Bentonite mud and Mud can be lubricated

with 3-4% by volume of diesel.

PHB pill will be used to clean the hole and since Bentonite has the best cake around

the well bore, it will make a good cake for hole stability.

Note:

If drilling water has the chloride concentration more than 6000 mg/Lit

Bentonite will not hydrated well and Polymer mud will be used as drilling mud.

24” Hole Section

This hole section will be drilled from 150 m to 2084 m, through Aghajari and Gachsaran

formation.

The lithology of this section is mostly Marl, Claystone, Minor Gypsum and Anhydrite with

some beds of Solid Anhydrite in the lower part.

Low weight and Low Viscosity mud at 5% by weight of KCl will be used for the beginning

this section and mud weight and also mud viscosity will be improved gradually according

to drilling condition and hole dictation. Inhibited mud will minimize hole problems such

as bit balling, plugged flow lines and hole washouts.

Blinding of shaker screens, excessive over pull on trips, washout and stuck pipes has

been experienced in the offset well and with all these problems ROP will be reduced.

Mud weight will be controlled from 67 to 90 pcf through this section according to hole

dictation.

17'' Hole Section

This section will be drilled from 2084 m to 2789 m consisting of mainly different

evaporated rock types, such as Anhydrite, Marl and Salt and associated with thin to

medium beds of Limestone.

Minor mud losses may occur while drilling in Limestone which usually cured by spotting

LCM.

The SS/ KCl/ Polymer Mud from previous section will be added to Fresh SS/ Polymer Mud

to drill this hole section and for mixing new mud KCl will not be added. For weighting up

mud the Barite and Hematite will be added to mud system

While drilling this section, Hardness of mud system must be checked and monitored

accurately at least three TIMES a DAY for any increment of Calcium ions for

distinguishing the salt water flow and influx.

Hardness of Gachsaran formation’s salt water flow is between 35000-53000 mg/lit so

any highly increment of hardness in mud, would be an indication of possible salt water

flow.

While drilling through the lower part of Gachsaran, a high mud weight must be used to

keep the plastic salt layers in place.

Mud weight will be controlled from 135 to 147pcf according to hole dictation.

Formulation &amp;amp; properties

The below concentration of chemicals can be changed according to mud

properties while drilling.

9 ½" x 14 ¼" Hole Section

This section will be drilled from 2789 m to 3040 m through Gachsaran, Asmari and Top

Kalhur formations contain majorly carbonated rock type such as Limestone, Dolomite,

Dolomitic Limestone, and Calcareous Dolomite, Salt towards the lower part of the hole

the Anhydrite, Claystone and Marl will be increased.

For drilling this section and passing through the Marl, Salt Formations Fresh SS/ Polymer

Mud and recycled mud from previous section can be used to weight up the fresh mud.

Mud weight will be controlled from 85 – 96 pcf through this section.

Formulation &amp;amp; properties

7 ½" x 12 ¼" Hole Section

This section will be drilled from 3040 m to 3539 m through Kalhur, Operculina, Pabdeh

and Gurpi formation.

The upper part of this section consists of Limestone and Anhydrite with minor

Claystone.

The lower part consists of highly argillaceous Limestone interbedded with Claystone and

Marl. According to lithology of this section which has mainly Argillaceous Limestone,

Chalky Limestone, Marl and clay, Mud from previous section will be used to drill this

section and its KCl containment is useful for drilling argillaceous Limestone and Marl of

this section and weighted up by adding Barite.

In this section Mud weight will be controlled from 112 to 137 pcf.

Completion Fluid

Clear Solid free Brine is the most commonly used fluid as the Completion Fluid and

Workover Operation to minimize the formation damage.

Chemicals for mixing completion fluid are as follows:

- Approximately NaCl at 115 lb/bbl

- Corrosion Inhibitor 0.5% V/V

- Caustic Soda pH =11

- Oxygen Scavenger 0.5 ppb

- Biocide 0.3 ppb

- H2S Scavenger 0.2 ppb

Introduction

This document covers the drilling of production well in AZAR Oilfield, Iran. The

well is intended to produce oil from Sarvak Formation (Upper &amp;amp; Lower Zones).

Well will be drilled vertically down to total depth @ 4696 m MD (-4586 m TVDss).

The exact TD will be determined based on the geologist confirmation and logging

results.

The AZR structure is an asymmetric anticline located in the foreland of the

Zagros fold and thrust belt. The width of the structure is ~30 km. The NE flank is

dipping with approximately 5-6 degrees, while the SW flank is dipping ~10

degrees and locally up to 17 degrees.

Location Map

AZR anticline is located in 1 km east of Mehran city and northwest of Changuleh

oil field. Based on geophysical map it has 22 km length and 13 km width on

Bangestan group. It has a single culmination which the azimuth of axial trend is

N60. Based on geophysical map it is a symmetric anticline.

The nearby well AZR-2 did not encounter any oil water contacts in Ilam and

Sarvak Formations. The dynamic test data indicate that two oil systems were

encountered, one in the Upper Sarvak and one in the Lower Sarvak. From the

available pressure data and the oil down to observations in the well, the Upper

Sarvak has an anticipated oil water contact around -4330 m, and the deeper

Drills

Drill shall be conducted specific intervals and attached by all required personnel.

List and Frequency of Drills:

 Fire and Rescue drills - once a month on rig

 Kick drill - once a week as per Well Control Manual

 H2S drill - once a week by each crew, when drilling in suspected or known H2S area

Fire Prevention and Protection

Whilst the risk of major fire damage in EPDS areas is considered by GPTK to be reasonably

minor, (with key risks presented by compressed gas cylinders, H2S &amp;amp; CH4 risk, painting and

insulation materials and general debris and rubbish), the risk in the camp and office areas is

considered to be high. In order to prevent such hazards materializing, GPTK will implement a

Client: Project:

Subcontractor:

Azar Oil Field Development

Doc. Title:

Document Number Contract No.:AP-1-91-17

ARPF EDRGEN ENPE DBBI 0014 G01 Page 44 of 185

project-wide fire prevention/protection strategy that is characterized by the following

general principles.

 Minimal bulk storage on site of flammable substances

 Isolation of flammables from sources of ignition

 Ongoing housekeeping program

 Training in fire prevention and suppression techniques

 Integrity of electrical equipment

 Permit to work control of all electrical activity

 Containment of sparks and flames from Hot Works will be highly forbidden in rig

area (Zone 0 ,1)

 Escape route planning

 Restricted smoking areas.

This approach will be supported by the employment and maintenance of fire extinguishers at

strategic locations throughout the worksite and also the deployment of a fire extinguishers &amp;amp;

fire pump, detectors, fix H2S &amp;amp; CH4 Gas detectors, personnel single gas detectors (Clips)

which will be applied permanently charged at a strategic location.

The fire prevention/protection strategy will include all worksite offices, warehouses, camp,

etc., and will be developed to include commissioning activities.

Electrical Equipment for Classified Areas

Classified areas

All electrical equipment installed in a classified area shall have a correct type of protection.

The classified areas drawings on each rig shall be defined by the GPTK Engineering

Department.

All GPTK rigs shall have clearly identified hazardous areas. Definition of classified areas:

Zone 1 in which an explosive gas/ mixture is likely to occur in normal operations.

Zone 2 in which an explosive gas/ mixture is not likely to occur in normal operation and if it

occurs, will exist only for a short time.

Non-hazardous area: manned or unmanned areas in which an explosive gas/mixture will not

occur in normal operations.

Client: Project:

Subcontractor:

Azar Oil Field Development

Doc. Title:

Document Number Contract No.:AP-1-91-17

ARPF EDRGEN ENPE DBBI 0014 G01 Page 45 of 185

Note: a “Zone 0” is also defined as a zone where explosive gas/air mixtures are continuously

present or present for long periods.

-Equipment suitable for classified areas

Electrical equipment shall comply with flag authority and API specifications for each of the

classified areas. Additional Clients requirements shall be referred to GPTK Engineering for

review.

-Combustion engines located inside zone 2

All combustion engines operated within a zone 2 area shall be equipped with:

 spark arresting system on exhaust (or spark arrestor silencer)

 Quick shut

 off device acting on fuel supply and/ or air intake manifold Engines permanently

located within a zone 2 area will be equipped with a flameproof starter (air).

Well Control Policy

Objectives

To cover the shut-in procedures and diverter procedures for a surface BOP. To cover A.P.I.

recommendations for these procedures which includes advantages and disadvantages.

General introduction to shut-in procedures on a fixed rig

Note: A fixed rig is defined as a drilling rig equipped with a surface BOP.

Shut-in procedure should be agreed by contractor and operating company and posted on rig

floor before drilling the well begins.

When any positive indication of a kick is observed such as a sudden increase in flow or an

increase in pit level, then the well should be shut in immediately without doing a flow check. If

the increase in flow or pit gain is hard to detect then a flow check can be done to confirm the

well is flowing.

If surface hole is being drilled and the conductor pipe is not set in a competent formation and a

shallow gas kick is taken then the gas should be diverted. This will be discussed at the end of

this section.

The procedures which follow are generalised suggestions and not necessarily applicable to any

specific rig.

Soft shut-in procedure while drilling on a fixed rig

1. When any indications are observed, while drilling, that the well may be flowing, stop

rotating the drill string, raise the drill string with pumps on until tool joint is above the

drill floor.

2. Stop pumps and check for flow, if positive

3. Open choke line HCR valve.

4. Close BOP.

5. Close choke. If the choke is not a positive closing choke then close a valve downstream

of choke.

Subcontractor:

ARPF EDRGEN ENPE DBBI 0014 G01 Page 51 of 185

6. Call supervisors and commence plotting a graph of shut in drill pipe pressure. Check

pit volume gain.

7. Refer to A.P.I. R.P. 59 section 3.8 for the advantages and disadvantages of the soft

shut-in.

Note: Choke in open position while drilling.

Soft shut-in procedure while tripping on a fixed rig

1. If there is an indication of swabbing and the well flows during a flow check proceed as

follows.

2. Set the slips.

3. Install full opening safety valve (Kelly cock).

4. Close safety valve.

5. Open choke line HCR valves.

6. Close BOP.

7. Close choke.

8. Call supervisor and check pressures.

9. Install inside blowout preventer (Gray valve or Non-Return Valve).

10. Open safety valve.

General

After commencing spud-in, drilling 32” hole will be started. The drilling would be

Casing point 26” casing @ 150 m

Formation Aghajari

problem Hole opener and bit balling

Sequence of Operation

 Make up 32” BHA as per BHA design (including hole opener). Tag formation at ±14 m.

 Drill ahead formation down to ±150 m (26” casing point in Aghajari formation). Pay

enough attention to drill a straight hole. Each 50 m a TOTCO survey will be run to

evaluate hole verticality.

 As contingency plan, in case of any deviation from vertical (based on TOTCO result),

adjust drilling parameters to drop the angle and return to vertical, such as

decreasing WOB, controlling ROP, increasing FR, etc.

o Use LCM pill if heavy loss is encountered. If loss couldn’t be cured by LCM

pill, use cement plug(s) to cure it.

o following parameters are recommended to drill this hole section:

Drilling 12-17 m

WOB: 0-5 klb, RPM: 30- 50,

FR: 200-300 gpm

Drilling 17-22 m

WOB: 0-5 klb, RPM: 40- 60,

FR: In steps of 300 gpm up to 500 gpm

Do not ream the first 10 m.

Drilling 22-32 m

WOB: 0-7 klb, RPM: 40-60,

FR: In steps of 500 gpm up to 900 gpm.

Drilling 32-150 m

WOB: Maximum available

RPM: 60-80, Back reaming: 60 rpm.

FR: 900- 1100 gpm.

Note:

o 32” hole section TD is based on about ±150 m inside Aghajari formation.

o TD should be adjusted to have 1 m of rat hole below casing shoe.

o The exact TD will be determined based on 26” casing tally.

o Run Totco™ each 50 m to evaluate the verticality of the hole.

o During trips, at surface, driller is responsible to check BHA.

o Significant deviations from programmed values should be permitted by

authorized responsible level and explained.

o A material balance to determine the theoretical concentrations of additives

in the mud should be calculated and reported to WSS.

o Ensure that all drilling tools and equipment are at well site and are in

serviceable condition.

o Ensure that adequate fishing tools for this section of hole are available.

o Enough mud materials, LCM and cement should be available at rig site to use

in case of needing.

 At TD, circulate and clean the hole. Spot high viscosity pill at bottom, drop Totco

and POOH to surface. Check the bit and hole opener condition.

 Perform hole condition prior to run casing. If any indication of drag is observed, run

back to bottom. Wash and ream to make sure that the hole condition is good.

 Weld the shoe on shoe joint before start of casing running job.

 Hold safety meeting.

 Rig up 26” casing running equipment.

 Run ±150 m (approx. 13 jts) 26" casing (136.2 ppf, X-42, HG5S, CSF= 1.5 ~ 65 pcf)

with stab-in type duplex shoe to bottom as per casing program. Casing shoe should

be adjusted to have 1 m of rat hole and enough stick up (1.5 m on rig floor). Ensure

that no connector is located at wellhead elevation. Fill casing by non LCM fresh

mud joint by joint.

o To prevent back off while shoe and cement drill out, weld straps on

connectors.

Note:

o When running casing, take care not to set down excessive weight if tight

hole or ledges are encountered.

 Run stinger on DP’s using the “C-plate” &amp;amp; 5” x 26" centralizer. Sting in (~3-5 klb).

M/U &amp;amp; test cementing lines to 3000 psi/ 5 min. Circulate as 1.5 annulus volume with

FR more than cementing pumping rate (350- 400 gpm). While circulating, check the

DP’s annulus for any return. Use all the weight of DP string if observing any minor

leakage through DP’s annulus.

 Cement casing as per program. Any minor adjustment regarding the corrected depth

will be done in due time. Displace with mud (1-2 bbl short). Monitor for pressures.

Record and report the final pressure. Sting out. Check the float for any back flow.

POOH one stand, circulate to flush/ clean drill pipes.

 After cement displacement, an upward force of ~35 klb will be exerted on

casing string. Before starting cement job, tighten string to prevent upward

movement.

 While cementing, pumping pressure should not exceed 80 % of casing collapse

pressure (275 psi).

 In case the float does not hold the cement and back flow is observed, POOH

stinger to surface. DO NOT fill up the casing/ open hole annulus. Cement top job

will be performed after cement setting.

 After cement returns to cellar floor, open the 2" nipple on conductor &amp;amp; flush it.

 POOH to surface. L/D stinger.

 Keep the 26" casing on the elevator until cement surface samples get hard. Check

for casing to be centered inside 42” conductor pipe. In case of any problem, report

immediately.

Note:

o Based on the results obtained from cementing, decision will be made to

perform top-up jobs.

o If there is no cement return to surface, a top-up job should be performed to

fill the annulus. Use same slurry weight as the primary cement slurry.

Ensure the availability of adequate X-over for connecting line pipes to

cementing line. The cement should be accelerated with max. (2%) Calcium

Chloride BWOC and no other additives. Wait for the top job cement to get

hard.

 Check casing by slacking off the weight.

 Cut 42” conductor pipe from cellar base. Cut 26" casing, L/D landing joint. Dress and

bevel same.

 N/U diverter flange and perform cement top up job meanwhile.

 N/U diverter bag and related lines and valves and test all to 200 psi in 3 steps,

gradually.

Note: The height of 26" casing must be designed where the outlet of spool placed

above the ground level.

 N/U bell nipple &amp;amp; flow line.

 P/U &amp;amp; M/U next BHA and make 2000 m 5 7/8” drill pipe stands.
