Regarding formation lithology (which consists of marl) and high ROP expected, before each

connection caution must be exercised to prevent sticking. Hole conditions will dictate the

necessary practices, nevertheless following steps can be considered as recommended

practices:

 While drilling, at 5 meters before reaching the end of stand, pump 30 bbl hi-vis pill

and continue drilling. Adjust pumping time so that the pill be inside the annulus at

least 200 m above BHA.

 Continue drilling to the end of stand. At this point stop rotation and while keeping

mud circulation, pull out last stand to check the hole condition. If any drag is

observed, wash and ream the interval. Condition the hole and clear any tight spot.

 RIH back to 1 m off the bottom. Stop circulation and proceed to make up next stand.

Connection time must be minimized as much as possible.

Note:

o Run Totco before each wiper trip. If more than 300 m is drilled

continuously without trip, a wiper trip should be done.

o Adjust mud weight according to program and as hole conditions dictate.

o TD should be adjusted in such a way to have 2 m of rat hole for

probable fillings, before running casing.

o Section TD maybe changed based on formation tops detected by

wellsite geologist.

o During trips, while at surface, driller is to check BHA.

o Significant deviations from programmed values should be explained.

o A material balance to determine the theoretical concentrations of

additives in the mud should be calculated and reported to WSS.

o The mud engineer shall check the mud properties for (Ca++, Chloride,

pH, Gels, mud weight and viscosity).

o Ensure that all drilling tools and equipment are at well site in

serviceable conditions.

o Ensure that adequate fishing tools for this section are available.

o Ensure that enough amount and type of LCM are available and keep

ready to mix and pump LCM pills to cure losses.

Sequence of Operations

 Drill out LDC, shoe track, 11 ¾” liner shoe and cement of rat hole. Observe the

well for any well flow. Watch carefully for any indication of abnormal torque, since

there might be a possibility of shoe being backed off. In this case, report problems

immediately.

 Continue drilling to 4 m below the shoe.

 Circulate BTM’s up. Perform FIT.

 Circulate mud &amp;amp; displace the hole to new mud.

 Continue drilling to 14 m below the shoe.

 R/U logging equipment, Run CCL/ GR log for 11 3/4" liner. L/D logging equipment.

 P/U 7 1/2" PDC bit and 10 ¼” x 12 1/4" Georeamer. RIH to bottom.

 Continue drilling to top of platy limestone zone of Pabdeh formation. Then if heavy

mud losses are encountered, drill 7 ½” or 8 3 /8” pilot hole first (using LCM in mud

system and bypassing shale shakers) and then enlarge it to 12 ¼”. Continue drilling to

9 5/8" Casing Point @ ±3533 m.

 Hang off BOP stack. Drop 13 ⅝” x 9 ⅝” casing slips hanger. Slack off 80 % of casing

weight on the hanger. Install BOP and test CSG slips to 2000 psi pressure (open casing

head spool side outlet valves while testing).

 M/U cement head. Load the plugs. WSS is to witness the loading. Test the lines to

3000 psi for 10 minutes. Make sure that the cementing head is capable of holding

pressure while displacing and testing cement (visually).

 Perform casing cementing as per program. Any minor adjustment regarding the

corrected depth will be done in due time. Displace with mud. Monitor for pressures.

Record and report the final pressure before bumping the plug. Bump the plug with

500 psi over the final circulating pressure (or 2000 psi pumping press.). Bleed off

pressure. Check for back flow. If any back flow is observed, hold the pressure inside

until cement sets.

 While waiting on cement to get hard, slack off casing weight. Hang off BOP stack.

Rough cut 9 ⅝” landing joint. L/D same. Dress and bevel 9 ⅝” casing neck.

 Install 13 ⅝"- 5k x 11"- 10k DSA pack off. Pack &amp;amp; test p-seals.

 N/U 11”- 10k x 11”- 10k Tubing Head Spool. Pack &amp;amp; test p-seals.

 Perform top job cementing after first stage cement gets hard (if required).

Note:

o Before installing the tubing head spool, open all the test ports and

clean inside it with water and air.

and related lines to 7500 psi pressure.

Well Suspension

Sequence of Operations

 RIH with 2 7/8”, 3 ½” and 5" open end DP’s to 50 m above 5" liner.

 L/U CMT lines and test same. Set 100 m balanced CMT plug. POOH 10 STD's and flush

the string. WOC. Run back. Tag and confirm cement. Try to wash. POOH to surface

and L/D 2 7/8" DP's jt by jt.

 P/U &amp;amp; M/U 6 1/8" Bit &amp;amp; BHA. RIH to top of cement. Dress cement to confirm hard

cement. CBU and sweep well with Hi-Vis pill. POOH to surface. L/D the bit.

 RIH w/ 3 1/2" x 5" open end DP's to 50m above 7" liner, L/U CMT lines and test same,

Set 100m balanced CMT plug, POOH 10 STD's and flush STRG. WOC, Run back, Tag and

confirm cement, Try to Wash. Continue POOH to Surface.

 P/U &amp;amp; M/U 8 3/8" Bit &amp;amp; RIH to top of cement, Dress cement to confirm hard cement,

CBU and sweep well with Hi-Vis pill, POOH to surface, L/D the bit.

 RIH w/ 3 1/2" x 5" open end DP to 2050 m, H/U CMT lines and test same, Set 100m

balanced CMT plug, POOH 10 STD's and flush STRG. WOC, Run back, Tag and confirm

cement, Try to wash. Continue POOH to surface.

 P/U &amp;amp; M/U 8 3/8" Bit &amp;amp; RIH to top of cement, Dress cement to confirm hard cement,

CBU, Displace the well w/ completion fluid f/ BTM to surface.

 POOH to surface, L/D DP's and bit.

 Remove kill, choke &amp;amp; related lines, N/D flow line, bell nipple, annular preventer, 13

5/8" 10k single &amp;amp; double rams &amp;amp; DSA.

 Install 11" Blind Flange and Test Same.

32'' Hole Section

This section will be drilled 150 m through Aghajari Formation and it contains the Red

marl and Claystone with thin bed of Sandstone also occasionally treads of Gypsum

will be drilled.

This hole section will be drilled by using Bentonite mud and Hole can be sweep with

PHG every stand to drill if required.

PHB pill will be used to clean the hole and since Bentonite has the best cake around

the well bore, it will make a good cake for hole stability.

Note:

If drilling water has the chloride concentration more than 6000 mg/Lit

Bentonite will not hydrated well and Polymer mud will be used as drilling mud.

Formulation &amp;amp; properties

FLUID PROPERTIES FORMULATION

Mud Type (32”) Hi- Vis pill / Bentonite mud

Property Range Product Concentration

(lb/bbl)

Mud weight (pcf) 65 - 67 Drill Water -----------

Viscosity(sec/qt) 80 - 100 Soda Ash 0.5

PV (cp) 8 - 20 Caustic Soda 0.4

YP (lbs/100 sq ft) 25 - 40 Bentonite 35-40

pH 9.5 - 11 Lime 3 – 4 As Needed

Gel Strength(10s/10m) 15 - 20 / 20 - 30

Fluid Loss NC

Chloride (mg/Lit) Less than 5000

Mud Materials

Water, Salt, KCl, Soda Ash, Caustic Soda or Lime, Starch,

PAC-LV, PAC-R, Xanthan Gum, Barite, LCM. PHPA, Mud

thinner

24” Hole Section

This hole section will be drilled from 150 m to 2030 m, through Aghajari and Gachsaran

formation.

The lithology of this section is mostly Marl, Claystone, Minor Gypsum and Anhydrite with

some beds of Solid Anhydrite in the lower part.

The Hole will be drilled with Drill water and sweep every stand with 30bbls PHG and

wash and reaming every stand to drill till 1.5 times Bottoms up observe shall shake if

still coming full cutting resume above procedure till clean Shakers. Use PHG with

maximum 100 sq/qt to avoid hole pack off.

Continue drilling with low viscosity and low with mud approximately to 1100 to 1500m

Till observe high torque and tight hole. Start to add salt to reach Saturate to maintain

mud weight and add polymer Starch and Pac LV to control water loss below 15cc/min.

At the bottom control water loss below 10cc/min during the hole condition and CSG

running.

During to drill interval keep run all solid control available to keep LGS% as low as

possible.

17'' Hole Section

This section will be drilled from 2030 m to 2758 m consisting of mainly different

evaporated rock types, such as Anhydrite, Marl and Salt and associated with thin to

medium beds of Limestone.

Minor mud losses may occur while drilling in Limestone which usually cured by spotting

LCM.

For this section Mixed fresh mud and For weighting up mud the Barite and Hematite will

be added to mud system

While drilling this section, Hardness of mud system must be checked and monitored

accurately at least three TIMES a DAY for any increment of Calcium ions for

distinguishing the salt water flow and influx.

While drilling through the lower part of Gachsaran, a high mud weight must be used to

keep the plastic salt layers in place.

Mud weight will be controlled from 135 to 147pcf according to hole dictation.

Use the solid control equipment to control mud rheology to prevent any losses.

Loss control method:

7 ½" x 12 ¼" Hole Section

This section will be drilled from 3032 m to 3533 m through Kalhur, Operculina, Pabdeh

and Gurpi formation.

The upper part of this section consists of Limestone and Anhydrite with minor

Claystone.

The lower part consists of highly argillaceous Limestone interbeded with Claystone and

Marl. According to lithology of this section which has mainly Argillaceous Limestone,

Chalky Limestone, Marl and clay, Mud from previous section will be used to drill this

section weighted up by adding Barite.

In this section Mud weight will be controlled from 112 to 135 pcf.

and 20 m inside Kazhdumi formations. The main part of this section is thick to thin

bedded of Limestone and Argillaceous Limestone. A thin bed of 7 to 10 meter shale (The

Surgah) will be presented.

Completion Fluid

Clear Solid free Brine is the most commonly fluid used as the Completion Fluid and Work

over Operation to minimize the formation damage.

Chemicals for mixing Completion Fluid are as the following:

- NaCl will be used to increase the weight of brine up to 75 pcf.

- Approximately NaCl at 115 lb/bbl

- Corrosion Inhibitor 0.5% V/V

- Caustic Soda pH =10-11

- Oxygen Scavenger 0.5 ppb

- Biocide 0.3 ppb

- H2S Scavenger 0.2 ppb

Introduction

This document covers the drilling of production well in AZAR Oilfield, Iran. The

well is intended to produce oil from Sarvak Formation (Upper &amp;amp; Lower Zones).

Well will be drilled vertically down to total depth @ 4656 m MD (-4546 m TVDss).

The exact TD will be determined based on the geologist confirmation and logging

results.

AZAR structure is an asymmetric anticline located in the foreland of the Zagros

fold and thrust belt. The width of the structure is ~30 km. The NE flank is

dipping with approximately 5-6 degrees, while the SW flank is dipping ~10

degrees and locally up to 17 degrees.

Location Map

AZAR anticline is located in 1 km east of Mehran city and northwest of Changuleh

oil field. Based on geophysical map it has 22 km length and 13 km width on

Bangestan group. It has a single culmination which the azimuth of axial trend is

N60. Based on geophysical map it is a symmetric anticline.

Client:

Project:

Azar Oil Field Development Subcontractor:

Doc. Title:

Document Number Contract No.:AP-1-91-17

ARPF EDRGEN ENPE DBBI 0015 G00 Page 8 of 187

The nearby well AZR-2 did not encounter any oil water contacts in Ilam and

Sarvak Formations. The dynamic test data indicate that two oil systems were

encountered, one in the Upper Sarvak and one in the Lower Sarvak. From the

available pressure data and the oil down to observations in the well, the Upper

Sarvak has an anticipated oil water contact around -4330 m, and the deeper

system in the Lower Sarvak has an anticipated oil water contact at around -4550

m.

Drills

Drill shall be conducted specific intervals and attached by all required personnel.

List and Frequency of Drills:

 Fire and Rescue drills - once a month on rig

 Kick drill - once a week as per Well Control Manual

 H2S drill - once a week by each crew, when drilling in suspected or known H2S area

Fire Prevention and Protection

Whilst the risk of major fire damage in EPDS areas is considered by GPTK to be reasonably

minor, (with key risks presented by compressed gas cylinders, H2S &amp;amp; CH4 risk, painting and

insulation materials and general debris and rubbish), the risk in the camp and office areas is

considered to be high. In order to prevent such hazards materializing, GPTK will implement a

project-wide fire prevention/protection strategy that is characterized by the following

general principles.

 Minimal bulk storage on site of flammable substances

 Isolation of flammables from sources of ignition

 Ongoing housekeeping program

 Training in fire prevention and suppression techniques

 Integrity of electrical equipment

 Permit to work control of all electrical activity

 Containment of sparks and flames from Hot Works will be highly forbidden in rig

area (Zone 0 ,1)

 Escape route planning

 Restricted smoking areas.

This approach will be supported by the employment and maintenance of fire extinguishers at

strategic locations throughout the worksite and also the deployment of a fire extinguishers &amp;amp;

Client: Project:

Subcontractor:

Azar Oil Field Development

Doc. Title:

Document Number Contract No.:AP-1-91-17

ARPF EDRGEN ENPE DBBI 0015 G00 Page 43 of 187

fire pump, detectors, fix H2S &amp;amp; CH4 Gas detectors, personnel single gas detectors (Clips)

which will be applied permanently charged at a strategic location.

The fire prevention/protection strategy will include all worksite offices, warehouses, camp,

etc., and will be developed to include commissioning activities.

Electrical Equipment for Classified Areas

Classified areas

All electrical equipment installed in a classified area shall have a correct type of protection.

The classified areas drawings on each rig shall be defined by the GPTK Engineering

Department.

All GPTK rigs shall have clearly identified hazardous areas. Definition of classified areas:

Zone 1 in which an explosive gas/ mixture is likely to occur in normal operations.

Zone 2 in which an explosive gas/ mixture is not likely to occur in normal operation and if it

occurs, will exist only for a short time.

Non-hazardous area: manned or unmanned areas in which an explosive gas/mixture will not

occur in normal operations.

Note: a “Zone 0” is also defined as a zone where explosive gas/air mixtures are continuously

present or present for long periods.

-Equipment suitable for classified areas

Electrical equipment shall comply with flag authority and API specifications for each of the

classified areas. Additional Clients requirements shall be referred to GPTK Engineering for

review.

-Combustion engines located inside zone 2

All combustion engines operated within a zone 2 area shall be equipped with:

 spark arresting system on exhaust (or spark arrestor silencer)

 Quick shut

 off device acting on fuel supply and/ or air intake manifold Engines permanently

located within a zone 2 area will be equipped with a flameproof starter (air).

Well Control Policy

Objectives

To cover the shut-in procedures and diverter procedures for a surface BOP. To cover

A.P.I. recommendations for these procedures which includes advantages and

disadvantages.

General introduction to shut-in procedures on a fixed rig

Note: A fixed rig is defined as a drilling rig equipped with a surface BOP.

Shut-in procedure should be agreed by contractor and operating company and posted on

rig floor before drilling the well begins.

When any positive indication of a kick is observed such as a sudden increase in flow or an

increase in pit level, then the well should be shut in immediately without doing a flow

check. If the increase in flow or pit gain is hard to detect then a flow check can be done

to confirm that the well is flowing.

If surface hole is being drilled and the conductor pipe is not set in a competent formation

and a shallow gas kick is taken then the gas should be diverted.

The procedures which follow are generalised suggestions and not necessarily applicable to

any specific rig.

Kick (Wellbore Influx) Indications

Kick Indications mean that there is possibility to get influx into wellbore. The indications

can be either kick or just formation react while drilling. You need to remember that just

only a single possible indicator cannot may not good enough to identify underbalanced

condition in wellbore and the possible kick indicators must be used collectively.

Therefore, drilling team on the rig needs to closely monitor the well and prepare

appropriate action plans. The indications include:

- Flow rate increase

- Pit volume increase

- Flowing well with pumps off

Subcontractor:

Azar Oil Field Development

Document Number Contract No.:AP-1-91-17

ARPF EDRGEN ENPE DBBI 0015 G00 Page 49 of 187

- Pump pressure decrease and pump stroke increase

- Improper hole fill-up on trips

- String weight change

- Drilling break

- Cut mud weight

Kick Tollerance:

Kick tollerance for different hole sections are as below:

24” hole secction: 150 bbl

17” hole secction: 100 bbl

14 1/4” hole secction: 50 bbl

12 1/4” hole secction: 50 bbl

8 3/8” hole secction: 25 bbl

24” hole secction: 25 bbl

Soft shut-in procedure while drilling on a fixed rig

1. When any indications are observed, while drilling, that the well may be flowing, stop

rotating the drill string, raise the drill string with pumps on until tool joint is above the

drill floor.

2. Stop pumps and check for flow, if positive

3. Open choke line HCR valve.

4. Close BOP.

5. Close choke. If the choke is not a positive closing choke then close a valve

downstream of choke.

6. Call supervisors and commence plotting a graph of shut in drill pipe pressure. Check

pit volume gain.

Client: Project:

Subcontractor:

Azar Oil Field Development

Doc. Title:

Document Number Contract No.:AP-1-91-17

ARPF EDRGEN ENPE DBBI 0015 G00 Page 50 of 187

7. Refer to A.P.I. R.P. 59 section 3.8 for the advantages and disadvantages of the soft

shut-in.

Note: Choke in open position while drilling.

Soft shut-in procedure while tripping on a fixed rig

1. If there is an indication of swabbing and the well flows during a flow check proceed

as follows.

2. Set the slips.

3. Install full opening safety valve (Kelly cock).

4. Close safety valve.

5. Open choke line HCR valves.

6. Close BOP.

7. Close choke.

8. Call supervisor and check pressures.

9. Install inside blowout preventer (Gray valve or Non-Return Valve).

10. Open safety valve.

24” holesection was drilled from 150m to

2074m MD (47m in Gachsaran#7 formation). Drilled litho logy

(AGHAJARI Formation) was mostly contains red marl, sand stone, silt

stone &amp;amp; some beds of solid anhydrite. Tight holes, bit balling, swelled

Clay and low ROP was the major problem during drilling this hole

section. Also string stuck on one occasion. In order to increase ROP &amp;amp;

apply maximum rotation 9 5/8" PDM used for this hole section.

Aforesaid hole section was mostly drilled with 24" PDC bit (IADC

Code: S223).

SS/ KCl/ Polymer Mud system (66 ‐ 90pcf) used for drilling 24" hole

section.

20 x18 5/8" casing string (0‐681m *18 5/8", 114ppf, K‐55, BTC* 681‐

1192.6m *18 5/8", 136ppf, N‐80, BTC* &amp;amp; 1192.6‐2073.5m *20",

169ppf, P‐110, Big Omega*) was ran in hole. Cementing operations

was performed with special cement head tool as CRRT (Cementing

Running &amp;amp; Retrieving Tool) in one stage (lead cement: 2420bbl, Class

"G" S.W: 96pcf &amp;amp; Tail cement: 180bbl, Class "G" S.W: 118pcf). NL‐NG

occurred during this hole section.

17" hole section was drilled from 2074 to

2764.5m (9.5m in Cap rock). Drilled litho logy (Gachsaran formation;

members: 6,5,4,3,2 and cap rock) were mostly contain different

evaporated rock types such as anhydrite, marl, salt and associated

with thin to medium beds of limestone.

For this hole section "Kelly assembly" was rig up &amp;amp; used to 2245m in

order to apply max rotation. FIT performed at 2078 with EMW

147pcf. NL‐NG occurred during this hole section. Aforesaid hole

section was mostly drilled with 17" PDC bit (IADC Code: M1665).

Salt Saturated Polymer Mud system (123 ‐149pcf) used for drilling

17" hole section.

Logging operations was performed in 3xRUN; RUN#1: GR+Sonic

RUN#2: Caliper+Sonic &amp;amp; RUN#3: Caliper+GR+Sonic,

14"x13‐5/8"x13‐3/8" Casing string (0‐678.93m *13 3/8", 72ppf, N‐

80, BTC* 678.93‐1370.68m *13 5/8", 88.2ppf, Q‐125, BTC &amp;amp;

1370.68‐2754m *14", 114ppf, Q‐125, BTC*) was ran in hole.

Cementing operations was performed in one stage (Lead cement

568.5bbl, Class "D" S.W: 152pcf Tail cement: 58bbl, Class "D" S.W:

125pcf). After Cement operations, Annuals return was observed

with max 50bbl/hr. Closed Annulus &amp;amp; monitored pressure behavior.

Then finally open Annuals to atm as per client &amp;amp; monitor return was

kept same. **Return stopped 43days after cementing operations

General

After commencing spud-in, drilling 32” hole will be started. The drilling would be

anticipated to go on fast.

Casing point 26” casing @ 150 m

Formation Aghajari

problem Hole opener and bit balling

Sequence of Operation

 Make up 32” BHA as per BHA design (including hole opener). Tag formation at ±14 m.

 Drill ahead formation down to ±150 m (26” casing point in Aghajari formation). Pay

enough attention to drill a straight hole. Each 50 m a TOTCO survey will be run to

evaluate hole verticality.

 As contingency plan, in case of any deviation from vertical (based on TOTCO result),

adjust drilling parameters to drop the angle and return to vertical, such as

decreasing WOB, controlling ROP, increasing FR, etc.

use cement plug(s) to cure it.

Drilling 12-17 m

WOB: 0-5 klb, RPM: 30- 50,

o A material balance to determine the theoretical concentrations of additives in

 At TD, circulate and clean the hole. Spot high viscosity pill at bottom, drop Totco

and POOH to surface. Check the bit and hole opener condition.

 Perform hole condition prior to run casing. If any indication of drag is observed, run

back to bottom. Wash and ream to make sure that the hole condition is good.

 Weld the shoe on shoe joint before start of casing running job.

 Hold safety meeting.

 Rig up 26” casing running equipment.

 Run ±150 m (approx. 13 jts) 26" casing (136.2 ppf, X-42, HG5S, CSF= 1.5 ~ 65 pcf)

with stab-in type duplex shoe to bottom as per casing program. Casing shoe should

be adjusted to have 1 m of rat hole and enough stick up (1.5 m on rig floor). Ensure

that no connector is located at wellhead elevation. Fill casing by non LCM fresh

mud joint by joint.

o To prevent back off while shoe and cement drill out, weld straps on connectors.

Note:

o When running casing, take care not to set down excessive weight if tight hole

or ledges are encountered.

 Run stinger on DP’s using the “C-plate” &amp;amp; 5” x 26" centralizer. Sting in (~3-5 klb).

M/U &amp;amp; test cementing lines to 3000 psi/ 5 min. Circulate as 1.5 annulus volume with

FR more than cementing pumping rate (350- 400 gpm). While circulating, check the

DP’s annulus for any return. Use all the weight of DP string if observing any minor

leakage through DP’s annulus.

 Cement casing as per program. Any minor adjustment regarding the corrected depth

will be done in due time. Displace with mud (1-2 bbl short). Monitor for pressures.

Record and report the final pressure. Sting out. Check the float for any back flow.

POOH one stand, circulate to flush/ clean drill pipes.

 After cement displacement, an upward force of ~35 klb will be exerted on

casing string. Before starting cement job, tighten string to prevent upward

movement.

 While cementing, to prevent collapse, pressure should not exceed 170 psi over

pumping pressure.

 In case the float does not hold the cement and back flow is observed, POOH

stinger to surface. DO NOT fill up the casing/ open hole annulus. Cement top job

will be performed after cement setting.

 After cement returns to cellar floor, open the 2" nipple on conductor &amp;amp; flush it.

 POOH to surface. L/D stinger.

 Keep the 26" casing on the elevator until cement surface samples get hard. Check

for casing to be centered inside 42” conductor pipe. In case of any problem, report

immediately.

Note:

o Based on the results obtained from cementing, decision will be made to

perform top-up jobs.

o If there is no cement return to surface, a top-up job should be performed to

fill the annulus. Use same slurry weight as the primary cement slurry. Ensure

the availability of adequate X-over for connecting line pipes to cementing line.

The cement should be accelerated with max. (2%) Calcium Chloride BWOC and

no other additives. Wait for the top job cement to get hard.

 Check casing by slacking off the weight.

 Cut 42” conductor pipe from cellar base. Cut 26" casing, L/D landing joint. Dress and

bevel same.

 N/U diverter flange and perform cement top up job meanwhile.

Regarding formation lithology (which consists of marl) and high ROP expected, before each

connection caution must be exercised to prevent sticking. Hole conditions will dictate the

necessary practices, nevertheless following steps can be considered as recommended

practices:

 While drilling, at 5 meters before reaching the end of stand, pump 30 bbl hi-vis pill

and continue drilling. Adjust pumping time so that the pill be inside the annulus at

least 200 m above BHA.

 Continue drilling to the end of stand. At this point stop rotation and while keeping

mud circulation, pull out last stand to check the hole condition. If any drag is

observed, wash and ream the interval. Condition the hole and clear any tight spot.

 RIH back to 1 m off the bottom. Stop circulation and proceed to make up next stand.

Connection time must be minimized as much as possible.

Note:

o Run Totco before each wiper trip. If more than 300 m is drilled

continuously without trip, a wiper trip should be done.

o Adjust mud weight according to program and as hole conditions dictate.

fillings, before running casing.

o Section TD maybe changed based on formation tops detected by wellsite

geologist.

o During trips, while at surface, driller is to check BHA.

o Significant deviations from programmed values should be explained.

 M/U 6 1/8" PDC bit and RIH to bottom. Continue drilling 6 1/8" hole section to well

TD at 4656 m (±20 m into Kazhdumi formation).

o To obtain optimum parameters for drilling, drill off test should be performed.

However, following parameters are recommended to drill this hole section:

WOB : 15- 20 klb

FR : 250- 350 gpm

Rotation : 60- 150 rpm

Note:

o Adjust mud weight according to program and as hole conditions dictate.

o Section TD may be changed based on formation tops detected by wellsite

geologist.

o Perform BOP stack pressure test every week, as per policy.

o Choke line and choke manifold must be lined up for Soft SHUT-IN.

o During trips, while at surface, driller is responsible to check BHA.

o A material balance to determine the theoretical concentrations of additives in

the mud should be calculated and reported to WSS.

o Ensure that all drilling tools and equipment are at well site and are in

serviceable condition.

o Ensure that adequate fishing tools for this section are available.

o Ensure that enough amounts of LCM are available

 At section TD, CBU and sweep the hole cleaned. Perform condition trip to 7" shoe

observe the well for one hour.

 RIH to bottom and circulate to clean hole. Check bottoms up for any drag and influx.

Prior to run log, adjust mud weight if needed.

 Spot 50 bbl of High Vis pill to stabilize the hole prior to run log. POOH to surface.

 R/U logging equipment. Run Litho Density/ Compensated Neutron/ GR Spectrometry/

Induction/ Micro Resistivity/ BHC and CDR logs.

 Perform condition trip prior to run Pressure Test Log. RIH to BTM, CBU and check

bottoms up for any influx; POOH to surface.

 R/U wireline logging equipment and run Pressure Test log. R/D wireline.

 RIH w/ 6 1/8" used milled tooth bit. Condition the hole prior to run 5" liner. Check

bottoms up for any kick; adjust mud weight if required before running 5” Liner. POOH

to surface.

ARPF EDRGEN ENPE DBBI 0015 G00 Page 90 of 187

 R/U 5" liner running tools. Hold pre-job safety meeting.

 Run 5" liner as per program to bottom. P/U and run liner hanger and accessories.

Follow liner string with 3 1/2” DP’s (pass drift through DP’s &amp;amp; perform SLM while RIH

with liner).

 Set liner hanger. Release setting tool. M/U cement manifold. Load pump-down plug.

WSS is to witness the loading. Test the lines to 4000 psi/ 10 min and 500 psi/ 5 min.

Make sure that the cement manifold is capable of holding pressure while displacing

and testing cement (visually).

 Circulate slowly 1.2 times of string volume with low FR. Mix and pump cement as per

program. Release pumpdown plug. Displace the plug and cement with mud. Monitor

pressures. Record and report the final pressure before bumping the plug.

 After bumping, green cement (liner and liner lap integrity) test should be done

to maximum 80 % of weakest casing burst rate and liner hanger pressure rating (4000

psi).

 If bumping was not observed, casing integrity test must be performed before

drilling out LDC and shoe track (at least 24 hours after cementing).

 Pull out setting tools 10 stands. Circulate out excess cement slurry &amp;amp; flush string.

POOH to surface.

 M/U 6 1/8" bit. Clean out well to top of 5" liner lap. POOH to surface.

 P/U 4 1/8" milled tooth bit or mill and new BHA. P/U 2 7/8" DP’s jt by jt. RIH and

clean out inside 5" liner to LDC.

 Displace the well w/ completion (non solid) fluid.

 POOH above liner lap.

 Perform pressure test of 5” liner lap. POOH to surface.

 M/U scraper and scrape dry test packer setting depth.

 RIH with dry test tools, fill up string with cushion fluid. Set packer and perform dry

test (negative test) of liner lap. POOH to surface.

Note:

o Cushion weight and height will be advised at appropriate time. However, this

scenario is considered as basis for pressure drawdown calculations: While

production, the well is full with reservoir fluid (0.3 psi/ft gradient) and

perforations are plugged.

Well Suspension

Sequence of Operations

 RIH with 2 7/8”, 3 ½” and 5" open end DP’s to 50 m above 5" liner.

 L/U CMT lines and test same. Set 100 m balanced CMT plug. POOH 10 STD's and flush

the string. WOC. Run back. Tag and confirm cement. Try to wash. POOH to surface

and L/D 2 7/8" DP's jt by jt.

 P/U &amp;amp; M/U 6 1/8" Bit &amp;amp; BHA. RIH to top of cement. Dress cement to confirm hard

cement. CBU and sweep well with Hi-Vis pill. POOH to surface. L/D the bit.

 RIH w/ 3 1/2" x 5" open end DP's to 50m above 7" liner, L/U CMT lines and test same,

Set 100m balanced CMT plug, POOH 10 STD's and flush STRG. WOC, Run back, Tag and

confirm cement, Try to Wash. Continue POOH to Surface.

 P/U &amp;amp; M/U 8 3/8" Bit &amp;amp; RIH to top of cement, Dress cement to confirm hard cement,

CBU and sweep well with Hi-Vis pill, POOH to surface, L/D the bit.

 RIH w/ 3 1/2" x 5" open end DP to 2050 m, H/U CMT lines and test same, Set 100m

balanced CMT plug, POOH 10 STD's and flush STRG. WOC, Run back, Tag and confirm

cement, Try to wash. Continue POOH to surface.

 P/U &amp;amp; M/U 8 3/8" Bit &amp;amp; RIH to top of cement, Dress cement to confirm hard cement,

CBU, Displace the well w/ completion fluid f/ BTM to surface.

 POOH to surface, L/D DP's and bit.

 Remove kill, choke &amp;amp; related lines, N/D flow line, bell nipple, annular preventer, 13

5/8" 10k single &amp;amp; double rams &amp;amp; DSA.

 Install 11" Blind Flange and Test Same.

32'' Hole Section

This section will be drilled 150 m through Aghajari Formation and it contains the Red

marl and Claystone with thin bed of Sandstone also occasionally treads of Gypsum

will be drilled.

This hole section will be drilled by using Bentonite mud and Hole can be sweep with

PHG every stand to drill if required.

PHB pill will be used to clean the hole and since Bentonite has the best cake around

the well bore, it will make a good cake for hole stability.

Note:

If drilling water has the chloride concentration more than 6000 mg/Lit

Bentonite will not hydrated well and Polymer mud will be used as drilling mud.

24” Hole Section

This hole section will be drilled from 150 m to 2027 m, through Aghajari and Gachsaran

formation.The lithology of this section is mostly Marl, Claystone, Minor Gypsum and

Anhydrite with some beds of Solid Anhydrite in the lower part.

The Hole will be drilled with Drill water and sweep every stand with 30 bbl PHG and

wash and reaming every stand to drill till 1.5 times Bottoms up observe shall shake if

still coming full cutting resume above procedure till clean Shakers. Use PHG with

maximum 100 sq/qt to avoid hole pack off.

Continue drilling with low viscosity and low with mud approximately to 1100 to 1500 m

till observe high torque and tight hole. Start to add salt to reach Saturate to maintain

mud weight and add polymer Starch and Pac LV to control water loss below 15cc/min.

At the bottom control water loss below 15 cc/30 min during the hole condition and CSG

running. While drilling interval keep all solid control equipment running available to

keep LGS% as low as possible.

Refer to loss control table (page 111).

17'' Hole Section

This section will be drilled from 2027 m to 2679 m consisting of mainly different

evaporated rock types, such as Anhydrite, Marl and Salt and associated with thin to

medium beds of Limestone.

Minor mud losses may occur while drilling in Limestone which usually cured by spotting

LCM.

For this section Mixed fresh mud and For weighting up mud the Barite and Hematite will

be added to mud system

While drilling this section, Hardness of mud system must be checked and monitored

accurately at least three TIMES a DAY for any increment of Calcium ions for

distinguishing the salt water flow and influx.

While drilling through the lower part of Gachsaran, a high mud weight must be used to

keep the plastic salt layers in place.

Mud weight will be controlled from 120 to 147pcf according to hole dictation.

Use the solid control equipment to control mud rheology to prevent any losses.

Loss control method:

Refer to loss control table (page 111).

Formulation &amp;amp; properties

The below concentration of chemicals can be changed according to mud properties

while drilling.

7 ½" x 12 ¼" Hole Section

This section will be drilled from 2990 m to 3490 m through Kalhur, Operculina, Pabdeh

and Gurpi formation.

The upper part of this section consists of Limestone and Anhydrite with minor

Claystone.

The lower part consists of highly argillaceous Limestone interbeded with Claystone and

Marl. According to lithology of this section which has mainly Argillaceous Limestone,

Chalky Limestone, Marl and clay, Mud from previous section will be used to drill this

section weighted up by adding Barite.

For cementing operation, note the followings:

 Conduct safety meeting prior to start operation.

 Circulate mud and clean inside casing and annulus.

 Flush all the lines with water. Test the lines to 3000 psi for 10

minutes.

 Mix and pump cement as per program. Total slurry volume is

calculated based on 100% excess in open hole.

 All samples should be stored until the success of the cement job has

been verified, then they may be discarded.

 Fill up the cementing operation sheet and send it to drilling office.

 Ensure that the 26" casing is full of mud before pumping cement and

stinger for leakage inside casing.

100% excess in open hole and 20% excess in cased hole.

 All samples should be stored until the success of the cement job has been

verified, then they may be discarded.

 Fill up the cementing operation sheet and send it to drilling office.

1 INTRODUCTION

1.1 History

The SAADAT ABAD oil-field is located in 90 Km. south west of Shiraz city and 11

Km. west of Sarvestan city. This oil field was discovered by drilling the first well at

1973 and existence of hydrocarbon is proved in Sarvak Formations. This project

including drilling and completion of 2 new vertical wells and re-entry one existing

well.

1 INTRODUCTION

The Saadat Abad oil field is located in the south of Iran in Fars province, about 60

kilometers south east of Shiraz. It has a saturated oil reservoir with a primary gascap

contained in the Ilam and Sarvak Formation. The Saadat Abad field was discovered in 1973

(1352 Iranian Calendar) by well SAA-1 which encountered a large oil column in Bangestan

reservoirs. A further appraisal well SAA-2 was drilled down dip (in northwest of north

flank) in 1975 (1354 Iranian Calendar).

The Saadat Abad field consists of an asymmetrical anticline with trending NE-SW with a

dip around 22° on the north flank and around 14° on south flank. Based on the Static

pressure of Zagros Company, Bangestan Reservoir is expected 4020psi in -1280mss in year-

97. Reservoir temperature is expected to be 179 Fahrenheit in -1280mss based on the

resources and statistic notebook report.

GOC and OWC based on Reservoir Engineering Proposal respectively, -1205, -1495mss,

seven drilled wells in this field until now.

The gas oil contact could not be observed in SAA-1 although the G.O.C was reported to be

at -1205mss and O.W.C was recorded at -1495mss (ICOFC proposal and SAA-3 data) and

the hydrocarbon thickness is approximately 411m in Saadat Abad field. In Saadat Abad Oil

field, sour oil is observed and it contains 0.63% H2S and 1.83% CO2 approximately.

SAA#1 was drilled to total depth of 2821m in Sarvak fm., SAA-2 was drilled as an

exploration well about 3.8 Km east of SAA-1 well. SAA-2 was spudded on 9March 1975

and reached a TD of 3480.90m in November 1975. The main objective was to test the Ilam

and Sarvak formation. The Sachun and Dariyan formation were considered secondary

objectives.

According to the last U.G.C map 1397, Saadat Abad-E014S is situated in the southeast flank

of Saadat Abad anticline, about 2914m in the east of well#3 and about 2784m in the

Southwest of well#4. This well in Plan will be drilled directionally from 2160m as a K.O.P.

to Total Depth of 3464.28m (+68.3m V.Thickness) inside of Sarvak Formation.

CBL/VDL&amp;amp; CCL/GR log Formation will be run from 7" liner shoe. CDR/Full suite will be

run in open hole 5 7/8".

This well will be completed as Sarvak oil producer through 5 7/8" open hole.

2 GENERAL FORMATION LITHOLOGY DESCRIPTION (In

Deviation Hole)

A normal stratigraphical sequence in Saadat Abad –006 (E014S) is expected from K.O.P.

(Through Gurpi Fm.) to total depth. In Sarvak Formation is as follows:

- Gurpi Fm. (From K.O.P.2160 m to 2897.55 m) drilled thickness + 737.55 m:

This formation consists of a thick sequence of dark gray to greenish gray calcareous silty

shale and greenish grey, soft and sticky marl, with subordinate layers of grey to dark

grayargillaceous and marly limestone.

Thickness of Gurpi formation is variable in Saadat Abad structure.

- Ilam Fm. 2897.55 – 3048.89m.) drilled thickness 151.34 m:

The top of Ilam formation is marked by a change in lithology from marl in to a dark brown,

brown to light brown limestone. This formation consists of light gray to grayish brown

crystalline, fossilliferous and porous limestone and as well as in lower part consists of brown

dark brown argillaceous limestone and in some part marly limestone.

- Sarvak Fm. (3048.89m to TD at 3464.28 m) drilled thickness +415.39m.:

It consists of a sequence of white-off white chalky and brownish gray well bedded

crystalline limestone, partly argillaceous and slightly chalky. The 1/3 basal of Sarvak

formation contains of a series of dark brown dense argillaceous, sparry limestone, which are

partly bituminous and partly glauconitic. Sarvak formation divided into 8 zones in Saadat

Abad field.

Note:

In Saadat Abad Oil field, sour oil is observed and it contains 0.63% H2S and 1.83% CO2.

Bangestan Reservoir is expected 4020psi in -1280mss in year-97.

Reservoir temperature is expected to be 179Fahrenheit at -1280mss. in year-96.

Losses are probable in Ilam &amp;amp; Sarvak Fms.

Gas &amp;amp; Oil in Ilam &amp;amp; Sarvak Fms can be present.

Structural uncertainties for top Formations estimated +/-50m.

5 Drilling Hazard

 Drilling through Ilam and Sarvak Formations in this field has been accompanied with

moderate losses and from Gurpi Formation to T.D. losses is expected.

 Drilling in Shale parts of Gurpi Formation in this field has been accompanied with tight holes

and stuck pipes; special care is recommended for Mud type and drilling in this formation.

 While drilling in Limestone lithology water flow is predicted, so special care is

recommended while drilling this section.

 Losses are probable in Ilam &amp;amp; Sarvak Fms.

 In drilling Ilam and Sarvak Fms; it possible to have signs of hydrocarbon, Mud cut and flow.

Especial care is recommended while drilling these Fms.

 In Saadat Abad Oil field, sour oil is observed and it contains 0.63% H2S and 1.83% CO2.

Due to the existence of H2S in this field, in this regards, safety regulations should be highly

considered.

 Structural uncertainties for top Fm. estimated +/- 50m.

 Mud Losses and Gas flow maybe occurred in Ilam and Sarvak Fm.

*So special care is recommended while drilling this section.

6 Sample Requirement and Procedure

Sampling from cutting, Thin Section preparing during drilling of

Geological Formations.

 The maximum sampling rate for non-reservoir and shallow Formation requested one sample

from each 5 meters intervals

 From the Formations with lithology of Limestone, Dolomite and Sandstone which are not

considered as reservoirs, sampling should be carried out such as Reservoir

Formations (every 2 meters).

 From reservoir Formation and nearby casing point and liner point for maximum of each 1

meters for Thin Section is necessary.

 During drilling of the wells, any lithology change should be sampled and investigated.

 During coring addition to core description and Thin Section preparation, resulted data should

be entered in Data base in specified forms and charts with standard format.

 During conventional coring (without Fiber glass) it is necessary to prepare for SCAL analysis

and should be seals as NIOC standard.

 form non-reservoir requested one thin section from each 10 meters intervals

 From the Formations with lithology of Limestone, Dolomite and Sandstone which are

considered as reservoirs, one thin section should be carried out from each 2 meters intervals.

For any decision such as Top Formations or members, casing point depth, K.O.P, logging

point and intervals and Total depth and other important issue during drilling of the well, well

site geologist should coordinate these issues with area geologist and head of operation.

1.2 Saadat Abad-1:

Saadat Abad well No.-1 was drilled to explore the Ilam-Sarvak units which are also the

reservoir rocks in Sarvestan structure. The Tarbur Formation was also considered as the

auxiliary objective.

During drilling of the well, some indication of gas and oil were observed in Sachun Formation,

but performed tests in Sachun and Tarbur Formations did not yield commercial oil or gas.

Production tests, intervals 2744.30-2748.50 and 2695.70-2718.70m, of Sarvak Formation

revealed the maximum recovery, after acidization, of 160bbls/hr of crude oil with 3/4" choke.

Based on the interpretation of the seismic records and obtained data of drilled wells (SAA-1

and SAA-2) the areal and vertical closures of Saadat Abad structure, on top of Ilam Formation,

are around 93Km2 and 770m respectively. The proved gas-oil column is 385m with the area of

closure of 37Km2. The well is temporarily abandoned.

Shows:

 No indications of gas or oil were observed in the formations younger than the Sachun

Formation.

 Oil-stained samples and gas indications along with asphaltic impregnations were

recorded in the Ilam Formation.

 Gas &amp;amp; Oil, with asphaltic impregnations were confirmed in the Sarvak

1.3 Saadat Abad-04:

This well is fourth well in Saadat Abad field with location (E025N) and situated in east of

structure in north flank in a distance of 2490m in the east of Saa-1 &amp;amp; 1360m west of SAA-2.

This well spudded and start drilling in 1389/01/29, normal geological succession was drilled

from surface (recent sediment) to total depth of 2945m in Sarvak Fm(zone-4), Withal The

Sarvak and Ilam formations has been recognized about 59m &amp;amp;38m lower than forecast

geology program. 26" open hole: this section was drilled to 156m (casing point18 5/8") with

65 pcf bentonite mud, 17 1/2" open hole: after drill out cement and 18 5/8" shoe (155m), this

section was drilled from 155 to 2018(casing point 13 3/8" 2017.5m) with 65-74 bentonit mud;

(during drilling in this Hole Washout (1868-1749) and tight hole (849), has been observed in

this well).

12 1/4" open hole: after running and cement 13 3/8" casing (2017.5m) start drilling from 2018

m in Gurpi formation to 27618m (in Ilam fm) and take CDR/GR log. After that continue

drilling with 71-73 pcf oil base mud to 2945m (Total Depth) in Sarvak formation, 9 5/8"

casing run and cemented in 2944.5m, Totally 4 cores were cut through in Ilam &amp;amp; Sarvak Fms.

 Hold pre-move meeting on location. Discuss contingency plans for:

 Safe arrangements for rig up and rig down.

 Safe standby areas for rig in case move have to be suspended.

 Loss of trucks in case of repair.

 Moving at night.

 Hold pre-move safety meeting. Ensure everyone understands individual

responsibilities:

a) Contractor

 Provide trucks and vehicles

 Defend GPTK/ICOFC property

 Co-ordinate overall moving operations with other parties in contractor

 Ensure HSE guidelines are followed

b) Contractor Rigs

 Rig down, rig up and rig modifications.

 Movement of rig.

Note: Only rig manager will give orders to moving crew during rig move.

 Personnel on Board

 Company representative on location

 Contractor Rig Manager - senior Rig representative on location. He has

ultimate responsibility for rig move.

 Position rig for optimal operations

 Rig up on cellar

 Finish rig up and commence operational procedure for SAA-006

Note: Before leaving previous location, all equipment should be checked.

 Test all manifold and surface safety valves.

 RKB – GLE and Elevation should be recorded.

 Spud date and time.

2 PRE SPUD

Company representative prepared a pre-spud checklist and distributed it in contractor rigs.

The checklist will be performed based on the aforementioned checklist. In addition to the

checklist, following matters should be checked:

 Check &amp;amp; observe the alignment of the rig. This check will be performed in four stages;

rig levelling, derrick verticality, derrick alignment with rotary table, rotary table

alignment with conductor pipe. To do this pick up 3 joints of 9 3/4” DC and check the

verticality of the derrick.

 Mechanical facilities for mud treatment such as:

Desander, Desilter, mud cleaner, proper size of shaker–screens, hoppers, mud guns &amp;amp;

mixers, should be all available on rig and functioning properly.

 All mud tanks, mud transfer lines &amp;amp; connection should be checked by filling them

with water &amp;amp; cross wellhead circulation.

 Mud engineer laboratory should be equipped with a complete set of testing

equipment. The calibration should be done under supervision of well site drilling

supervisor before starting the operation.

 Weight indicator, rotary speed gauge, any smart drilling instrumentation, Stroke

meter, pressure gauges on manifold and in the drilling console, loss / gain gauge and

any other gauges should be checked and calibrated.

 Stand pipe manifold valves &amp;amp; connection must be checked &amp;amp; pressure tested.

 All motors should be checked under load prior to start drilling.

 Check &amp;amp; control mud stock &amp;amp; cement stock every day &amp;amp; if there is any necessity to

request mud material, cement or any drilling tool, it should be prepared &amp;amp; requested

at proper time.

Note: Fill up pre-spud check list and send it to drilling office.

4.1 Sequence of Operations

 Inspect and service well head and annulus valves by wellhead crew

 Install kill and choke lines, Pressure test same

 Read and record the pressure inside 9 5/8" casing and tubing, Check the pressures

of all annulus (Bleed off the pressure to zero, if any and check for re build same),

Test all P-seals, Monitor the well at least 5 hours.

 R/U wire line and test, Retrieve the 3SV pump in C.L to sure it's free. Install

Dummy, Test control line.

 Bull head the well w/67 pcf Mud, Observed W/H &amp;amp; tubing annulus pressure, make

sure No pressure in annulus.

 R/U Wire line, install plug &amp;amp; prong in NO GO below Packer &amp;amp; test same. Recheck

pressure in annulus.

 Open SSD, displace 67 pcf mud in tubing and completion fluid in annlus with 74

pcf mud. Close SSD.

 Install two way check valve in TBG Hanger, test same, N/D X-Mass Tree. While

circulation cross wellhead

 N/U 13 5/8"- 5 k BOP stack, choke manifold, bell nipple and related lines, test it as

per policy. Remove two way check valve from hanger.

 Make about 110 stands of 5", 55 stand of 3 1/2" DP, 12 stand of 3 1/2" HWDP, 12

stand 5" HWDP meanwhile prepare ±80 pcf WBM.

 R/U wire line and Recover Prong and plug through No Go nipple, N/D wire line

equipment.

 P/U landing joint, screw in tubing hanger, Loose tie down screw, Test glands to

1000psi, Pick up string till travel joint opened, Make 2000lb overpull, Release

completion string from anchor seal by 20 right turn, circulate out completion fluid

and balance MW. POOH &amp;amp; L/D completion string. (Packer Completion@ 2280.35m

inside 7" liner)

 RIH w/ 8 1/2" Mill and BHA to top of Liner lap@ 2213m, POOH to surface.

 RIH 2 7/8" open end pipes and set 116m cement plug on top of 7" Completion

Packer, wait on cement to get hard, tag cement. POOH to surface.

 RIH 8 1/2" Bit to top of cement, Drill out cement to 2180m,CBU, Pressure test

casing to 2000psi and make sure no pressure drop, CBU 80 pcf mud, POOH to

surface.

 RIH w/ 8 1/2" mill and 9 5/8" scraper to Scrape whipstoke setting depth to 2180m,

CBU, POOH to surface

 RIH with Whipstoke &amp;amp; BHA to 2160m, Run Gyro and set tool face &amp;amp; Set

whipstoke.

1 8.5" HOLE SECTION

1.1 8-1/2” Hole Section Characteristics

This section will be drilled to 3064 m MD in Sarvak formation.

8 1/2" Hole Section

Formations Ilam, Sarvak

Drilling Interval 2160 to 3064 m MD

Interval Length (m) 904

In case of any losses, the only remedy considered is to use LCM in Viscose pill

1.2 Drilling Fluid Properties

Inhibitive Salt water KCL/Polymer mud is proposed to drill this section which will

provide inhibition against anhydrates and problematic shale inter-beds through the hole

section. Fluid loss should be controlled through the section, it could start from 6 ranges

then firmly controlled down to below 3 prior to drilling shales beds.

Viscosity is maintained using purified Starch, high YP and low end rheologies should be

kept in range.

Monitor hole cleaning and sweep the hole with high viscosity pills as needed.

Perform periodic wiper trips to monitor hole integrity.

Drill to the well total depth, circulate hole clean and spot a viscous pill on bottom before

tripping out to run casing.

1.3 Drilling Fluid Mixing

Drilling water should be treated for hardness before additions of purified polymers.

PAC LV or CMC-LV will assist to control fluid loss, XC-Polymer with Starch &amp;amp; HPHTStarch will require the Viscosity and mud rheology

KCl / NaCl and Calcium Carbonate will maintain required MW. On top of weight

resulted from Brine/Calcium Carbonate, Mud Weight to be provided by addition of

weighting agent (Barite).

2.4 Sequence of Operations

 WSS is to supervise the loading of liner wiper plug in liner running tool, and loading

of drill pipe wiper dart in cementing head.

 The liner hanger engineer is to be on the rig floor at all times that the liner is being

run in open hole.

 Hold pre-job safety meeting. When running-in, apply thread lock to all connections of

the shoe track.

 After making up the shoe track, lower through rotary table and check that the

floats are holding. Fill up with mud and pick up to check float functionality.

Circulate for 10 min.

 Run liner in at controlled speed to minimize pressure surges (approx.10

joints/hr.). Check returns constantly.

 Fill up each liner joint whilst running in the hole. Fill up liner completely

every 10 joints run.

SAADAT ABAD OIL FIELD DEVELOPMENT

DRILLING PROGRAM – Well-006 WO1 LEG1

Page 59

 When the required numbers of liner joints have been made up, make up the

liner hanger &amp;amp; liner top packer, running tool as per liner hanger engineer’s

instructions.

 Circulate 120% of the liner capacity. (Record Liner weight)

 Run the liner with 5” drill pipe to the casing shoe. Circulate a minimum of

one string capacity before running into open hole, RIH in the open hole at 4-5

min/stand. Liner hanger engineer should be on rig floor while running liner

into open hole. (Check the loss while RIH if need decrease the speed of the

RIH). SLM &amp;amp; drift the drill pipe while RIH the liner.

 Work through any tight spots with maximum 50 klbs slack off / over pull and

wash down if necessary. Establish full circulation slowly prior to washing

down. Immediately call the WSS and Tool pusher to the rig floor, if there is

tight hole.

 The hanger will be set 120m above the 9 5/8” casing shoe. Try to avoid setting

hanger on casing coupling. Set the Hanger as per hanger engineer procedures.

Ensure that the running tool is free of the liner (work string 0.5m up and down

– record loss of weight as the hanger sets) before starting to cement.

 Circulate 120% of the string contents.

 Cement 7" liner as per cementing program.

 Displace the cement with the cementing pump to the liner wiper plug. Shear

out liner wiper plug (Record the volume pumped and shearing pressure).

Displace combined wiper plugs to latch down collar.

 Bump the plug with 500 psi over final displacement pressure (or 2000 psi

bumping press.) (Record and report final displacement pressure prior to bump

the plug). If there is no bump, do not displace more than 50% of the shoetrack volume. Displace with Cementing Pump.

 Hold bumping pressure for 5 minutes. If the plugs bumped.

 If plugs bumped, pressure up and test liner to 2000 psi for 15 minutes.

 Bleed off pressure slowly and check for back-flow.

 P/U setting tool for two meters and apply weight to set liner packer (If

available). Apply maximum 15,000 lbs (based on Hanger man instruction) to

make sure that the packer is set. CBU clean hole. Check the bottom’s up for

cement return.

1 COMPLETION PROGRAM

1.1 Completion running procedure

 Scraper Trip

Objective

The objective is to run the 9-5/8″ scraper BHA to scrape inside 9-5/8” casing @

Packer setting depth.

Risk Evaluation

• Junk falls in hole

• Debris on top of Liner hanger

• BHA stuck in the hole

• Fish scraper parts in well.

HSE Focus Points

 Well has to be stable before running the BHA.

 Monitor well for loss/gain over the trip tank.

 Good communication among all parties responsible for well control.

 Pre-job meeting will focus on well control, contingency procedures to be understood

by all involved parties.

 Volume and well control shall be focused upon throughout running/pulling. Fill out

kick sheet prior to run in hole.

 On a positive indication of a kick, unexpected pit gain or flow return rate increase,

well shall be shut in without performing flow check

 A kick stand shall be readily available at all times.

Technical

Note: 9-5/8” scraper shall be suitable for 47 ppf casing.

Well Status

• 11” wear bushing installed in wellhead.

Operation Sequence

1. P/U &amp;amp; M/U 8-1/2” Bit + 9-5/8” Scrapper + 6 ½” DC + 5” DP

2. RIH to packer depth @ 2031m.

3. Scrape packer depth interval 2000m to 2038m Several times while pumping.

5. POOH to surface while observe the well to make sure well is static.

 Completion Installation

Objectives

The objective is to install the completion components, 7” &amp;amp; 4 ½” production tubing, tubing

hanger and X-mas tree.

Risk Evaluation

 Fluid left in tubing is not properly inhibited.

 Losing control line clamps in hole

 Junk falls in the well before or during completion

 Well/completion fluid not clean before running completion string

 Over torque tubing connections

 Leak in DHSV control line when pressure testing

 Damage to DHSV control lines from manual slips

 Tubing head wear/damage if the rig is not centered on hole

 Taking kick/inflow during completion

 Damage to tubing hanger when running through riser/BOP

 Poor make up graphs due to poor supervision

HSE Focus Points

 Maintain good housekeeping on the drill floor at all times.

 The well shall be lined up to the trip tank. Keep the trip tank pump running.

 Perform pre job meetings with all involved personnel at critical stages of the

operation.

 Perform kick drill prior to commencement.

Completion Installation Operational Sequence

Note: Perform pre-job safety meeting with special instruction to completion crew

regarding correct dope application, make up torque and tubing handling (Under HSEQ

supervision).

Note: Flush tubing head spool as per Wellhead service Engineer instruction. Do perfect

wash and check the return form side outlet to make sure it's free of debris.

Note: Measure accurate distance from tubing landing shoulder to rotary table

Note: A single joint elevator same as tubing size will be used as backup to secure the

assemblies in the beginning when there is low weight hanging in the side door. This will

be installed directly on TOP of the compact spider frame.

Note: Rigging up of the assembly should take place with extra care while using the air

hoist and the Crane at the same time.

Note: all the completion equipment are already made up with 1 pup jt. above and 1 pup

jt. below, torque up and pressure tested, all valves of X-mas tree already tested in

workshop.

Note: Lift all emergency well control subs to rig floor and make up to cock valve.

 Open all the tubing protectors in the rack, wash and clean all the threads.

 Rig up completion running tools.

 3. M/U and RIH all equipment’s step by step as per tally.

Note: F/up 100m on top of SSD plug with H-Vis polymer pill (100sec) and the rest

each 10 jt W/ mud. Test string up to 4500psi for each 100 joints.

to have torque-turn graph. Any connection with improper torque-turn graph shall be

rejected.

Note: Cross over 4 ½” pin * DP connection box attached with FOSV (TIW valve)

shall be made up and lay aside at rig floor ready to install on tubing in case of well

control issue to secure the well from inside string. Same configuration also shall be

made up and to be ready at rig floor for 7” pin * DP connection attached with FOSV.

 Connect 7” WR-SSSV Landing Nipple with flow couplings and pup jts up and down.

 Connect C/L to WR-SSSV Landing Nipple and test with 4,500 psi for 15 min. RIH with

3000 psi inside C/L. (put clamp-on C/L protector on every joint to hold C/L).

 M/U and RIH 7” tubing till surface.

 P/U and M/U tubing hanger, release pressure inside C/L and connect C/L to tubing

hanger and test with 4,500 psi for 15 mins.

 P/up 7” Landing jt. and connect to Hanger. Touch with hanger inside the bowl of TBG

HD Spool, pull &amp;amp; space out, Mark String.

 Pull out string to half of traveling joint stroke.

 R/U Golp. Flange and R/U slick line

 Remove plug and prong from SSD

 Install plug and prong in top No-Go

 R/D slick line equipment

 Install swage on landing joint

 Perform 500psi pressure for 5min and increase pressure gradually step by step 500psi to

set packer.

 Pressure test inside tubing to 4500psi and inside annulus to 2500psi.

 Release pressure and perform weight on string to shear pins of landing joint, Install

hanger in THS.

 Tighten tie down screw

 Pressure test inside tubing w/4500psi and annulus w/2500 psi.

 Back off landing joint

1 INTRODUCTION

1.1 History

The SAADAT ABAD oil-field is located in 90 Km. south west of Shiraz city and 11 Km. west of Sarvestan city. This oil field was discovered by drilling the first well at 1973 and existence of hydrocarbon is proved in Sarvak Formations. This project including drilling and completion of 2 new vertical wells and re-entry one existing well.

1.2 Introduction

This program covers the drilling of Production / Directional Well in SAADAT ABAD oil field, Iran. The well is intended to produce oil from Sarvak Reservoir. The well will be sidetracked from depth of 2138 m and directional drilling 8 ½” hole section to 2842m and cased with 7” liner. Continue directional drilling 6 1/8” hole section to 3390m(TD), set cement plug and run 5” liner at 3034m (15m in sarvak formation), drill out cement. The well will be completed with Run completion string.

4 WELL OBJECTIVES

• According to client’s preliminary plan, the well SAA-006 WO1 LEG2 is intended to

sidetracked from depth of 2138 m and directional drilling 8 ½” hole section to 2842m

and cased with 7” liner. Continue directional drilling 6 1/8” hole section to 3390m(TD),

set Magneset plug and run 5” liner at 3034m (15m in sarvak formation), drill out

Magneset plug. The well will be completed with Run completion string and flow it for

produce the oil in sarvak reservoir

• CBL/VDL &amp;amp; CCL/GR logs will be run from 7" Liner shoe to 9 5/8" casing.

• CBL/VDL &amp;amp; CCL/GR logs will be run from 5" Liner shoe to Liner Lap.

• Full suite logs will be run from 6 1/8” hole section TD to 7” Liner shoe.

1 INTRODUCTION

The Saadat Abad oil field is located in the south of Iran in Fars province, about 60 kilometers south east of Shiraz. It has a saturated oil reservoir with a primary gascap contained in the Ilam and Sarvak Formation. The Saadat Abad field was discovered in 1973 (1352 Iranian Calendar) by well SAA-1 which encountered a large oil column in Bangestan reservoirs. A further appraisal well SAA-2 was drilled down dip (in northwest of north flank) in 1975 (1354 Iranian Calendar).

The Saadat Abad field consists of an asymmetrical anticline with trending NE-SW with a dip around 22° on the north flank and around 14° on south flank. Based on the Static pressure of Zagros Company, Bangestan Reservoir is expected 4020psi in -1280mss in year- 97. Reservoir temperature is expected to be 179 Fahrenheit in -1280mss based on the resources and statistic notebook report.

GOC and OWC based on Reservoir Engineering Proposal respectively, -1205, -1495mss, seven drilled wells in this field until now.

The gas oil contact could not be observed in SAA-1 although the G.O.C was reported to be at -1205mss and O.W.C was recorded at -1495mss (ICOFC proposal and SAA-3 data) and the hydrocarbon thickness is approximately 411m in Saadat Abad field. In Saadat Abad Oil field, sour oil is observed and it contains 0.63% H2S and 1.83% CO2 approximately.

SAA#1 was drilled to total depth of 2821m in Sarvak fm., SAA-2 was drilled as an exploration well about 3.8 Km east of SAA-1 well. SAA-2 was spudded on 9March 1975 and reached a TD of 3480.90m in November 1975. The main objective was to test the Ilam and Sarvak formation. The Sachun and Dariyan formation were considered secondary objectives.

According to the last U.G.C map 1397, Saadat Abad-E014S is situated in the southeast flank of Saadat Abad anticline, about 2914m in the east of well#3 and about 2784m in the Southwest of well#4. This well in Plan will be drilled directionally from 2160m as a K.O.P. to Total Depth of 3464.28m (+68.3m V.Thickness) inside of Sarvak Formation.

CBL/VDL&amp;amp; CCL/GR log Formation will be run from 7" liner shoe. CDR/Full suite will be run in open hole 6 1/8".

This well will be completed as Sarvak oil producer through 6 1/8" open hole.

2 GENERAL FORMATION LITHOLOGY DESCRIPTION (In Deviation Hole)

A normal stratigraphical sequence in Saadat Abad –006 (E014S) is expected from K.O.P. (Through Gurpi Fm.) to total depth. In Sarvak Formation is as follows:

- Gurpi Fm. (From K.O.P.2138 m to 2872.2 m) drilled thickness + 734.2 m:

This formation consists of a thick sequence of dark gray to greenish gray calcareous silty shale and greenish grey, soft and sticky marl, with subordinate layers of grey to dark grayargillaceous and marly limestone.

Thickness of Gurpi formation is variable in Saadat Abad structure.

- Ilam Fm. 2872.2– 3019.72.) drilled thickness 147.52 m:

The top of Ilam formation is marked by a change in lithology from marl in to a dark brown, brown to light brown limestone. This formation consists of light gray to grayish brown crystalline, fossilliferous and porous limestone and as well as in lower part consists of brown dark brown argillaceous limestone and in some part marly limestone.

- Sarvak Fm. (3019.72m to TD at 3389.42 m) drilled thickness +369.7m.:

It consists of a sequence of white-off white chalky and brownish gray well bedded crystalline limestone, partly argillaceous and slightly chalky. The 1/3 basal of Sarvak formation contains of a series of dark brown dense argillaceous, sparry limestone, which are partly bituminous and partly glauconitic. Sarvak formation divided into 8 zones in Saadat Abad field.

Note:

In Saadat Abad Oil field, sour oil is observed and it contains 0.63% H2S and 1.83% CO2.

Bangestan Reservoir is expected 4020psi in -1280mss in year-97.

Reservoir temperature is expected to be 179Fahrenheit at -1280mss. in year-96.

Losses are probable in Ilam &amp;amp; Sarvak Fms.

Gas &amp;amp; Oil in Ilam &amp;amp; Sarvak Fms can be present.

Structural uncertainties for top Formations estimated +/-50m.

Note: The zonation will be finalized after running the logs.

5 Drilling Hazard

 Drilling through Ilam and Sarvak Formations in this field has been accompanied with

moderate losses and from Gurpi Formation to T.D. losses is expected.

 Drilling in Shale parts of Gurpi Formation in this field has been accompanied with tight holes

and stuck pipes; special care is recommended for Mud type and drilling in this formation.

 While drilling in Limestone lithology water flow is predicted, so special care is

recommended while drilling this section.

 Losses are probable in Ilam &amp;amp; Sarvak Fms.

 In drilling Ilam and Sarvak Fms; it possible to have signs of hydrocarbon, Mud cut and flow.

Especial care is recommended while drilling these Fms.

 In Saadat Abad Oil field, sour oil is observed and it contains 0.63% H2S and 1.83% CO2.

Due to the existence of H2S in this field, in this regards, safety regulations should be highly

considered.

 Structural uncertainties for top Fm. estimated +/- 50m.

 Mud Losses and Gas flow maybe occurred in Ilam and Sarvak Fm.

*So special care is recommended while drilling 8 ½” Hole section section.

1.2 Saadat Abad-1:

Saadat Abad well No.-1 was drilled to explore the Ilam-Sarvak units which are also the reservoir rocks in Sarvestan structure. The Tarbur Formation was also considered as the auxiliary objective.

During drilling of the well, some indication of gas and oil were observed in Sachun Formation, but performed tests in Sachun and Tarbur Formations did not yield commercial oil or gas.

Production tests, intervals 2744.30-2748.50 and 2695.70-2718.70m, of Sarvak Formation revealed the maximum recovery, after acidization, of 160bbls/hr of crude oil with 3/4" choke.

Based on the interpretation of the seismic records and obtained data of drilled wells (SAA-1 and SAA-2) the areal and vertical closures of Saadat Abad structure, on top of Ilam Formation, are around 93Km2 and 770m respectively. The proved gas-oil column is 385m with the area of closure of 37Km2. The well is temporarily abandoned.

Shows:

• No indications of gas or oil were observed in the formations younger than the Sachun

Formation.

• Oil-stained samples and gas indications along with asphaltic impregnations were

recorded in the Ilam Formation.

• Gas &amp;amp; Oil, with asphaltic impregnations were confirmed in the Sarvak

2 PRE SPUD

Company representative prepared a pre-spud checklist and distributed it in contractor rigs. The checklist will be performed based on the aforementioned checklist. In addition to the checklist, following matters should be checked:

 Check &amp;amp; observe the alignment of the rig. This check will be performed in four stages;

rig levelling, derrick verticality, derrick alignment with rotary table, rotary table

alignment with conductor pipe. To do this pick up 3 joints of 9 3/4” DC and check the

verticality of the derrick.

 Mechanical facilities for mud treatment such as:

Desander, Desilter, mud cleaner, proper size of shaker–screens, hoppers, mud guns &amp;amp; mixers, should be all available on rig and functioning properly.

 All mud tanks, mud transfer lines &amp;amp; connection should be checked by filling them

with water &amp;amp; cross wellhead circulation.

 Mud engineer laboratory should be equipped with a complete set of testing

equipment. The calibration should be done under supervision of well site drilling

supervisor before starting the operation.

 Weight indicator, rotary speed gauge, any smart drilling instrumentation, Stroke

meter, pressure gauges on manifold and in the drilling console, loss / gain gauge and

any other gauges should be checked and calibrated.

 Stand pipe manifold valves &amp;amp; connection must be checked &amp;amp; pressure tested.

 All motors should be checked under load prior to start drilling.

 Check &amp;amp; control mud stock &amp;amp; cement stock every day &amp;amp; if there is any necessity to

request mud material, cement or any drilling tool, it should be prepared &amp;amp; requested

at proper time.

4 Well Securing

4.1 Sequence of Operations

• Inspect and service well head and annulus valves by wellhead crew

• Install kill and choke lines, Pressure test same

• Read and record the pressure inside 9 5/8" casing and tubing, Check the pressures

of all annulus (Bleed off the pressure to zero, if any and check for re build same),

Test all P-seals, Monitor the well at least 5 hours.

• R/U wire line and test, Retrieve the 3SV pump in C.L to sure it's free. Install

Dummy, Test control line.

• Bull head the well w/67 pcf Mud, Observed W/H &amp;amp; tubing annulus pressure, make

sure No pressure in annulus.

• R/U Wire line, install plug &amp;amp; prong in NO GO below Packer &amp;amp; test same. Recheck

pressure in annulus.

• Install two way check valve in TBG Hanger, test same, N/D X-Mass Tree. While

circulation cross wellhead

• N/U 13 5/8"- 5 k BOP stack, choke manifold, bell nipple and related lines, test it as

per policy. Remove two way check valve from hanger.

• Make about 110 stands of 5", 55 stand of 3 1/2" DP, 12 stand of 3 1/2" HWDP, 12

stand 5" HWDP meanwhile prepare ±80 pcf WBM.

• R/U wire line and Recover Prong and plug through No Go nipple, N/D wire line

equipment.

• P/U landing joint, screw in tubing hanger, loose tie down screw, Test glands to

1000psi, pick up string till travel joint opened, make 2000lb overpull, Release

completion string from anchor seal by 20 right turn, circulate out completion fluid

and balance MW. POOH &amp;amp; L/D completion string w/plug in SSD.

• RIH w/ 8 1/2" Mill and BHA to top of Liner lap, POOH to surface.

• RIH 3 1/2" open end pipes and set 200m cement plug on top of 7" packer, wait on

cement to get hard, tag cement. POOH to surface.

• RIH 8 1/2" Bit to top of cement, drill out cement to 2180m, CBU, Pressure test

casing to 2000psi and make sure no pressure drop, CBU 80 pcf mud, POOH to

surface.

1 8.5" HOLE SECTION

1.1 8-1/2” Hole Section Characteristics

This section will be drilled to 2842 m MD. (According to geologies department)

8 1/2" Hole SectionDrilling Interval 2138 to 2842 m MDInterval Length (m) 704

In case of any losses, the only remedy considered is to use LCM in Viscose pill

1.2 Drilling Fluid Properties

Inhibitive Salt water KCL/Polymer mud is proposed to drill this section which will provide inhibition against anhydrates and problematic shale inter-beds through the hole section. Fluid loss should be controlled through the section; it could start from 6 ranges then firmly controlled down to below 3 prior to drilling shales beds.

Viscosity is maintained using purified Starch, high YP and low end rheologies should be kept in range.

Monitor hole cleaning and sweep the hole with high viscosity pills as needed.

Drill to the well total depth, circulate hole clean and spot a viscous pill on bottom before tripping out to run casing.

1.3 Drilling Fluid Mixing

Drilling water should be treated for hardness before additions of purified polymers.

PAC LV will assist to control fluid loss, XC-Polymer with Starch &amp;amp; HPHT-Starch will require the Viscosity and mud rheology

KCl / NaCl and Calcium Carbonate will maintain required MW. On top of weight resulted from Brine/Calcium Carbonate, Mud Weight to be provided by addition of weighting agent.

In event of experiencing salt water flows, maintain a contingency supply of Caustic and Soda ash to treat magnesium and calcium ions in solution.

2.1 6-1/8” Hole Section Characteristics

This section will be drilled to 3390 m MD in Sarvak formation.

6 1/8" Hole SectionDrilling Interval 2842 to 3390 m MDInterval Length (m) 548

In case of any losses, the only remedy considered is to use LCM in Viscose pill

2.2 Drilling Fluid Properties

Inhibitive Salt water KCL/Polymer mud is proposed to drill this section which will provide inhibition against anhydrates and problematic shale inter-beds through the hole section. Fluid loss should be controlled through the section; it could start from 6 ranges then firmly controlled down to below 3 prior to drilling shales beds.

Viscosity is maintained using purified Starch, high YP and low end rheologies should be kept in range.

Monitor hole cleaning and sweep the hole with high viscosity pills as needed.

Perform periodic wiper trips to monitor hole integrity.

Drill to the well total depth, circulate hole clean and spot a viscous pill on bottom before tripping out to run casing.

2.3 Drilling Fluid Mixing

Drilling water should be treated for hardness before additions of purified polymers.

PAC LV will assist to control fluid loss, XC-Polymer with Starch &amp;amp; HPHT-Starch will require the Viscosity and mud rheology

KCl / NaCl and Calcium Carbonate will maintain required MW. On top of weight resulted from Brine/Calcium Carbonate, Mud Weight to be provided by addition of weighting agent.

In event of experiencing salt water flows, maintain a contingency supply of Caustic and Soda ash to treat magnesium and calcium ions in solution.

2.4 Sequence of Operations

• WSS is to supervise the loading of liner wiper plug in liner running tool, and loading

of drill pipe wiper dart in cementing head.

• The liner hanger engineer is to be on the rig floor at all times that the liner is being

run in open hole.

• Hold pre-job safety meeting. When running-in, apply thread lock to all connections of

the shoe track.

 After making up the shoe track, lower through rotary table and check that the

floats are holding. Fill up with mud and pick up to check float functionality.

Circulate for 10 min.

 Run liner in at controlled speed to minimize pressure surges (approx.10

joints/hr.). Check returns constantly.

 Fill up each liner joint whilst running in the hole. Fill up liner completely

every 10 joints run.

Page 56

 When the required numbers of liner joints have been made up, make up the

liner hanger &amp;amp; liner top packer, running tool as per liner hanger engineer’s

instructions.

 Circulate 120% of the liner capacity. (Record Liner weight)

 Run the liner with 5” drill pipe to the casing shoe. Circulate a minimum of

one string capacity before running into open hole, RIH in the open hole at 4-5

min/stand. Liner hanger engineer should be on rig floor while running liner

into open hole. (Check the loss while RIH if need decrease the speed of the

RIH). SLM &amp;amp; drift the drill pipe while RIH the liner.

 Work through any tight spots with maximum 50 klbs slack off / over pull and

wash down if necessary. Establish full circulation slowly prior to washing

down. Immediately call the WSS and Tool pusher to the rig floor, if there is

tight hole.

 The hanger will be set 120m above the 9 5/8” casing shoe. Try to avoid setting

hanger on casing coupling. Set the Hanger as per hanger engineer procedures.

Ensure that the running tool is free of the liner (work string 0.5m up and down

– record loss of weight as the hanger sets) before starting to cement.

 Circulate 120% of the string contents.

 Cement 7" liner as per cementing program.

 Displace the cement with the cementing pump to the liner wiper plug. Shear

out liner wiper plug (Record the volume pumped and shearing pressure).

Displace combined wiper plugs to latch down collar.

 Bump the plug with 500 psi over final displacement pressure (or 2000 psi

bumping press.) (Record and report final displacement pressure prior to bump

the plug). If there is no bump, do not displace more than 50% of the shoetrack volume. Displace with Cementing Pump.

 Hold bumping pressure for 5 minutes. If the plugs bumped.

 If plugs bumped, pressure up and test liner to 2000 psi for 15 minutes.

 Bleed off pressure slowly and check for back-flow.

 P/U setting tool for two meters and apply weight to set liner packer (If

available). Apply maximum 15,000 lbs (based on Hanger man instruction) to

make sure that the packer is set. CBU clean hole. Check the bottom’s up for

cement return.

Note: All calculation of Cement program and hanger setting procedure and liner tally shall be submitted in due time.
