1 COMPLETION PROGRAM

1.1 Completion running procedure

• Scraper Trip

Objective

The objective is to run the 9-5/8″ scraper BHA to scrape inside 9-5/8” casing @ 2009m Packer setting depth.

Risk Evaluation

• Junk falls in hole

• Debris on top of Liner hanger

• BHA stuck in the hole

• Fish scraper parts in well.

HSE Focus Points

 Well has to be stable before running the BHA.

 Monitor well for loss/gain over the trip tank.

 Good communication among all parties responsible for well control.

 Pre-job meeting will focus on well control, contingency procedures to be understood

by all involved parties.

 Volume and well control shall be focused upon throughout running/pulling. Fill out

kick sheet prior to run in hole.

 On a positive indication of a kick, unexpected pit gain or flow return rate increase,

well shall be shut in without performing flow check

 A kick stand shall be readily available at all times.

Technical

Note: 9-5/8” scraper shall be suitable for 47 ppf casing.

Well Status

• 11” wear bushing installed in wellhead.

Company: Project:

SAADAT ABAD OIL FIELD DEVELOPMENT

Subcontractor:

DRILLING PROGRAM – Well-006 WO1 LEG2

03/09/2020: تاریخSA 06 2GP F DRG DR WO PLDR 0001 D3

Page 66

Operation Sequence

1. P/U &amp;amp; M/U 8-1/2” Bit + 9-5/8” Scrapper + 6 ½” DC + 5” DP

2. RIH to packer depth @ 2009m.

3. Scrape packer depth interval 1985m to 2015m Several times while pumping.

5. POOH to surface while observe the well to make sure well is static.

• Completion Installation

Objectives

The objective is to install the completion components, 7” &amp;amp; 4 ½” production tubing, tubing hanger and X-mas tree.

Risk Evaluation

 Fluid left in tubing is not properly inhibited.

 Losing control line clamps in hole

 Junk falls in the well before or during completion

 Well/completion fluid not clean before running completion string

 Over torque tubing connections

 Leak in DHSV control line when pressure testing

 Damage to DHSV control lines from manual slips

 Tubing head wear/damage if the rig is not centered on hole

 Taking kick/inflow during completion

 Damage to tubing hanger when running through riser/BOP

 Poor make up graphs due to poor supervision

HSE Focus Points

 Maintain good housekeeping on the drill floor at all times.

 The well shall be lined up to the trip tank. Keep the trip tank pump running.

 Perform pre job meetings with all involved personnel at critical stages of the

operation.

 Perform kick drill prior to commencement.

Note: Measure accurate distance from tubing landing shoulder to rotary table

Note: A single joint elevator same as tubing size will be used as backup to secure the assemblies in the beginning when there is low weight hanging in the side door. This will be installed directly on TOP of the compact spider frame.

Note: Rigging up of the assembly should take place with extra care while using the air hoist and the Crane at the same time.

Note: all the completion equipment are already made up with 1 pup jt. above and 1 pup jt. below, torque up and pressure tested, all valves of X-mas tree already tested in workshop.

Note: Lift all emergency well control subs to rig floor and make up to cock valve.

• Open all the tubing protectors in the rack, wash and clean all the threads.

• Rig up completion running tools.

• 3. M/U and RIH all equipment’s step by step as per tally.

3.1 General Formation Lithology Descriptions

1) In a typical geological section, one massive oolitic to pellety limestone with minor contemporaneous

brecciation in the basal part developed in Fahliyan Formation (James and Wynd, 1965). The Fahliyan

Formation has been drilled in Well AZN-1, AZN-2, AZN-4, AZN-5 and AZN-6 and the Fahliyan

Formation in Well AZN-1, AZN-2 and AZN-5 are mainly consisted of poorly fossiliferous, generally

micritic limestone, often argillaceous, and marls with no porosity butextensive and thick porous

micritic and chalky limestones were developed in Well AZN-4 and AZN-6.

2) In the Gadvan Formation, a variety of lithological rock types such as carbonates, rich organic shales

and sandstones were deposited in various environments. The lower part of the Gadvan Formation is

composed of low-energy, but not very deep, micritic, often argillaceous limestone with echinoids and

algal fragments. Two sandstone units were defined in the Gadvan Formation， lateral changes and

especially discontinuity of the sandstone layers which are consist of fine clastics (shales and

siltstones) may be expected.

3) The thicknees of Khalij Member is about 14m in the Azadegan Field, and main lightology is

limestone, containing algal and echinoid debris. Although fair porosity values were observed, the

limestone was very tight and has a very low permeability.The Dariyan Formation in the Azadegan

Field developed grey to brown thick-bedded limestone which is rich in Orbitorina.

4) In the Azadegan Field, the upper part of the Kazhdumi Formation is made up of dark-grey to

dark-brown marls, the middle part developed light-grey, micritic to chalky limestone, the low part, is

around40-60m in thichnessclean channel sands interbeded argillaceous sands with streaks of shale.

5) The Sarvak Formation developed a carbonate unit which was gradually overlying the Kazhdumi

Formation, and it was abruptly terminated by an erosion phase and covered by various late

Cretaceous sediments. A Typical geological section of the Sarvak Formation in Azadegan reveals

that dark grey fine grained nodulary argillaceous limestone interbedded with thin marls in the bottom,

and graded upward into a white-to-buff massive chalky limestone with siliceous nodules;it was

developed a very massive tan-to-brown limestone containing abundant rudist debris in the middle

part; the upper part is made up of rubbly limestone with red staining and leached zones of breccia

and the top of Sarvak Formation is very ferruginous.

6) The Laffan Formation developed a thin greenish-grey pyritic shale layer, capping the Sarvak

Formation. It was encountered in the Azadegan wells and only ostracods were found. It is a cap rock

for the upper part of the Sarvak reservoir.

SOUTH AZADEGAN PROJECT

S378H on Pad 50 Drilling Program

Version:3 rd

Drilling Program Page 5

7) In the Azadegan Field, the Ilam Formation consists of grey micritic limestone, often argillaceous,

rarely pyritic, limestones. Microfauna, mostly pelagic, including rotalids and oligostegina

assemblage, a few algae, bryozoa, and rudist fragments exist.

8) The Gurpi Formation in the Azadegan Field consists of grey to dark-brownish, slightly argillaceous

micritic limestone with Maestrichtian to Campanian aged fauna. At Well AZN-1, about 50 meters of

chalky limestones were encountered in the middle of the Gurpi formation, which contains abundant

fragments of rudists, bryozoa, corals, and Orbitoides.

9) Pabdeh Formation is divided into two parts in the Azadegan field. The upper part is made of grey to

dark-brown argillaceous limestones and marls. Planktonic fauna dates that this part was deposited in

Oligocene. The lower part is composed of dark-brown, slightly argillaceous limestone. Pelagic fauna,

mostly Globigerina and Globorotalia, indicates that this part was formed during late Paleocene to late

Eocene in age. It seems that no early Paleocene Formation exists in the Azadegan area.

10) The Asmari Formation in Azadegan Field developed a massive sandstone interval, with a few thin

argillaceous layers in the upper sections. Sands are clear, fine to medium-sorted, and poorly

consolidated. On the other hand, the lower sections consist of intercalation of sandy, chalky, slightly

dolomitic high-energy limestone with sands layers.

11) The Gachsaran Formation with a thickness ranges from 400 m to 600 m, thicken towards the north.

Deposition of the Gachsaran Formation is cyclic. The cycle began with a deposition of shallow-water

marine carbonates, and then it was overlain by a thick evaporitic phase. The evaporites were capped

by red to variegated marl, which represented the end of cycle.

12) The AghaJari Formation consists of a repetition of brown to grey calcareous sandstones, chert debris

and gypsum-veined red marl. A fauna of brackish to freshwater was observed, together with more

marine fauna.

3.2 Key Reservoir Descriptions

There are three key reservoirs that we need to focus on. Gross thickness of Sarvak-3 ranges from 16m to 30m and averaged at 21.4m.The average thickness of net-pay zone in Sarvak-3 is 15.8m and the Net/Gross ratio 1s 79% .It is mainly composed of light brown or dark brown bituminous dolomitic limestone, which is dominated by bioturbated and bioclastic packstones and grainstone. It is a main oil-bearing zone with a better petrophysical property with respect to others of Sarvak Formation in the south azadegan. The mean porosity is 16.8% and the mean permeability is 20.7 md and So is 89.1%. The forecasted top depth is -2752m in S378.

4. Formation or Pore Pressure and Temperature

4.1 Formation or Pore Pressure Prediction

According to the statistic data of drilled wells in Azadegan oil field, formation pressure forecast is done mainly based on the off-set wells testing in this field, especially based on the DST testing results and RFT data in Sarvak formations.

It is known that there exist two sets of different formation pressure system from north to south blocks as the boundary by AZN-10 in this oil field according to drilling fluid density, logging data and formation pressure analysis results from existing wells. In North of AZN-10(Figure3a), there are two abnormal

SOUTH AZADEGAN PROJECT

S378H on Pad 50 Drilling Program

Version:3 rd

Drilling Program Page 6

pressure formations, one in Gachsaran (1330~1950m) with the pore pressure coefficient 1.6~2.0, and the other in Fahliyan reservoir formation with the pore pressure coefficient around 1.6~1.3 (F2:1.6, F4:1.3). In South of AZN 10(Figure 3b), the formation pore pressure of Gachsaran tends to become normal pressure system, but the formation pore pressure of Fahliyan has also a pore pressure coefficient around 1.6~1.3 (F2:1.6, F4:1.3).

All the other reservoirs such as Gadvan, Kazhdumi and Sarvak formations exists in normal pressure systems, with pore pressure coefficient between 1.1 and 1.20. Caving pressure coefficient is lower than that of pore pressure in some formations, and the fracture pressure coefficient is between 1.8 and 2.2. 6. Drilling History and Lessons learnt

6.1 Drilling History

The Azadegan Oil field was discovered when Well AZN-1 was drilled in 1999 whose total depth is 4643m at the Cretaceous formation.

Before CNPCI (Iran), 40 wells (7 exploration wells, 2 appraisal well and 31 producing wells) have been drilled in the Azadegan Field, among which 23 wells are located in the South Azadegan Contract Area, 5 wells (AZNS-026, AZNS-027, AZNS-028, AZNS-029 &amp;amp; AZNS-030) has been drilled by CNPCI (Iran) and 3 well (AZNS-031, AZNS-032 and AZNS-033) are currently being drilled.

Carbonate reservoir of Sarvak in the Cretaceous formation is broadly developed in Azadegan Field and was penetrated in 6 exploration wells (AZN-1, AZN-2, AZN-3, AZN-4, AZN-5 and AZN-6). Classic oil bearing zones of Kazhdumi Formation developed in main anticline of Azedegan Field from north to center of South Azadegan. Classic oil bearing zones of Gadvan Formation developed only in crest area and south parts of South Azadegan Filed, which was discovered by AZN-1 in crest and AZN-4 in south parts.

AZN-17H (Offset well)

26” Hole Section:

Rig Fath-86 spudded on well AZNS-17@ 18:00 O’Clock, date: 2009.02.25 (1387/12/07).

6.2 Lesson learning

Well AZNS-17H:

The 17 ½” hole section had been drilled to 1140m with 70-82 PCF W.B.M, the formation drilled is Aghajari-Gachsaran, tight hole (1140-50m) was encounter when during the condition trip, wash and ream several times this interval. Totally operation is smoothly, a proper mud weight in this section is important for the well’s operations.

The 12 ¼”hole is drilled to 1479 m with 85-88 PCF W.B.M, the drilled formation is Gachsaran. Tight hole was encountered during the condition trip, wash and ream several times this interval and increase MW f/88 to 100 pcf. Totally operation is smoothly, a proper mud weight in this section is important for the well’s operations.

While drilled 17 ½” and 12 ¼” hole section in Aghajari and Gachsaran formation observed bit and stabilizer balled up.

The best approach is to use good fundamentals: an inhibitive mud, optimal hydraulics and a quality ROP enhancer.

Cure bit balling

• Work the bit by rotating fast off bottom and reciprocating the string to shake off the clay coating.

• Reduce ROP for a short time.

• Spot a walnut pill.

• Circulation.

• Fresh water.

• If bit balling is observed while drilling, a detergent is usually added to disperse the balled clays.

• The use of a small percentage of glycol also helps to reduce bit balling.

• Consider fresh water pill.

• Keep the API fluid loss as low as possible.

The 8 ½” hole is drilled to 1970m with 75 pcf salt water w/2-12 BPH losses. For the mud losses, a mud system with LCM is required.

The 6⅛” hole was drilled to 3595.5m MD with 76 PCF O.B.M, the formation drilled was Gachsaran-Asmari-Pabdeh-Ilam-Sarvak-Kazhdumi, the main problem is stuck pipe @ 3595.5m , MD in Kazhdumi Fm. work on stuck with over pull, pipe got free and continue drilled to TD with 73 PCF O.B.M so a proper mud weight in this section is important for the well’s operations.

4. Requirement of Drilling and completion Fluid

4.1 Formation or Pore Pressure and Mud Weight

Primary Well Control relies on the hydrostatic pressure of drilling fluid to balance the formation pore pressure. In order to counteract any minor pressure reductions on bottom due to swabbing

SOUTH AZADEGAN PROJECT

S378H on Pad 50 Drilling Program

Version: 3 rd

Drilling Program Page 20

effect when tripping, it is customary to maintain a hydrostatic column with a pressure slightly exceeding the pore pressure of the exposed formation. This overbalance, safety margin, or trip margin, Ptm, varies depending on circumstances but it is generally of the order of 200 psi for conventional operations. The required density Pf to control a formation at a depth, D, with a pressure, Po, is given by: Pf = (Po+Ptm), or Df = (Po+Ptm)/D

To gas cut or contaminated mud, Df = Do + (0.07-0.15) sg,

To oil and/or salt water contaminated mud, Df = Do + (0.05-0.10) sg;

4.2 Requirement of Solid Control

1) Each kind of solid control equipment should be designed to process 100% to 150% of the maximum

anticipated circulating volume of mud. Shale shaker, de-sander, de-silter and cleaner are required to

run all the time during drilling and centrifuge is recommended to run at least 80% of drilling time.

2) The sand content and MBT should be kept as low as possible by solid removal and dilution.

Batchwise dilution (replacement of 20-30% of the total drilling fluid volume in one circulation) is

more effective than continuous dilution.

3) When drilling 12-1/4″ hole section the centrifuges should be run in barite recovery mode to minimize

waste volumes generated. Two centrifuges are recommended for processing salt-saturate mud to

maintain mud weight.

4.3 Guideline for Mud Program

1) This is a preliminary program. The contractor should provide Drilling Fluid Program based on this

basic proposal.

2) The lowest possible PV is essential for: low frictional losses &amp;amp; optimal hole cleaning.

3) The Yield Point (YP) is calculated by subtracting the PV from the Fan reading at 300 rpm, giving a

result in lbs/100ft2. YP = 2xR300 - R600. An optimal YP is essential for: carry capacity of drilling

fluid (a rule of thumb is that YP = 0.75 x hole size in inches); stability of drilling fluid towards

settling of solids (a rule of thumb is that YP = 9 x specific gravity) &amp;amp; the hole capacity of the drilling

fluid.

4) Optimally the 10’ gel value is 1.5 x the 10” gel value.

5) Always maintain the readings of 6 rpm between 1.2 and 1.5 times of hole size in inches.

6) Drill from Asmari to Sarvak, Formation, KCl polymer mud will be mixed for this section. Losses are

common (even with the light mud weights used) in the Asmari, Sarvak formations. Sized CaCO3

materials are used as lost circulation material. Mud weight shall be kept as low as possible. High pH

shall be maintained to control any small amounts of H2S and CO2 gas. In the Sarvak Wells, lubricant

may be required as the hole dictates. KCl Polymer mud will be transferred to CaCO3 based Drill-In

fluid to drill the Sarvak reservoir. Mud weight shall be kept as low as possible. CaCO3 is the optimal

weighting material and barite is back up as required.

4.4 Kill Fluid and Chemical Storage

1) The kill fluid should be prepared prior to commence of each hole section. The density of kill fluid is

usually heavier than the formation coefficient by 0.4sg and the volume of kill fluid is following the

regulation of South Azadegan Oil Field:

For formation pore pressure coefficient more than 1.20 and pay zone without H2S, the volume of kill mud is 0.5 times of full hole volume;

For formation pore pressure coefficient more than 1.20 and pay zone with H2S, the volume of kill mud is 1.5 times of full hole volume;

2) The following emergency or contingency materials should be kept on the rig site at all times to

supplement the proposed mud system. Kick, lost circulation, stuck pipe scenarios, lubrication and

general purpose operations may require the following products to be on storage or standby.

4.5 Requirement of Completion Fluid

1) As the base case, completion fluid for all production wells will be KCl and CaCl2 clear brine with

1.19-1.36 g/cm3 density according to the formation pressure (Sarvak, Kazhdumi, Fahliyan, Gadvan

and Asmari) and due to requirements of well control density of completion fluid should be 0.05-0.10

g/cm3 above formation coefficient.

2) The packer fluid is to be KCl brine with corrosion inhibitor, oxygen scavenger, bactericide, etc for

preserving tubular.

3) The performance requirements designed for the completion fluid system is as below:

Particle Plugging Test and Recovered permeability: ≥90%; or NTU: ≤30; Corrosion rate: ＜0.076 mm/a;

4) Cartridge filters must be used and diameter of solid particle: ≤2μm.

5) PH shall be kept in the range of 9.5-10

5.2 Preparation for Running Casing

1) Prior to running casing wiper trip should be conducted and any tight spots should be reamed to

ensure borehole in good condition. Especially, for 8-1/2″ hole section the wiper trip BHA with two

stabilizers is highly recommended please refer to 6.2 BHA.

2) Circulate to condition mud to ensure hole static, no loss and no gain.

3) Change BOP ram to casing size and test same to the pressure equal to the value of 70-80% casing

burst with fresh water.

4) Cross check the casing tally, casing accessories such as, floating equipment, centralizer, stop collar

and pin, drift rabbit, cement head, crossover for cement head, cement plugs, circulation swage, thread

dope, thread lock compound, etc.

5) Double check the casing running equipment and tools according to the detail list.

6) Pilot lab test for slurry and contamination test with different ratio of mud and slurry have been done

and the measures are considered in cement program as per the result of pilot test.

7) Ensure cement and additives available on site and keep silo, cement unit, water tank, surface high

pressure lines and manifold in good condition.

8) The cement program should be submitted to review and approve by drilling superintendent 24 hrs

before cementing job.

5.3 Guideline for Cement Program

1) Overall design philosophy is to achieve simplicity as far as possible while keeping the high operation

quality for all wells.

2) As bottom of hole static temperatures exceed 230℉ , or 110℃, 35% of silica flour will be used in

cementing composition to maintain low permeability and help prevent loss of compressive strength

of cement sheath.

3) Cement slurry of high density is required for ultra-high pressure wells. Heavyweight materials such

as hematite should be prepared for increasing cement slurry density.

4) Cement additives for improving elastic properties of cement rock could be used for cementing the

hole with slim annulus clearance.

5) Rotating Liner hanger with integral top packer and rotating spiral centralizers will be used.

6) The other guideline is listed in the table as follows. And refer to the detail cement program,

Attachment-2. This should be prepared by Contractor, and return to Company at least 2 weeks

before spud in.

7) After cementing job, it is required to close BOP and apply back pressure on annulus to wait on tail

slurry thickening. The back pressure is depending on the density of tail slurry and at annulus in

VERTICAL HEIGHT. The formula is: Back Pressure = (Dts-1.07sg)*Htvd*(0.0098*145 ) (psi);

e.g., after cement 9-5/8″ casing, Back Pressure = (1.94-1.07sg)*550m*(0.0098*145) = 680 (psi).

7. Directional Drilling

7.1 Anti-collision measures

Anti-collision should be considered if more than one wells on the same pad. The distance between every two cellars is only 15m. The risk of collision between two slots likely occurs in vertical section. Anti-collision issue of long vertical section is a big challenge and anti-collision measures are as following:

1) From surface to kick off point: In upper formation, adopt pendulum BHA and low WOB and high

RPM to guarantee drilling upper hole vertically.

2) Single-shot and Multi-shot will be used to monitor and survey the well trajectory. Take survey of

single-shot every 400-500 m, if the deviation is nearly or larger than required, then survey should be

taken more frequently and well straightening measure should be performed. The multi-shot survey

should be taken during the last trip and the survey interval of multi-shot is not more than 30m.

3) After survey, the drilled well path should be compared to existing and other proposed wells. The

distances between other wells and the drilled well are calculated at frequent depth intervals in the

critical section. These calculations can be performed using the application COMPASS, WELLPLAN

or NAVIGATOR. Survey uncertainty must also be computed both for the drilled well and the critical

existing wells.

4) Steering BHA (Motor and MWD) should be back-up. Run Steering BHA (Motor and MWD)

whenever potential collision risk increased.

5) Existing well survey data

The well AZN-17 and S377 are the nearest offset well, which is 54m far away from this well, anti-collision scan is required with the survey data I in the detailed directional drilling program.

Both the burning line and bleed off line shall be installed with flanged type connections, no welding is allowed.

9.5 Pressure Test

1) Accumulator, BOP, Wellhead and Choke/Kill Manifold

 The BOP, wellhead, choke manifold, and related equipment are normally to be tested on 14 days

basis. This period can be extended depending on the well operations and the specifications in the

Drilling Program and the applicable Regulations.

 The accumulator is to be tested prior to the first test of the BOP, or any time after repairs are

made to the accumulator unit. The accumulator bottles pre-charge pressure shall be checked

before drilling out the casing shoe or every 4 weeks whichever is earlier.

 All the pressure tests shall be performed with both low pressure test, usually 300 psi and high

pressure test, usually to the rated value (for annular BOP is 70% of WP) or as per Drilling

Program. All high pressure tests should be maintained for 10-30 minutes, and low pressure test 5

minutes, unless the Drilling Program dictates otherwise.

2) Casing and Liner

In the below table, casing or liner integrity test pressure, surface SIP, is given when test medium is fresh water. As usual, green test casing integrity after bump plug is recommended in the cement procedure. If rigs use the displacement mud (density &amp;gt;1.0sg) to test casing, the pressure applied on surface cement head should be considered the mud hydrostatic pressure at casing collar! And the surface SIP is given as the following formula:

Surface shut-in Pressure = 80% Casing Burst – B (psi)

B=Drilling fluid hydrostatic pressure - fresh water hydrostatic pressure;

Notes: the assumption in the formula above is the external fluid of the casing is fresh water(density:1.01sg), in order to simply the calculation the test fluid inside casing is also assumed as fresh water(density:1.01sg), the actual test pressure at well site need to be recalculated and are subject to the real mud weight in hole.

3) Wellhead

 For port seal: Install a test pump to the port and inject test fluid and test pressure to which is less

than 80% of casing collapse. Hold and monitor the test pressure for 15 minutes. In the event of a

leak, remove the Wellhead and replace the seals as required. Once a satisfactory test is achieved,

carefully bleed off all test pressure, drain the test fluid and reinstall the dust cap.

 For flange seal: Flange seal and body integrity test will be conducted at the same time when

pressure test for ram BOP together.

4) LOT/FIT

 LOT will be performed in the first well in every area and in all appraisal wells to determine the

equivalent mud weight at which the formation will take fluid. LOT will be conducted after drill

out 20″, 13-3/8″, 9-5/8″ and 7″ shoe track to the first weak zone, especially the sand zone, but no

more than 20 m in the new section hole.

 FIT will be performed in the other wells. The test is not designed to breakdown or fracture

formation, just to test the capacity of formation strength. Shut in pressure in wellhead during FIT

should be the value that the hydrostatic pressure at casing shoe equals to max mud weight that

will be used plus 0.2sg, or 12.5pcf. EMW (sg) = MWmax (sg) + 0.2 sg; or EMW (pcf) = MWmax

(pcf) + 12.5 pcf.

9.6 Well Control during Special operation

The well control while wireline logging and running casing is important and critical, best practices shall be followed, including but not limited to:

1) Change BOP ram to casing size and pressure test same to 1500 psi of surface SIP or the value of 80%

casing burst with fresh water.

2) The crossover for casing connection to drill pipe must available on floor. A good practice is to keep a

joint of DP with casing crossover at lower end and full opened safety valve at upper end to be ready

for picking up on V-door.

3) Prior to wireline logging, install shooting nipple and pressure test same to again WL BOP to 1500

psi.

4) The cable cutter should be available on rig floor. If kick occurs, cut logging cable and to close blend

BOP is optional

5) The contractor shall perform relative pressure test, drills, safety checks etc as per detailed well

control procedure of CNPCI during the well operations.

10. Drilling Operation Procedure

10.1 Pre-spud Preparation

1) Certificate

 Conduct rig accept inspection to make sure that the rig is as per Drilling Contract, all rig

equipment is on location, properly rigged up and function-tested. Check availability and content

of hoisting equipment inspection &amp;amp; maintenance records according to API.

 Make sure that all HSE procedures and systems are in place according to the HSE specifications,

and that all personnel has been made aware of relevant HSE guidelines and procedures. Check

certification of rig crane and rig crane operator; Check validity of well control certificates for key

contractor personnel, e.g. Tool pusher, drillers, assistant drillers.

2) Safety Device

 Test draw-works crown block saver and record results on daily drilling report; test derrick man

escape device (Geronimo line) and record time required for test weight on daily drilling report;

test rig intercom system, especially for Driller-Derrick Man and Driller-Mud Logger

communication link.

 Check that all rig safety equipment, e.g. fire extinguishers, eye-wash stations etc., is installed at

the proper locations as per rig layout diagrams.

 Verify that substructure is level and foundation adequate to support drilling unit during whole

well period and that mast is centered above rotary table.

 Ensure rig alignment with Top Drive System also. Make sure rig tongs and rig floor hoisting

equipment are adequate for handling 8″ and 9-1/2″ drill collars. Make sure that mechanical tong

torque gauges for drill pipe/drill collar are properly functioning and have been calibrated;

re-calibrate as required.

3) Rig Equipment

 Check condition of contractor’s tubular to be utilized during the 26″ section, including all subs,

X/O, DC and HWDP, on conformity with the drilling contract’s specifications. Verify that the 26″

tri-cone bit is ready to be picked up, all nozzles installed, and 26″ bit breakers are on the rig floor.

Make sure single-shot or multi-shot inclinator available for vertical section survey.

 Make sure all solids control equipment are correctly installed and have been function-tested with

charging pressure gauges in place where applicable. Make sure adequate screen inventory for the

shale shakers is available in the sizes required for the well. Make sure water tanks are completely

filled and transfer lines from water tanks to mud system are hooked up. Make sure all mud

materials and chemicals required to drill 26″ section are on location, in sound condition and

suitably stored. Make sure that bentonite is pre-hydrated and sufficient volume has been built for

top section and for well-kill.

 Make sure that all mud pumps have been fitted with new consumable parts: liners, pistons,

SOUTH AZADEGAN PROJECT

S378H on Pad 50 Drilling Program

Version: 3 rd

Drilling Program Page 44

valves, seats etc. Make sure that pulsation dampeners are charged with Nitrogen to the proper

pre-charge pressure, 30% of expected standpipe pressure during drilling of the 26″ hole section;

check if sufficient Nitrogen bottles are available on location to adjust pulsation dampener

pre-charge pressure as required. Make sure that mud pump pop-off valves are set at the proper

pressure for the liner sizes installed and that the mud discharge lines from the pop-off valves to

the mud tanks are properly secured. Check that all high-pressure hoses are properly secured with

safety chains. P/T should be done to high-pressure surface line of circulating system.

4) Wellhead &amp;amp; BOP

 Make sure that BOP handling system is working. Have 2″ line pipe nipple with 2″ ball valve

welded to 42″ conductor pipe 0.2m above cellar bottom to drain cement from conductor/riser

pipe after cementing 20″ surface casing. Verify that pre-installed 42″ conductor pipe is vertical

and that no angle/bend exists between conductor and 42″ riser pipe.

 Make sure that adequate supply of 20″ casing is on location, inspected and ready to be run, float

shoe should already be made up, centralizers should be pre-installed on the pipe-rack prior to

spud in the well.

 Ensure mud logging unit is functioning and equipment are calibrated and tested properly.

5) Others

 Verify that the rig’s fuel tanks are full to meet minimum of three days rig consumption available

on site.

 Make sure all waste treatment equipment available and commissioning test is ok.

 Hold pre-spud meeting with relevant service Company personnel on location. Discuss procedures

involved throughout 26″ hole section drilling, reporting system and critical safety operation

measures.

10.2 Drill 26” Hole

10.2.1 Drill 26″ hole to section TD

1) Tag the bottom of cellar and control ROP to start drilling. Drill with pre-hydrated bentonite mud the

first and second stands at 60-70 RPM with 400 GPM of low flow rate to avoid washing out the

conductor.

2) Pump Hi-Vis pill to sweep hole when every stand drilled down. Continue drilling to section TD with

normal parameters.

3) Circulate hole clean. POOH to surface. Check bit if balling or not. Make condition trip. Spot Hi-Vis

pill after circulate hole clean. Drop Totco survey, POOH and retrieve Totco.

4) Hold pre-job safety meeting with involve personnel for running 20″ casing.

5) Rig up and function test 20″ casing running equipment.

6) Match the stab-in sub with float shoe on surface.

SOUTH AZADEGAN PROJECT

S378H on Pad 50 Drilling Program

Version: 3 rd

Drilling Program Page 45

10.2.2 Run 20″ casing

1) Run 20”casing as per casing tally.

2) Lock shoe track connections. Fill casing with weighted mud every joint to keep weight balance

between inside casing and annular. Monitor WOH during running casing to detect excessive drag.

3) Rig up C-plate. Run stab-in sub (with new O-ring seal), 5″ pup joint (with 5″ x 20″ bow spring

centralizer) and 5″ HWDP as stinger string in 20″ casing

4) Slowly lower stinger string and make sure stab into float shoe ok.

5) Make up circulating head. Fill up annulus (5″ x 20″) with weighted mud and check the stinger seal.

6) Secure the inner string to the rig substructure with slings.

7) Break circulation slowly. And circulate 200% of annular volume with mud at 800-1000 GPM.

10.2.3 Cement 20″ casing

1) Cement 20″casing as cement program.

2) P/U stinger, circulate to flush string inside. POOH.

3) If no slurry returns to surface, top-fill job should be performed.

4) WOC &amp;amp; L/D 26″ BHA.

10.2.4 Install Wellhead Section A

1) Install Wellhead Section A as per wellhead engineer.

2) Correctly determine elevation from top flange of CHH to RKB and then cut CP &amp;amp; 20″ casing.

3) Install wellhead section A, 20″ SOL x 20-3/4″ 3K Casing Head Housing following the right

direction.

4) Pressure test CHH port seal and refer to 9.5 Pressure Test.

5) N/U Spacer, kill/choke manifold and 20-3/4″ 3K BOP stack.

6) P/T wellhead &amp;amp; BOP system as required.

7) Set wear bushing.

10.3 Drill 17-1/2” Hole

10.3.1 Drill 17-1/2″ hole to section TD

1) M/U and RIH with 17-1/2″ drilling BHA.

SOUTH AZADEGAN PROJECT

S378H on Pad 50 Drilling Program

Version: 3 rd

Drilling Program Page 46

2) Tag TOC. Circulate.

3) P/T casing integrity as per 9.5: Pressure Test.

4) Displace new mud into hole.

5) Drill out shoe track with reduced parameters.

6) Continue drilling to the first weakest zone, especially the sand zone. New hole is not more than 20m.

7) Circulate hole clean. POOH into casing shoe.

8) Perform LOT as procedure.

9) Drill with reduced parameters before stabilizer in casing shoe.

10) Drill to section TD, with optimized parameter.

11) Take survey following 7.1 anti-collision measures.

12) Wiper trip every 300m or depending on hole condition.

13) Drill hole to TD, wiper trip, circulate, run multi-shot survey. Perform flow check before POOH and

bit enter the casing shoe.

10.3.2 Wire-line logging

1) Perform wire-line log for GR/CDR.

2) Perform condition trip for running casing.

10.3.3 Run 13-3/8″ Casing

1) Retrieve wear bushing;

2) R/U casing running tools;

3) Run 13-3/8″ casing and install centralizers as per tally;

4) Function test floating equipment.

5) Thread-lock all shoe track connections. Function test float equipment.

6) Fill up casing every joint with fill-up tool. Monitor hook loads during running of the casing to detect

excessive drag.

7) Tag bottom to confirm casing setting depth.

8) Rig up cementing head, connect cement line and pressure test same

9) Circulate at least one bottom up or till shale shaker clean.

10.3.4 Cement 13-3/8″ casing

SOUTH AZADEGAN PROJECT

S378H on Pad 50 Drilling Program

Version: 3 rd

Drilling Program Page 47

1) Hook up cement line and cement pump, pressure test with same.

2) Hold safety meeting with related persons

3) Perform cement 13-3/8″casing as cement program.

4) If no slurry returns to surface, top-fill job should be considered.

5) WOC.

10.3.5 Install Wellhead Section B

1) Set 13-3/8″ casing hanger in CHH with required tension.

2) L/D cementing head &amp;amp; landing joint.

3) N/D 20-3/4″ BOP and Spacer Spool.

4) N/U 20-3/4″ 3k x 13-5/8″ 5k casing spool, and P/T port seal.

5) N/U BOP stack.

6) P/T BOP system and casing spool as per 9.5: Pressure Test.

7) Retrieve test plug and install wear bushing.

10.4 Drill 12-1/4” Vertical Hole

10.4.1 Drill 12-1/4″ Hole to KOP

1) M/U &amp;amp; RIH 12-1/4″ BHA and tag TOC.

2) Drill Cement plug till 7m above the 13-3/8” shoe, Circulate a bottoms up.

3) Pressure test 13-3/8″ casing integrity as per 9.5: Pressure Test.

4) Displace new mud into hole.

5) Cont. drill out the shoe track and drill the new formation to the first weakest zone, especially the sand

zone, but new hole is not more than 20m.

6) Circulate hole clean. POOH into casing shoe.

7) Perform LOT as procedure and note it in DDR.

8) Drill ahead with reduced parameters till stabilizer has passed through casing shoe.

9) Drill to KOP with optimized parameter.

10) Take survey following 7.1 anti-collision measures.

11) Wiper trip every 300m or depending on hole condition.

12) Drill to KOP depth, perform wiper trip, circulate, drop .multi-shot survey tool. POOH. Perform flow

check before POOH and entering the casing shoe.

SOUTH AZADEGAN PROJECT

S378H on Pad 50 Drilling Program

Version: 3 rd

Drilling Program Page 48

10.4.2 Wireline logging

Perform wireline logging: GR/CDR/CALI

10.5 Drill 12-1/4” Directional Hole

10.5.1 Drill 12-1/4” Directional Hole

1) Install wear bushing.

2) M/U 12-1/4" directional BHA and function test same on surface.

3) RIH W/12-1/4" directional BHA to KOP and drill to section TD with optimized parameters.

4) Wiper trip will be performed once every 300m footages drilled or depending on hole condition, take

survey as required.

5) Circulate bottoms up. Wiper trip to 13-3/8″ casing shoe. RIH to bottom and wipe out any tight spots.

Circulate hole clean. POOH, Conduct flow check before POOH and entering the shoe.

6) Check trip with drilling BHA. Note any tight spots in DDR. Circulate hole clean and POOH.

10.5.2 Run 9-5/8″ Casing

1) Retrieve wear bushing.

2) R/U casing running tools, PJSM for running casing.

3) Run 9-5/8″ casing as per casing tally.

4) Function test floating equipment.

5) Thread lock connections of all shoe track joints.

6) Fill up casing every joint with fill-up tool;

7) Break circulation before run out of previous casing shoe.

8) Tag bottom and P/U to confirm the casing set depth.

9) Rig up cementing head, connect cementing line and pressure test same.

10) Slowly break circulation and circulate.

10.5.3 Cement 9-5/8″ casing

1) Cement 9-5/8″casing as cement program.

2) Apply back pressure on annulus and WOC.

3) L/D 12-1/4″ BHA during WOC.

SOUTH AZADEGAN PROJECT

S378H on Pad 50 Drilling Program

Version: 3 rd

Drilling Program Page 49

10.5.4 Install Wellhead Section C, tubing head assemble

1) Set 9-5/8″ casing hanger in 20-3/4″ 3k x 13-5/8″ 5k casing spool with required tension.

2) L/D cement head &amp;amp; landing joint.

3) N/U 13-5/8″ x 11″ 5 K casing head and P/T port seal.

4) N/U BOP stack.

5) M/U test plug and set in casing head spool. Ensure casing valve below test plug is open.

6) P/T all ram preventers, choke and kill manifolds, annular preventer, all surface BOP equipment

including kelly cocks and safety valves as per 9.5: Pressure Test.

7) Retrieve test plug and install wear bushing.

10.6 Drill 8-1/2” Horizontal Hole

10.6.1 CBL logging

1) Install wear bushing.

2) M/U 8-1/2″ directional BHA and function test same, RIH to tag TOC.

3) Drill out cement plug to 7m above 9-5/8” shoe.

4) POOH. Conduct wireline logging, CCL/GR/CBL-VDL.

5) M/U 8-1/2″ directional BHA and function test same, RIH to bottom.

6) Circulate bottoms up; P/T 9-5/8″ casing integrity as per 9.5: Pressure Test.

10.6.2 Drill 8-1/2″ Horizontal Hole

7) Drill 8-1/2" hole to TD with optimized parameters, take survey as required.

8) Wiper trip will be performed once every 300m footages drilled or depending on hole condition.

9) Circulate bottoms up. Wiper trip to 9-5/8″ casing shoe. RIH to bottom and wipe out any tight spots.

Circulate hole clean. POOH, Conduct flow check before POOH and entering the shoe.

10) Check trip with drilling BHA. Note any tight spots in DDR. Circulate hole clean and POOH.

11) RIH 9-5/8″ casing scraper to scrape liner hanger setting interval 3 times.

10.6.3 Well Completion

Refer to completion program

2. Completion Program

The completion program and production well testing includes the following parts:

 Completion fluid

 Lower and Upper Completion string

1) To ensure the compatibility with litho logy in order to minimize damage to the reservoir.

Operation Procedure for Lower Completion

2.2.3.1 Well bore preparation

1) Back reaming and hole condition.

2) RIH 9-5/8” casing scraper, scrape the expected liner hanger setting depth: 2650m~2710m

and production packer setting depth: 2450m~2540m, circulate hole clean with mud.

Note: Scraper running into open hole is not allowed.

3) POOH scraper string.

2.2.3.2 Running 5-1/2” Screen pipe

1) Hold PJSM with all relevant personnel of rig crew and relevant personnel.

2) Rig up liner running equipment on the drilling floor and function test.

3) Run 5-1/2” liner as follows:

5-1/2” guide shoe + 5-1/2” liner + 5-1/2” perforated liner + 5-1/2” liner + 5-1/2” x 9-5/8” rotating liner hanger with top packer

Note: Centralizer program recommended - For first joint of liner, one spiral rigid type centralizer at 3m below guide shoe with stop collar and one right below couple, then one centralizer for each two joints.

4) Monitor hook loads during running of the casing to detect excessive drag.

5) Make up liner hanger assembly on top of last joint of liner.

 Prior to make up the liner hanger assembly, loose the elevator to avoid the left hand

torque to release the running tool. Use the chain tong to thread before tightness.

 Don’t remove off slips; pick up around 1m to verify the connections of liner hanger

assembly.

 The first stand DP RIH, check and record the P/U weight, S/O weight. Locked rotary

table to avoid any rotation.

 All utilized 5” DP should be drifted with rabbit more than 2.56” same.

 If need to rotate the string to through the tight point, limit the torque lower 5kft.lbs,

meantime stop the pump, rotate speed lower 10 rpm. Utilize the brake to control

reactive torque to avoid premature release running tool while stop rotation.

 Limit the pump pressure less than 800psi while working string up and down.

 If need to increase P/U &amp;amp; S/O weight to deal with tight pull, the maximum allowed

slack off weight is 30 Ton except liner weight, too much weight will damage the

running tool.

2.2.3.3 Setting liner hanger

SOUTH AZADEGAN PROJECT

S378H on Pad 50 Drilling Program

Version: 3 rd

Drilling Department Page 61

1) RIH to design depth, start pump to establish circulation, if need, circulate one bottom’s up,

remove off total gas, break off the TDS and drop the ball into the string.

2) Re-make up TDS and space out. Drop ball and start pump with 2~3 bpm to chase the ball or

limit the pump pressure less than 500psi until the pressure comes up sharply.

3) Note: If the pressure comes up sharply, stop pump at once.

4) Verify the weight and recalculate the extension distance whether it is suitable.

5) Slowly pressure up to 200psi over designed set pressure hold for 2 min.

6) Slack off, check the weight of the hook, if the hook load drop down continuously, it can

proof that the liner hanger has been activated, continue to slack off until set down 10~15T

running string weight on the liner hanger.

7) After the liner hanger is successful set, commence the releasing operation procedure. If the

liner hanger cannot be set, increase 100 psi per time to repeat the setting program. Until the

pressure get same as the running tool releasing pressure.

2.2.3.4 Release the setting tool

1) After the liner hanger is successful set, set down 5T running string weight on liner hanger.

2) Pressure up to 200psi over designed, hold for 2min.

3) Bleed off, pressure up to 500psi again, pick up 1m (cannot over 2m) to verify if released.

4) If the liner weight has been lost, it indicates setting tool released successfully.

Note: If hook load continuously increase, limit over pull lower 5T than the liner weight to keep the hanger function. (If too much over pull, the liner hanger maybe un-hung)

2.2.3.5 Set top packer

1) Pick up approximately 3m, slowly slack of 15~20T to set top packer.

2) Hold 5T on packer top, close the BOP and increase annulus pressure to1000 ~ 2000psi to

check the seal ability of the packer.

Note: Control the pick up distance no more than 3m during setting top packer.

3) POOH.

2.2.3.6 Displace open-hole mud with completion fluid

1) Running 2-3/8” DP into the bottom of 5-1/2”screen to displace mud with completion fluid.

2) BHA: 2-3/8” DP + X/O+ 3-1/2” drill-pipe +X/O+ 5” drill-pipe

3) POOH and L/D DPs.

4) Prepare for running upper completion string.

2) Retrieve wear bushing, M/U jet sub and flush BOP stack &amp;amp; wellhead with fresh water.

3) All crossovers, pup joint for space out measured put in right place.

4) Lift control line and protectors on rig floor.

5) Lift all emergency well control subs in the right place of the rig floor.

1) P/U &amp;amp; M/U 3-1/2” re-entry guide shoe + 2.75” landing nipple as per running tally.

2) P/U &amp;amp; M/U 9-5/8” hydraulic-set retrievable production packer carefully.

3) M/U and RIH 3-1/2”SSD + 3-1/2” travel joint as per running tally (keep the SSD close)

Note: slick line test plug should be installed in SSD on the surface and Pressure test tubing 2,000psi/15min every 1000 meter by slick line tool.

4) Running required joints 3-1/2” 10.2# TPEX tubing as per running tally.

5) Make up 3-1/2” TRSCSSV assembly be set at approximately 100m under ground level.

6) Install 1/4”control line to TRSCSSV and pressure test control line 5000psi x 15mins. And

then keep 4000psi pressure while running to ensure TRSCSSV open. Install TRSCSSV

protector for the 1/4”control line.

7) Continue to run 3-1/2” 10.2# TPEX tubing as per running tally.

8) R/U slick line unit to pull out test plug. R/D slick line unit.

2.2.4.3 Space out and install tubing hanger

1) Space out as required with pup joints

2) Pick up &amp;amp; M/U tubing hanger with double pin crossover. M/U landing joint.

3) Roughly cut control line enough length to reach rig floor, and wrap 2-3 turns under tubing

hanger, then feed through tubing hanger. Connect the line back to reels, pressure test as the

same.

4) Plug off the cable port on tubing hanger.

5) Record P/U &amp;amp; S/O WT.

2.2.4.4 Landing tubing hanger

6) Land tubing hanger into tubing head spool carefully.

7) Lock all tie-down bolts.

8) Close annular BOP.

9) Pressure up 3000psi /15min in annulus through kill manifold to test Tubing Hanger Seal,

observe for any pressure loss.

10) Monitor if any fluid leak from gate valve.

2.2.4.5 Set production packer

11) R/U cement unit and surface line. Pressure test.

12) Pressure up 1/4” Control Line to 5,000psi to open the TRSCSSV.

13) RIH with gauge cutter for 3-1/2" tubing. POOH.

14) RIH with 2.75" X selective testing tool and set it at Landing Nipple, Leave the slick line

attached.

15) Make up the surface line and pressure test to 500psi/5mins, 1000psi/5mins, 2000psi/5mins,

3000psi/15min, to set packer, and then bleed off pressure to zero.

16) Pressure test annulus to 2000 psi/15mins to confirm the packer’s setting and sealing. Bleed

off pressure to zero slowly.

17) Pull out the 2.75" X selective testing tool

18) R/D slick line unit.

19) B/O &amp;amp; L/D landing joint.

2.2.4.6 N/D BOP &amp;amp; N/U X-mas tree

1) Close TRSCSSV.

2) Set TWCV in tubing hanger.

3) N/D bell nipple and BOP.

4) N/U tree adapter and X-mas tree. Feeding through X-mas tree adapter with 1/4” control

line.

5) Pressure test X-mas tree 5000psi holding 15mins.

6) Retrieve TWCV and set BPV.

2.2.4.7 Secure well for rig moving out

1) Close swab valve &amp;amp; wing gate valves on both sides, open master valve and SSV.

2) Open TRSCSSV.

3) Record SIWHP (shut-in wellhead pressure), if there is any.

4) Bleed off control line pressure to close TRSCSSV.

5) Bleed off WHP (tubing pressure above TRSCSSV), if there is any, measure return

(completion fluid) volume if possible. Be aware of H2S.

6) Monitor WHP for 30 min which should be zero (report to drilling/completion supervisor if

there is any pressure build up), for leak-off test TRSCSSV.

7) Close master valve. And keep gate wing valves in close position.

8) Check the annulus pressure; bleed off to zero if there is any.

2.2.4.8 Release Rig

1) R/D all rig equipment.

2) Rig release.

3) Move out rig equipment.

4) Move in well test equipment if need.

Section D: HSE Management

1. Basic HSE Requirements

1) Contractor should establish an effective HSE system and implement it strictly.

2) Contractor must adhere to the standards and regulations of Health, Safe and Environment constituted

by the local government.

3) Contractor must strictly adhere to the procedures / standards and regulations of Health, Safety and

Environment promulgated by CNPC.

4) Contractor should comply with all applicable local government regulations including guidelines and

recommended practices and any other Iranian authorities having jurisdiction.

5) All personnel should respect the local culture, traditions and social values of the indigenous

population of the Iran and South Azadegan region.

6) Contractor shall hire qualified and experienced worker and familiar his personnel with hazards

especially with H2S and Mine and UXO (unexploded ordinance) according to related procedure.

7) Contractor shall conduct proper training about UXO (unexploded ordinance) and mine awareness to

all personnel

2. Well Control

All the drilling operation shall obey the requirement of Well Control Manual of CNPC and contractor’s well control manual; Under no circumstances should the deviation from well control policy be permitted without prior approval through CNPCI (Iran) Company. If the contractor’s well control manual or anywhere has conflict with Well Control Manual of CNPC， take Well Control Manual of CNPC as the standard.

(1) Recording Reference

All BOP tests, drills, function tests, any malfunctions, repair or maintenance to the mud system and well control equipment shall be recorded in the IADC daily reports and shall be signed by both the Drilling Contractor's Tool Pusher and Drilling Supervisor on the well site. They shall also be recorded in the Daily Drilling Report.

(2) Flow Check Procedure

To avoid a kick situation, it is recommended that a flow check be conducted at specific times during the drilling operation.

1) While drilling(any warning sign)

2) Prior to tripping the drill string

3) While tripping(any warning sign)

4) While out of hole(continuously)

5) Trip out:

 After pulling 5% of the drill pipe

 At the midpoint depth of the wellbore

 Prior to pulling the first stand of drill collars

 After all the drill string is out of hole.

6) Trip in:

SOUTH AZADEGAN PROJECT

S378H on Pad 50 Drilling Program

Version: 3 rd

Drilling Department Page 69

 Upon reaching surface casing shoe

 At midpoint of the wellbore

(3) Primary Control Reference

It is the responsibility of the Drilling Contractor to keep the hole full at all times by using all the available equipment. The Drilling Supervisor shall monitor that the correct preventive practices are being implemented and/or conducted at all times.

Extreme care shall be taken to monitor mud volume, drilling breaks and gas cut mud.

The MACP (Maximum allowable casing pressure) shall be confirmed by the Drilling Supervisor, either after setting each new casing string or, whenever the density of the drilling mud changes.

The MACP shall be clearly written on a kick control sheet that will be posted near the choke control panel.

The predetermined distance at which the Tool Joint is to be pulled above the rotary should be posted on rig floor near the BOP control panel.

The Driller is responsible for carefully measuring and recording the slow pump pressure. Awareness of these values is an important element in killing operations, in order to avoid formation breakdown.

Take a measure and record the slow pump pressure at three different flow rates with all pumps at the following times:

 Once per tour.

 Whenever changes occur in the mud density/rheology.

 Whenever changes occur in the dimension and characteristics of the string, BHA, jet size, jet

plugged or jet lost, etc.

(4) Secondary Control Reference

Any time a drilling break is noticed, drilling shall stop and a static monitoring of the well shall be carried out. Space-out for all Pipe Rams and Annular Preventer must be known to the Driller at all times to keep tool joints clear of annular preventer and rams.

(5) Kick Detection Procedure While Drilling

If there is an indication of a possible kick occurring, the Driller shall follow the kick detection procedures outlined below:

Stop drilling with the pump onPick up top drive to a predetermined space-out positionShut off the pumps and check for well flow by visual examination on the bell nipple or flow line.

1) If the well is not flowing:

 Immediately notify the rig manager, Drilling Supervisor and Tool pusher.

 The Drilling Supervisor will decide whether to circulate bottoms up or resume drilling. The

penetration rate will be limited as long as the cause of the abnormal situation is undetermined.

Always be aware that some hydrocarbons (gas or oil cut mud) may rise to the surface. Ensure that

the proper monitoring and safety systems all in place.

2) If the well is flowing:

 Close the well as per the Shut-in Procedure.

 Immediately notify the Wellsite Drilling Supervisor, rig manager and Tool pusher.

S378H on Pad 50 Drilling Program

3. Health

1) This well is committed to develop for oil in a responsible manner that promotes employees' and local

inhabitants' health.

2) A trained Paramedic and proper MEDIVAC equipment and ambulance shall be stationed on the

drilling rig during the drilling campaign.

3) An emergency medical evacuation plan shall be coordinated, and shall keep in touch with emergency

response centres manned by qualified doctor 24-hours per day in Tehran or Ahwaz city.

4) Medical emergency report and investigation shall be performed as soon as possible in accordance

with Medical Emergency Procedures.

4. Safety

1) Contractor shall make detail operation procedures which have covered all related activities.

2) Due to high concentration of H2S in Sarvak, Kazhdumi and Gadvan reservoirs, Make detail H2S

operation procedures, in particular, and carry it out strictly.

3) Contractor must provide lifesaving equipment like SCBA, Escape Mask, H2S detectors (Multi

portable and personal detector) and implement the H2S Services system during drilling activity.

4) All lifting equipment and cranes must be certified by approved 3rd party (approved by Institute of

Standards &amp;amp; Industrial Research of Iran)

5) All electrical equipment should be designed for such locations, and listed by nationally recognized

testing laboratory. All wiring components and electrical equipment should be maintained in

accordance with the manufacturers’ recommendation.

6) Contractor shall implement the risk assessment and Job Safety Analysis before starting the drilling

activity.

7) PSSR (Pre-Startup Safety Review) before spud-in and penetrating into oil and gas formations are

mandatory by contractor under the supervision of Company and approved by Company.

8) Contractor shall pay much attention to fire, explosion prevention and well control.

9) Contractor shall make detail Emergency Response Plan and Evacuation Plan.

10) Contractor shall do efforts to keep employees safety as possible.

5. Environment

Requirement on location

1) The access road and well location construction shall be accorded with construction program of well

location. It minimizes any impacts on the local residents, prevent all soil contamination, prevent all

ground water contamination, and prevent all surface water contamination. Cutting and waste water

pit shall be lining and drainage system shall be good and to avoid farm and season canal

contamination.

2) Management regulation for transportation truck, drilling operation machine and tools shall be

carried out strictly to avoid damage farm and trees, etc.

3) Well site shall be flat and clean. All the equipment, materials, drilling tools shall be put in order.

4) Control the rig noise to decrease the influence to surroundings while drilling at the inhabitation area.

SOUTH AZADEGAN PROJECT

S378H on Pad 50 Drilling Program

Version: 3 rd

Drilling Department Page 71

5) Contractor shall perform on‐site segregation of wastes prior to transfer to the transfer area and/or

delivery to the transportation Contractor in accordance with the following waste hazard

classification.

Non-Hazardous Wastes (Re-usable, Recyclable and Recoverable Wastes)

1) Ferrous and non-ferrous metals, plastics, and wood wastes, PETs and potentially paper and glass

2) Materials shall be separately segregated and provision may be made for size reduction and

containerization equipment.

3) The Contractor/Generators are encouraged to seek for recycle/re-use alternatives based on the Local

available facilities, for final disposal of these materials.

4) It should be noted that landfill disposal of metal waste materials and wood wastes shall be prohibited.

For wood wastes re-use of and/or salvage of commercial timber, or deliver/release to

5) local community are recommended.

Hazardous Wastes

Hazardous Waste, such as clinic waste, oil waste, waste produced by painting, insulation works shall be duly segregated.

Facilities of environment protection supplied to well site

1) Mud purifying circulation system

2) Cooling water spraying and circulating system for drilling pump

3) Special recovery tank for deposed oil

4) Reserve house for valuable mud chemicals

5) Automatic mud weighting supply system

6) BOP stack is equipped according to drilling design

7) Define a separation area for gathering all waste according to waste management procedure

Requirement of environment protection on location

1) Sewage pit Area of the sewage pit: 1500 m2

2) Prior to spud， mud pit and sewage pit must comply with the standard. Install cooling water spraying

and circulating system for drilling pump and sewage circulating system for cleaning rig floor and

equipment.

3) Install BOP stack and pressure test shall be operated according to the drilling design to avoid

blowout.

4) Install oil supply lines and check whether there is any leakage.

Management of environment protection on location

1) In drilling operation， keep mud and sewage from overflowing. If it happens, clean up timely.

2) Mud chemicals shall be stored according to the standard and shall not be scattered around well

site. If mud chemicals scatter while loading or unloading, clean it up at once. The sack of mud

chemicals shall be recovered. Do not dispose it on site.

3) Enhance water management at well location and do not wash equipment with fresh water. Stop

water flowing for long time. Overhead tanks shall be utilized.

4) Oil management shall be carefully at the well site. No oil dirt on site, no dripping and leaking at

oil tank and manifold system area.

SOUTH AZADEGAN PROJECT

5) After the well is completed, reinforce the sewage pit， solidify the disposed mud and have

environment procedure fulfilled.

6) Install fuel supply lines and keep them in good condition.

7) All the drilling fluid materials shall be recovered and shall not be left at the well site after

completion.

8) The environmental protection personnel from contractor and operator side shall check and accept

the well site environment according to the regulation after completion. Only well site

environment is qualified, the well can be delivered.

9) Transition Area for Hazardous Waste shall also be provided by each Contractor in his allocated

area,

Company shall approve each area before use as well. The transition area of hazardous waste shall

be:

 Paved, fenced, marked and illuminated

 Equipped with appropriate Fire Extinguisher and other emergency response equipment

 (e.g. Eye-Wash and Emergency Shower, appropriate First Aid kits, neutralizer substances

etc.).

 In compliance with the requirements of handling, transportation and storage of hazardous

waste (based on usage chemical MSDS).

 Configured to accommodate a safe physical separation of incompatible waste materials (e.g.

acids, and alkalis, organic materials and strong oxidizing agents).

 Capable enough to provide storage for the entire range of hazardous wastes generated during

the work.

 The area shall be provided with Spill Containment and means of preventing run‐off to and

from the area.

 All waste containers to be stored shall be appropriately labeled.

 Hazardous Waste shall be transferred in a timely manner, within a maximum period of 48

hours, for any period in excess of this permission shall be granted from Company and/or

PEDEC.

Standard of utilization and discharging of wastes on location

1) Conduct drilling operation according to the design, drilling mud is needed before spud.

2) Sewage that cannot be recovered shall be put into the pit， do not discharge. If the volume of sewage

is too big and some should be discharged， the quality of drainage must comply with the following

regulations.

Maximum permitted concentration of wastes in water

Drilling Department Page 73

3) Make full use of waste water. Water in mud pump and water brake must be utilized by circulating.

Water that is used to wash drill floor, shall be recovered after deposition. The recovery rate of

waste water shall reach 85％.

4) Disposed oil shall be recovered entirely. Recovery rate shall be 100％.Dumping of waste oil shall

be prohibited.

5) In drilling operation, non-chrome thinner high temperature mud system shall be used often if

engineering is qualified.

6) While drilling in special area， adopt mud creation inhabitation techniques to decrease the waste

mud creation.

7) After completion, all the mud chemicals, bentonite, clays shall be recovered and shall not be left at

the well site. Mud in purifying tank shall also be recovered after completion.

8) In case of any flammable or noxious gas encountered， steps shall be taken at once to prevent kicks

and blowout. Gas shall be guided into ignition equipment to burn it away.

9) Burning material that may result in serious smog or horrible smell at the well site is not allowed.

For cement or barite that may result in granular dust pollution， operation shall be performed in a

closed system.

10) For abandoned well， filled with cement plugs to seal the oil, gas or water formation.

11) Contractor/Generators are required to transport all generated wastes to the location/facilities

designated, and licensed by authorities and/or approved/verified by the Company/PEDEC (as

appropriate).

12) All wastes shall be transferred by approved Sub ‐Contractor (which could be a 3rd party

Sub-Contractor of the Contractor/Generator itself). The Waste Transporter and any other waste

management service Contractor shall be licensed in accordance with local regulations and are in

compliance with such regulations. Company shall verify and approve the Waste Transportation

Contractor by checking licenses and qualifications, audit and inspections, verification of human

resources and received trainings etc.

13) The transportation Contractor shall ensure that all wastes are transported in a safe and responsible

manner.

6. H2S monitoring and prevention measure

6.1 Monitoring H2S

1) Somewhere on the well site is apt to accumulate H2S, such as mud pit, shale shaker, and drilling

platform, should be installed one set of. Make sure H2S monitor and alarm system can be used.

2) Alarm threshold setting for H2S warning indicator: the first warning level is 10mg/m3, unable

warning sound, just show present value of H2S content to operators. The second warning level is

20mg/m3, when the H2S content in air exceed 20mg/m3, H2S warning indicator can give an alarm

automatically, and warning sound should be heard by everyone work in well site. The audible alarm

should be installed on Kelly board.

3) Equip enough gas masks on drilling platform, shaker screen (total amount should large than 24), and

equip 12 sets of 30min positive pressure Air Aspirators， 2 sets of portable H2S monitor and

SOUTH AZADEGAN PROJECT

S378H on Pad 50 Drilling Program

Version: 3 rd

Drilling Department Page 74

appropriative H2S warning indicator. Arrange a person specially assigned for taking charge all the

protective apparatus. This man must do periodical check to keep these equipment in a good

condition.

4) H2S monitor should be done weekly check and compulsory examination.

5) After drilling into the pay zone, strengthen the detection of H2S content in mud.

6) Contractor shall implement H2S service system by himself or 3rd party for controlling the risk of H2S

leakage.

6.2 Measures for H2S prevention

1) Windsocks shall be set on the drill floor and in the monsoon direction or/and prevailing wind

direction of Azadegan oil field, off well site. In emergency, employees must follow the evacuation

procedure.

2) Explosion-proof blowers shall be installed around the rig, shale shaker, and drilling fluid tanks to

blow away toxic and flammable gas at the well site.

3) The rig crew in the H2S area shall be furnished with H2S monitors and adequate protective apparatus

in accordance with SY/T 5087. Everybody shall be able to use, maintain, and check the apparatus.

4) The technicians of rig crew are responsible for H2S proof training and the tool pusher is in charge of

the supervision and examination.

5) The pH value of drilling fluid in the H2S area shall be kept over 9.5. Pay attention to measurement of

H2S concentration in drilling fluid. The H2S concentration shall be kept at less than 50mg/cm3 by

using sulphur removal agents and degassers.

6) Personnel safety and protection shall be carried out according to SY/T5087 during operations in

polluted areas where H2S content exceeds the critical concentration.

7) When the rig crew makes decision to bleed and fire because well control cannot be performed due to

well site conditions, operations shall be performed according to procedures in SY/T5087.

8) Once blowout occurs, the incident shall be reported to the higher level department as soon as possible

and fire fighting trucks, ambulances, medical care personnel and technicians shall be on duty at the

well site.

9) After the blowout is controlled, H2S concentration should be measured in the places where H2S is

possible to gather.

10) The personnel are not allowed to access until the H2S concentration is below the critical

concentration.

1 Introduction

1.1 Program Introduction

The initial exploration/delineation drilling in Azadegan oil field has proved the presence of a very prolific hydrocarbon bearing sedimentary layers, particularly within the Cretaceous sequences. Sarvak formation being the main reservoir is divided to 13 zones (Sarvak-1 to Sarvak-12 and Sarvak Intra). The Sarvak-1 to Sarvak-10 zones are oil bearing with a tilted WOC.

The well S372 a highly deviated well, is planned to be drilled in the well Pad-47 as a Sarvak producer well. This pad is located in the middle part of South Azadegan oil field in Area-I. Figure 1 shows the position of S372 well in this Pad.

The objective of this well is producing from Sarvak-3 and 4 to provide maximum drainage from reservoir. According to the Petro-physical log of AZN-10 which is the closest well to pad-47, Sarvak-3 and Sarvak-4 are capable for production.

Although Sarvak 6 and 7 have appropriate reservoir properties but these zones are near to water transition zone. Well S372 has been designed with azimuth of 125 degree according to keep the proper distance from AZN-10 and AZNS-36 wells.

1.2 South Azadegan Structure

The Azadegan field is located on a large long-axis anticline with N-S trending, an approximate length of 60 km and width of 20 km. The South Azadegan oil field is the southern part of the Azadegan oil field. The trap area of the south Azadegan is limited to 43.2x17.2 km. The Azadegan Oil field was discovered in 1999, when Well AZN-1 was drilled vertically down to the Cretaceous Fahliyan formation with total depth of 4,643m. The results of this well, revealed the reservoir characteristics of the field. Following to the result of the well no.AZN-1, another 5 exploration wells was drilled in different parts of this huge field down to Fahliyan Formation. In the later stage the well No.10 assumed as exploration well for evaluation of deeper formations. This well was drilled in 2008, down to the depth of 5315 m, mainly to evaluate the Jurassic formations (Figure 2).

This new well that located in the middle part of South Azadegan oil field in Area-I will be drilled directionally to the reservoirs in the Sarvak Formations, and will be completed by perforated liner. Production from the Sarvak is considered for producing Azadegan field in order to evaluate potential producing of South Azadegan oil field.

6 Key Reservoir Description

Sarvak Formation

The Sarvak Formation is regionally overlain by Laffan shale with unconformity and Comprises thick limestone and dolomitic limestone with minor clayey and argillaceous interlays, attaining totally 600~700m in thickness. For the importance of hydrocarbon accumulation, which is lithologically dominated by bioclastic wackestone and packstone of shallow marine origin, whereas the lower part mainly comprises argillaceous wackestone and mudstone, representing a more basin setting. The upper part of the formation is to be defined arbitrarily as the interval from the top of the formation down to the seismic marker, Intra-Sarvak.

For the layering scheme of the reservoir section, sequence stratigraphic concept was applied to the Azadegan wells. Judging from the characteristics of gamma ray and other wireline logs, relative sealevel change during the deposition of the reservoir sections were interpreted in terms of sequence stratigraphic context. Based upon the sea-level change inferred, the sections were interpreted as vertical accumulation of a number of zones, each of which is geologically termed as a depositional sequence, implicitly representing a genetically related body of sedimentary sequence. The formation was divided totally into thirteen zones by interpreting

Sar-1

Gross thickness of Sar-1 is in the range of 16m to 26m and the average gross is 20.9m in thickness. Net/Gross ratio is 71.1% and Net-pay is 11.4m. Although properties (Porosity is 12.5%, Perm is 10.6md) are higher, oiliness (So is 57.7%) is lower, It comprises mainly light brown, brown and bituminous oiliness limestone with fossils, rudist debris and echinoid chalky, Nezzazata.

Sar-2

Gross thickness of Sar-2 is in the range of 8m to 19m and the average gross is 14.6m in thickness with the lower Net/Gross ratio of 13.7%. It is mainly composed of bioclastic mudstone, lamellational limestone and argillaceous limestone. Terrigenous mud is present. Property is poor. Mean porosity is 9.3% and mean permeability is 1.8md.This zone is a compact layer and can be a stable barrier.

Sar-3

Gross thickness of Sar-3 is in the range of 16m to 30m with average of 21.4m in thickness. Net/Gross ratio is 79% and Net-pay is 15.8m. It is mainly composed of light brown or dark brown bituminous oil dolomitic limestone, which is dominated by bioturbated and bioclastic packstones and grainstone. It is a main oil-bearing zone with the best property and oiliness of Sarvak formation in the Azadegan. Mean porosity is 16.8% and mean permeability is 20.7md and So is 83%.

Sar-4

Gross thickness of Sar-4 ranges from 19m to 33m and the average gross is 24.5m in thickness and Net/Gross ratio is 77.2% and Net-pay is 17.6m. Light brown, brown and dark brown limestone with fossils or bituminous dominate and majority is peloidal or bioclastic wackestone, packstone and grainstone containing slight mudstone. Property and oiliness are moderate. Mean porosity is 12.7% and mean permeability is 8.5md and So is 69%.

Sar-5

Gross thickness of Sar-5 is in range of 21m to 37m and the average gross is 28.2m in thickness. The higher Net/Gross ratio is 91% and the thicker Net-pay is 24.6m. It comprises brown green gray calcareous shale, brown to darkbrown oil bituminous limestone and bioclastic limestone with fossils, Nezzazata, rudist debris, Ovalveolina, Dukhania, Cisalveolis and Miliolid. Majority is wackestone and packstone. Property and oiliness are moderate next to Sarvak-3 and Sarvak-8. Mean porosity is 12.7% and mean permeability is 8.2md and So is 70%.

Sar-6

Gross thickness of Sar-6 is in range of 29m to 54m and the average gross is 41.4m in thickness with the higher Net/Gross ratio of 86.1% and the thicker Net-pay of 26.2m. It is lithologiclly dominated by light brown, brown and dark brown bituminous limestone with fossils, Nezzazata, Rudistdebris, Ovalveolina, Dukhania, Cisalveolis, Miliolid, Echinoid and partly with oil. Majority is peloidal and bioclastic wackestone, packstone and grainstone. Both property and oiliness are moderate. Mean porosity is 12.1% and mean permeability is 4.3md and So is 69.6%.

Sar-7

Gross thickness of Sar-7 is in ranges of 11m to 20m and the average gross is 15.6m in thickness. Net/Gross ratio is 78.5% and Net-pay is 6m. It is lithologically dominated by light brown to dark brown bituminous limestone with foraminifera and comprises bioclastic packstone, wackestone and mudstone. Property and oiliness are poor. Mean porosity is 10% and mean permeability is 1.4md and So is 63.8%.

Sar-8

Gross thickness of Sar-8 is in range of 47m to 72m and the average gross is 57.3m in thickness with the higher Net/Gross ratio of 98% and the thicker Net-pay of 14.1m. It is mainly composed of thick light brown to darkbrown bituminous limestone with fossils, Nezzazata, Rudistdebris, Ovalveolina, Dukhania, Cisalveolis, Miliolid, Echinoid with middle-thin buff limestone interbed and partly with oil. Bioclastic packstone and grainstone dominate. Property and oiliness are better next to Sarvak-3 of Sarvak formation in the Azadegan. Mean porosity is 15.3% and mean permeability is 13.5md and So is 75%, but It is an oil and water bearing zone.

Sar-9

Gross thickness of Sar-9 is in range of 16m to 31m and the average gross is 23.3m in thickness. Net/Gross ratio is 77.4% and Net-pay is only 3.2m. Lithology is dominated by light brown or brown limestone with fossils and bituminous. It is an oil and water-bearing zone. Property is moderate. Mean porosity is 12.3% and mean permeability is 3.7md. Oiliness is poor and So is 61.3%.

Sar-10

Gross thickness of Sar-10 is in range of 20m to 37m and the average gross is 31.2m in thickness. Net/Gross ratio is 60.8% and Net-pay is only 1.5m. Property and oiliness is very poor. Mean porosity is 10.8% and mean permeability is 8.3md and So is 53.6%. It comprises light brown to brown and buff limestone and partly with oil and marl interbeds. It is an oil and water-bearing zone.

Sar-11

Gross thickness of Sar-11 is in range of 58m to 96m and the average gross is 80.8m in thickness. Net/Gross ratio is 63.2% and it is a water-bearing zone. Lithology is dominated by Light brown, brown and buff limestone with slight dolomite. Property is moderate. Mean porosity is 13.4% and mean permeability is 6.3md. It is a water-bearing zone.

Sar-12

Gross thickness of Sar-12 is in range of 36m to 62m and the average gross is 48.4m in thickness. Net/Gross ratio is 87.6% and it is a water-bearing and no oil pay zone. Lithology of this zone is

Sar_Intra

Gross thickness of Sar_intra is in range of 204m to 257m and the average gross is 237.7m in thickness. Net/Gross ratio is 61% and it is a water bearing and no oil pay zone. It is dominated by thick limestone with thin shale interbeds and involves light gray to light brown dolomitic and chalky limestone with some cherts, light brown coarse limestone containing pyrite and oil crack, light brown or gray medium-coarse grains limestone, brown and light gray argillaceous limestone, green gray to gray sticky marl and black medium hard slight calcareous shale interbeds. Property is better. Mean porosity is 15.8% and mean permeability is 16.1md. It is a water-bearing zone too.

11 Rig Move

 Hold pre-move meeting on location. Discuss contingency plans for:

o Safe arrangements for rig up and rig down.

o Safe standby areas for rig in case move have to be suspended.

o Loss of trucks in case of repair.

o Moving at night.

 Hold pre-move safety meeting. Ensure everyone understands individual

Responsibilities.

 Commence rigging down. The ordering of trucks will be done by rig manager.

 Commence rig move to AZNS#084, S372, PAD NO. 47

 Position rig for optimal operations

 Rig up on cellar

 Finish rig up and commence operational procedure for AZNS#084.

 Before leaving previous location, all equipment should be checked.

 Test all manifold and surface safety valves

o RKB – GLE and Elevation

o Spud date and time.

 Mud tanks should be empty during move. Fill water tanks and keep as full as

possible.
