12 Pre Spud

1) Certificate

 All rig equipment are on location, properly rigged up and function-tested. Check

availability and content of hoisting equipment inspection &amp;amp; maintenance records according to

API.

2) Safety Device

 Test draw-works crown block saver and record results on daily drilling report;

test derrick man escape device (Geronimo line) and record time required for test weight on daily

drilling report; test rig intercom system, especially for Driller-Derrick Man and Driller-Mud

Logger communication link.

 Check that all rig safety equipment, e.g. fire extinguishers, eye-wash stations etc.,

is installed at the proper locations as per rig layout diagrams.

 Verify that substructure is level and foundation adequate to support drilling

unit during whole well period and that mast is centred above rotary table.

 Ensure rig alignment with Top Drive System. Make sure rig tongs and rig

floor hoisting equipment are adequate for handling 8-1/2″ and 9-1/2″ drill collars. Make sure

that mechanical tong torque gauges for drill pipe/drill collar are properly functioning and have

been calibrated; re-calibrated as required.

3) Rig Equipment

 Verify that the 26″ tri-cone bit is ready to be picked up, all nozzles installed, and

26″ bit breakers are on the rig floor. Make sure single-shot or multi-shot survey tools available

for vertical section survey.

 Make sure all solids control equipment are correctly installed and have been

function-tested with charging pressure gauges in place where applicable. Make sure adequate

screen inventory for the shale shakers is available in the sizes required for the well. Make sure

water tanks are completely filled and transfer lines from water tanks to mud system are hooked

up. Make sure all mud materials and chemicals required to drill 26″ section are on location, in

sound condition and suitably stored. Make sure that bentonite is pre-hydrated and sufficient

volume has been built for top section and for well-kill.

 Make sure that all mud pumps have been fitted with new consumable parts:

liners, pistons, valves, seats etc. Make sure that pulsation dampeners are charged with Nitrogen

to the proper pre-charge pressure, 30% of expected standpipe pressure during drilling of the 26″

hole section; check if sufficient Nitrogen bottles are available on location to adjust pulsation

dampener pre-charge pressure as required. Make sure that mud pump pop-off valves are set at

the proper pressure for the liner sizes installed and that the mud discharge lines from the pop-off

valves to the mud tanks are properly secured. Check that all high-pressure hoses are properly

secured with safety chains. P/T should be done to high-pressure surface line of circulating

system.

4) Wellhead &amp;amp; BOP

 Have 2″ line pipe nipple with 2″ ball valve welded to 30″ conductor pipe 0.2m

above cellar bottom to drain cement from conductor/riser pipe after cementing 20″ surface

casing. Verify that pre-installed 30″ conductor pipe is vertical and that no angle/bend exists

between conductor and 30″ riser pipe.

 Make sure that adequate supply of 20″ casing is on location, inspected and ready

to be run, float shoe should already be made up, centralizers should be pre-installed on the piperack prior to spud in the well.

 Ensure mud logging unit is functioning and equipment are calibrated and tested

5) Others

 Verify that the rig’s fuel tanks are full to meet minimum of three days rig

consumption available on site.

 Make sure all waste treatment equipment available and commissioning test is ok.

 Hold pre-spud meeting with relevant service Company personnel on location.

Discuss procedures involved throughout 26″ hole section drilling, reporting system and critical

safety operation measures.

NIDC prepared a pre-spud checklist and distributed it in rigs. The checklist will be performed based on the aforementioned checklist. In addition to the checklist, following matters should be checked:

 Check &amp;amp; observe the alignment of the rig. This check will be performed in

four stages; rig levelling, derrick verticality, derrick alignment with rotary

table, rotary table alignment with conductor pipe. To do this pick up 3 joints

of 9 1/2” DC and check the verticality of the derrick.

 Mechanical facilities for mud treatment such as :

Desander, Desilter, mud cleaner, proper size of shaker–screens, hoppers, mud guns &amp;amp; mixers, should be all available on rig and functioning properly.

 All mud tanks, mud transfer lines &amp;amp; connection should be checked by filling

them with water &amp;amp; cross wellhead circulation.

 Mud engineer laboratory should be equipped with a complete set of testing

equipment. The calibration should be done under supervision of well site

drilling supervisor before starting the operation.

 Weight indicator, rotary speed gauge, any smart drilling instrumentation, Top

Drive, Stroke meter, pressure gauges on manifold and in the drilling console,

loss / gain gauge and any other gauges should be checked and calibrated.

 Stand pipe manifold valves &amp;amp; connection must be checked &amp;amp; pressure tested.

 All motors should be checked under load prior to start drilling.

1 STRUCTURAL GEOLOGY:

The Azadegan oil field is located at 80km west of Ahwaz and the Azadegan Field is an elongated anticline, trending in N-S direction, belongs to Arabian Trend which is different from “Zagros Trend”. There is no outcrop for Azadegan structure and it was detected by 3D seismic interpretation.

2 LITHO-STRATIGRAPHY DESCRIPTION:

The stratigraphy sequence of the field includes Aghajari, Gachsaran, Asmari, Pabdeh, Gurpi, Ilam, Laffan, Sarvak, Kazhdumi, Dariyan, Gadvan and Fahliyan Formations, from top to bottom. This sequence in well no. AZN-10, the deepest up to now drilled well of the field, continues with Garau, Gotnia, Najmah, Sargalu, Alan, Mus and Neyriz formations.

Fars Group

Fars group originally divided into two formations, Aghajari and Gachsaran formations.

Aghajari Formation

Depth: Surface to 1147 D r i l l e d Thickness: 1147m Age: MIOCENEPLIOCENE Lithology: This Formation begins with light cream, light gray, yellow, reddish brown, quartz, subrounded, good sorted Sandstone. This formation is mostly consisting of red marl interbedded with sandstone and red claystone layers. The Red claystone increase toward the base of the formation. The Sandstones are variably consolidated and generally light brown, light gray in colour, fine to medium grain size, generally fine grained, rarely coarse grained, generally well sorted and dominated by sub-angular to sub-rounded quartz grains, loose, friable to moderately hard, slightly calcareous. The Marls are red brown to brown and pale red brown, generally sticky and slightly silty, soft to firm and locally very low calcareous grading to claystone. The Red claystones are brown, moderate to dark brown, generally soft, sticky and amorphous, locally some calcareous grading to marl, generally non silty and occasionally mottled. A fauna of brackish to freshwater was observed, together with more marine fauna.

Gachsaran Formation

Depth: 1147-1502 m Drilled Thickness: 355 m Age: Middle Miocene - Early Miocene Lithology: This Formation begins with white, glassy, soft, medium, hard Anhydrite and off white, light gray to gray, soft to medium hard, Dolomitic Limestone. Comprises of anhydrite interbedded with gray marl and red marl, salt beds of variable thickness and some thin limestone beds. This formation in type section not divided to other member. The Anhydrite is white off white, milky, soft, partly crystalline to crystalline, medium hard to hard. The Gray marl is gray to light gray, soft. The Red marl is red brown to brown, soft, sticky. The Limestone is gray to light gray, buff to buff gray, hard, slightly dolomitic.

Asmari Formation

Depth: 1502-1785m Drilled Thickness: 283 m Age: Oligocene - Miocene Lithology: This Formation begins with cream, light gray, soft to medium hard, poor Fossil Dolomitic Limestone. Consisting of white, off white, light gray to gray, soft to medium hard, I/II,I, II, Dolomitic Limestone particularly in upper part. The Sandstone increase toward the base with interbedded gray marl, dolomite and claystone of the beds formation. The Sandstone is gray, light to gray, medium to coarse with partly pyritic, medium sorted. The Gray marl is gray, light gray, soft. The Dolomite is light cream to cream, porous. The Claystone is red light brown, soft, sticky.

Pabdeh Formation

Depth: 1785-2193m Drilled Thickness: 408m Age: Paleocene-Eocene

The Pabdeh Formation is divided into two parts in the Azadegan field.

Lithology: This formation starts with Marl, gradually replaces by Argillaceous Limestone. The upper part is made of grey to dark-brown Argillaceous Limestone and Marls. Planktonic fauna dates that this part was deposited in Oligocene. The lower part is composed of dark-brown, slightly Argillaceous Limestone. Pelagic fauna, mostly Globigerina and Globorotalia, indicates that this part was formed during late Paleocene to late Eocene in age. It seems that no early Paleocene deposits exist in the Azadegan area.

Gurpi Formation

This is formation consists of three main units:

A) Upper Gurpi Member

B) Tarbour Tongue

C) Lower Gurpi Member

Upper Gurpi Member

Depth: 2193-2314 m Drilled Thickness: 121m Age: Campanian- Maastrichtian

Lithology: This Member begins with light gray, gray, off white, soft to medium , sticky Argillaceous limestone. The Upper Gurpi Member is mostly consisting of gray buff to gray with of trace partly buff gray, dark gray, medium hard to hard argillaceous, high argillaceous graded to marl Argillaceous limestone interbedded with anhydrite marl and chalky limestone beds. The Anhydritic marl is light gray to gray, soft, sticky, graded to high argillaceous calcareous. The Chalky Limestone is light gray to buff gray, medium hard to soft,chalky II,A slightly argillaceous.

Tarbour Tongue

Depth: 2314-2410m Drilled Thickness: 96m Age: Campanian- Maastrichtian Lithology: This Member begins with cream, light brown, porosity, oil stained Limestone.

Tarbour Tongue consisting of cream to light gray, light brown, buff, medium hard, II,A Limestone interbedded with chalky limestone and marl beds. The Chalky limestone is light cream, soft. The Dolomite medium bedded dark gray. The Marl is light gray to gray, soft, sticky.

Lower Gurpi Member

Depth:2410-2542m Drilled Thickness: 132m Age: Campanian- Maastrichtian Lithology: This Member begins with off white, cream, soft to medium hard Argillaceous limestone and light gray to gray, soft, sticky Marl. The Member consisting of dark gray to gray, light gray, soft to medium hard Argillaceous limestone and light cream and soft. II, A. Chalky Limestone beds.

Bangestan Group

Bangestan group is divided into four formations: Ilam, Laffan, Sarvak and Kazhdumi.

Ilam Formation

Depth: 2542-2699m Drilled Thickness: 157m Age: Coniacian -Santonian Limestone. This formation is mostly consisting of limestone interbedded with shale and clay stone beds. The Limestone is cream, buff to buff gray, light brown, soft to medium hard, chalky, II, A, Oil stained Partly slightly argillaceous. The Shale is green gray to light green gray, mostly brown gray, medium hard, pyritic, slightly calcareous. The Clay stone is green gray to light green gray and soft, slightly calcareous.

Laffan Formation

Depth: 2699-2712m Drilled Thickness: 13m Age: Coniacian

Lithology: This Formation begins with greenish gray, green, Soft, sticky, pyrite, slightly and calcareous Claystone and green, light greenish gray, light gray, medium to hard, fissile Shale. This formation is mostly consisting of shale interbedded with clay stone beds. The Shale green gray to light green gray, mostly brown gray medium hard, pyritic, medium hard, slightly calcareous. The Clay stone green gray to light green gray, soft and slightly calcareous.

Sarvak Formation

Depth: 2712-3600m Drilled Thickness: 888m Age: Cenomanian

Lithology: This Formation begins with light brown, cream, light cream, I/II, I and Oil stained Limestone. This formation is mostly consisting of off white, cream, buff to cream and white to cream, soft, soft to medium hard, chalky Limestone interbedded with claystone, argillaceous limestone, shale, argillaceous dolomite and dolomite limestone beds. The Claystone is gray, soft, sticky, high calcareous. The Argillaceous Limestone is white gray to light gray, light buff, medium hard and slightly bituminous. The Shale is dark brown, dark gray, black, medium hard and calcareous. The Argillaceous Dolomite is buff gray, hard. The

12 1/4" Hole Section: 12-1/4” hole section was started from 1485 with 75 pcf KCL/Polymer mud. FIT was

performed @ 1489m &amp;amp; EMW was 83 pcf. MW was increase from 75 to 77 pcf as per program. Drilling was

continued to 2300m. While wiper trip, Tight Hole was detected, so MW was increased to 78 pcf. While POOH

for new BHA, survey was taken every 100m. Drilling as a deviated hole started from 2340 to 2764 (9 5/8"

CSG shoe). During wiper trip @ 2648, Mechanical Stuck was occurred (No returned mud). Over pull (Max.

250 Klbs), Pumping KCL brine &amp;amp; using PIPE LAX solution (110 bbl. G.OIL+ 5 gal/bbl. PIPE LAX) wasn't

successful. After CCL/SINKERBAR &amp;amp; FPIT log had been run, The CCL/ELECTRICAL back off was run &amp;amp;

2 Lesson learned

Understanding and anticipating drilling problems, understanding their causes, and planning solutions are necessary for overall-well-cost control and for successfully reaching the target zone. According to report of nearby wells, the following items has been considered to drilling the new well:

1- Bit balling is common problem. A rough bit surface will increase the surface area and

increase the adhesive forces. When the mud flow stops, or if a bit with poor hydraulic

design is used, an electrostatic force may cause clays to stick in the bit surface. With several

work such as increase flow rate, Pump a caustic pill, Spin the bit as fast as possible can be

prevented this problem.

2- Stuck is another problems in the perevius wells. stuck can be classified under two

categories: differential and mechanical. In the nearby wells, it can be said that Mechanical

type wasn’t happened except stuck 13 3/8” casing in AZN 047 at 765m (Aghajari formation

and got free with 250 Klbs overpull). More stuck in the mentioned wells often is associated

with complete loss, so differential type may be happened. In AZN 047, string got stuck with

71 PCF mud from 1928m to 1945m (Pabdeh formation) and got free with 40 Klbs Over

pull. Another stuck in this well was happened with 76 PCF mud at 2675m to 2714m

(Sarvak Formation) and got free with 60-100 Klbs over pull.

3- Tight hole is a common problem in the mentioned wells and usally for curing this problem,

mud weight is increased. The serius tight hole was reported in Jahrum/Pabdeh and Gurpi. It

should be noted that when tight hole is cured, mud weight don’t excess from critical value.

4- The costly problem that may be happened in future wells is twist off string. Twisting off is

ocurred when the drill string parts by failing catastrophically under the torsional stress. This

may happen if the drill string has been encountered either fatigue or excessive torque. This

problem has been occurred four times in AZN 025(2660m, 3445m, 3472m and 3542m) and

fish was recovered. Because of string got stuck, twist off bit sub was happened in

Jahrum/Pabdeh formation. Due to fish hasn’t been recovered, side tracking was perform

from 1533m.

WELL AZN 17H:

5- The 17 ½” hole section had been drilled to 1140m with 70-82 PCF W.B.M, the formation

drilled is Aghajari-Gachsaran, tight hole (1140-50m) was encounter when during the

condition trip, wash and ream several times this interval. Totally operation is smoothly, a

proper mud weight in this section is important for the well’s operations.

6- While drilled 17 ½” and 12 ¼” hole section in Aghajari and Gachsaran formation observed

bit and stabilizer balled up.

7- The best approach is to use good fundamentals: an inhibitive mud, optimal hydraulics and a

quality ROP enhancer.

- Cure bit balling

- Work the bit by rotating fast off bottom and reciprocating the string to

shake off the clay coating.

- Reduce ROP for a short time.

- Spot a walnut pill.

- Circulation.

- Fresh water.

- If bit balling is observed while drilling, a detergent is usually added to

disperse the balled clays.

- The use of a small percentage of glycol also helps to reduce bit balling.

- Consider fresh water pill.

- Keep the API fluid loss as low as possible.

8- The 8 ½” hole is drilled to 1970m with 75 pcf salt water w/2-12 BPH losses. For the mud

losses, a mud system with LCM is required.

9- The 6 ⅛” hole was drilled to 3595.5m MD with 76 PCF O.B.M, the formation drilled was

Gachsaran-Asmari-Pabdeh-Ilam-Sarvak-Kazhdumi, the main problem is stuck pipe @

3595.5m , MD in Kazhdumi Fm. work on stuck with over pull, pipe got free and continue

drilled to TD with 73 PCF O.B.M so a proper mud weight in this section is important for

the well’s operations.

10- In well AZNS-026, mud properties in 17 ½” interval are poor due to the shortage of

materials such as polymer, ultrafine powder and LCM. This led to time lost about 25days. It

is recommended that KCL-polymer mud system be adopted.

11- In 8 ½” interval of well AZNS-027, overflow occurred at 2663m in Ilam formation, then

lost circulation happened at interval 2342-2381m when mud weight increased for

controlling kicking, 25 days lost in treating loss of circulation and kicking. It is

recommended that the pump rate is no more than 500gpm in formations which are

vulnerable to lost circulation such as Asmari and Gurpi. Meanwhile, mud weight shall not

be changed sharply.

12- In 8 ½ interval of well AZNS-027, lost circulation control operation was executed 6 times

with kinds of LCM such as coarse, mediate and fine nutshell, mica and so on, but it was not

controlled entirely. Maybe cementing plug is the most efficient measurement to control lost

circulation.

13- In 8 ½” hole section of well AZNS 045 while coring operation due to pump hi- vis. Pill

before coring, plug string and pipe sticking. Back off string from Slick sub, fishing

operation was not successful and finally side track hole. It is recommended that NO

PUMPING PILL BERFORE CORING. before back off String, observe shoot up pressure

while coring operation, It is recommended that if observe pressure shoot up while coring

stop operation and pull out string for checking.

Well AZN 12 in 12 ¼” hole section:

Drilling formation was continued to 1441m, due to tight hole, MW was increased to 77 pcf. Continued drilling to 1585m, complete loss was happened. Drilling has been continued to1600m meanwhile LCM pill was pumped. Also, MW has been deceased to 75pcf. drilling was continued as blind to 1860m W/ 250-480 BPH loss and suddenly (pressure drop 500 psi), twist off has been occurred F/ 8-1/2" DC. Fish was recovered with Overshoot. Cement was pumped (with 40-50 BPH loss) in two stage with 68 pcf mud.

It is recommended that at first care about MW and hold MW as low as possible and second if complete loss is happened, attempt to cure loss by LCM, by pass system and reinforce loss zone then continued drilling.

In this well twist off string was happened several times so be careful about flowing pressure while drilling and if observed any pressure drop, it must be check surface equipment and check string by slow rate pump. If observed unmoral condition pull string of hole for checking.

While spud rig, be sure that all down hole equipment has inspeced. Check inspection sheets and

1 26” Hole Section / 20” Surface Casing

1.1 General

Casing Point 20” Casing @ 150m (20”, 94#, K-55, BTC)Formation AghajariRisks &amp;amp; Hole problems No Significant Hole ProblemDeviation control TotcoLogging ---Drilling FluidBentonite MudMW 65-68 pcfVis. 70-80 secPH ≥ 11Drilling ParametersWOB Maximum AvailableGPM 600-1100RPM 90-130

1.2 Formation Sampling

On each 5 meters one sample would be taken. In addition to this general rule, geologist may decide to take more samples.

1.3 Sequence of Operation

 Make up 26” BHA as per BHA design

 Tag the bottom of cellar and control ROP to start drilling. Drill the first and second

stands at 60-70 RPM with 300 GPM of low flow rate to avoid washing out the

conductor.

 Pump Hi-Vis pill to sweep hole when every stand drilled down. Continue drilling to

±150 m (20”casing point in Aghajari formation). Pay enough attention to drill

straight hole. Use LCM pill if encountered heavy losses. If loss couldn’t be cured by

LCM pill next program will be issue later.

Note:

- TD should be adjusted in such a way to have 1 meters of rat hole under casing shoe.

- The exact TD will be determined based on 20”casing tally.

- Do not forget to strap pipe while POOH.

- Run Totco each 50 m. to evaluate the verticality of hole.

- Use following parameters to drill this hole section:

-WOB = Maximum available {Pay enough attention to drill straight hole}

-RPM = 90-130

-GPM = 600-1100

 At TD, Circulate hole clean. POOH to surface. Check bit if balling. Perform

condition trip. Spot Hi-Vis pills after circulate hole clean. Drop Totco, POOH and

retrieve survey tool.

 Hold pre-job safety meeting with involved personnel for running 20″ casing.

 R/U 20” casing running gear &amp;amp; function test 20″ casing running equipment. Perform

Safety meeting.

 Match the stab-in stinger with float shoe on surface.

 P/U and M/U shoe joint.

 Thread-lock shoe connections. Function test float shoe, Fill up casing with weighted

mud every joint to keep weight balance between inside casing and annular. Monitor

WOH during running casing to detect excessive drag.

 Run ±150m (Approx. 13 Jts) 20", 94 ppf, K-55, BTC casing with stab-in type float

shoe to bottom as per casing program (install centralizers as per casing tally). Casing

shoe should be adjusted in such a way to have 1 meters of rat hole and enough stick

up (1.5 m) on rig floor. Fill casing by non LCM fresh mud joint by joint.

 Rig up C-plate. Run stab-in stinger (with new O-ring seal), 5″ pup joint (with 5″ x

20″ bow spring centralizer) and 5″ HWDP as stinger string in 20″ casing

 Slowly lower stinger string and make sure stab into float shoe ok.

 Make up circulating head. Fill up annulus (5″ x 20″) with weighted mud and check

for sealing.

 Secure the inner string to the rig substructure with slings.

 Break circulation slowly. And circulate 200% of annular volume with mud at 800-

1000 GPM.

Note:

- Take care when running casing not to set down excessive weight if tight hole or ledges are encountered.

 Hook up cement line and pressure test same (Test Pressure:3000 psi).

 Hold pre job safety meeting with related people.

 Cement 20″ casing as per cement program.

 P/U stinger, circulate to flush string inside. POOH.

 WOC.

Note:

- Based on the results obtained from cementing, decision will be made to perform top-up jobs.

 If there is no cement return to surface, a top-up job should be performed to fill the

annulus, stage by stage until cement reaches the surface. Use the same weight as the

primary cement slurry. Ensure adequate X-Over for connecting line pipe to cement

line is available. Wait for the top job cement to get hard.

 Correctly determine elevation from top flange of CHH to RKB and then Rough cut

20” landing joint and L/D same. L/D and remove 30” conductor pipe.

 Dress casing neck suitable to install and to weld casing head spool. (If C.H.H is slip

 Install and weld casing head housing 20 3/4” – 3000 psi on casing stub and test the

sealing of welded casing (limit pressure to a maximum of 80% of the collapse

strength of the casing or maximum 400 psi). Outlets to align with cellar stairs.

 N/U spacer, kill/choke manifold and 20-3/4″ 3K Hydrill.

 P/T wellhead &amp;amp; BOP system as per NIOC Policy.

 Install wear bushing.

2.3 Sequence of Operations

 Conduct Wire-line logging as program.

 If the hole dictates, Perform condition trip for running casing.

 Retrieve wear bushing.

 R/U casing running tools and equipment.

 P/U and M/U float shoe and float collar, Thread-lock all shoe track connections.

 Function test floating equipment.

 Run 13-3/8″ casing (68#, N-80, BTC) and install centralizers as per tally.

 Fill up casing every 5-10 joints. Monitor hook loads during running of the casing to

detect excessive drag.

 Break circulation when run to mid depth of borehole.

 Tag bottom to confirm casing setting depth.

 Rig up cementing head, connect cement line and pressure test same (Test Pressure:

3000 psi).

 Circulate at least one bottom up or till clean the hole.

 Hold safety meeting with related persons while circulating.

 Cement 13-3/8″ casing as cement program.

 If observe bumping, increase pressure to 1500 psi and hold it for 15 min. &amp;amp;

report as casing integrity test.

 If no slurry returns to surface, top-fill job is required.

 Set 13-3/8″ casing hanger in CHH with required tension.

 Note: 13-3/8” casing slips should be tested to 800-1000 psi

 L/D cementing head &amp;amp; landing joint.

 N/D 20-3/4″,3K Hydrill and Spacer Spool

 N/U 20-3/4″ 3k x 13-5/8″ 5K C.H.S. and P/T p-seals (75% of casing collapse

pressure rate).

 P/T BOP system and C.H.S.

 Retrieve test plug and install wear bushing.

Note:

-Perform BOP's test on each 14 days as per NIOC Policy.

-Adjust mud weight with respect to the hole condition.

-TD should be adjusted in such a way to have 1 meters of rat hole for probable fillings.

-The Section TD maybe changed based on formation tops detected by the well site geologist.

-Do not forget to strap pipe while POOH.

-POOH. If observed any indication of drag, run back to bottom. Wash and ream to make sure that the hole condition is good.

3 12-1/4” Hole Section / 9-5/8” Production Casing

3.1 General

Casing Point 9-5/8” Casing@ 1497m MD(47#, L-80(1), Gas Tight)Formation GachsaranRisks &amp;amp; Hole problemsTight Hole, Hole stability problem, Salt water influx, Pipe sticking, High pressure salt water contamination, Calcium contamination.Deviation control Single shot each 100 m &amp;amp; Multi shot each 300 m.Logging GR/DT/Deviation Tool , CBL/VDL/CCL/GRDrilling FluidSalt Saturated mudMW 90 -110 pcfVis. 45-55 Sec/[[Q.PH](http://Q.PH)]([http://Q.PH](http://Q.PH)) 9.5-10Drilling ParametersWOB 10- 40 KlbRPM 90-150GPM 600-800PDC bit drilling parameters will be issued in due time.

3.2 Formation Sampling

From 1202 m to section TD: on each 2-5 meters one sample would be taken.

Note: As per well site Geologist request, the sample program may be changed.

3.3 Sequence of Operations

 M/U &amp;amp; RIH 12-1/4″ BHA to tag TOC.

 Circulate. Drill plugs, float collar and cement to 7m above float shoe with reduced

parameters.

 Displace new mud and circulate to condition same.

 If observe NO bumping while 13 3/8” cement job, Circulate and uniform mud then

performed P/T 13 3/8” casing integrity test to 1500 PSI.

 Drill out cement shoe track, shoe and cement of rat hole, Watch carefully for any

indication of abnormal torque, since there might be a possibility of shoe being

backed off. In case, report immediately.

 Continue drill 15-20m new formation.

 Circulate hole clean It. POOH to casing shoe.

 Perform FIT as per procedure (EMW= Max hole MW+2 PCF).

Drilling Program WELL NO. AZNS-084(S372) Page 52

 Drill ahead with reduced parameters till stabilizer has passed through casing shoe.

 Drill ahead with optimized drilling parameter.

 Take survey (Single shot each 100 m &amp;amp; Multi shot each 300 m.)

 Perform short trip every 300m or depending on hole condition.

 Drill to section TD, perform wiper trip, circulate, spot Hi-Vis pill if necessary.

-Use following parameters to drill this hole at vertical section:

-WOB = 10 - 40 Klbs

-RPM = 90-150 RPM

-GPM= 600-800

Note: PDC bit drilling parameters will be issued in due time.

 POOH.

 Perform wire line logging: GR/DT/Deviation Tool

 If the hole dictates, Condition trip for running casing (adjust mud weight if needed to

run 9-5/8” casing).

 Retrieve wear bushing.

 Change rams to 9 5/8” and perform function &amp;amp; body test.

 R/U casing running tools include jam system, PJSM for running casing.

 P/U and M/U float shoe and float collar, Thread lock all shoe track joints.

 Function test floating equipment.

 Run 9-5/8″ casing (47#, L-80(1), Gas tight) and install centralizers as per casing

tally.

 Fill up casing every 10 joints.

 Break circulation at previous casing shoe.

 Tag bottom and P/U to confirm the casing setting depth.

 Rig up cementing head, connect cementing line and pressure test same (Testing

pressure: 5000 psi).

 Slowly break circulation and circulate hole clean with optimal flow rate.

 Cement 9-5/8″ casing as per cementing program.

 If observe bumping, increase pressure to 3000 psi and hold it for 15 min. &amp;amp;

report as casing integrity test.

 If no slurry returns to surface, top-fill job is required.

 Set 9-5/8″ casing hanger in 20-3/4″ 3k x 13-5/8″ 5k CHS with required tension as

per Wellhead engineer instruction.

 Note: 9-5/8” casing slips should be tested to 2000 psi.

 R/D cementing head &amp;amp; landing joint.

 N/U 13-5/8″ x 11″ 5K T.H.S and P/T port seals (75% of casing collapse pressure

rate).

 N/U 13-5/8”- 5K BOP stack.

 M/U test plug and set in THS. Ensure outlet valve of casing head spool below test

plug is open.

 P/T all ram preventers, choke and kill manifolds, annular preventer, all surface BOP

equipment including IBOP and safety valves as NIOC Policy.

4 8 1/2” Hole Section / 7” Production Liner

4.1 General

Liner point 7” Liner @ 2804m, MD / 2679 m TVD« 2m TVD above Top of Sarvak 3 »Liner specification: 7”, 29#, L-80(1)- (6-1/8” Special drift)Formation Asmari, Pabdeh, Gurpi, Ilam, Laffan, Sarvak 1, 2.Risks &amp;amp; Hole problemsLoss of circulation, Tight hole, Pipe sticking, H2S and poisonous gas. Pipe twisting off or corrosion by sour gas, Shale and hole instability problem, Shale swelling, Pack off, Caving Hole.Deviation control MWDLogging GR/DT/Deviation Tool , CBL/VDL/CCL/GRCoring ------Drilling FluidGlycol/KCL/Polymer MUDMW 77-79 pcfVis. 40-50 Sec/QPV 13-18cpYP 12-18 Lb/100ft²Drilling ParametersWOB 10-30 KlbRPM 90-150GPM 400-600Directional drilling parameters will be specified by directional driller.PDC bit drilling parameters will be issued in due time.

4.2 Formation Sampling

On each 2-5 meters one sample would be taken. In addition to this general rule, geologist may decide to take more samples.

4.3 Sequence of Operations

 M/U 8-1/2″ drilling BHA, RIH to tag TOC.

 Drill out cement to 7m above float shoe with reduced parameters.

 If observe NO bumping while 9 5/8” cement job, Circulate and uniform mud then

performed P/T 9 5/8” casing integrity test to 3000 PSI.

 Continue drill out cement and shoe.

 Displace and adjust new mud in hole @ 3 steps and after each step observe well.

 Commence drilling formation with reduced parameters.

 Continue drill 15-20m new formation.

 Circulate hole to clean It. POOH to casing shoe.

 Perform FIT as per procedure, (EMW= Max hole MW+2 PCF).

 Continue drill about 25m new formation. Circulate hole clean, POOH.

 Perform CBL/VDL/CCL/GR logging.

 M/U 8-1/2″drilling BHA, RIH to 9-5/8" casing shoe.

 Drill 8-1/2″ hole with optimized parameters to KOP.

 Take survey as required (Single shot each 100 m &amp;amp; Multi shot each 300 m).

 Wiper trip will be performed once every 300m footages drilled or depending on hole

condition.

 At KOP, circulate clean hole, POOH.

 Perform wire line logging: GR/DT/Deviation Tool

 M/U and RIH 8-1/2" directional BHA and function test same on surface. RIH to

KOP.

 Directional drilling 8-1/2" hole to section TD as per DD’s instruction and optimized

drilling parameters.

Note:

- In order to ensure hole cleaning, at least 500gpm pump rate should be required to drill high angle section which is more than 50 degrees.

- Short trip shall be performed once every 300m footages drilled or depending on hole condition.

- TD shall be confirmed by the well site Geologist.

- Circulate hole clean with maximum flow rate as possible at TD.

 Wiper trip to 9-5/8″ casing shoe. RIH to bottom, record and wipe out any tight spots.

 Circulate hole clean with maximum flow rate as possible, spot Hi-Vis if necessary.

 POOH. Perform flow check before pull the bit above the previous shoe.

 Condition trip for running 7” liner (adjust mud weight if needed to run 7” liner).

 Retrieve wear bushing.

 R/U 7” casing running tools include jam system, PJSM for running liner.

 P/U and M/U 7” float shoe, 7” float collar and 7” LDC, Thread lock connections of

all shoe track joints.

 Function test floating equipment.

 Run 7″ liner and install centralizers as per liner tally.

 Fill up Liner every 10 joints to full.

 M/U liner hanger with top packer. Cont. running 7″ liner on DP.

 Fill up pipe every 5 stands. Break circulation when running to 9-5/8″ casing shoe.

 Tag bottom and P/U to confirm the liner setting depth.

 Hold PJSM for cementing.

 R/U cementing head and connect cementing line (Testing pressure:5000 psi)

 Slowly break circulation and circulate hole clean with optimal flow rate.

 Set liner hanger and release running tool following the instruction of L.H engineer.

 Cement liner as per program.

 If observe bumping, increase pressure to 3000 psi and hold it for 15 min. &amp;amp;

report as CIT.

 Set liner packer (If Available).

 Pull out setting tools 15 std’s, Circulate to clean the string. POOH. L/D liner setting

tools.

 Clean well to liner lap @ 1427 m.

 C.B.U to clean the hole, POOH 30 m above 7” Liner lap, Closed top rams and

perform liner lap pressure test (Step by Step to 2000 psi for 30 minutes).

 If pressure test results, not ok, next program will be issued later.

 If observed bumping while cementing, Perform Dry test liner lap.

 If not observed bumping while cementing, D/O 5m of hard cement inside 7” liner (if

observe hard cement above LDC, Continue D/O to LDC).

Circulate, clean hole (with high PH mud), POOH to surface.

Dry test liner lap.

Note: Dry test program will be offered in due time, (If dry test result is not ok, The next operation program will be issued later).

5 6 1/8” Hole Section / Open hole

5.1 General

T.D: 6-1/8“ Open hole to 3600 m, MD / 2727.73 m, TVDFormation SARVAK 3, 4Risks &amp;amp; Hole problemsLoss of circulation, Tight hole, Pipe sticking, Asphalt, H2S and poisonous gas, Pipe twisting off or corrosion by sour gas.Deviation control MWDLogging GR-MWD , Full Suite logsDrilling FluidKCL POLYMER MUDMW 80-81 pcfVis 40-50 secPV 14-20YP 14-18 Lbs/100ft²Directional Drilling Parameters Directional drilling parameters will be specified by directional driller.

5.2 Formation Sampling

On each 2-5 meters one sample would be taken. In addition to this general rule, geologist may decide to take more samples.

5.3 Sequence of Operations

 RIH with 6-1/8” drilling BHA, Drill out LDC and cement and shoe and cement of rat

hole. Observe well for any well flow. Watch carefully for any indication of abnormal

torque, since there might be a possibility of shoe being backed off. In case, report

immediately.

 Drilling formation to 1-2 m from new formation below the shoe.

 Circulate &amp;amp; clean hole. Perform FIT with EMW= Max hole MW+2 PCF. Record the

results in DDR.

 Cont. Drilling Formation to 15-20 m below the shoe, POOH.

 Perform CBL/VDL/CCL log.

 Directional drill 6 1/8″ hole to section TD as per DD’s instruction with optimal

drilling parameters.

Note:

- Short trip every 300m or depending on hole condition.

- TD will be confirmed by well site Geologist.

 Circulate at least 2 bottoms up or till shakers clean at TD with maximum flow rate as

possible.

 Wiper trip to 7" liner shoe, RIH to bottom. Circulate hole clean and spot Hi-Vis if

necessary. POOH. Perform flow check before POOH and in the previous shoe.

 Retrieve wear bushing.

 Perform logging as Full Suite log (TLC Log).

 Retrieve wear bushing.

 R/U casing running tools, PJSM for running 4 ½” perforated liner.

 P/U and M/U 4 ½”guide shoe, 1 JTs blank liner.

 Run 4 1/2″P. liner string (40 m 4-1/2” blanked liner should be used before liner

hanger) and install centralizers as per liner tally.

 M/U liner hanger with top packer. Cont. running 4 1/2″ liner on DP.

 Tag bottom and P/U to confirm the liner setting depth, POOH to have 1 m rat hole.

 Set liner hanger and release running tool following the instruction of LH engineer.

 POOH. L/D liner setting tools.

 P/U and M/U 3 ¾” clean out BHA and RIH to BTM.

 CBU and clean hole.

 Circulate and displace mud by completion fluid.

Note: Completion Program will be issued in due time.

Note: Suspension program will be issued in due time if decided to suspend the well due to lack of Completion equipment.

Note:

- Adjust mud weight according to the hole condition.

- Perform BOP's test on each 7 days as per NIOC policy.

- During trips and while at surface, driller has to check BHA.

Note: Do not forget to change top rams before running log to proper size and test same.

2 26" Hole Section

2.1 Section Discussion

The 26” hole is planned to drill with Bentonite Hi Vis. Mud to Section TD at 150 m to run 20” surface casing.

After drilling of each stand, 40 bbl. of High viscous pill should be pumped to clean hole or more if the hole condition dictates. Once TD is reached, pump 80 bbl. of high viscous pill, circulate it out and prior to pull out the BHA for running the 20" casing,

General practices to help avoiding hole to pack off during connection:

*Circulate out the whole with 100 bbl. Hi-Vis pill prior to any Totco run in hole

*Prior to POOH for BHA change, spot sufficient amount of Hi-Vis pill at bottom

3 17 1/2" Hole Section

3.1 Section Discussion

The 17 1/2” hole section will be drilled from 20" casing shoe at 150 ± m to an estimated depth of 1202 ± m. The interval consists of two formations, Aghajari, and Gachsaran formations. The formations are predominately made up of Sandstone, Clay stone, Marl, and anhydrate.

This section will be drilled down using bentonite mud to 300 m from previous section. After drilling 300 m interval, mud should be dumped and the hole will be displaced with KCl / Polymer system and drilling continues to the depth of 1202 m (MD)(55 MT in Gachsaran formation) .

Before entering Gachsaran formation density should reach to 75 PCF and fluid loss control is the critical issue while drilling this section and should be maintained as program.

3.2 Drilling Hazards

Wellbore and formation related problems are identified as follows:

* Swelling clays

*Partial losses

3.2.1 Hole instability

In addition to KCl mud and PHPA can be added to provide extra inhibition in clay section. PHPA acts as encapsulating polymer, minimizing the hydration dispersion of cutting. Pump low Vis and hivis pill periodic

3.2.2 Lost circulation

The concentration of LCM will vary according to losses. In the event of seepage losses, treat system with a fine to medium grade of LCM at 10 lb. /bbl. to 20 lb. /bbl. In the event of moderate

3.4 Mixing procedures

3.4.1 Interval of 150-300 m

1. Fill the tanks with the required volume of drill water

2. Treat out any hardness greater than 600 ppm with soda ash (1-3b/bbl.)

3. Add 25-30lb/bbl. of bentonite and allow hydrating for as long as possible

4. Raise PH to ±11 with additional of caustic soda (1-2 lb. /bbl.)

3.4.2 Interval of 300-1202 m

After drilling up to 300 m, displace the previous mud with the new mud:

1. Fill the tanks with the required volume of drill water

2. Treat out any hardness greater than 800 ppm with soda ash 1-3 ppb

3. Add KCl for shale inhibitor to reach %3-%5 w/w about10.5-18 ppb.(The calculated amount of

KCl as per the lower concentration mentioned in the program)

4. Add NaCl to M.W 74 PCF

5. Add Potato starch 9 -11 ppb then wait 10 to 15 minute on mixing

6. Use 1-2 ppb PAC-L and wait 5 minute

7. Use 1-2 ppb PAC-R and wait 5 minute

8. Use Barite to weight up above 74 PCF as needed

9. Add about 0.5-2 ppb caustic soda to control pH and reduce hardness, PH value should not

exceed more than 10.

10. Add anti-bacterial "the useful value will say after determine situation"

Notices

4 12 1/4" Hole Section

4.1 Section Discussion

The 12 1/4" hole section will be drilled from 13 3/8" casing shoe at 1202± m to an estimated section TD of 1497± m (MD) (base of Gachsaran formation in the anhydrite below the salt bed)

The 9 5/8" casing shall cover Gachsaran formation. Mud from previous section should be dumped after drill out cement; the hole will be displaced with Salt saturate mud system and then drill this section.

The section will be drilled through Gachsaran formation. The formation composed of Anhydrite, Claystone, Marl, and salt. The risk of influx in this section is very high and mud should be adjusted to control the flow. Barite stock should be kept at maximum in this phase. Intensive care should be paid to the mud in order to have proper hole cleaning.

4.2 Drilling Hazards

Well bore and formation related problems are identified as follows:

* Hole instability

* Salt water influx

4.2.1 Hole Instability

It is important to maintain mud weight as per pore pressure curve dictates in the drilling program. Ensure the concentrations are as per program and that these are determined and reported every tour. This should provide optimum hole instability and less hole problem.

4.2.2 Salt Water Influx

There is possibility of salt water flow in Gachsaran formation. This has caused severe contamination to the mud which necessitated a lot of dump and dilution and high products

1.Fill the tanks with the required volume of drill water

2.Treat out any hardness greater than 1000 ppm with soda ash

3.Weight up with salt up to 74 PCF adjusted with the whole condition

4.Add Potato starch 10 - 12 ppb then wait 10 to 15 minute on mixing.

5.Add Barite to weight up as program

6.Raise PH to 9 -9.5 with additional of Lime

7.Add XC-polymer to increase YP and viscosity as needed.

5 8 1/2" Hole Section

5.1 Section Discussion

The 8 1/2" hole section will be drilled from 9 5/8" casing shoe at 1497 ± m to an estimated section TD of 2804± m (MD. The 7" liner shall cover Asmari, pabdeh, Gurpi, Ilam, Laffan, and Sarvak 1 to 2 Mud from previous section should be dumped after drilling out cement; the hole will be displaced with Glycol / KCl / Polymer system.

5.2 Drilling Hazards

Well bore and formation related problems are identified as follows:

* Possible losses

* Present of H2S

5.2.1 Lost circulation

The concentration of LCM will vary according to losses. Partial to severe losses are expected in Sarvak formation and therefore sufficient stocks of acid soluble graded LCM, such as fine CaCO3 and oyster shell should be kept on board. In case of seepage losses, the system should be treated with medium grade of LCM. For moderate to severe losses, prepare pills at different graded concentrations and spot across the thief zone.

In order to avoid LCM plugging MWD tools a circulation sub should be installed in the drill string. The MWD engineer is to advise on the size and concentration of LCM that can be pumped through MWD tools. Ensure that the drilling displace all LCM pill out of string prior to shutting down the mud pump.

5.2.2 Presence of H2S

Treat system with H2S scavenger, keep high alkalinity and use Garret gas train to determine concentration.

7 Solid control

1) Each kind of solid control equipment should be designed to process 100% to 150% of the

maximum anticipated circulating volume of mud. Shale shaker, de-sander, de-silter and cleaner

are required to run all the time during drilling and centrifuge is recommended to run at least 80%

of drilling time.

2) The sand content and MBT should be kept as low as possible by solid removal and dilution. Batch

wise dilution (replacement of 20-30% of the total drilling fluid volume in one circulation) is more

effective than continuous dilution.

3) The detailed requirement of solid control equipment are as follows:

The capacity of Solids Control Equipment

8 Guidelines for Kill mud preparation

1) The kill fluid should be prepared prior to commence of each hole section, If well flow observed. The density of kill fluid is determined usually heavier than the formation coefficient should be recalculated this coefficient by new situation. Volume of kill fluid is following the regulation of South Azadegan Oil Field:

For pore pressure coefficient of formation increase and pay zone without H2S, the volume of kill mud will changed and need to recalculate.

If in case pore pressure coefficient of formation increase and pay zone has H2S, the volume of kill mud will changed and need to recalculate.

2) The following emergency or contingency materials should be kept on the rig site at all times to supplement the proposed mud system. Kick, lost circulation, stuck pipe scenarios, lubrication and general purpose operations may require the following products to be on storage or standby.

9 Formation or Pore Pressure and Mud Weight

Primary Well Control relies on the hydrostatic pressure of drilling fluid to balance the formation pore pressure. In order to counteract any minor pressure reductions on bottom due to swabbing effect when

tripping, it is customary to maintain a hydrostatic column with a pressure slightly exceeding the pore pressure of the exposed formation. This overbalance, safety margin, or trip margin, Ptm, varies depending on circumstances but it is generally of the order of 200 psi for conventional operations. The required density Pf to control a formation at a depth, D, with a pressure, Po, is given by: Pf = (Po+Ptm), or Df = (Po+Ptm)/D

To gas cut or contaminated mud, Df = Do + (0.07-0.15) sg,

To oil and/or salt water contaminated mud, Df = Do + (0.05-0.10) sg;

4 Casing running procedure

4.1 26” Hole Section / 20” Surface Casing

String Design

 20” Casing Stab-in Float Shoe, 94 ppf, K-55, BTC.

 ±150m (Approx.13 Jts) 20” Casing, 94 ppf, K-55, BTC. (Est. length for each joint of CSG=12m) to

Surface.

 26” x 20” bow Centralisers on each 2 Joints.

Preparation

 Visually and mechanically check the Stab-in Float Shoe for proper operation.

 Ensure all connections are thoroughly cleaned using steam or a grease solvent.

 Ensure that all casing running equipment are available and in good operation condition.

 Ensure the correct casing drifts are supplied to the rig.

 Ensure that all casing joints have been drifted.

 Ensure all cement bulk lines have been checked for blockage with bulk tanks fluffed and pressurized to the

required transfer pressure.

 Inspect and pressure test cement manifold.

Sequence of Operations

 Conduct safety meeting with all crews involved.

 Rig up casing handling and running equipment.

 P/U 20”, 94 ppf, K-55, BTC, float shoe, soft make up on first joint, P/U and make up to the optimum

torque. Do not engage the tong close to bottom of shoe. Use thread lock compound for shoe.

 Run 20” casing &amp;amp; centralisers according to tally.

 Run casing at speed calculated by WSS. A rate of 5 Joints/hr could be used as a guide.

 Work slightly through any tight spots if necessary. Circulate if deemed necessary.

 Fill casing while running in each joint.

4.2 17-1/2" Hole Section / 13 3/8” Intermediate Casing

String Design

 13-3/8” Casing float Shoe, 68 ppf, N-80, BTC.

 Two Joints (Approx. ±24m) of 13-3/8” Casing, 68 ppf, N-80, BTC.

 13-3/8” Casing float Collar, 68 ppf, N-80, BTC.

 ±1178m (Approx. ±98Jts) of 13-3/8” Casing, 68 ppf, N-80, BTC. (Est. length for each joint of CSG=12m).

 Bow Centralizer on the first 4 joints.

 Bow Centralisers 1 ea every four joints.

 Rigid centraliser on third and fourth joints from top.

Preparation

 Visually and mechanically check the float shoe and collar for proper operation.

 Ensure all connections are thoroughly cleaned using steam or a grease solvent.

 Ensure that all casing running equipment are available and in good condition.

 Ensure the correct casing drifts are supplied to the rig.

 Check the plugs fins not to be squeezed or damaged.

 Ensure that all casing joints have been drifted. Including 13 3/8”swedge (If required to wash casing down).

 Ensure all cement bulk lines have been checked for blockage with bulk tanks fluffed and pressurized to the

required transfer pressure. Ensure that the air supply for cement is functioning properly.

 Inspect and pressure test cement manifold.

Sequence of operations

 Rig up casing handling and running equipment.

 M/U 13 3/8”, 68 ppf, N-80, BTC, float shoe. If it is not already made up on joint, soft make up on first

joint, P/U and make up to the optimum make up torque based on triangle using casing tong. Do not engage

the tong close to bottom of shoe. Repeat the same for collar.

 Use thread locking compound for shoe track plus two joints on top of float collar. Take special care on

thread locking these joints, since the consequence of improper locking would be disastrous.

 Run two joints of 13 3/8”, 68 ppf, N-80, BTC casings.

 Make up 13 3/8”, 68 ppf, BTC, float collar.

 Run Approx. ±1178m (±98 Jts) of 13 3/8” Casing, 68ppf, N-80, BTC. (Est. length for each joint of

CSG=12m).

Note: Circulate through casing after running of totally 5 Jts for one Casing capacity.

 Note: Manage to have one meters of rat hole and 1.5 meters of casing stick up on rig floor.

 Pump one and half the casing volume @ 20” shoe and on TD.

 Run casing at speed calculated by Company Man. a rate of 10 Joints/hr could be used as a guide.

 Using stabbing board &amp;amp; single joint elevator to run casing would be time saving.

 Work slightly through any tight spots. Circulate if deemed necessary.

 Precautionary wash the last joint.

 When landed the casing, M/U cement head. Load the plugs accordingly. Check the flag to operate properly.

Sequence of Operations

1. WSS is to supervise the loading of liner wiper plug in liner running tool, and loading of drill pipe

wiper dart in cementing head.

2. The liner hanger engineer is to be on the rig floor at all times that the liner is being run in open hole.

3. Hold pre-job safety meeting. When running-in, apply thread lock to all connections of the shoe track.

4. Rig up liner running equipment. ,(Including jam system).Run 7” liner string considering the

following arrangements:

 7”, 29 ppf, L-80(1), TPCQ, float shoe.

 Two joints (Approx. 24m) of 7”, 29 ppf, L-80(1), TPCQ.

 7”, 29 ppf, L-80(1), TPCQ, float collar.

 One joints (Approx. 12m) of 7”, 29 ppf, L-80(1), TPCQ.

 7”, 29 ppf, L-80(1), TPCQ. Latch down collar.

 Approx. ±1341m (±1112 Joints) 7”, 29 ppf, L-80(1), TPCQ. liner.

(Est. length for each joint of liner=12m).

 Hydraulic set liner hanger + liner top packer (if available).

 Liner setting sleeve C/W liner setting tool connected

 5”, 19.5 lb/ft, drill pipe to surface.

Centralizers:

- 1 Bow centralizers for the first 4 joints (1ea per joint).

- 1 Bow centralizer per 3 joint for the rest of the open hole.

- 1 Bow centralizer per 3 joint for the rest liner joints inside 9 5/8” casing

- Use rigid centralizer on the third and fourth joint from the top.

5. Place each centralizer between stop collar and casing collar. Do not place centralizers over casing

collars

6. After making up the shoe track, lower through rotary table and check that the floats are holding. Fill up

with mud and pick up to check float functionality. Circulate for 10 min.

NIDC

NIDC Drilling Projects Management

Drilling Engineering &amp;amp; Programming Division

South Azadegan Oil field

AZNS#084 (S372 – Area I ) Rev 0.0 PEDEC

Drilling Program WELL NO. AZNS-084(S372) Page 116

7. Run liner in at controlled speed to minimize pressure surges (approx.12 joints/hr). Check returns

constantly.

8. Fill up liner completely every 10 joints run.

9. When the required numbers of liner joints have been made up, make up the liner hanger &amp;amp; liner top

packer, running tool as per liner hanger engineer’s instructions.

10. Use Liner setting tool retrievable pack off assembly for positive cement job.

11. Circulate 120% of the liner capacity. (Record Liner weight)

12. Run the liner with 5” drill pipe to the casing shoe. Circulate a minimum of one string capacity before

running into open hole, RIH in the open hole at 4-5 min/stand. Liner hanger engineer should be on rig

floor while running liner into open hole. (check the loss while RIH if need decrease the speed of the

RIH).SLM &amp;amp; drift the drill pipe while RIH the liner.

Note: before loading the drill pipe wiper plug try to pass it from safety valve.

13. M/U combination plug dropping head to the last joint. Use pup joint, if necessary. Check flag sub for

proper functioning.

14. The hanger will be set 120m above the 9 5/8” casing shoe. Try to avoid setting hanger on casing

coupling. Set the Hanger as per hanger engineer procedures.

15. Ensure that the running tool is free of the liner (work string 0.5m up and down – record loss of weight

as the hanger sets) before starting to cement.

16. Circulate 120% of the string contents.

17. Cement 7" liner as per cementing program.

18. Displace the cement with the cementing pump to the liner wiper plug. Shear out liner wiper plug

(Record the volume pumped and shearing pressure). Displace combined wiper plugs to latch down

collar.

19. Bump the plug to 3000 psi over final displacement pressure (Record and report final displacement

pressure prior to bump the plug). If there is no bump, do not displace more than 25% of the shoe-track

volume. Displace with Cementing Pump and record cement losses.

20. Hold bumping pressure for 15 minutes. If the plugs bumped and Record it as 7” liner integrity test.

21. Bleed off pressure slowly and check for back-flow.

22. Set packer (If available) as per liner hanger engineer instruction.

23. Circulate at least one mud circulation clean the hole. Check the bottom’s up for cement return. In case

of not available packer, check for U tube f/ DPs. N/D cementing head. POOH to 100 m above Est. top

of cement, After flush string &amp;amp; Circulate at least one mud circulation, POOH 4 stands, close the well

&amp;amp; monitor pressure till cement get hard. Open and fill up the well, record mud volume to fill the well.

24. Clean out well to liner lap @ 1427 m with 8-1/2” bit.

25. Circulate and POOH to 1397 m, pressure test liner lap to 2000 psi for 30 min.

26. If not observed bumping while cementing, D/O 5m of hard cement (if observe hard cement above

LDC, Continue D/O to LDC).

27. Dry test liner lap.

Note:

- Drift Drill pipe while run the liner with suitable Drift.

- Perform injectivity test into 7” liner lap if necessary and inject cement around same.

2-4- Cementing Procedure

1) Clean up tanks and preparing chemicals for mixing fluid.

2) Fill tanks with fresh water for mixing fluids.

3) Before finished running casings with company man approval, start mixing cement additives and preparing mixing fluids according to below cement additives mixing procedure:

a. Add Antifoam to fresh water and allow mixing for 5 minutes. b. Add CaCl2 and allow mixing for 40 minutes.

c. Add Dispersant and allow mixing until the cement operation will finish.

4) Before running casing, check the stinger and stab-in shoe &amp;amp; Install stab-in shoe to end of first casing.

5) After running casing, install stinger to end of first 5" drill pipe.

7) Set the stinger &amp;amp; circulation mud if observed flowing of mud in casing, try again to setting the stinger.

8) Hang drill pipe.

10) Test cement line W/ 3000 psi.

11) Pump spacer.

12) Mix and pump cement slurry.

13) Displace cement with drilling fluid.

14) Sting out and check for float valve working.

3-4- Cementing Procedure

Tail cement mixing procedure:

with mud engineer to measure drilling fluid &amp;amp; cement loss/gain during cement job.

10- Pump per-flush and spacer.

11- Mix and pump lead cement slurry &amp;amp; pump it in the well.

12- Mix and pump tail cement slurry &amp;amp; pump it in the well.

13- Release pump down plug.

14- Displace With mud at optimum rate. Slow pump rate 10 Bbl before Pump down Plug reaches

Wiper Plug (Drill Pipe Displacement is ……. Bbl) at +/- …….Psi.

5 Pressure Test

5.1 Accumulator, BOP, Wellhead and Choke/Kill Manifold

 The BOP, wellhead, choke manifold, and related equipment are normally to be tested on 14

days basis. This period can be extended depending on the well operations and the

specifications in the Drilling Program and the applicable Regulations.

 The accumulator is to be tested prior to the first test of the BOP, or any time after repairs are

made to the accumulator unit. The accumulator bottles pre-charge pressure shall be checked

before drilling out the casing shoe or every 4 weeks.

5.2 Casing and Liner

In the below table, casing or liner integrity test pressure, surface SIP, is given when test medium is fresh water. As usual, green test casing integrity after bump plug is recommended in the cement procedure. If rigs use the displacement mud (density &amp;gt;1.0sg) to test casing, the pressure applied on surface cement head should be considered the mud hydrostatic pressure at casing collar And the surface SIP is given as the following formula:

Surface shut-in Pressure = 80% Casing Burst – B (psi)

B=Drilling fluid hydrostatic pressure - fresh water hydrostatic pressure

Notes: the assumption in the formula above is the external fluid of the casing is fresh water(density:1.0sg), in order to simply the calculation the test fluid inside casing is also assumed as

6 Well Control during Special operation

The well control while wireline logging and running casing is important and critical, best practices shall be followed, including but not limited to:

1) Change BOP ram to casing size and pressure test same to 1500 psi of surface SIP or the value of

80% casing burst with fresh water.

2) The crossover for casing connection to drill pipe must available on floor. A good practice is to

keep a joint of DP with casing crossover at lower end and full opened safety valve at upper end to

be ready for picking up on V-door.

3) Prior to wireline logging, install shooting nipple and pressure test same to again WL BOP to 1500

psi.

4) The cable cutter should be available on rig floor. If kick occurs, cut logging cable and to close

blend BOP is optional

5) The contractor shall perform relative pressure test, drills, safety checks etc as per NIOC/NIDC

Policy during the well operations.

MUD LOGGING PROGRAM:

The Mud logging services for all wells should start from the beginning of 26" hole and will continue to the total depth (TD).

A complete mud logging services for all wells must be provided by the contractor with 24 hours (two working shifts of 2 mud loggers + 1 sample catcher + 1 engineer shall be provided by contractor for each 12 hours shift, consisting of four person as day shift and four at night).

LOGS AND REPORTS

Prepared during each shift on a translucent sepia form or paper print (log scale 1:500 meters or according to COMPANY requirements):

Drilling Parameters

Shale density

1 Basic HSE Requirements

1. Contractor should establish an effective HSE system and implement it strictly.

2. Contractor must adhere to the standards and regulations of Health, Safe and Environment constituted by

the local government.

3. Contractor must strictly adhere to the procedures / standards and regulations of Health, Safety and

Environment promulgated by NIDC.

4. Contractor should comply with all applicable local government regulations including guidelines and

recommended practices and any other Iranian authorities having jurisdiction.

5. All personnel should respect the local culture, traditions and social values of the indigenous population of

the Iran and South Azadegan region.

6. Contractor shall hire qualified and experienced worker and familiar his personnel with hazards especially

with H2S and Mine and UXO (unexploded ordinance) according to related procedure.

7. Contractor shall conduct proper training about UXO (unexploded ordinance) and mine awareness to all

personnel

2 Well Control

All the drilling operation shall obey the requirement of Well Control Manual of NIDC and contractor’s well control manual; Under no circumstances should the deviation from well control policy be permitted without prior approval through NIDC. If the contractor’s well control manual or anywhere has conflict with Well Control Manual of NIDC， take Well Control Manual of NIDC as the standard.

(1) RECORDING REFERENCE

All BOP tests, drills, function tests, any malfunctions, repair or maintenance to the mud system and well control equipment shall be recorded in the IADC daily reports and shall be signed by both the Drilling Contractor's Tool Pusher and Drilling Supervisor on the well site. They shall also be recorded in the Daily Drilling Report.

(2) FLOW CHECK PROCEDURE

To avoid a kick situation, it is recommended that a flow check be conducted at specific times during the drilling operation.

1) While drilling(any warning sign)

NIDC

NIDC Drilling Projects Management

Drilling Engineering &amp;amp; Programming Division

South Azadegan Oil field

AZNS#084 (S372 – Area I ) Rev 0.0 PEDEC

Drilling Program WELL NO. AZNS-084(S372) Page 158

2) Prior to tripping the drill string

3) While tripping(any warning sign)

4) While out of hole(continuously)

5) Trip out:

 After pulling 5% of the drill pipe

 At the midpoint depth of the wellbore

 Prior to pulling the first stand of drill collars

 After all the drill string is out of hole.

6) Trip in:

 Upon reaching surface casing shoe

 At midpoint of the wellbore

(3) PRIMARY CONTROL REFERENCE

It is the responsibility of the Drilling Contractor to keep the hole full at all times by using all the available equipment. The Drilling Supervisor shall monitor that the correct preventive practices are being implemented and/or conducted at all times.

Extreme care shall be taken to monitor mud volume, drilling breaks and gas cut mud.

The MACP (Maximum allowable casing pressure) shall be confirmed by the Drilling Supervisor, either after setting each new casing string or, whenever the density of the drilling mud changes.

The MACP shall be clearly written on a kick control sheet that will be posted near the choke control panel.

The predetermined distance at which the Tool Joint is to be pulled above the rotary should be posted on rig floor near the BOP control panel.

The Driller is responsible for carefully measuring and recording the slow pump pressure. Awareness of these values is an important element in killing operations, in order to avoid formation breakdown.

Take a measure and record the slow pump pressure at three different flow rates with all pumps at the following times:

 Once per tour.

 Whenever changes occur in the mud density/rheology.

 Whenever changes occur in the dimension and characteristics of the string, BHA, jet size, jet plugged

or jet lost, etc.

(4) SECONDARY CONTROL REFERENCE

Any time a drilling break is noticed, drilling shall stop and a static monitoring of the well shall be carried out. Space-out for all Pipe Rams and Annular Preventer must be known to the Driller at all times to keep tool joints clear of annular preventer and rams.

(5) KICK DETECTION PROCEDURE WHILE DRILLING

If there is an indication of a possible kick occurring, the Driller shall follow the kick detection procedures outlined below:

Stop drilling with the pump onPick up top drive to a predetermined space-out positionShut off the pumps and check for well flow by visual examination on the bell nipple or flow line.

1) If the well is not flowing:

 Immediately notify the rig manager, Drilling Supervisor and Tool pusher.

 The Drilling Supervisor will decide whether to circulate bottoms up or resume drilling. The

penetration rate will be limited as long as the cause of the abnormal situation is undetermined.

Always be aware that some hydrocarbons (gas or oil cut mud) may rise to the surface. Ensure that the

proper monitoring and safety systems all in place.

2) If the well is flowing:

 Close the well as per the Shut-in Procedure.

 Immediately notify the Wellsite Drilling Supervisor, rig manager and Tool pusher.

3 Health

1. This well is committed to develop for oil in a responsible manner that promotes employees'

and local inhabitants' health.

2. A trained Paramedic and proper MEDIVAC equipment and ambulance shall be stationed on

the drilling rig during the drilling campaign.

3. An emergency medical evacuation plan shall be coordinated, and shall keep in touch with

emergency response centres manned by qualified doctor 24-hours per day in Ahwaz city.

4. Medical emergency report and investigation shall be performed as soon as possible in

accordance with Medical Emergency Procedures.

4 Safety

1. Contractor shall make detail operation procedures which have covered all related

activities.

2. Due to high concentration of H2S in Sarvak, Kazhdumi and Gadvan reservoirs, Make

detail H2S operation procedures, in particular, and carry it out strictly.

3. Contractor must provide lifesaving equipment like SCBA, Escape Mask, H2S detectors (Multi

portable and personal detector) and implement the H2S Services system during drilling activity.

4. All lifting equipment and cranes must be certified by approved 3rd party (approved by Institute of

Standards &amp;amp; Industrial Research of Iran)

5. All electrical equipment should be designed for such locations, and listed by nationally recognized

testing laboratory. All wiring components and electrical equipment should be maintained in

accordance with the manufacturers’ recommendation.

6. Contractor shall implement the risk assessment and Job Safety Analysis before starting the drilling

activity.

7. PSSR (Pre-Startup Safety Review) before spud-in and penetrating into oil and gas formations are

mandatory by contractor under the supervision of Company and approved by Company.

8. Contractor shall pay much attention to fire, explosion prevention and well control.

9. Contractor shall make detail Emergency Response Plan and Evacuation Plan.

10. Contractor shall do efforts to keep employees safety as possible.

5 Environment

Requirement on location

1) The access road and well location construction shall be accorded with construction program of

well location. It minimizes any impacts on the local residents, prevent all soil contamination,

prevent all ground water contamination, and prevent all surface water contamination. Cutting and

waste water pit shall be lining and drainage system shall be good and to avoid farm and season

canal contamination.

2) Management regulation for transportation truck, drilling operation machine and tools shall be

carried out strictly to avoid damage farm and trees, etc.

3) Well site shall be flat and clean. All the equipment, materials, drilling tools shall be put in order.

4) Control the rig noise to decrease the influence to surroundings while drilling at the inhabitation

5) Contractor shall perform on‐site segregation of wastes prior to transfer to the transfer area and/or

delivery to the transportation Contractor in accordance with the following waste hazard

classification.

Non-Hazardous Wastes (Re-usable, Recyclable and Recoverable Wastes)

1) Ferrous and non-ferrous metals, plastics, and wood wastes, PETs and potentially paper and glass

2) Materials shall be separately segregated and provision may be made for size reduction and

containerization equipment.

3) The Contractor/Generators are encouraged to seek for recycle/re-use alternatives based on the

Local available facilities, for final disposal of these materials.

4) It should be noted that landfill disposal of metal waste materials and wood wastes shall be

prohibited. For wood wastes re-use of and/or salvage of commercial timber, or deliver/release to

5) Local community are recommended.

Hazardous Wastes

Hazardous Waste, such as clinic waste, oil waste, waste produced by painting, insulation works shall be duly segregated.

Facilities of environment protection supplied to well site

1) Mud purifying circulation system

2) Cooling water spraying and circulating system for drilling pump

3) Special recovery tank for deposed oil

4) Reserve house for valuable mud chemicals

5) Automatic mud weighting supply system

6) BOP stack is equipped according to drilling design

7) Define a separation area for gathering all waste according to waste management procedure

Requirement of environment protection on location

1) Sewage pit Area of the sewage pit: 1500 m2

2) Prior to spud， mud pit and sewage pit must comply with the standard. Install cooling water

spraying and circulating system for drilling pump and sewage circulating system for cleaning rig

floor and equipment.

3) Install BOP stack and pressure test shall be operated according to the drilling design to avoid

blowout.

4) Install oil supply lines and check whether there is any leakage.

Management of environment protection on location

1) In drilling operation， keep mud and sewage from overflowing. If it happens, clean up timely.

2) Mud chemicals shall be stored according to the standard and shall not be scattered around well

site. If mud chemicals scatter while loading or unloading, clean it up at once. The sack of mud

chemicals shall be recovered. Do not dispose it on site.

3) Enhance water management at well location and do not wash equipment with fresh water.

Stop water flowing for long time. Overhead tanks shall be utilized.

4) Oil management shall be carefully at the well site. No oil dirt on site, no dripping and leaking

at oil tank and manifold system area.

5) After the well is completed, reinforce the sewage pit， solidify the disposed mud and have

environment procedure fulfilled.

6) Install fuel supply lines and keep them in good condition.

7) All the drilling fluid materials shall be recovered and shall not be left at the well site after

completion.

8) The environmental protection personnel from contractor and operator side shall check and

accept the well site environment according to the regulation after completion. Only well site

environment is qualified, the well can be delivered.

9) Transition Area for Hazardous Waste shall also be provided by each Contractor in his

allocated area,

Standard of utilization and discharging of wastes on location

1) Conduct drilling operation according to the design, drilling mud is needed before spud.

2) Sewage that cannot be recovered shall be put into the pit， do not discharge. If the volume of

sewage is too big and some should be discharged， the quality of drainage must comply with the

following regulations.

Maximum permitted concentration of wastes in water

3) Make full use of waste water. Water in mud pump and water brake must be utilized by

circulating. Water that is used to wash drill floor, shall be recovered after deposition. The

recovery rate of waste water shall reach 85％.

4) Disposed oil shall be recovered entirely. Recovery rate shall be 100％.Dumping of waste oil

shall be prohibited.

5) In drilling operation, non-chrome thinner high temperature mud system shall be used often if

engineering is qualified.

6) While drilling in special area， adopt mud creation inhabitation techniques to decrease the waste

mud creation.

7) After completion, all the mud chemicals, bentonite, clays shall be recovered and shall not be left

at the well site. Mud in purifying tank shall also be recovered after completion.

8) In case of any flammable or noxious gas encountered， steps shall be taken at once to prevent

kicks and blowout. Gas shall be guided into ignition equipment to burn it away.

9) Burning material that may result in serious smog or horrible smell at the well site is not allowed.

For cement or barite that may result in granular dust pollution， operation shall be performed in

a closed system.

10) For abandoned well， filled with cement plugs to seal the oil, gas or water formation.

11) Contractor/Generators are required to transport all generated wastes to the location/facilities

designated, and licensed by authorities and/or approved/verified by the Company/PEDEC (as

appropriate).

12) All wastes shall be transferred by approved Sub‐Contractor (which could be a 3rd party SubContractor of the Contractor/Generator itself). The Waste Transporter and any other waste

management service Contractor shall be licensed in accordance with local regulations and are in

compliance with such regulations. Company shall verify and approve the Waste Transportation

Contractor by checking licenses and qualifications, audit and inspections, verification of human

resources and received trainings etc.

13) The transportation Contractor shall ensure that all wastes are transported in a safe and

responsible manner.

6 H2S monitoring and prevention measure

6.1 Monitoring H2S

1) Somewhere on the well site is apt to accumulate H2S, such as mud pit, shale shaker,

and drilling platform, should be installed one set of. Make sure H2S monitor and

alarm system can be used.

2) Alarm threshold setting for H2S warning indicator: the first warning level is

10mg/m3, unable warning sound, just show present value of H2S content to

operators. The second warning level is 20mg/m3, when the H2S content in air exceed

20mg/m3, H2S warning indicator can give an alarm automatically, and warning

sound should be heard by everyone work in well site. The audible alarm should be

installed on Kelly board.

3) Equip enough gas masks on drilling platform, shaker screen (total amount should

large than 24), and equip 12 sets of 30min positive pressure Air Aspirators， 2 sets of

portable H2S monitor and appropriative H2S warning indicator. Arrange a person

specially assigned for taking charge all the protective apparatus. This man must do

periodical check to keep these equipment in a good condition.

4) H2S monitor should be done weekly check and compulsory examination.

5) After drilling into the pay zone, strengthen the detection of H2S content in mud.

NIDC Drilling Projects Management

Drilling Engineering &amp;amp; Programming Division

South Azadegan Oil field

AZNS#084 (S372 – Area I ) Rev 0.0 PEDEC

Drilling Program WELL NO. AZNS-084(S372) Page 166

6.2 Measures for H2S prevention

1) Windsocks shall be set on the drill floor and in the monsoon direction or/and

prevailing wind direction of Azadegan oil field, off well site. In emergency,

employees must follow the evacuation procedure.

2) Explosion-proof blowers shall be installed around the rig, shale shaker, and drilling

fluid tanks to blow away toxic and flammable gas at the well site.

3) The rig crew in the H2S area shall be furnished with H2S monitors and adequate

protective apparatus. Everybody shall be able to use, maintain, and check the

apparatus.

4) The technicians of rig crew are responsible for H2S proof training and the tool

pusher is in charge of the supervision and examination.

5) The pH value of drilling fluid in the H2S area shall be kept over 9.5. Pay attention to

measurement of H2S concentration in drilling fluid. The H2S concentration shall be

kept at less than 50mg/cm3 by using sulphur removal agents and degassers.

6) Personnel safety and protection shall be carried out according to SY/T5087 during

operations in polluted areas where H2S content exceeds the critical concentration.

7) When the rig crew makes decision to bleed and fire because well control cannot be

performed due to well site conditions, operations shall be performed according to

procedures in SY/T5087.

8) Once blowout occurs, the incident shall be reported to the higher level department as

soon as possible and firefighting trucks, ambulances, medical care personnel and

technicians shall be on duty at the well site.

9) After the blowout is controlled, H2S concentration should be measured in the places

where H2S is possible to gather.

10) The personnel are not allowed to access until the H2S concentration is below the

critical concentration.

General Information Page 9 of 175

Development Well

Introduction

The AZADEGAN Oilfield is Located in Khuzestan Province and is Approximately Located 80 Kilometers West of Ahwaz City, Near to Iran-Iraq Border. It is in The Northwest of The YADAVARAN Field and in The West of JUFEYR Field. The Average Monthly Temperature is 45ºc in summer, and Highest Temperature is 52ºc. The Lowest Temperature is -4.4ºc in winter. Maximum Rainfall is 78 mm in February, Winter Season.

The Field is in Flooding Plain Area with Convenient Road Network which Extends to Ahwaz. Most of The Oil Fields in The Region are Located in The Foothill Zone Zagros Folded Zone of the NW-SE Trending Zagros Mountain Range, and Have Similar Trends to The Zagros Mountain Range Elongated Anticline Structure.

This Document Covers the Drilling of Gadvan Producer Well in South Azadegan Oilfield, Iran. Well G-04 Shall Be Considered to Produce from the Gadvan Reservoir. Plan is to KOP 3585m. Commence Directional Drilling 8-1/2” Hole to 7” Liner Setting Depth at 3934 M. Then 7” Liner will be Run and Cemented and Continue Operation with Directional drilling 6 1/8” Hole Section about 350 m horizontally in Gadvan 5C Formation to 4284 M. The 4-1/2” Slotted Liner will be run to TD &amp;amp; Run Standard Completion String, N/Up Well Head and Complete Well.

General Information Page 11 of 175

Development Well

S373 Highly Deviated Well on Pad-48 Objectives

As The Previous Exploration/Delineation Drilling in AZADEGAN Oil Field has Proved Presence of a Very Prolific Hydrocarbon Bearing Sedimentary Column, Particularly within the Cretaceous Sequences.

G-04 Gadvan producer well is planned to be drilled in Pad-26 which is located in the North part

of South Azadegan oil field in Area-I.

Far away from Gadvan OWC and achieve the better reservoir quality, this well is planned as

Horizontal well with Azimuth of 40 degree.

Figure 1 shows the position of Pad-26 on the underground contour map on top of Gadvan.

The Horizontal well (G-04) will be drilled down to Gadvan Reservoir and subsequently will be

completed as a Gadvan reservoir oil producer.
