General Information Page 12 of 175

Development Well

Pore and Fracture Press Prediction

Since the Formation Pressure of Gachsaran Formation is Different between North Area and South Near and Decreases Greatly and Complete Loss Took Place at all Four Existing Wells in South Area, the Oilfield is divided into three Areas.

Area I (North of AZN-10): Area I Located in North of Line1(Y-Coordinate: 3452051), in this Area, Gachsaran Formation is Characterized with Abnormal High Pressure. For No Wells have ever been Drilled in the Area between Line1 (Y-Coordinate: 3452051) and Line 3 (Y-Coordinate: 3457993), This Area Exists Greater Uncertainties and is Delimited to the Area I Temporarily.

Area II (Between AZN-10 and AZN-11): Area II Located between Line1 (Ycoordinate: 3452051) and Line 2 (Y-Coordinate: 3443549), in this Area, the Formation of Gachsaran Formation Decreases Greatly.

Area III (South of AZN-11): Area III Located the South of Line 2 (Y-Coordinate: 3443549), in this Area, the Formation of Gachsaran Formation Decreases Greatly and all Existing Wells Occurred Complete Loss at Pabdeh Formation.

The Area Division shall be Adjusted According to Further Actual Drilling Operation, and Quantity of Wells in Different Areas could be also Adjusted Accordingly.

Well : AZNS-118 (G04)

Type : IGH

General Information Page 13 of 175

Development Well

Program Outline

It is planned to drill and complete a Gadvan Horizontal well.

26" Hole section:

The 26” Hole Section will be Drilled 154 M through Aghajari Formation. Aghajari Formation Consists of A Marl, Sand-Shale. For Drilling This Section 67-69 pcf Pre-Hydrated Bentonite Mud will be used for Hole Cleaning. Also PHB Pill Will Be Used to Clean the Hole and Since Bentonite has the Best Cake around the Well Bore, It will make a Good Cake for Hole Stability. According to Previous Wells in this Field, this Section is almost Problem Free. The 20" Casing will be set at ±150 M and it will be cemented in One Stage with Stinger (Exact CMT Program will be issued in Due Time). N/U 20-3/4" 3k C.H.H &amp;amp; 21 1/4" 2K Annular BOP and Single Rams.

17-1/2" Hole section:

This Section will be drilled from ±154 M to ±1400 M through Aghajari Formation. According to offset Wells tight spots, Hard Back Ream, W&amp;amp;R while RIH and Bit Balling Up in surface was recorded. For Drilling This Section 70-80 Pcf Kcl/Nacl Polymer Mud will be Used. Also PHB Pill will be used to clean the Hole. CDR/GR log will be run in open hole. 13 3/8" Casing Shoe will Be Set at ±1400 M about 55m below the Top of Gachsaran to Case off Full Soft Unconsolidated Formation of Lower Aghajari and Drill the next Hole Section with different Mud Density. It will be cemented in One Stage (Lead &amp;amp; Tail - Exact CMT Program will be issued in Due Time). N/Up C.H.S 20-3/4" 3k x 13-5/8” 5K. N/U 13-5/8" 10K BOP’s Stack (13 5/8" 5K Annular Preventer + 13 5/8" 10K Double Rams + 13 5/8" 10K Single).

12 ¼" Hole Section:

This Section will be drilled from ±1400 to ±1780 M through Gachsaran. For Drilling this Section the 115-125 Pcf KCl Polymer Mud can be used. The Risks of Drilling this Section is Heavy MW &amp;amp; High pressure formation, Low ROP, Tight Hole and Stuck Pipe Based on Offset Wells. CDR/GR Log Will Be Run in Open Hole. 9 5/8" Casing Shoe will be set at ±1780 M at the 5m above Top of Asmari to Isolate High Pressure Formation for Drilling to Next Section to TD with low Mud Weight. It will be cemented in One Stage (Lead &amp;amp; Tail -Exact CMT Program will be issued in Due Time). CCL/GR/CBL-VDL Will Be Run. N/U T.H.S 13 5/8" 5k x 11" 10k. N/U 13-5/8” 10K BOP’s Stack. (13 5/8" 5k Annular BOP + 13 5/8" 10k Double Rams + 13 5/8" 10K Single).

Well : AZNS-118 (G04)

Type : IGH

General Information Page 14 of 175

Development Well

8 ½” Hole Section (Vertical and Directional):

This Section will be drilled from ±1780 to 3585 M (KOP) &amp;amp; Cont’ drlg to 3934M (7” Liner Setting Depth) will be drilled as Directionally through Dariyan &amp;amp; Gadvan Formations. Which Consist of Sandstone &amp;amp; lime stone, marl &amp;amp; shale. MWD/LWD with GR Should be used in Directional Drilling as Survey &amp;amp; Resistivity Tools from KOP to Hole Section TD. The CDR log should run on wireline. The Full suite log should be run with TLC method. 75-81 Pcf Kcl Polymer Mud Will Be Used For Drilling This Section. Then 7” Liner will be run ±3934M and Cemented in One Stage (Exact CMT Program will be issued in Due Time). CCL/GR/CBLVDL Will Be Run after Perform 7” Cementing Job.

6 1/8" Hole Section (Directional):

This Section will be Drilled from ±3934 M MD to ±4284 M MD in Gadvan Formation Zone-5C As Horizontal. 81-82 Pcf Kcl Polymer Mud will Be Used for Drilling this Section. The Risks of Drilling This Section is Drilling Fluid Loss, Tight Hole and Stuck Pipe Based on Offset Wells. MWD/LWD/GR will be used in Horizontal open Hole. Run a full suite log as TLC method. 4-1/2” Slotted Liner will be run to ±4284 mMD and Hang Off. Displace hole with completion fluid. Then the Well will be completed as Gadvan Producer well.

 If well is not completed the temporary abandon program will be issued at due

time by contractor

A brief description of the stratigraphic units expected to be drilled in South Azadegan typical well has been presented in the following breakdown.

 Recent/Aghajari Formation

The Aghajari Formation consists of a repetition of brown to grey calcareous Sandstones, chert debris and gypsum-veined red marl. A fauna of brackish to freshwater was observed, together with more marine fauna.

 Gachsaran Formation

The Gachsaran Formation with a thickness ranges from 400 m to 600 m, thicken towards the north. Deposition of the Gachsaran Formation is cyclic. The cycle began with a deposition of shallow-water marine carbonates, and then it was overlain by a thick evaporitic phase. The evaporites were capped by red to variegated marl, which represented the end of cycle.

 Asmari Formation

The Asmari Formation in Azadegan Field developed a massive sandstone interval, with a few thin argillaceous layers in the upper sections. Sands are clear, fine to medium-sorted, and poorly consolidated. On the other hand, the lower sections consist of intercalation of sandy, chalky, slightly dolomitic high-energy limestone with sands layers.

 Pabdeh Formation

Pabdeh Formation is divided into two parts in the Azadegan field. The upper part is made of grey to dark-brown argillaceous limestones and marls. Planktonic fauna dates that this part. was deposited in Oligocene. The lower part is composed of dark-brown, slightly argillaceous limestone. Pelagic fauna, mostly Globigerina and Globorotalia, indicates that this part was formed during late Paleocene to late Eocene in age. It seems that no early Paleocene Formation exists in the Azadegan area.

 Gurpi Formation

The Gurpi Formation in the Azadegan Field consists of grey to dark-brownish, slightly argillaceous micritic limestone with Maestrichtian to Campanian aged fauna. At Well AZN-1,

about 50 meters of chalky limestones were encountered in the middle of the Gurpi formation,

which contains abundant fragments of rudists, bryozoa, corals, and Orbitoides.

 Ilam Formation

In the Azadegan Field, the Ilam Formation consists of grey micritic limestone, often argillaceous, rarely pyritic, limestones. Microfauna, mostly pelagic, including rotalids and oligostegina assemblage, a few algae, bryozoa, and rudist fragments exist.

 Laffan Formation

The Laffan Formation developed a thin greenish-grey pyritic shale layer, capping the Sarvak Formation. It was encountered in the Azadegan wells and only ostracods were found. It is a cap rock for the upper part of the Sarvak reservoir.

 Sarvak Formation

The Sarvak Formation developed a carbonate unit which was gradually overlying the Kazhdumi Formation, and it was abruptly terminated by an erosion phase and covered by various late Cretaceous sediments. A Typical geological section of the Sarvak Formation in Azadegan reveals that dark grey fine grained nodulary argillaceous limestone interbedded with thin marls in the bottom, and graded upward into a white-to-buff massive chalky limestone with siliceous nodules; it was developed a very massive tan-to-brown limestone containing abundant rudist debris in the middle part; the upper part is made up of rubbly limestone with red staining and leached zones of breccia and the top of Sarvak Formation is very ferruginous

 Kazhdumi Formation

In the Azadegan Field, the upper part of the Kazhdumi Formation is made up of dark - grey to dark-brown marls, the middle part developed light-grey, micritic to chalky limestone, the low part, is around40-60m in thickness clean channel sands interbeded argillaceous sands with streaks of shale.

 Gadvan Formation

In the Gadvan Formation, a variety of lithological rock types such as carbonates, rich organic shales and sandstones were deposited in various environments. The lower part of the Gadvan Formation is composed of low-energy, but not very deep, micritic, often argillaceous limestone with echinoids and algal fragments. Two sandstone units were defined in the Gadvan Formation lateral changes and especially discontinuity of the sandstone layers which are onsist of fine clastics (shales and siltstones) may be expected
